text: Summary A WooCommerce website typically costs from a few thousand dollars for a simple store to well over fifty thousand for a custom or B2B build. The price depends on design, features, integrations, data migration and who builds it. This guide gives typical ranges by store type, the ongoing costs to budget for, and how to choose between DIY, a freelancer and an agency. Ranges are market guides, not a quote. Introduction The honest answer to “how much does a WooCommerce website cost?” is that it depends on what the store has to do. A store that sells twenty products with a ready-made theme is a different project from one that connects to an ERP, takes quotes and serves wholesale buyers. WooCommerce itself is free software, which is why many owners start there. The cost sits around it: design, development, hosting, extensions, payments and ongoing care. Knowing those parts lets you compare quotes fairly. Use this guide to set a realistic budget, then try our ecommerce website cost calculator for a number based on your own features. If you want a quote from a team that builds WooCommerce stores every week, see our WooCommerce development services . Table of Contents What is the average cost of a WooCommerce website? How much does a WooCommerce store cost by store type? What drives the price of a WooCommerce site? What are the ongoing costs after launch? Should you build it yourself, hire a freelancer or use an agency? What hidden costs do store owners often miss? How can you reduce the cost without cutting quality? Which WooCommerce costs do people forget to budget for? Should you build it yourself, hire a freelancer or use an agency? What does it cost to run a WooCommerce store each month? How can you lower the cost without hurting quality? What does a realistic budget look like for different stores? How long does a WooCommerce project take, and how does time affect cost? What is the average cost of a WooCommerce website? Most small businesses spend between roughly $3,000 and $15,000 for a straightforward WooCommerce store. Growing stores with custom design and several integrations commonly land between $15,000 and $50,000. Complex builds with custom features, large catalogs, B2B pricing or ERP links can go beyond that. These are typical market ranges and vary by country, team and scope. They are useful for planning, but only a scoped quote tells you your real cost. How much does a WooCommerce store cost by store type? The easiest way to estimate is to place your store in one of four groups. Store type What it includes Typical range Typical timeline Starter store Premium theme, core pages, payments, shipping, basic SEO setup $3,000 to $10,000 2 to 6 weeks Growth store Custom design, product filters, marketing tools, a few integrations $10,000 to $30,000 6 to 12 weeks Custom store Custom features, subscriptions or bundles, advanced search, data migration $30,000 to $60,000 3 to 5 months B2B or enterprise Account pricing, quotes, net terms, portal, ERP or CRM integration $50,000 and up 4 to 8 months Treat each range as a starting point. A starter store with a large product import, or a growth store with a tricky checkout, can move up a group. What drives the price of a WooCommerce site? Five things move the number more than anything else. Design: a premium theme with light changes costs far less than a custom design built around your brand and customer journey. Features: subscriptions, bundles, product configurators, wholesale pricing and quotes each add build and testing time. Integrations: connecting to an ERP, accounting tool, warehouse or marketing platform often costs more than the storefront itself. Data migration: moving products, customers and orders from another platform takes planning, especially if you want to keep your SEO rankings and URLs. Content volume: a large catalog needs import tools, clean data and image work. If you are moving from another platform, read our guide to a safe migration first, because migration planning shapes the whole budget. What are the ongoing costs after launch? A WooCommerce store keeps costing money after it goes live. Plan for these every year. Hosting: from a basic plan for a small store to managed or cloud hosting for a busy one Extensions and plugin licences, which renew yearly Maintenance: updates, security checks, backups and fixes Payment fees charged on every order Marketing, SEO and conversion work if you want the store to grow Should you build it yourself, hire a freelancer or use an agency? Each route fits a different situation. The cheapest option at launch is not always the cheapest over two years. Route Cost Best for Main risk Do it yourself Lowest upfront Very small catalogs and tight budgets Time cost and limits on security, speed and SEO Freelancer Moderate Defined, simple projects One person to cover design, code and support Agency Highest upfront Growing stores, custom features, integrations Needs a clear scope to control cost If you expect to add features, integrations or a bigger catalog within a year, an experienced team usually saves money by getting the structure right the first time. What hidden costs do store owners often miss? The ones that surprise people most are data migration, redirect planning, third-party licences that renew every year, payment gateway setup for restricted products, accessibility fixes, and the time needed to write product content. Add a buffer of ten to twenty percent for changes during the build. How can you reduce the cost without cutting quality? Start with the features that make money and add the rest later. Reuse a quality theme where design is not the selling point. Prepare your product data before the build starts. And agree a clear scope with a fixed deliverable list so changes are priced rather than absorbed. Which WooCommerce costs do people forget to budget for? Most quotes cover design and development, but a store has more moving parts than that. The items below catch many owners by surprise in the first year. Premium plugins are the biggest one. WooCommerce itself is free, yet subscriptions, bookings, shipping rates, product filters and advanced search often come as paid add-ons with yearly renewals. Add up the renewals before you commit to a plugin stack. Data work is the next one. Moving products, customers and order history from an older platform needs cleanup, mapping and testing. If you are coming from another platform, plan time for it. Our ecommerce website migration checklist shows what that involves. Finally, there are the small recurring items: transactional email service, backups, security scanning, a CDN, tax tools and a spam filter. None is expensive alone, but together they can reach a meaningful monthly figure. Premium plugin renewals each year. Data migration and product cleanup. Product photography and copywriting. Email service, backups and security tools. Legal pages, tax setup and compliance checks. Should you build it yourself, hire a freelancer or use an agency? The right choice depends on how complex the store is and how much of your own time you can spend. Here is a plain comparison. Option Typical fit Main risk Best when Build it yourself Small catalog, simple needs Slow launch, missed SEO and speed basics You have time and a tight budget Freelancer Standard store with a few custom needs Single point of failure, limited support You can manage the project yourself Agency Custom features, integrations, growth plans Higher upfront cost You need a team, a clear scope and ongoing support If you are weighing the agency route, see our WooCommerce development services to understand what is normally included. What does it cost to run a WooCommerce store each month? After launch, the store needs hosting, updates and care. A small store can run on modest managed hosting, while a busy store with thousands of products needs stronger servers and caching. Maintenance is the line people skip. WordPress, WooCommerce and every plugin need regular updates, and a skipped update is how many stores end up hacked or broken before a big sales day. A support plan covers updates, backups, uptime checks and small fixes so you are not paying emergency rates later. Marketing also belongs in the monthly figure. A beautiful store that nobody finds does not pay back, so set aside a budget for SEO, email and ads from the first month. How can you lower the cost without hurting quality? Spending less is possible, but cut the right things. Cutting speed, security or checkout testing will cost you more later. Launch with the products and features you need first, then add the rest in phases. Use a proven theme and customize the parts that matter, instead of a fully custom design. Choose fewer, better plugins. Every extra plugin adds cost, risk and load time. Prepare your product data, images and copy before the build starts. Delays here are billed time. Agree on a written scope so changes are planned, not surprises. What does a realistic budget look like for different stores? These are illustrative examples to help you think in categories, not quotes. Real prices depend on your scope and your location. A starter store with a ready made theme, under a hundred products and standard payments is the simplest case. The work is mostly setup, branding and product entry. A growing store with a few hundred products, shipping rules, subscriptions or a customer account area needs more design and configuration, plus testing of every checkout path. A custom or B2B store with negotiated pricing, ERP or inventory integrations and complex shipping is a larger project that needs discovery, planning and phased delivery. For that kind of build, read about B2B ecommerce development . How long does a WooCommerce project take, and how does time affect cost? Time and cost move together. A ready made theme with standard payments can be live in a few weeks, while a custom store with integrations may take several months. The longer the discovery, design and testing phases run, the more hours the project needs. You can protect your budget by deciding what is needed for launch and what can wait. A clear scope, quick feedback and complete content on day one are the three things that most often keep a project on schedule. Ask any provider for a timeline with milestones, not only a final date. It shows how they think about the work and makes delays visible early. Conclusion A WooCommerce website can cost very little or a great deal, and the difference is scope. Place your store in the right group, add the ongoing costs, and compare quotes on the same scope. If you want a scoped estimate for your store, contact Virtina and we will break it down feature by feature. Frequently Asked Questions Is WooCommerce really free? The plugin itself is free. You still pay for hosting, a theme, extensions, payment fees and development or maintenance time. How long does it take to build a WooCommerce store? A simple store can launch in a few weeks. Custom and B2B builds commonly take several months because of design, integrations and testing. Is WooCommerce cheaper than Shopify? It can be cheaper in software fees and more flexible, but you manage hosting and maintenance. Compare total cost over two or three years, not only the first month. How much does a WooCommerce redesign cost? A redesign usually costs less than a new build because products and data already exist, but it depends on how much changes in design, features and structure. Can I start small and grow later? Yes. WooCommerce scales well if the first build is clean and extensible. Choose a structure that lets you add features without rebuilding.

text: Summary Firearms and ammo stores are treated as high risk by many processors, so approvals take longer and accounts can be frozen without warning. To stay stable, apply with a processor that knows the category, keep clean policies and records, hold chargebacks under one percent and set up a backup gateway before you need it. Introduction Selling firearms, ammo and accessories online is legal, but payment processing is harder than for most stores. Big names often decline the category or close accounts after launch. This guide explains what underwriters check, which options exist and how to protect your account. For platform choices, read our gun store ecommerce platforms comparison . Table of Contents Why are firearms and ammo stores treated as high risk? What do underwriters look for? What payment options exist for firearms stores? How can you reduce chargebacks and freezes? Why do you need a backup processor? Which ecommerce platform works best with these gateways? Which documents do you need before you apply? How do FFL transfers affect payment processing? Is selling ammo and accessories easier than selling firearms? What fees and reserves should you expect? How do you keep your store compliant on the website side? What should you do if your account is frozen or declined? What types of processors work with firearms stores? How do you prevent chargebacks on firearms orders? How should you plan payments as your volume grows? What does a stable payment setup look like for a firearms store? Which mistakes cause firearms stores to lose their accounts? What is a quick checklist before you apply? Why are firearms and ammo stores treated as high risk? Processors worry about regulation, brand reputation and chargeback exposure. Some banks also set policies that exclude the category entirely. That is why many merchants find themselves approved by one provider and refused by another with the same paperwork. What do underwriters look for? Valid licenses and a clear compliance process for shipping to FFL dealers. Clear refund, shipping and age verification policies on the site. Business history, processing statements and owner credit. Low chargeback and refund ratios. A professional site with real contact details. What payment options exist for firearms stores? Here is how the main routes compare. Option Approval Stability Notes Mainstream processors Often declined Can freeze later Check terms before applying High risk merchant accounts Easier Good with clean history Higher rates and reserves Gateways with firearm friendly banks Category aware Strong Best for steady volume Alternative checkout methods Varies Varies Use as a backup only Our high risk payment processing guide compares gateways in more detail, and merchant account underwriting in 2026 explains the review process. How can you reduce chargebacks and freezes? Verify age and ship firearms only to licensed dealers. Send clear order and shipping confirmations. Use a recognizable billing descriptor. Respond to disputes quickly with evidence. Avoid sudden jumps in volume without telling your processor. Why do you need a backup processor? Even stable merchants can lose an account because of a bank policy change. A second approved gateway lets you keep taking orders while you resolve the issue. Set it up in advance, since approval can take weeks. Which ecommerce platform works best with these gateways? WooCommerce and Magento give the most flexibility for adding firearm friendly gateways and compliance steps. Read how to sell firearms online or see our custom firearms ecommerce solutions . Which documents do you need before you apply? Preparation shortens approval. Underwriters want proof that your business is legitimate and your processes are safe. Business registration and your federal and state licenses. A list of what you sell and where you ship. Your website policies: refunds, shipping, age checks and FFL transfers. Several months of bank statements and prior processing statements, if you have them. Owner identification and credit information. How do FFL transfers affect payment processing? Firearms usually ship to a licensed dealer, not to the buyer. Processors like this because it shows a compliant sales process, so describe it clearly on your site and in your application. Make the steps visible at checkout: the buyer chooses a dealer, the dealer confirms, and the order ships. That reduces disputes from buyers who did not understand how the sale works. Is selling ammo and accessories easier than selling firearms? Policies differ by processor and by state. Some will approve accessories and optics but restrict ammo or firearms, while others accept all three with the right documents. Tell the underwriter exactly what you sell on day one. Surprises after approval, such as a new product line, are a common reason for account reviews. What fees and reserves should you expect? High risk accounts usually cost more than standard ones. Compare the full picture, not only the headline rate. Cost item What to ask Why it matters Processing rate Is it flat or tiered? Tiered pricing hides extra fees Reserve How much and for how long? It holds part of your cash Chargeback fee How much per dispute? Fees add up with volume Monthly and gateway fees What is included? Small fees compound Early termination fee Is there a long contract? It limits switching Our guide to best high risk payment gateways for WooCommerce compares real options in more detail. How do you keep your store compliant on the website side? Processors review your site, so keep it clean. Show company details, contact information, clear terms and an obvious age verification step. Avoid language that promises quick delivery without legal checks, and keep product descriptions factual. A professional, transparent site helps approval and reduces freeze risk. What should you do if your account is frozen or declined? Stay calm and respond quickly. Ask for the reason in writing, send any requested documents and keep taking orders on your backup gateway if you have one. Do not apply to many processors at once, because repeated applications can hurt your chances. Fix the underlying issue, such as missing policies or high disputes, and then apply to a processor that knows the category. What types of processors work with firearms stores? Not every provider is a fit, and the label on the website does not always tell you. Three groups are worth knowing. Specialist high risk providers accept the category as a normal business and price for it. They tend to be the most stable option, although rates and reserves are higher than for standard accounts. Payment facilitators group many merchants under one master account. They are quick to sign up with, but they can freeze or close accounts fast if a policy changes, so they work best as a backup. Direct merchant accounts through an acquiring bank take longer to set up and need full underwriting, yet they give the most control and the best long term pricing for steady volume. How do you prevent chargebacks on firearms orders? Most disputes come from confusion, not fraud. A buyer who does not understand why the order is going to a dealer, or who sees an unfamiliar name on a statement, may call the bank. Send an order confirmation that explains each step, show the descriptor your customers will see and send tracking updates. Keep proof of age checks, dealer confirmations and delivery records so you can answer any dispute within the deadline. Explain the FFL transfer steps at checkout and in email. Use a billing descriptor that matches your store name. Keep dealer confirmations and carrier tracking on file. Answer disputes the same week with clear documents. Review disputes monthly to find patterns. How should you plan payments as your volume grows? Processors set limits based on what you tell them to expect. If sales double, tell them first, because a sudden jump looks like a risk signal and can trigger a review or a hold. Review your setup every quarter. Compare rates, check your reserve, confirm your backup account still works and update your documents. A short review is much cheaper than an emergency search after a freeze. For the store itself, see our firearms ecommerce solutions and the guide on how to sell guns online . What does a stable payment setup look like for a firearms store? A healthy setup has three layers. The first is a primary account with a provider that accepts the category and has reviewed your documents. The second is a backup gateway that is approved but used lightly, so it stays active. The third is a short routine for monitoring disputes and volume. When something goes wrong, such as a hold on the primary account, you switch more traffic to the backup and keep selling while you solve the issue. Stores that build this layer before they need it avoid the worst surprises. Which mistakes cause firearms stores to lose their accounts? Most closures come from a short list of avoidable problems. Applying with incomplete or inconsistent documents. Selling products that were not disclosed during underwriting. Allowing disputes to climb above one percent. Using a personal account or mixing business and personal funds. Having only one processor and no backup. Making big changes in volume without telling the provider. What is a quick checklist before you apply? Gather your licenses and registration, prepare your website policies, collect bank and processing statements, choose a backup provider and write a short description of how an order moves from checkout to the dealer. Submit everything together so the underwriter can make a decision in one pass. Then follow up politely and respond within a day to every request, since slow replies delay approval more than anything else. Conclusion Stable processing for a firearms store comes from the right processor, clean records and a backup plan. Start the application early and keep policies visible. If you want help with setup, our team builds compliant stores for the firearms industry. See our ecommerce solutions for firearm retailers . Frequently Asked Questions Can a firearms store use Stripe or PayPal? Policies change often and many mainstream providers restrict the category, so read their current terms before relying on them. What is a good chargeback rate? Aim to stay under one percent. Higher rates can lead to fines, reserves or account closure. How long does approval take? High risk approvals often take one to three weeks, depending on documents and the processor. Do I need a reserve? Some processors hold a rolling reserve for the first months. Ask about the terms before you sign. Can I sell ammo online? Yes, subject to state and local rules. Your processor will also have its own policy for ammo, so confirm it first. Why was my account frozen? Common causes are a sudden volume spike, high disputes, missing documents or a bank policy change.

title: Volusion to BigCommerce Migration: What Changes and What Breaks
headings: Why are Volusion merchants moving to BigCommerce?
How does a Volusion to BigCommerce migration work?
What changes when you move from Volusion to BigCommerce?
What breaks during a Volusion to BigCommerce migration?
Do customer passwords move from Volusion to BigCommerce?
How do Volusion URLs map to BigCommerce URLs?
What happens to your Volusion theme, apps and integrations?
Your theme gets rebuilt, not converted
Your apps and integrations get reconnected
Your checkout needs a full test
How long does it take and what does it cost?
Is BigCommerce the right place to land after Volusion?
How does Virtina run a Volusion to BigCommerce migration?
Can I migrate Volusion to BigCommerce myself?
Will I lose SEO when I move from Volusion to BigCommerce?
How long should I keep my Volusion account after migrating?
text: Summary Moving from Volusion to BigCommerce is a realistic switch for most stores, and products, customers, orders and categories can all be carried across. What does not carry across cleanly is the part that decides whether the launch goes well: your URLs, customer passwords, theme, apps and checkout rules. Those need to be planned, rebuilt and tested. The biggest risk is SEO. Volusion product and category URLs end in -p and -s patterns that BigCommerce does not use, so every ranked page needs a 301 redirect. Plan on a redirect map, a password reset email, a rebuilt theme and a tested checkout before you cut over. Introduction So, how do you move from Volusion to BigCommerce? You export your catalog, customers and orders, import them into a new BigCommerce store, rebuild the design on a BigCommerce theme, redirect your old URLs, reconnect your payment and shipping tools, test everything, and then point your domain at the new store. Most of that is routine. The trouble sits in the four or five things that never move on their own. This guide is the practical version. It tells you what changes, what breaks, and what to do about each item before launch day. If you would rather have a team handle it, our Volusion migration services team has moved stores like yours before. Table of Contents → Why are Volusion merchants moving to BigCommerce? → How does a Volusion to BigCommerce migration work? → What changes when you move from Volusion to BigCommerce? → What breaks during a Volusion to BigCommerce migration? → Do customer passwords move from Volusion to BigCommerce? → How do Volusion URLs map to BigCommerce URLs? → What happens to your Volusion theme, apps and integrations? → How long does it take and what does it cost? → Is BigCommerce the right place to land after Volusion? → How does Virtina run a Volusion to BigCommerce migration? → People also ask → Conclusion → Frequently asked questions Why are Volusion merchants moving to BigCommerce? Most stores we talk to do not leave because of one bad day. They leave because the platform has stopped keeping up. The usual reasons are sales-based plan limits that push you into a higher tier as you grow, a template system that is hard to customize, a small app ecosystem, and a worry about the long-term direction of the company after its 2020 bankruptcy filing. If you want the background, we covered it in our post on Volusion filing for bankruptcy . BigCommerce attracts these merchants for practical reasons. It is a hosted platform, so you do not manage servers or security patches. It has strong built-in features for products with many options, multi-currency, and B2B pricing. It also has an open API, which matters once you need to connect an ERP, an accounting tool or a marketplace feed. For many Volusion stores, it feels like the same simplicity with fewer ceilings. That said, BigCommerce is not the only landing spot. If you want full control over code and hosting, WooCommerce may fit better, and we return to the platform decision near the end of this guide. How does a Volusion to BigCommerce migration work? Every migration, whether done by an agency or with a tool, follows the same basic path. Here is the order we recommend. Audit the Volusion store. List your products, categories, customer groups, apps, payment gateways, shipping rules, discount codes and any custom code. Also pull your top landing pages from Google Search Console, because those pages are the ones you cannot afford to lose. Export your data. Volusion lets you export products, customers and orders as CSV files. Check each file for blanks, duplicates and messy option data before you import anything. Set up the BigCommerce store. Choose a plan, add your tax, shipping and payment settings, and create categories and brands so the imported products have somewhere to land. Import the data. Use BigCommerce import tools, a migration app such as Cart2Cart or LitExtension, or a custom script. Run a small test batch first, then the full import. Rebuild the design. Volusion templates do not convert. Your look and feel is rebuilt on a BigCommerce theme. Build the redirect map. Match every old Volusion URL to its new BigCommerce address and load the 301 redirects. Test, then cut over. Place real test orders, check emails and taxes, then switch your domain and watch the first weeks closely. Our eCommerce migration checklist is a good companion if you plan to manage parts of this yourself. A simple catalog can move quickly. A store with thousands of products, custom options, a B2B price structure or several integrations takes longer. We cover timing below. What changes when you move from Volusion to BigCommerce? Even when the data moves perfectly, the way you run the store changes. Here are the differences that merchants notice first. Area On Volusion On BigCommerce Plans and limits Plans are tied to trailing annual sales, and stores can be moved up a tier as they grow Plans are also tiered by sales volume, so confirm the current limits and any payment provider fees on the BigCommerce pricing page Design Volusion templates with limited customization Stencil themes, with a visual editor and full code access Product options Option sets that can be tricky to structure Variants and modifiers, with limits on variants per product that should be checked for large catalogs URLs Product and category pages end in -p and -s patterns Clean, shorter URLs with no -p or -s suffix Apps and integrations A smaller marketplace, often custom work A larger app marketplace plus an open API B2B and wholesale Customer groups and basic pricing rules Customer groups, price lists and B2B tools, depending on your plan and setup One practical point: the price you pay for a platform is more than the monthly plan. Payment processing, apps and developer time all count. Compare the full yearly cost, not only the headline price. What breaks during a Volusion to BigCommerce migration? Here is the honest answer. Your core catalog data usually moves well. The items below are where migrations go wrong, so treat this as your pre-launch checklist. Item Moves automatically? What to do Products, SKUs, prices, images Usually yes Clean the export first, then spot check 20 to 30 products Categories Usually yes Rebuild nested category trees and check for orphaned products Customer records and addresses Usually yes Import and test login and checkout with real accounts Order history Usually yes Confirm totals, taxes and statuses after import Customer passwords No Send a password reset email at launch Product options and variants Partly Review option sets and rebuild any that merged or split badly URLs and SEO settings No Build and load a full 301 redirect map Theme and layout No Rebuild on a BigCommerce theme Apps and integrations No Reconnect or replace each one and test the data flow Discount codes and promotions Partly Recreate rules and test totals at checkout Reviews Depends on the tool Check export options and import with a review app if needed Tools differ in what they carry, so always run a test migration and read the results before you trust the full run. Do customer passwords move from Volusion to BigCommerce? No, in practice they do not. Stores generally cannot export customer passwords, and BigCommerce only accepts a password during import if you supply one in the file. Customers who are imported without one must go through the password reset process before they can log in. This is easy to handle if you plan for it, and painful if you do not. Write a short, friendly email that explains the new store and links to the reset page. Send it the day you launch, and add a banner on the login page for the first few weeks. For B2B customers who reorder often, a personal note from your sales team works better than a mass email. How do Volusion URLs map to BigCommerce URLs? This is the step that protects your rankings. Volusion uses addresses like /blue-widget-p/BW100.htm for products and /widgets-s/12.htm for categories. BigCommerce uses cleaner paths such as /blue-widget/ and /widgets/ . Every old address that has rankings, backlinks or bookmarks needs a permanent 301 redirect to its new home. Here is how we build the map: Export every indexed URL from your sitemap and from Google Search Console. Sort by clicks and impressions so the pages that earn traffic are handled first. Match each old URL to the closest new page. Do not send everything to the home page, because search engines treat that as a soft 404. Load the redirects into BigCommerce and test a sample of them in a browser before launch. After launch, check Search Console for crawl errors and fix any missed URLs within days. Rankings often wobble for a few weeks after any platform change, and they usually settle once the new pages are crawled. A clean redirect map is what keeps that wobble small. If SEO is a worry, we also run a full eCommerce SEO review around the move. What happens to your Volusion theme, apps and integrations? Your theme gets rebuilt, not converted Volusion templates and BigCommerce Stencil themes are built differently, so there is nothing to convert. Think of it as a chance to modernize. Keep what your customers like, such as your logo, colors and navigation habits, and fix what slowed them down, such as heavy pages and clumsy mobile menus. Your apps and integrations get reconnected List every tool that touches your store: accounting, shipping, email marketing, reviews, live chat, marketplaces and your ERP. Some have a BigCommerce version, some have a close replacement, and a few need a custom connector. Decide on each one early, because integrations are the most common reason a launch date slips. Your checkout needs a full test Payment gateways, tax rules, shipping rates and discount codes are all configured again. Place test orders for each shipping method, a coupon, a tax-exempt customer and a failed card. It takes an afternoon and saves a bad first week. How long does it take and what does it cost? Time depends on catalog size, how much custom work your Volusion store carries, and how many integrations you use. As a rough guide, a small store with a standard catalog can often be live in a few weeks, while a larger store with custom options, B2B pricing and several integrations is more likely to take a couple of months. Cost depends on the same factors, along with how much design work you want. Be careful with any quote that is a single low number without a scope, since the gaps usually show up later as extra charges. A good partner will review your store first and give you a fixed scope. That is how we work, and the assessment is free. Is BigCommerce the right place to land after Volusion? Often yes, but not always. Use this quick guide. Choose BigCommerce if you want a hosted platform, strong B2B and multi-currency features, and an open API without running your own servers. Consider WooCommerce if you want full ownership of your code and content and already use WordPress (read From Volusion to WooCommerce: The Migration Story for that route). Consider Shopify if you want the simplest setup and a large app store, and your catalog is not heavily customized. Consider Magento if you are a large store with complex pricing or ERP needs. If you are still deciding, compare them side by side before you export a single file. How does Virtina run a Volusion to BigCommerce migration? We keep the process simple and visible. First comes a free store review, where we list what will move, what needs rebuilding and where the risks are. Then we build the new store alongside your live Volusion store, so your sales do not stop. We load the redirect map, test checkout with real scenarios, and handle the cutover with a rollback plan ready. After launch, we monitor rankings, errors and orders closely. Virtina has handled more than 2,500 projects across 14 years, including many platform moves. Our BigCommerce migration services cover the build on the new platform, from theme to checkout. People also ask Is BigCommerce better than Volusion? For most growing stores, yes. BigCommerce offers more flexible themes, a larger app marketplace, an open API and stronger tools for B2B and large catalogs. Volusion can still work for a small, stable store, but many owners outgrow it. Can I migrate Volusion to BigCommerce myself? You can, if your catalog is small and you are comfortable with CSV files. The risks are messy option data, missed redirects and an untested checkout. Many owners do the data import themselves and bring in help for the redirects and theme. Will I lose SEO when I move from Volusion to BigCommerce? Not if the redirects are done properly. A temporary dip is common, but a complete 301 map, preserved titles and descriptions and a quick post-launch check keep it small. How long should I keep my Volusion account after migrating? Keep it active for a few weeks, so you can cross-check orders and customer data against the new store before you cancel. Conclusion A Volusion to BigCommerce move is very doable. Your products, customers and orders can travel with you. What decides the outcome is how well you handle the parts that do not: the URL redirects, the password reset, the rebuilt theme, the reconnected apps and the tested checkout. Plan those five items first, run a test migration, and keep your Volusion store live until the new one has proven itself. If you want an expert team to take it off your plate, talk to our Volusion migration services team for a free assessment. Frequently asked questions Will my customer reviews move to BigCommerce? It depends on the migration tool and the review app you use. Some tools export reviews, and others do not. Check this during the test migration, and plan to import reviews with a review app if they matter to your sales. What about gift certificates and store credit? These often need to be recreated by hand or through a script, because balances are not always exported. List every active balance before launch so customers do not lose value. Does my order history come across? Yes, in most cases. Past orders are imported so customers can see them in their account. Check totals, taxes and statuses on a sample before you rely on the data. Can I keep selling during the migration? Yes. The new store is built while your Volusion store stays live. The only pause is the short cutover window, which is planned for a quiet time. Do my payment gateway settings transfer? No. Gateways, tax rules and shipping settings are set up again in BigCommerce and tested with real orders. Check that your processor supports BigCommerce before you commit. How do product options and variants migrate? Simple options usually do. Complex option sets, such as combinations with different prices or stock levels, often need cleanup and may need to be rebuilt as variants or modifiers. Review a sample of your trickiest products first. What happens to my email list and abandoned cart emails? Subscribers can be exported and imported into your email tool, but automations are rebuilt. Make sure you have consent records exported along with the list. Can a B2B or wholesale store move to BigCommerce? Yes. Customer groups, tiered pricing and net terms need to be mapped and rebuilt, and some depend on your BigCommerce plan and apps. This is worth planning separately from the catalog.

text: Summary A B2B ecommerce build for manufacturers needs more than a catalog. The core features are customer specific pricing, quote requests, reorder tools, ERP integration and account permissions. Start with the buyers and processes you already have, pick a platform that supports them, and launch in phases so sales teams adopt it. Introduction Manufacturers sell differently from consumer brands. Orders are larger, prices are negotiated and buyers expect to reorder quickly. A standard online store rarely fits. This guide covers the features, platform choices and rollout plan that work. For services, see our B2B ecommerce development . Table of Contents What features do manufacturers need in a B2B store? How do B2B buyers behave online? Which platform fits a manufacturer? How do quotes and negotiated pricing work online? Why does ERP integration matter? How should you roll out a B2B store? How should manufacturers structure a B2B product catalog? How do you handle customer specific pricing? What account features do business buyers expect? How should payments and net terms work? Which systems should connect to your store? How do manufacturers get found online? How do you get your sales team and customers to use the store? How do you design a quote process that does not slow your team down? What mistakes do manufacturers make when they launch a B2B store? How do you measure whether your B2B store is working? What does a successful manufacturer rollout look like? How do you protect customer data and pricing? What should you ask a B2B development partner? What features do manufacturers need in a B2B store? Customer specific pricing and tiered discounts. Quote requests and approvals. Quick order forms and reorder lists. Account hierarchies with roles and spending limits. Net terms and invoice payments. Technical specs, datasheets and CAD downloads. How do B2B buyers behave online? Buyers research on their own before talking to sales. They want accurate specs, availability and pricing without waiting for a call. Read more in our guide to B2B ecommerce for manufacturers . Which platform fits a manufacturer? Platform Strength Consider if WooCommerce Flexible and cost effective You want custom pricing rules Adobe Commerce Deep B2B features You have complex catalogs BigCommerce Strong built in B2B tools You want faster setup Shopify Plus Easy to run Your pricing is simpler Our B2B pricing and access setup guide shows how this works on WooCommerce. How do quotes and negotiated pricing work online? Quote tools let buyers request a price for large or custom orders, then approve it online. A B2B quote chatbot can collect details and speed up responses. Why does ERP integration matter? Stock levels, prices and orders should sync with your ERP so staff do not retype data. Plan integrations early because they drive time and cost. How should you roll out a B2B store? Map current buyers, products and pricing rules. Launch a pilot with a few key accounts. Add quotes, reorders and integrations in phases. Train the sales team and measure adoption. How should manufacturers structure a B2B product catalog? Industrial buyers search by part number, specification and compatibility, not by marketing names. Your catalog should support all three. Use clear categories, filters for key attributes such as size, material and rating, and a spec table on every product. Add downloadable datasheets, certifications and CAD files, because engineers often need them before they can buy. A well structured catalog also helps search engines and AI assistants understand your products, which improves visibility. Read our guide to gated catalogs and AI visibility for the trade offs of hiding prices. How do you handle customer specific pricing? Manufacturers rarely have one price list. Distributors, contractors and key accounts all negotiate their own terms, and the store has to reflect that. Most platforms support price lists by customer group, tiered discounts by quantity and contract prices after login. Decide early whether you will show public prices, hide them or show a starting price, because that choice affects both sales and SEO. See B2B pricing and access setup on WooCommerce for a practical example. What account features do business buyers expect? A business account is more than a login. Buyers expect to share an account across a team with different roles. Multiple users per company with approval limits. Saved shipping addresses and billing contacts. Order history, invoices and easy reorder. Saved lists and quick order by part number. Net payment terms for approved accounts. How should payments and net terms work? Many B2B orders are paid by invoice, purchase order or bank transfer instead of card. Your store should offer the methods your buyers already use. Net terms need credit checks and clear limits, so approve accounts before offering them. Read more in our guides to WooCommerce B2B net payment terms and B2B ecommerce checkout best practices . Which systems should connect to your store? The store should not live on an island. The more it connects to your daily tools, the less manual work your team has. System What it syncs Benefit ERP Stock, prices, orders, invoices One source of truth CRM Accounts and quote history Sales sees online activity Shipping tools Rates and tracking Accurate delivery info Accounting Invoices and payments Fewer manual entries PIM or spreadsheets Product data Faster catalog updates How do manufacturers get found online? Buyers search with specific questions, such as which material suits a certain use or what standard a part meets. Pages that answer those questions clearly earn both rankings and mentions in AI answers. Write product pages with real specifications, add guides for common applications and use structured data. Include a short, direct answer at the top of every guide so search engines and AI tools can quote it. How do you get your sales team and customers to use the store? Even a great store fails if people keep calling and emailing orders. Start by moving a few key accounts, collect their feedback and fix problems before a wider rollout. Train your reps to send customers to the portal for reorders, so they can spend time on new business. Share simple results, such as hours saved and faster payments, to keep the whole team on board. How do you design a quote process that does not slow your team down? Quotes work best when the first step is automatic. A form or chat collects the part numbers, quantities, delivery date and company details, so your team starts with complete information. Set rules for what can be answered instantly, such as standard items with contract pricing, and what needs a person, such as custom parts. Show buyers the status of each quote and let them accept it with one click. This shortens the sales cycle and removes the long email chains most manufacturers live with today. What mistakes do manufacturers make when they launch a B2B store? The most common mistake is copying a consumer store. Business buyers do not want banners and countdown timers, they want accurate specs, their own prices and a fast reorder. Others include launching without ERP sync, hiding all information behind a login, ignoring mobile use on the shop floor and failing to train the sales team. Each one is easy to avoid with a short plan. Copying a consumer design instead of building for buyers. No integration with stock and pricing systems. Poor search by part number. Weak product data and missing documents. No plan for adoption by sales reps and customers. How do you measure whether your B2B store is working? Pick a few numbers and review them monthly. Useful ones include the share of orders placed online, average order value, repeat order rate, time to quote and the number of support calls avoided. Also track search terms used on your site. They show what buyers cannot find, which tells you what to add to the catalog next. Compare results with your original goals and adjust the roadmap every quarter. If you want a team to plan this with you, see our B2B ecommerce development and B2B quote chatbot pages. What does a successful manufacturer rollout look like? Picture a manufacturer of industrial fittings with 4,000 parts and 300 active accounts. Orders arrive by phone and email, and reps spend hours retyping them. The company launches an online store with customer pricing and quick order by part number. It starts with twenty large accounts, then adds quotes for custom parts and ERP sync for stock. Within a year, most routine orders arrive online and reps focus on new accounts and complex projects. The lesson is that a phased plan, a clear owner and real buyer feedback matter more than any single feature. How do you protect customer data and pricing? Contract prices and account data are sensitive. Use role based access, strong passwords or single sign on, and keep pricing behind a login where needed. Keep software updated, back up daily and limit admin access to the people who need it. Review account permissions every quarter. What should you ask a B2B development partner? Ask for examples with similar pricing, quotes and integrations, and ask how they handle ERP sync, testing and training. Have you built stores with customer specific pricing? How do you connect to our ERP? What does support look like after launch? How will you help our sales team adopt the store? What is the plan if requirements change mid project? Conclusion A strong B2B build starts with your real buyers and processes. Choose a platform that supports pricing, quotes and ERP, and launch in phases. Talk to our team about B2B ecommerce development for your business. Frequently Asked Questions What is B2B ecommerce development? It is the design and build of online stores for business buyers, including custom pricing, quotes, accounts and integrations. Can customers see different prices? Yes. B2B stores can show prices by customer, group or contract after login. Do I need an ERP integration? It is not required, but it removes manual entry and keeps stock and pricing accurate. How long does a B2B build take? Many projects take two to five months, depending on integrations and catalog size. Can buyers pay by invoice? Yes. Net terms and invoice payments can be offered to approved accounts. Should I keep my sales team? Yes. Online ordering handles routine orders while reps focus on large accounts and negotiations.

text: Summary To find out whether old plugins will break on WooCommerce HPOS, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features, click View and manage to see any plugin flagged as incompatible, then test checkout, refunds and reports on a staging copy of your store with sync on and off. WooCommerce says HPOS can make order creation up to 5x faster and order lookups up to 40x faster, but only plugins that declare support can use it. This is a store owner checklist. For the migration steps themselves, see our HPOS migration guide . Introduction Your store runs fine today, and then someone tells you to turn on HPOS. The switch is a few clicks. The risk is the plugin you installed years ago and never thought about again. We kept this page to one question: which of your plugins and tools will break, and how do you find out before customers do? The definition of HPOS, the reasons to switch and the full migration plan live in our HPOS migration guide , so we do not repeat them here. Everything below follows WooCommerce’s own documentation and developer announcements, checked in October 2026. Table of Contents Summary Introduction What is HPOS, and why does plugin compatibility matter? Is HPOS already turned on in your store? How do you find which plugins are not HPOS compatible? What should you do about a plugin that is not compatible? What does a plugin that breaks on HPOS look like? How do you test plugin compatibility before you switch? What changed in 2026 that affects older plugins? Should you wait if a plugin you need is not ready? People also ask Conclusion Frequently Asked Questions What is HPOS, and why does plugin compatibility matter? HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) moves WooCommerce orders out of the general WordPress posts tables and into dedicated order tables. WooCommerce announced it in October 2023 and claimed up to 5x faster order creation, up to 1.5x faster checkout and up to 40x faster order lookups. It published no test method for those numbers, so treat them as a ceiling, not a promise. Compatibility matters because a plugin or snippet that reads or writes orders the old way, straight in the posts tables, may stop seeing or saving orders correctly once HPOS is the main storage. Plugins that use WooCommerce’s own order functions keep working. Is HPOS already turned on in your store? You can check in under a minute: In your WordPress admin, go to WooCommerce, then Settings, then Advanced. Open the Features tab. Look at Order data storage. It shows either WordPress posts storage (legacy) or High-performance order storage. Look at the checkbox labelled Enable compatibility mode (synchronizes orders to the posts table). If it is ticked, WooCommerce keeps both order tables in step. Stores created on or after October 10, 2023 (WooCommerce 8.2) have HPOS on by default. Older stores were not switched automatically, so if yours is older you are probably still on legacy storage. How do you find which plugins are not HPOS compatible? WooCommerce does the first pass for you. Plugin developers declare whether their plugin supports HPOS, and WooCommerce lists the ones that do not. On the same Features screen, find the compatibility notice and click View and manage. You will see your plugin list filtered to the incompatible ones. Prefer a shortcut? Type this after your domain name: /wp-admin/plugins.php?plugin_status=incompatible_with_feature&feature_id=custom_order_tables While an incompatible plugin is active, the HPOS option stays greyed out, so WooCommerce will not let you switch by accident. In 2023 WooCommerce also told developers to update their extensions and said those that were not updated would be removed from its Marketplace. Copies you already installed keep working without HPOS. Why is a clean list not the same as a safe store? The flag only covers plugins that declare support. It cannot see your custom code snippets, your accounting connector, a shipping tracker or a reporting tool that reads the database directly. WooCommerce’s own large-store guide calls these direct database readers the most likely hidden failure, because a system outside PHP can break without showing any error. What should you do about a plugin that is not compatible? The right move depends on what kind of problem you have. Situation What it means What to do Flagged as incompatible The developer has not declared HPOS support. Update the plugin first. If no update exists, ask the developer for a date, or plan a replacement. No flag, but not updated for years It may work, or it may still write orders the old way. Test it on staging with sync on and off before you switch. Custom code or snippets Code that uses wp_update_post, update_post_meta or direct SQL on orders can bypass HPOS. Ask your developer to move it to WooCommerce’s order functions. Accounting, shipping or reporting tool reading the database It may read the old tables and show empty or stale data. Ask the vendor how it reads orders, then compare an export with the orders screen. Plugin declares compatibility The developer says it supports HPOS. Still run the checkout and refund tests below. You are not forced to switch. If one plugin you cannot live without is not ready, staying on legacy storage is a sound choice until it is. What does a plugin that breaks on HPOS look like? Most failures are quiet. Watch for these signs when you test or switch: Recent orders missing from the WooCommerce orders screen, or order counts that do not match your payment provider. Reports, exports or accounting syncs that return zero rows or old data. Reports that read the old postmeta table directly are a common cause. Order statuses that flip back after you change them, or older data overwriting new orders. WooCommerce’s February 2026 advisory links these problems to sync on read. Custom order fields that go blank in the admin or in customer emails. Refunds or subscription renewals that fail during testing. How do you test plugin compatibility before you switch? Test on a copy of your store, never on the live site first. Ask your host for a staging site, or ask your developer to set one up. Then follow the order WooCommerce recommends for large stores, simplified: Update WooCommerce, your theme and every plugin to the latest version. Copy the live store, with its real orders, to staging and turn on compatibility mode so both order tables stay in sync. Switch the staging store to High-performance order storage. Run the test list below once with compatibility mode on, then again with it off. Check your outside systems: export orders into your accounting tool, shipping tracker or report and compare them with the orders screen. Only then plan the live change, ideally in a low-order period. Test What to do It passes when Checkout Place a test order with every payment method you offer. The order appears in the orders screen with the right status and totals. Refunds Refund one test order in full and another in part. The refund shows on the order and in your payment provider. Subscriptions If you sell subscriptions, buy one and run a renewal. A renewal order is created and paid. Order changes Change a status, add a note and edit an address. The change is still there after you reload the page. Reports and exports Run your usual sales report and accounting export. Totals match the orders screen. Custom fields Open an order that has custom fields and view its email. The fields show in the admin and in the email. Large stores should also plan for the sync itself. WooCommerce backfills orders in batches of 25, and the author of its large-store guide reported about a week for a store with 9 million orders. That is one store’s experience, so time your own sync on staging. What changed in 2026 that affects older plugins? On February 16, 2026, the WooCommerce team announced that sync on read would be disabled by default starting in WooCommerce 10.7, which was released on April 14, 2026. Sync on read copied changes from the old posts table back into HPOS when the old record looked newer. WooCommerce said that could cause order status reversions or stale data overwriting current orders. It affects stores that run HPOS with compatibility mode on and also use custom code or plugins that write order data straight to the posts table. Stores that use only HPOS-compatible plugins should see no impact, and stores on legacy storage are not affected. Affected stores see a one-time, dismissible admin notice after the upgrade. If you see that notice, do not just dismiss it. Send it to your developer and ask which plugin or snippet writes to the posts table. WooCommerce’s guidance is to move that code to its order functions, and developers can temporarily switch sync on read back on with a filter while they fix it. WooCommerce also suggests that if orders have run smoothly, you can consider turning compatibility mode off under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features. The 10.7 release post lists a related database update but does not restate the change, so confirm how your own store behaves. Should you wait if a plugin you need is not ready? Often, yes. HPOS helps most on stores with large order volumes, where the shared postmeta table slows searches and reports. If you process a modest number of orders, the gain may be small, and a broken checkout plugin costs more than it saves. WooCommerce has said HPOS will eventually become the default for all stores but has not given a firm date. Wait if your payment, shipping or subscription plugin is flagged. Move ahead when the list is clean, the staging tests pass and your outside tools have been checked. If your store feels slow for other reasons, our WooCommerce performance diagnostic covers the other common causes, since order storage is only one of them. People also ask Is HPOS on by default? For stores created on or after October 10, 2023 (WooCommerce 8.2), yes. Older stores must opt in. Can I turn HPOS off after switching? Yes. Make sure compatibility mode is on, wait for the sync to finish, then choose WordPress posts storage (legacy). While compatibility mode stays on, going back is instant. Do I need a developer to check compatibility? Not for the first check, which is a menu in WooCommerce. You will want help for staging, custom code and outside tools. Conclusion HPOS is worth it when your plugins are ready for it. Check the Features screen, look past the flag at custom code and outside tools, test on staging with sync on and off, and switch only when the tests pass. Need a hand? Our team can audit your plugins and fix what breaks. See our WooCommerce bug fix service , or read our HPOS migration guide for the full migration plan. Frequently Asked Questions Should I deactivate my subscription or booking plugins before switching? No. WooCommerce advises keeping extensions that use custom post types, such as WooCommerce Subscriptions or Bookings, active before you enable HPOS. Deactivating them first can cause data discrepancies. How long does the order sync take? It depends on your order volume. With compatibility mode on, WooCommerce copies orders in background batches of 25, and your developer can run the sync from the command line to time it on staging. One large store with 9 million orders reported about a week. Will an incompatible plugin stop my store from working? No. It stops you from switching to HPOS, because the option stays disabled while an incompatible plugin is active. Your store keeps running on legacy storage. Does a store created recently need to do anything? Stores created on or after October 10, 2023 already have HPOS on by default. The job for those stores is keeping every new plugin and snippet compatible, so check the Features screen after each plugin install.

It was a “normal” spam update, which means it targets sites that break Google’s spam policies, not sites that are simply average. For online stores, the usual culprits are mass-produced product or category pages, thin affiliate pages, copied manufacturer text, hacked pages and spam in reviews or comments. There is no reconsideration request for an algorithmic spam update, so the only route back is to fix the problems and wait. This guide shows you how to confirm whether you were hit, what to fix first, and what a realistic recovery looks like. Introduction If your store’s organic traffic slid at the end of September or the start of October, you are probably wondering whether Google just penalized you. The short answer: it might have, but you should not guess. Spam updates and core updates look similar in a traffic chart, yet they need very different fixes. Our main guide, Google Algorithm Updates: What Changed From 2018 to 2026 , walks through the full history. This post goes deeper on one question that guide only touches: what do you do when a spam update is the likely cause? We will cover the September 2026 rollout, how to diagnose it from Search Console in plain steps, which spam policies catch online stores most often, and a recovery plan you can follow without writing a line of code. Table of Contents How is a spam update different from a core update? What happened in the September 2026 spam update? What did site owners actually see? How do you know if your store was hit? Which spam policies catch online stores most often? How do you recover from a spam update? Should you file a reconsideration request? Is AI-written product content a spam risk? Will a core update follow? How can Virtina help? People also ask Conclusion Frequently asked questions How is a spam update different from a core update? A spam update is aimed at pages and sites that break Google’s published spam policies. A core update is a broad re-evaluation of how Google judges relevance and quality across the whole web. One punishes specific bad behavior. The other re-ranks everyone. That difference matters because the fix is different. After a spam update, you look for violations and remove them. After a core update, you improve the overall usefulness of your pages. Mixing the two up is the most common reason stores waste weeks fixing the wrong thing.   Spam update Core update What it targets Pages that break spam policies Overall relevance and quality Who is usually affected A smaller group of sites with clear violations Many sites, with winners and losers Typical 2026 rollout 19 hours to 13 days About 12 days What you do Find and remove violations, then wait Raise the quality of key pages Appeal option None for the algorithmic part None Google’s official Search Status Dashboard is where rollout dates are confirmed. What happened in the September 2026 spam update? Google began rolling out the September 2026 spam update on 24 September 2026 at about 9:15 a.m. Pacific time and marked it complete on 8 October 2026. Google called it “a normal spam update” that applies globally and to all languages. It did not say how many queries were affected or give details of what it targeted, and it announced no policy changes alongside it. The length is the unusual part. Google said the rollout could take up to two weeks, and it used almost all of that. Here is how it compares with the other spam updates of 2026: 2026 spam update Started Rollout length March 24 March About 19.5 hours June 24 June About 2 days August 18 August About 2 days 16 hours September 24 September About 13 days 16 hours Four spam updates in one year is a clear change in pace. Industry trackers count one in 2025 and three in 2024. Two spam updates in back-to-back months, August and September, is the part worth pausing on. It suggests Google is enforcing its spam policies more often, so a quick clean-up once a year is no longer enough. What did site owners actually see during the rollout? Most of what we know about the impact comes from third parties, and Google has confirmed none of it. Reports describe uneven drops in three waves and a small overall shift in organic search share. Still, the patterns are useful: Uneven timing. Search Engine Roundtable logged noticeable movement on 25 to 27 September, again on 30 September, and again on 4 to 6 October. A long rollout means a store can drop, partly recover, and drop again. A small but measurable shift. Analytics firm Diib, looking at 32,569 sites, reported that the median share of visits coming from unpaid Google search fell from 34% to 31% over 24 to 26 September compared with a week earlier. Overall traffic also dipped that week, so treat this as a signal, not proof. Rank trackers can mislead. SEOmonitor reported that many rank trackers showed sudden changes from 26 September that real searchers never saw. Real spam-update effects tend to last several days and show up in Search Console. The takeaway: do not react to a rank tracker alone. Your own Search Console data is the evidence that counts. How do you know if your store was hit by the spam update? Compare 24 September to 8 October against the two weeks before, in Google Search Console, and look for a drop that lasts several days in both clicks and impressions. If the drop is concentrated in certain page types, a spam policy problem is far more likely than a general quality issue. Here is the click-by-click version: Step 1: Set up the comparison Open Search Console, click Performance in the left menu, then Search results . Click the Date filter, choose Compare , and pick the custom range 24 September to 8 October against the previous period. Make sure Clicks and Impressions are both ticked. Step 2: Find where the loss sits Scroll to the table below the chart and click the Pages tab. Sort by the biggest click loss. Ask yourself: are the losers mostly one type of page, such as filtered category URLs, tag pages, blog posts, or a batch of product pages added recently? A cluster is the strongest clue you will get. Step 3: Check for a manual action In the left menu, open Security & Manual Actions , then Manual actions . If it says “No issues detected,” your drop is algorithmic. If a message is listed, that is a different process with a reconsideration option. Also check Security issues in the same menu for hacked content. Step 4: Rule out other causes Check whether your paid, email, and direct traffic moved too. If everything fell together, the cause may be seasonal demand, a broken tracking tag, or a site change rather than Google. Also ask your team whether a plugin update, theme change, migration, or bulk product import happened in the same window. If a hack or a bulk import is on that list, the fix is often quicker than you expect. If you cannot find a cause, our WooCommerce SEO guide covers the technical basics worth checking next. Which spam policies catch online stores most often? The policies most likely to catch an online store are scaled content abuse, thin affiliation, doorway abuse, scraping, hacked content and user-generated spam. Google publishes a list of spam policies, and several of them describe things that happen by accident on eCommerce sites. Stores rarely set out to spam. They end up in trouble through scale: thousands of pages created by a plugin, a feed, or an AI tool with nobody checking the result. Here is how the main policies tend to show up on a store, and what to do about each. The patterns below are based on what the policies describe and the kinds of problems we look for in store audits, not on a Google statement about this specific update. Spam policy How it shows up on a store What to do Scaled content abuse Hundreds or thousands of templated or AI-written product, category, or location pages with little unique value Merge, rewrite, or remove the weakest pages. Keep only pages that offer something specific. Thin affiliation Affiliate product pages that copy the merchant’s description and add nothing Add original photos, testing notes, and honest comparisons, or drop the page. Doorway abuse Near-identical landing pages for every city or keyword variation that lead to the same product list Consolidate into one strong page per real need. Scraping Supplier or competitor descriptions published at scale with little change Rewrite best sellers and top category pages first. Hacked content Injected pages, hidden links, or odd redirects added through an outdated plugin or weak password Clean the site, update everything, change credentials, and add monitoring. Sneaky redirects and cloaking Visitors sent somewhere different from what Google saw, often by a script or compromised plugin Test pages as a visitor and as Google, then remove the cause. User-generated spam Fake reviews, spam comments, junk product questions, or bot-created accounts with links Turn on moderation, add spam filters, and delete the junk. Keyword stuffing and hidden text Footers or category text crammed with repeated phrases, or text hidden from shoppers Rewrite in plain language written for the shopper. Back button hijacking Pop-ups or scripts that stop shoppers from leaving by pressing Back Remove the script or plugin that causes it. One more store-specific trap deserves a mention: filter and sort URLs. A catalog with colour, size, price, and brand filters can generate tens of thousands of near-duplicate pages. They are not spam by intent, but when they flood the index they can look like exactly the low-value, scaled pages the policies describe. Ask your developer or our team to check how many of them are indexable. How do you recover from a Google spam update? You recover by removing the violations, replacing them with truly useful pages, and then waiting for Google to reassess your site. Google has said recovery can take months, and a case study published after the August 2026 update described a recovery that took around five months of sustained cleanup. There is no switch to flip and no form to submit. Here is a working timeline we recommend. It is our own planning guide, not a promise from Google, because the real speed depends on how much needs fixing and when Google next reassesses your site. When What to do Done when Days 1 to 3 Confirm the drop and the date, check manual actions and security issues, stop any risky tactic You know if it is spam, core, or something else Weeks 1 to 2 Audit every page type against the spam policies and label pages keep, improve, merge, or remove A full list of problem pages exists Weeks 2 to 6 Remove or merge the weakest pages, fix hacks and redirects, clean up reviews and comments No policy violations remain Months 2 to 3 Rewrite top categories and best sellers with original detail, add real photos, buying guides, and expert input Your key pages are clearly better than competitors’ Months 3 to 6 Keep publishing carefully, earn real mentions, and track Search Console monthly Impressions and clicks trend back up Fix the biggest page group first Start with the page type that lost the most clicks in Step 2 above. If 3,000 programmatic city pages account for most of the loss, rewriting your home page will not help. Prioritize by damage, not by what is easiest. Remove or merge instead of polishing weak pages A hundred pages that say almost the same thing are better as one great page. Merge them and redirect the old addresses to the new one. Pages with no traffic, no links, and no purpose can usually be removed. Add what only you can add The pages that hold up are the ones with something a feed cannot supply: your own photos, sizing advice from real returns, how a product performs after months of use, delivery details, and honest “who this is not for” notes. That is also the content AI search tools prefer to cite. Our article on eCommerce SEO in the age of AI search explains how this builds visibility across both. Do not undo the work The case studies on the August update stress that recovery needs ongoing compliance, not a one-time cleanup. If a plugin or feed will regenerate the thin pages next month, switch it off or fix its settings first. Should you file a reconsideration request? Only if you have a manual action. An algorithmic spam update has no reconsideration process, so filing one when Search Console shows “No issues detected” will not help. If you do have a manual action, fix the problem first, explain what you changed in plain language, and submit the request from the Manual actions report. Is AI-written product content a spam risk? AI-written content is not banned, but publishing it at scale without human review is the risk. Google’s policy is about mass-producing low-value pages to manipulate rankings, not about the tool used. In the August 2026 case studies shared by SEO consultant Glenn Gabe, the sites that lost visibility combined large programmatic page sets with content that looked entirely machine-generated and added little original value. A safe rule for a store: let AI help with a first draft, then have someone who knows the product add real details, correct mistakes, and decide whether the page deserves to exist at all. Ten reviewed pages beat a thousand unreviewed ones. Will a core update follow, and how should you prepare? Nobody outside Google can say when. Another core update is expected eventually, and the long gap since May makes one unsurprising, but Google has announced nothing. The last core update began on 21 May and finished around 2 June, and by early October more than 130 days had passed. Over 2022 to 2025 Google released roughly three or four core updates a year, so another one would not be a surprise. A spam update does not reliably predict a core update, and an active spam update does not seem to make one less likely. The best preparation is the same work you would do for recovery: strong category pages, original product detail, and a clean technical foundation. If you also sell to businesses, make sure your catalog is not hidden behind a login, as we explain in why gated B2B catalogs are invisible to AI search . How can Virtina help? Virtina has been building and optimizing WooCommerce and other eCommerce stores for more than 14 years. For a suspected spam update hit, we can run a page-by-page audit against Google’s spam policies, clean up hacked or injected content, consolidate thin and duplicate pages, and rebuild your key category and product pages. We will also tell you plainly when your traffic drop is not Google’s doing. Talk to our team and we will start with your Search Console data. People also ask These are common questions based on search intent. They were not copied from Google’s live “People also ask” box. Is a Google spam update a penalty? Not in the manual sense. A spam update is an automatic change to Google’s ranking systems that demotes pages breaking spam policies. Nothing appears in Search Console, and you cannot appeal it. A manual action, by contrast, is a reviewed penalty that appears in your Manual actions report. What is the difference between a manual action and a spam update? A manual action is applied by a human reviewer, is listed in Search Console, and can be cleared with a reconsideration request. A spam update is algorithmic, shows no notice, and has no appeal. Both can come from the same kind of violation, so check the Manual actions report first. How long does a Google spam update take to roll out? Between about 19 hours and two weeks in 2026. The March update took roughly 19.5 hours, June and August took two to three days, and September ran for 13 days and 16 hours. Google usually says up to two weeks and confirms completion on the Search Status Dashboard. Can a spam update make my pages disappear from Google? Yes, in severe cases. Google says sites that violate its spam policies may drop in rankings or not rank at all. Check the Pages report in Search Console to see whether your pages are still indexed or have only lost visibility. Does a spam update hit the whole site or only some pages? It can be either. In the August 2026 case studies, one site with more than a million indexed URLs lost visibility across the whole site, while others lost rankings on specific programmatic page sets. Check which page types lost clicks before assuming the whole store is affected. Conclusion The September 2026 spam update was long, uneven, and only the latest in a busy year. If your store lost traffic between 24 September and 8 October, confirm it in Search Console, look for clusters of thin, scaled, copied, or hacked pages, and fix those before anything else. Recovery is slow, but it is predictable when you remove the violations, add real value, and keep your catalog clean going forward. Start with the data, fix the biggest problem first, and resist the urge to change everything at once. Frequently asked questions Do I have to delete all my AI-written pages? No. Remove or rewrite the pages that are thin, repetitive, or inaccurate, and keep the ones that are useful, reviewed, and unique. Quality and purpose matter more than how the first draft was written. Can a rank tracker tell me if the spam update hit me? Not reliably. Rank trackers can show sudden changes that real searchers do not see. Use Search Console clicks and impressions over several days as your evidence, and treat the rank tracker as a hint. Should I stop publishing new content while I recover? No, but slow down and raise the bar. Pause any bulk or automated publishing, then keep adding carefully reviewed pages with original detail. Will fixing the problems bring my traffic back quickly? Usually not. Google has said improvements can take months to be reassessed, and some recoveries only show after later updates. Small improvements in the first weeks are a good sign, but plan for months. Does a spam update affect AI Overviews and AI Mode too? It can. Spam-policy demotions affect how a site is treated in Google’s search systems, and industry observers expect visible changes across regular results, AI Overviews, and AI Mode. Cleaning up your site helps in all three places. My store was hacked months ago. Could that still matter? Yes, if injected pages or redirects are still live or still indexed. Check Search Console for security issues and search Google for your site name plus unusual terms. Cleaning and securing the site is the first step.
