You are dealing with case and pallet pricing, buyers who reorder the same 40 SKUs every week, lot numbers, expiry dates and shipping that cannot sit in a hot truck. This guide compares the four platforms food and beverage brands actually build on, based on the stores we have built for coffee roasters, distilleries, specialty food makers and wholesale distributors. Introduction Choosing an eCommerce platform for a food and beverage business takes more than comparing feature lists. Wholesale buyers expect their own prices, case and pallet ordering, Net 30 terms and fast reorders, while you have to think about lot numbers, expiry dates and cold-chain shipping. This guide compares WooCommerce, BigCommerce B2B Edition, Adobe Commerce and Shopify Plus against the requirements food and beverage brands actually face. It is written for owners and operations leads who need to pick a platform or brief a developer. By the end, you will know which platform fits your catalog, how to handle traceability, and what to do next. Table of Contents Summary Introduction What is the best B2B eCommerce platform for a food and beverage business? Why is food and beverage B2B different from other B2B? How do the four platforms compare for food and beverage B2B? How does each of the four platforms work for food and beverage? How do you handle lot numbers, expiry dates and traceability? Should you sell on marketplaces or your own B2B store? Which food and beverage brands has Virtina built stores for? Conclusion Frequently Asked Questions What is the best B2B eCommerce platform for a food and beverage business? WooCommerce is the best fit for most small and mid-sized food and beverage brands that sell both wholesale and direct, because it is the most flexible on pricing rules and the cheapest to run. BigCommerce B2B Edition suits distributors with large catalogs who want strong B2B features without managing hosting. Adobe Commerce fits enterprise manufacturers with complex catalogs, multiple brands and deep ERP integration. Shopify Plus suits DTC-first brands adding a wholesale channel who value speed over customization. None of the four tracks lot numbers and expiry dates out of the box. All of them can, through an ERP connection or an inventory extension. More on that below. Why is food and beverage B2B different from other B2B? A generic eCommerce platform assumes one price, one unit and one buyer. Wholesale food breaks all three assumptions. Before comparing platforms, it helps to know what your store actually has to handle. Lot and expiry tracking: every batch needs a lot number and a best-before date, and stock should ship first-expired, first-out (FEFO). Unit, case and pallet pricing: the same product sells by the unit, the case of 12 and the pallet, each at a different price and minimum. Customer-specific price lists: a restaurant group, a regional grocer and a single café should each see their own negotiated prices. Fast reordering: buyers reorder the same items weekly, so saved lists and quick order forms matter more than a pretty product page. Net terms and on-account ordering: most wholesale buyers pay on Net 30, not by card at checkout. Perishable shipping rules: cold-chain products need ship-day restrictions, insulated packaging surcharges and delivery zones. Allergen and nutrition data: buyers need allergens, ingredients and spec sheets on every product, in a consistent format. Traceability records: the FDA Food Traceability Rule (FSMA 204) requires records for foods on its traceability list, with compliance due by July 20, 2028. How do the four platforms compare for food and beverage B2B? How each platform handles the requirements above. “Native” means built in. “Extension” means a plugin, app or integration is needed. Requirement WooCommerce BigCommerce B2B Edition Adobe Commerce Shopify Plus Customer-specific price lists Extension (B2BKing, Wholesale Suite) Native Native (shared catalogs) Native (catalogs) Unit, case and pallet pricing Extension, very flexible Native Native Native quantity rules, limited Quick order and reorder lists Extension Native Native (requisition lists) Partial, apps for more Net terms and on-account ordering Extension Native Native Native (payment terms) Wholesale buyer approval Extension Native Native (company accounts) Native (company accounts) Lot and expiry tracking Extension or ERP ERP or app ERP or extension ERP or app ERP integration Plugins or custom Connectors and API Deepest options Apps and API Hosting You manage it Fully hosted Cloud or self-hosted Fully hosted Relative cost to run Lowest Mid Highest Mid to high Best for Small to mid brands selling wholesale and direct Distributors with large catalogs Enterprise and multi-brand manufacturers DTC-first brands adding wholesale Feature availability changes often, especially on Shopify, where B2B tools have expanded beyond Plus in limited form. Check current plan details before you commit. How does each of the four platforms work for food and beverage? 1. WooCommerce Best for: small and mid-sized food and beverage brands selling both wholesale and direct to consumer. WooCommerce runs on WordPress, so you own the store, the data and the hosting. Out of the box it is a B2C platform. A B2B plugin such as B2BKing or Wholesale Suite adds buyer approval, customer-group pricing, minimum order quantities, net terms and quick order forms. Because the pricing engine is open, it handles awkward food pricing rules (tiered case pricing, mix-and-match cases, per-account discounts) better than most hosted platforms . Strengths Watch out for Most flexible pricing and checkout logic You are responsible for hosting, updates and security Lowest running cost, no revenue share B2B features depend on plugin quality One store for wholesale and retail Very large catalogs need performance tuning Huge plugin ecosystem for shipping and inventory From our work: The Fruitful Grind wanted a dedicated wholesale channel for retailers and multi-location customers. We built it on WooCommerce with B2BKing Pro: buyers register and upload a tax certificate, an admin approves them, and they are placed in the right pricing tier automatically. Tiered pricing, net-terms ordering, multi-location accounts and bulk ordering all run in the same store as retail. Read the case study . 2. BigCommerce B2B Edition Best for: distributors and wholesalers with large catalogs who want B2B features without managing servers. BigCommerce is fully hosted, and its B2B Edition adds company accounts with buyer roles, shared price lists, quotes, quick order pads, shopping lists and an invoice portal. It handles large catalogs well and has ready connectors for popular ERPs. For a food distributor with thousands of SKUs and a sales team that issues quotes, it is often the fastest route to a capable B2B store. Strengths Watch out for Strong native B2B feature set Plan pricing rises with sales volume No hosting or patching to manage Less freedom than WooCommerce for unusual pricing logic Handles large catalogs and variants well Lot and expiry tracking still needs an ERP or app 3. Adobe Commerce (Magento) Best for: enterprise food manufacturers, multi-brand groups and businesses with complex ERP workflows. Adobe Commerce has the deepest native B2B module of the four: company accounts with hierarchies, shared catalogs, requisition lists, quick order, negotiable quotes, purchase orders and payment on account. It supports multiple brands and regions from one installation. The trade-off is cost and complexity. It needs a skilled development partner and a larger budget to build and run. Strengths Watch out for Most complete native B2B features Highest licence and build cost Multi-brand, multi-region, multi-currency Longer implementation timelines Deepest ERP and PIM integration options Overkill for most small and mid-sized brands 4. Shopify Plus Best for: DTC-first food and beverage brands adding a wholesale channel. Shopify built B2B into its platform, with company accounts, catalogs with custom prices, payment terms and quantity rules, and the deepest set of these tools sits on Shopify Plus . If your brand already sells direct on Shopify and wants a clean wholesale portal quickly, it is a sensible choice. Brands with complex pricing, heavy customization needs or large distributor catalogs usually outgrow it faster than the other options. Book the free fit check → No cost · No obligation How do you handle lot numbers, expiry dates and traceability? This is the question food brands ask most, and the honest answer is that no mainstream eCommerce platform is a traceability system on its own. The store is the sales channel. Lot and expiry data usually lives in one of three places: Your ERP or inventory system (for example NetSuite, Acumatica, SAP Business One or a food-specific ERP) holds lots and expiry dates, and the store syncs available stock from it. This is the most reliable setup and the one we recommend for anything beyond a small operation. A warehouse or 3PL system assigns lots at pick time and passes them back to the order record. A store extension records lot and expiry on products and orders. Workable for smaller brands, but it becomes hard to manage as SKU counts grow. If any of your products are on the FDA Food Traceability List, plan the data flow now. The FSMA 204 compliance date is July 20, 2028, and retrofitting lot capture into a live store is much harder than designing it in. Should you sell on marketplaces or your own B2B store? Wholesale marketplaces such as Alibaba, Amazon Business, Faire and eWorldTrade help you find new buyers. They are useful for reach, but they are not a replacement for your own store. Marketplaces Your own B2B store Instant access to new buyers You keep the margin and the customer data Commission on every order Negotiated pricing stays private The marketplace owns the customer relationship Reordering is built around your buyers Your prices sit next to competitors Integrates with your ERP and fulfilment Most growing food and beverage brands use both: marketplaces to find buyers, and their own store to keep them. Which food and beverage brands has Virtina built stores for? We have built and supported stores for coffee roasters, distilleries, specialty food makers, confectioners and wholesale suppliers, most of them on WooCommerce, including Magic Beans Coffee Roasters , SF Distilling Co , Ithaca Hummus , Famous Cookies , Mi Oliva Gourmet , The Fruitful Grind , Kosher Now , Battlefield Coffee , Tea Time and Love of Candy . Wagshal’s, a Washington, DC specialty food company operating since 1925, is another example: we extended WooCommerce to run its holiday and grocery menus online. Read the Wagshal’s case study , or see all our work on the food and beverage eCommerce page. Distributor with a large catalog? Buyers often know what they need but not your SKU codes. ChatSKU lets them ask questions in plain language, find the right product and request a quote from your catalog. Conclusion There is no single best platform for food and beverage B2B, only the one that fits how you sell. WooCommerce suits small and mid-sized brands selling wholesale and direct, BigCommerce B2B Edition suits distributors with large catalogs, Adobe Commerce suits enterprise manufacturers, and Shopify Plus suits DTC-first brands adding a wholesale channel. Whichever you choose, plan your lot, expiry and traceability data flow early, and decide whether marketplaces, your own store or both will carry your wholesale buyers. title: Core Web Vitals in 2026: LCP, INP and CLS Guide for eCommerce
headings: What changed with Core Web Vitals since 2021?
What are the three Core Web Vitals in 2026?
What is INP and why did it replace FID?
Do Core Web Vitals still affect Google rankings?
How do you measure Core Web Vitals?
How do you fix LCP, INP and CLS?
How do you fix Core Web Vitals on WooCommerce, Shopify and Magento?
What is a 30-day plan to pass Core Web Vitals?
text: Summary Core Web Vitals are three measurements of real shopper experience: LCP for loading, INP for responsiveness and CLS for visual stability. INP replaced FID in March 2024, so any report that still talks about FID is out of date. A page passes when LCP is 2.5 seconds or less, INP is 200 milliseconds or less and CLS is 0.1 or less for 75 percent of visits. This updated 2026 guide explains each metric, how to measure it, and how to fix it on WooCommerce, Shopify and Magento stores. Introduction When Google announced the page experience update in 2020, many store owners treated Core Web Vitals as a one-time project. The picture is different now. One metric was swapped out, the tools matured, and shoppers are less patient on mobile than ever. This guide replaces our 2021 article. It covers what changed, the current thresholds, how to read your scores and what to fix first. If you want a team to run the audit for you, our page speed optimization service covers all three metrics. Table of Contents Summary Introduction What changed with Core Web Vitals since 2021? What are the three Core Web Vitals in 2026? What is INP and why did it replace FID? Do Core Web Vitals still affect Google rankings? How do you measure Core Web Vitals? How do you fix LCP, INP and CLS? How do you fix Core Web Vitals on WooCommerce, Shopify and Magento? What is a 30-day plan to pass Core Web Vitals? Frequently asked questions Conclusion What changed with Core Web Vitals since 2021? The 2021 version of this article said Core Web Vitals would matter “from June 2021” and listed First Input Delay as the interactivity metric. Three things are different today. FID is gone. Google promoted Interaction to Next Paint to a Core Web Vital on March 12, 2024 and retired FID. INP is a tougher test because it checks every interaction, not only the first. The rollout is finished. The page experience update rolled out through 2021 and early 2022. Core Web Vitals are now a permanent part of how Google judges real-world page quality. The tools improved. Search Console, PageSpeed Insights and the Chrome UX Report give field data you can act on, and the web-vitals library lets you track the metrics in your own analytics. What are the three Core Web Vitals in 2026? Google judges each metric at the 75th percentile of page loads, split by mobile and desktop. In plain words, three out of four real visits must be good. Metric What it measures Good Needs improvement Poor LCP Largest Contentful Paint How fast the main content, usually the hero or product image, appears 2.5 s or less 2.5 to 4 s Over 4 s INP Interaction to Next Paint How quickly the page responds visually after a tap, click or key press 200 ms or less 200 to 500 ms Over 500 ms CLS Cumulative Layout Shift How much the layout jumps while loading 0.1 or less 0.1 to 0.25 Over 0.25 Details for the two older metrics are in our guides to Largest Contentful Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift . What is INP and why did it replace FID? First Input Delay only measured the wait before the browser began handling the very first interaction. A page could pass FID and still feel sluggish every time you opened a menu or changed a variant. INP fixes that by timing the full journey of each interaction, from the tap to the next frame painted, and reporting roughly the slowest one of the visit. Every interaction has three parts: input delay (the main thread is busy), processing time (your event handlers run) and presentation delay (the browser draws the result). Stores suffer most on add to cart, variant pickers, filters and coupon fields, because these trigger scripts, network calls and layout changes at once. Do Core Web Vitals still affect Google rankings? Yes, with perspective. Google uses Core Web Vitals as part of its page experience signals, and it has been clear that relevant, helpful content still wins over a fast but thin page. The practical value of passing is twofold: it removes a negative on competitive queries, and it lifts conversion, because fast, stable pages sell more. For the wider picture, read our notes on Google algorithm updates and eCommerce SEO . How do you measure Core Web Vitals? The most common mistake is trusting a single lab score. Use both kinds of data, but make decisions from field data. Tool Data type Best for Search Console, Core Web Vitals report Field, 28 days of real users Finding groups of failing URLs across the site PageSpeed Insights Field plus lab Checking one URL and seeing the opportunities Chrome UX Report Field Tracking trends and comparing competitors Lighthouse and DevTools Performance panel Lab Debugging causes, including slow interactions for INP web-vitals JavaScript library Field, your own visitors Sending LCP, INP and CLS to GA4 or your analytics Low-traffic pages may have no field data. Use lab tools to find problems, then confirm in Search Console as traffic builds. After a fix, allow up to 28 days for the report to catch up. How do you fix LCP, INP and CLS? Improve LCP Find the real LCP element. On product pages it is usually the main image. Never lazy-load the LCP image. Load it eagerly with high fetch priority. Serve WebP or AVIF at the size shown on screen, not a 3000 px original. Cut server response time with full-page caching, a CDN and decent hosting. Remove render-blocking CSS and JavaScript from the top of the page. Improve INP Hunt long tasks. Anything that blocks the main thread for over 50 ms delays taps, so split big scripts and yield between chunks. Audit third-party scripts. Chat widgets, review badges, popups, heatmaps and tag managers are the usual offenders. Delay them until the shopper interacts, or remove them. Keep event handlers light: paint the visual change first, do heavy work after. Shrink the DOM. Category pages with thousands of nodes slow every layout change. Improve CLS Set width and height or an aspect ratio on every image, video and embed. Reserve space for banners, cookie notices and review widgets. Load fonts safely with font-display and preload the key ones. Never inject content above existing content after load, such as late promo bars. How do you fix Core Web Vitals on WooCommerce, Shopify and Magento? WooCommerce WooCommerce stores usually fail on plugin weight and caching. Remove unused plugins and their scripts, use full-page caching with sensible cart and checkout exclusions, delay non-critical JavaScript, review how the cart fragments request behaves on your theme, compress product images and upgrade hosting if server response is slow. Our WooCommerce speed tips walk through the setup, and the page speed and conversion guide covers the business side. Shopify Shopify handles hosting and the CDN, so your levers are the theme and the apps. Remove apps that left code in the theme after uninstalling, choose a lightweight Online Store 2.0 theme, trim sliders and autoplay video, limit custom fonts and load review, popup and upsell apps only where needed. Weighing a move? See our Shopify migration services . Magento Magento stores often struggle with INP and LCP because of heavy JavaScript in the default frontend. Use proper full-page cache and Varnish, review bundling and minification, lazy-load below the fold, and consider a lighter frontend such as Hyvä . Also check that your version is still supported, since old releases miss performance and security work. What is a 30-day plan to pass Core Web Vitals? When What to do Days 1 to 3 Open the Search Console Core Web Vitals report. Note failing URL groups on mobile first. Record baseline LCP, INP and CLS. Days 4 to 10 Fix the biggest LCP problems: hero and product images, caching and server response. Days 11 to 20 Audit scripts and apps. Remove, delay or replace the worst INP offenders. Fix layout shifts from banners and fonts. Days 21 to 30 Retest with PageSpeed Insights and DevTools. Add web-vitals tracking. Review the 28-day field data once it updates. Related reading: page speed optimization , eCommerce website loading time and conversion rate optimization . Frequently asked questions Is FID still a Core Web Vital? No. Google replaced First Input Delay with Interaction to Next Paint in March 2024. Use INP in all new audits. What are the Core Web Vitals thresholds in 2026? Good means LCP of 2.5 seconds or less, INP of 200 milliseconds or less and CLS of 0.1 or less, at the 75th percentile of real visits. Poor starts above 4 seconds, 500 milliseconds and 0.25. Do Core Web Vitals affect Google rankings? They are part of Google page experience signals, but Google has said helpful, relevant content still matters more. Treat good vitals as a tie-breaker and a conversion booster. Why does PageSpeed Insights differ from Search Console? PageSpeed Insights mixes one simulated lab run with field data. Search Console shows only field data from real Chrome users over 28 days, and that is the data that counts. Which tool measures INP? INP needs real interactions, so use field data from Search Console, the Chrome UX Report or PageSpeed Insights. To debug, use the Chrome DevTools Performance panel or the web-vitals library. Can WooCommerce and Shopify stores pass Core Web Vitals? Yes. Most slow stores share the same causes: heavy apps or plugins, oversized images, unneeded scripts and weak hosting. A focused audit usually finds the top fixes quickly. Conclusion Core Web Vitals in 2026 come down to three numbers: LCP under 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 milliseconds and CLS under 0.1. FID is no longer one of them, and the fastest wins on most stores come from images, caching and third-party scripts. Start with the Search Console report, fix the worst page group first, and measure again after 28 days. text: Summary Square has told hemp and CBD sellers to stop. Mixed catalogs lose their CBD listings on October 15, 2026. Accounts built mainly on hemp close entirely on November 5, 2026. Two more dates sit behind those. Before you move your store, sort which of your products are still hemp in December. Then find out what your Square Loan does the day the account closes. Introduction The notice went out to affected accounts around August 7, 2026. You found out by email, from a company you have never spoken to. The wording was plain: “selling CBD and hemp-derived products, online or in person, will no longer be permitted.” Two dates came with it, and they are not the same for every seller. This guide covers which deadline is yours, what happens to your money, and what you can take with you. It also covers the order to do things in, which matters more than most people expect. Table of Contents What did Square actually tell hemp and CBD sellers? Which Square deadline applies to you, October 15 or November 5? Did the hemp law date move, and what does that mean for you? Which of your products still count as hemp? What happens to your money and your Square Loan? What can you take with you when you leave Square? What is the right order to do this in? People also ask Conclusion Frequently asked questions What did Square actually tell hemp and CBD sellers? Square told sellers that CBD and hemp products can no longer go through Square, in stores or online. The notice reached affected accounts around August 7, 2026. It named a product category rather than a particular business. That wording comes from the seller notice, as merchants who received it have described it. Square has not published a policy page saying the same thing. Treat the dates as reported. This was a decision about a whole category. Nobody at Square looked at your refund rate, your paperwork, or your lab results. None of this is your fault. Square is not the first hosted platform to drop a category at short notice, as vape retailers on Shopify found. Federal law changed what the word hemp means, and that is the bigger story. Which Square deadline applies to you, October 15 or November 5? Your deadline is October 15 for a mixed catalog, or November 5 if hemp is your main business. Square sent different instructions to the two groups. Work out which group you are in before you do anything else. October 15, 2026, if CBD is one part of a wider catalog If CBD sits alongside other products, those items have to be gone by October 15, 2026. That covers every CBD, hemp, and hemp-derived item, in person and online. Hemp-derived simply means the compound came from the hemp plant. CBD, delta-8, and THCA all count. The rest of the account stays open, so your other sales, your card reader, and your payouts carry on. November 5, 2026, if hemp is your main business If hemp and CBD are most of what you sell, the whole Square account closes on November 5, 2026. The reported cutoff is 11:59pm EST. Not the listings. The account. That means your point of sale card reader, your online store, your customer list, and your payouts. One honest caveat: reported closure dates have varied between sellers, so treat November 5 as the outside edge. How do you work out which group you are in? Pull last quarter’s sales by item and work out what share came from hemp and CBD products. Your Square transaction report gives you that number in about twenty minutes. If those items are most of your revenue and most of your catalog, plan for the November 5 outcome. If you sit on the line between the two groups, plan for the worse one. The work is the same either way, and a Square hemp store migration takes longer than a catalog edit. Did the hemp law date move, and what does that mean for you? Part of it moved. The full hemp redefinition now lands on December 11, 2026. A narrower piece still lands on November 12, 2026. Congress split the date in two on September 2, 2026. Here is where each piece landed. What changed on September 2, 2026 The rule underneath this is Section 781, part of Public Law 119-37. It has been law since November 12, 2025, with a one-year delay written into it. Then Congress passed H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027. The House voted it through 370 to 48 on September 1. It was signed the next day. Section 2019 of that act limits what Section 781 covers until December 11, 2026. The wording sits in the H.R. 6500 bill text if you want to read it yourself. What each of the two dates covers On November 12, 2026, Section 781 applies only to cannabinoids the plant cannot produce on its own. In practice that means delta-8, delta-10, HHC, THC-O, and other converted cannabinoids. On December 11, 2026, Section 781 applies to everything. That is when the new measuring stick and the new cap reach ordinary CBD. So a converted product falls out of the definition in November. A plain full-spectrum tincture follows about four weeks later. Why 0.4 milligrams per container is the number to check From December 11, a finished product is hemp only if its container holds 0.4 mg of total THC or less. Total THC now includes THCA, the acid form that turns into THC when heated. It is milligrams per container, not a percentage, and not per serving. A small tincture and a large drink get the same allowance. The plant standard tightens as well, to 0.3% total THC by dry weight. Fiber, stalk, grain, seed oil, and edible greens keep their own carve-out. Does the later date reopen your Square account? No. Square set its own dates for its own commercial reasons, and federal law does not move them. December 11 is being read as a reprieve, but not for your Square account. Which of your products still count as hemp? A finished product still counts as hemp only if its container holds no more than 0.4 mg of total THC. Moving your store does not change that number. No migration makes a 5 mg gummy legal. That is why this is the first job rather than the last one. It costs an afternoon and no money, and it stops you paying for a fix that cannot help. How do you sort your catalog into two lists? Work through every product once. Pull the lab report. Get the current certificate of analysis, or COA, for every product you sell. Read total THC. Use the total THC line that includes THCA, not the delta-9 line on its own. Convert to milligrams. Work out milligrams per container, not per serving and not as a percentage. Flag the converted items. Mark anything made with a cannabinoid produced outside the plant. Separate industrial hemp. Put fiber, seed oil, and grain lines into their own group. Two lists come out of that afternoon. One survives Section 781. One does not. What if most of your catalog lands on the wrong list? Then this is a product problem before it is a platform problem. The honest answer may be a reformulated line rather than a new store. The FDA has also concluded that CBD does not fit the existing rules for food and supplements. No agency, ours included, can make a product compliant that is not. If your catalog clears the cap, your problem is the store and the payments, and that is fixable. CBD store setup is the build side of it. Confirm your own product conclusions with a lawyer and with your lab. We build and move stores, and this article is not legal advice. What happens to your money and your Square Loan? Square can hold part of your money after the account closes. An open Square Loan can also come due in full. Both are written into agreements you already accepted. The 120-day tail on refunds Square documents that refunds can be processed up to 120 days from the day you took the payment. A sale you made in September can still come back at you in January. That is long after the store is gone, and it is why a payment processor keeps money back. Square’s terms let it hold funds in reserve and delay a payout at its own discretion. A chargeback, which is a customer asking their bank to reverse a payment, stays your liability either way. What a Square Loan does when the account closes A Square Loan repays itself out of your daily card sales, at a fixed percentage. A minimum payment is due regardless, and closing the business does not pause it. Square’s own help pages go further. Closing the business before the loan is repaid puts it in default under your loan agreement. On default, Square Financial Services may demand the whole outstanding balance at once. It may also debit past-due amounts from your linked bank account and raise your repayment rate. There is a way through, but it is not automatic. Square says an alternative repayment option may exist, and tells borrowers who cannot repay to contact them. Do that in writing, and do it before the account closes rather than after. Square’s guidance for closed businesses sets out what happens if you do not. Is the 90-day hold on Square funds real? No. The widely repeated 90-day hold appears nowhere in Square’s terms, and neither does the 180-day version. Both figures circulate through blogs published by firms selling competing merchant accounts. The documented number is the 120-day refund window above. Expect that same slant almost everywhere you read about high-risk payment processing this month. Nobody has published a neutral count of affected sellers either. What can you take with you when you leave Square? You can export your products, your sales history, and your customer list yourself. Saved cards are the exception, and they need a phone call. The self-serve exports take about half an hour. The exports you can run yourself this week Item library. Dashboard, then Items and services, Items, Item library, Actions, Export Library. Square recommends the Excel file. Transactions. Reports, then Transactions, set your date range, then Export. Customer names come with it. Customer directory. Export it from the Dashboard, along with your 1099-K forms. Do these this week, not on deadline day. Keep a copy off the machine you run the store on. That catalog export is what your next store gets built from. Saved cards, the one export with a two-week clock Cards on file are the card details saved for repeat customers. Square will move them, but the route is narrow. Only the account owner can ask, and the request goes in by phone rather than through the Dashboard. Square sends card data only to a processor certified at PCI DSS Level 1, the top card-security tier. Square’s stated timeframe is up to two weeks. The order catches people out, so read the next part twice. You have to be approved by the new processor before Square will release the cards. So choosing how you take payments next is the gate on rescuing your saved cards. Picture a hemp drinks seller with 400 subscription customers who phones Square on November 3. Without a receiving processor already approved, those 400 customers have to enter their card details again. If you are still comparing payment gateway providers , that is the job to finish first. What does not come with you Reviews, loyalty balances, gift card balances, and booking history do not transfer. Budget time to rebuild them. A Square Online store is not portable either. The storefront gets rebuilt rather than moved, which is a design job. The WooCommerce migration guide walks through what that involves. What is the right order to do this in? Sort your catalog first, sort payments second, and move the store third. Every step below exists because the step after it cannot start until it is done. Week 1, sort and export, do not buy Step 1. Do not buy anything this week. Step 2. Sort every product into survives and does not, using total THC per container. Step 3. Export your item library, transactions, and customer directory. Save a copy off-site. Step 4. Confirm which Square deadline is yours and write the date where you will see it daily. Step 5. Email Square about any open loan balance, and keep the reply. Step 1 is not a delay tactic. Until the catalog is sorted, you do not know what you are buying. Weeks 2 to 4, new payments and a new store Square is the merchant of record right now, which means Square holds the bank relationship, not you. Your own account, often called a high-risk merchant account in this category, puts that relationship in your name. It takes documents and time, so start early. Step 6. Apply for your own merchant account. Have lab reports, processing statements, and formation documents ready, and allow about six weeks. Step 7. Start the new store in parallel, as a self-hosted store you control. Import the item library you already exported. Step 8. Once the processor approves you, phone Square for the card on file export. Allow the full two weeks. What the reviewers ask for, and why they say no, is a subject on its own. Merchant account underwriting covers it. Approval is the long pole, so steps 6 and 7 run at the same time. WooCommerce migration services covers running both tracks at once. Weeks 5 to 6, switch over and leave the tail running Step 9. Test checkout on the new store with a real card before you switch anything off. Step 10. Email your customers before Square does. A subscriber who hears it from you re-enters a card. Step 11. Keep the Square account open, with hemp items removed, until the 120-day refund window runs down. Step 11 matters more than it looks, because closing in a hurry does not release money faster. If your date is November 5, that option is gone and the tail runs without you. Square CBD migration support exists for exactly that case. The one-page checklist Screenshot this. Nothing below the line you are stuck on can move yet. Catalog sorted. Two lists exist, by total THC per container. Exports saved. Products, transactions, and customers, stored off-site. Deadline confirmed. October 15 or November 5, written down. Loan asked about. Question sent to Square in writing, reply kept. Application in. Documents attached, six weeks allowed. Card export requested. Phone call made, new processor approved first. People also ask Does the December 11 delay change Square’s deadlines? No. Square set its own dates, October 15 for mixed catalogs and November 5 for hemp-first accounts. The federal change moves what the law covers, not what a private company decides. What happens to my Square Loan if my account closes? Closing the business without repaying puts the loan in default under your loan agreement. Square may then demand the full balance and debit your linked bank account. Ask Square in writing about an alternative repayment option before the account closes. Can I take my saved customer cards with me? Yes, with conditions. Only the account owner can request it, only by phone, and only to a PCI DSS Level 1 processor. Square’s stated timeframe is up to two weeks, so the new processor has to be approved first. Conclusion You are dealing with two problems that look like one. The first is your setup: where the store lives and whose name is on the payments. That one is fixable. The second is your catalog, and no platform, processor, or agency fixes it for you. Sort that this week, before you spend a dollar on anything else. Square’s dates are October 15 and November 5. The law’s are November 12 for converted cannabinoids and December 11 for everything else. Frequently Asked Questions How do I know if Square counts my business as hemp-primary? Check the notice Square sent you first, because it names your category. If it does not, pull last quarter’s sales by item and total your hemp revenue. If hemp is most of your revenue and most of your catalog, plan for the November 5 closure. What does total THC mean, and why does THCA count now? Total THC counts all the THC a product can produce, not only the THC already present. THCA is the acid form that turns into THC when heated, so a delta-9 test misses it. Section 781 measures total THC including THCA, at 0.3% or less by dry weight. What does 0.4 mg per container mean for a ten-pack of gummies? It means the whole ten-pack has to hold no more than 0.4 mg of total THC, not each gummy. The cap applies to the container that encloses the finished product for retail sale. Reading it per serving instead of per container puts products on the wrong list. My products are all CBD with no delta-8. Does November 12 affect me? Not directly. November 12, 2026 applies to cannabinoids the plant cannot produce naturally, such as delta-8, delta-10, and HHC. Ordinary hemp-derived CBD is caught on December 11, 2026 instead, when the full rule applies. Can I export my Square item library and customer list myself? Yes, apart from saved cards on file. The item library exports from Dashboard, then Items and services, Items, Item library, Actions, Export Library. Transactions export from Reports, and the customer directory exports from the Dashboard. How long does a new merchant account take to approve? Plan on about six weeks from application to live, and start earlier if you can. The review is the slow part, which is why step 6 runs in parallel with the store build. Virtina is an eCommerce solutions partner working across WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, and Shopify, with named industry experience in CBD and other regulated categories. We build and move stores. We do not sell merchant accounts, and nothing here is legal advice.

text: Summary Your Magento version fell out of support on 11 August 2026. The store still runs and the licence stays valid. Adobe also states that an unsupported version is no longer PCI compliant. Four responses are available: upgrade to a supported 2.4.x, move to Adobe Commerce Cloud, replatform, or document the risk. For most merchants the right move is the upgrade, not a replatform. This guide walks all four, starting with the one that earns us the least. Introduction Two things happened to Magento on 11 August 2026, and most merchants noticed one. The 2.4.6 line left regular support that day, per Adobe’s published release documentation. On the same date, 2.4.5 left extended support, its final phase of ordinary coverage. A month later nothing has broken, which is exactly what makes this decision hard. Your board wants a position and your agency has an interest in the answer. This article walks four paths, ordered by how little each one earns us. Every date below comes from Adobe’s own documentation, checked on 10 September 2026. Table of Contents What changed for Magento on 11 August 2026? Are you out of PCI compliance now? Does your Magento edition change your deadline? Which of the four paths fits your store? Path 1: upgrade to a supported 2.4.x release Path 2: move to Adobe Commerce Cloud Path 3: replatform to a different eCommerce platform Path 4: document the risk and buy a quarter What should you check this week? People also ask Conclusion Frequently asked questions What changed for Magento on 11 August 2026? On 11 August 2026 Adobe stopped issuing quality fixes and security patches for the 2.4.6 line. Adobe’s published release documentation puts 2.4.5 out of extended support, its last ordinary phase, on the same date. Which Magento versions are still supported? 2.4.7, 2.4.8 and 2.4.9 remain in regular support, and 2.4.7 exits on 31 May 2027. Release line Regular support ends Extended support ends Additional security fixes end 2.4.9 31 May 2029 Not published Not published 2.4.8 31 May 2028 Not published Not published 2.4.7 31 May 2027 31 May 2028 Not published 2.4.6 11 August 2026 31 August 2027 31 May 2028 2.4.5 12 August 2025 11 August 2026 31 May 2027 2.4.4 12 April 2025 14 April 2026 31 May 2027 Magento release lifecycle dates from Adobe’s published release documentation, checked 10 September 2026. Confirm your own edition’s dates on Adobe’s versions page. What Adobe stops doing after the end-of-support date Your store keeps running and your licence stays valid, per Adobe’s end-of-support FAQ. Adobe calls this end of support (EOS), not end of life (EOL). Tickets raised after the date are not resolved, and no further product changes are made. That includes security and PCI compliance changes, and community pull requests are no longer merged. Adobe’s lifecycle policy sets a three-year standard support window from each version’s GA date. The same policy states that Adobe does not patch third-party dependencies such as PHP and MySQL. Are you out of PCI compliance now? Adobe says yes, and that is Adobe’s published position on its own software. Your acquiring bank, not Adobe, is the party that acts on it. What Adobe states about unsupported versions Adobe’s end-of-support FAQ, checked on 10 September 2026, states that an unsupported version is “no longer PCI compliant.” The same FAQ names fines, loss of card processing ability, or other penalties as consequences. We are reporting Adobe’s statement, not a clause of the PCI DSS standard itself. We did not read that standard, so we will not name a requirement number. Why your acquiring bank and QSA decide this The practical consequence does not run through Adobe at all. It runs through your acquiring bank and your qualified security assessor, who judge your PCI DSS compliance. They decide whether an unsupported release line is a finding, and on what timetable. So confirm your own position with your QSA before you assume either safety or catastrophe. Assuming is the expensive option. Does your Magento edition change your deadline? Possibly, and you need to confirm that yourself rather than take any agency’s word for it, including ours. What we could and could not verify about edition differences Adobe’s published versions page lists the lifecycle dates without drawing a distinction between editions. We checked it on 10 September 2026 and it does not mention Magento Open Source. Several agency articles assert that extended-support patches reach Adobe Commerce customers only. We could not verify that split against Adobe’s documentation, so we will not repeat it. Confirm your own edition’s dates on Adobe’s published versions page before you plan around extended support. If you cannot confirm that you receive extended support, plan as though 11 August 2026 was your end date. Which of the four paths fits your store? Four paths exist, and the table below orders them by how little each one earns us. None of the four is a default. Each is right for a nameable situation and wrong for the others. The order is deliberate, because the cheapest honest answer belongs at the top. Path Choose this if Do not choose this if 1. Upgrade to a supported 2.4.x The platform still fits and customisation is moderate Every upgrade has already become a rebuild 2. Adobe Commerce Cloud You are on Adobe Commerce licensing and infrastructure is the pain You are on Open Source, or cost predictability matters more than managed infrastructure 3. Replatform Run cost is dominated by keeping Magento alive, or requirements genuinely simplified You have complex B2B catalogues, multi-store, or deep ERP integration 4. Document the risk, short term You cannot move before peak You have no dated commitment to move afterwards Four responses to the August 2026 support cliff, ordered by how little each benefits Virtina. Compiled 10 September 2026. How to read this decision table Start at path 1 and only move down when a row’s do-not-choose column describes you. That rule takes thirty seconds and it is the whole method. Most readers stop at path 1, which is the point. The paths below it are not upgrades in disguise. They are different projects, with different budgets and different risk. Path 1: upgrade to a supported 2.4.x release For most readers this is the right answer, and it is the one that sells us the least. Your install still fits, and the platform is not the reason growth stalled. If that describes you, our Magento version upgrade steps guide covers the mechanics. Should you target 2.4.8 or 2.4.9? Target 2.4.8 if you carry a heavy extension footprint, and 2.4.9 if you want the extra year. Requirement 2.4.8 2.4.9 Regular support ends 31 May 2028 31 May 2029 PHP 8.4 or 8.3 8.5 MariaDB 11.4 or 11.8 12.3 recommended, 11.8 supported MySQL 8.4 8.4 OpenSearch 3 3 Valkey 8.1 9 Adobe’s published system requirements for 2.4.8 and 2.4.9, checked 10 September 2026. 2.4.9 buys one more year, but Adobe’s system requirements put it on PHP 8.5. php.net dates that release to 20 November 2025, so vendors have had roughly ten months to certify. 2.4.8 runs on PHP 8.4 or 8.3, where extension compatibility is far more likely to already exist. What actually drives upgrade cost and effort An upgrade quote is built from six lines, none of them your revenue. Those six are extension re-certification, module remediation, theme rework, integration re-testing, infrastructure changes, and QA with UAT. Five numbers price all six. Installed extensions. Each needs re-certification on the target version. Core overrides. Remediation scales with how far you forked core. Store views. Each multiplies theme, content and QA work. Live integrations. ERP, PIM, tax and gateway need re-testing. PHP distance. A big jump is where frontend rework bites. Budget a staging environment and a rollback plan into the same figure. Our Magento development services team scopes upgrades against those five numbers. Path 2: move to Adobe Commerce Cloud This fits you only if you are already on Adobe Commerce licensing and infrastructure management is the actual pain. You are handing the stack to Adobe and paying for that. Adobe does not publish Adobe Commerce Cloud pricing or packaging, so we will not estimate it. Price it directly with Adobe, and ask what the licence covers before you compare it to an upgrade. This section is short because the pricing is not public and we did not research it this pass. Path 3: replatform to a different eCommerce platform Leaving is right when the upgrade has stopped being a version bump and become a rebuild. Every upgrade is a project rather than maintenance, and total cost of ownership is dominated by upkeep. Or you cannot staff it at a price you will pay, or your requirements genuinely simplified since you chose Magento. If three describe you, put eCommerce replatforming services on the table. Five store profiles that should stay on Magento Five profiles should stay. Complex B2B catalogues. Company accounts, contract pricing and approval hierarchies are native to Adobe Commerce B2B features . Multi-store hierarchies. Website, store and store-view structures lack a clean equivalent, per Magento 2 multistore configuration . Deep ERP integration. A tested connector is the asset, so Magento ERP integration work restarts elsewhere. Large attributed catalogues. Many attribute combinations do not map cleanly elsewhere. Mid-peak timing. Nobody should cut a store over between October and January. If two or more describe you, upgrade. Where merchants who do leave usually land Most merchants who leave Magento land on WooCommerce, and we will say so. Our Magento vs WooCommerce comparison sets out where each wins. Run the destination choice as eCommerce platform selection work, scored against your own requirements. A destination decided under deadline pressure is the most expensive kind. Path 4: document the risk and buy a quarter If you cannot move before your next peak, the honest position is not that you are fine. It is that you write the risk down. What a defensible risk acceptance contains Tell your acquiring bank and your QSA exactly where you are, in writing. Apply what hardening you can at the WAF layer, which our Magento store security guide covers. Put a dated commitment in front of your board, naming a target release. 2.4.6 stores sit better here than 2.4.5 stores. 2.4.6 still carries extended support to 31 August 2027 and security provisioning to 31 May 2028. Adobe calls that extension a one-time exception, so do not plan a second one. 2.4.5’s last ordinary phase ended on 11 August 2026. A documented, dated, temporary position is defensible. Silence is not. What should you check this week? Magento Upgrade Readiness Inspection Five checks you can finish before Friday decide which path you are on. Version and edition. Confirm both from the admin, not from memory. Third-party extensions. Count them and list the vendors behind them. Store views and websites. Count both, because each multiplies the work. Live integrations. List every one, including ERP, PIM, tax and gateway. Current PHP version. Compare it against your target version’s requirement. Then check the second clock. php.net ends security support for PHP 8.2 on 31 December 2026. An unsupported Magento version on PHP 8.2 has two clocks expiring five months apart. For a second opinion on which path fits, talk to the Virtina eCommerce team . People also ask Does Magento stop working after end of support? No. The software keeps running and the licence stays valid while your account is in good standing. Adobe’s end-of-support FAQ says so directly. What stops is patching, ticket resolution and further product changes. Is Magento 2.4.6 still safe to run in 2026? Not indefinitely. Every vulnerability found after 11 August 2026 is patched on supported lines and left open on yours. The public fix effectively documents the flaw. Risk compounds from here rather than decaying. How long does a Magento version upgrade take? Agencies typically quote 2 to 6 weeks for a straightforward version upgrade. That is what agencies quote, not a figure we can verify. Effort scales with extension count, core overrides and store views. Conclusion Most readers should upgrade to a supported 2.4.x and stay on Magento. That is the smallest project on the list and the one we profit from least. The deadline is real and the panic version of it is not. Replatforming is right for a narrow profile you can name in a sentence. If complex B2B, multi-store or a working ERP connector describes you, upgrade instead. And if you cannot move this quarter, write the risk down with a date on it. Frequently Asked Questions When did Magento 2.4.6 lose support? 11 August 2026, the end of regular support, per Adobe’s published release documentation. Ignore the March 2026 date in agency coverage, because Adobe’s own page contradicts it. Do I have to replatform because there is no upgrade path? No, and Adobe documents direct upgrades to supported 2.4.x release lines. The no-upgrade-path framing comes from parties who benefit when replatforming looks inevitable. Should I upgrade to Magento 2.4.8 or 2.4.9? 2.4.8 if you carry many extensions, because PHP 8.4 and 8.3 have broader vendor support. 2.4.9 if you want the extra year and your extensions already certify on PHP 8.5. Does an unsupported version break PCI compliance? Adobe’s end-of-support FAQ states that an unsupported version is no longer PCI compliant. That is Adobe’s position on its own software, not a named clause of PCI DSS. Confirm your own position with your QSA and acquiring bank. Does Magento Open Source get the same extended support as Adobe Commerce? Adobe’s versions page lists the dates without drawing an edition split, though agency coverage claims one. We could not verify it, so confirm your edition’s dates on Adobe’s versions page. What PHP version does Magento 2.4.9 need? PHP 8.5, per Adobe’s system requirements documentation. 2.4.8 accepts PHP 8.4 or 8.3, which is why it is often safer. When does Magento 2.4.7 lose regular support? 31 May 2027, per Adobe’s release documentation, with extended support to 31 May 2028. If you are on 2.4.7, that is the deadline to budget against now. Virtina is a Magento certified eCommerce partner that also runs WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Shopify practices. That mix is why we can tell you to stay on Magento when staying is the right call.
