rankings, enhanced customer engagement Choosing the Right AI Tool for Your eCommerce  Business Choosing the right AI tool is one of the most consequential actions that can define the future of your eCommerce enterprise. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the key factors to consider: Integration The interaction of an AI tool with one or another enterprise solution, including your eCommerce platform, CRM, ERP, or marketing tools, determines the effectiveness of the AI tool. If the integration is not done well, it creates problems in the organization’s functionality or requires much re-engineering. It is also important that the AI tool integrates with existing technologies. Its features should already have extensions in Shopify, Magento, or WooCommerce. Interface compatibility could also be more flexible, especially with selected third-party APIs. Capabilities Many sectors of business and transactional activity can benefit from various AI tools. Choosing a tool with the right ability ensures that it solves the required business problem. Find out what problems your business experiences and what areas are essential. For instance, if you want to employ AI to improve customers’ experience or make your content more personalized, it is better to focus on AI software for recommendation engines. If security is a priority, focus on the tools with great options for fraud detection. Scalability Another factor about the AI tool is that as your business expands, it should also be able to scale. What is effective in the small business environment may require additional effort to be effective in the large and complex environment. Select technologies so that they can scale up to handle a larger number of users, larger sets of data, and more computation. Products with additional/customary functions or cost-benefit schemes are easier to scale. Data Security M-commerce organizations transact with customers’ personal information, such as payment and personal information. Data protection is vital if the firm is to build confidence with its clients and meet industry standards. Ensure the AI tool complies with GDPR, CCPA, or any other regional data protection regulation. Some features to look for are encryption, data anonymization, and the level of access control. Buy from vendors with security certifications from third parties or those who have had an audit on their products. Ease of Use Implementing a steep learning curve AI tool is challenging, which leads to fewer users on your team accepting the tool’s use. Evaluate the user interface, the instructions for the item, and how easy or difficult it is to set up. Tools with simple dashboards and visualizations are more often simple to use. Some vendors even provide demos, trial periods, or other ways to help judge its usability only. The Advantages and Disadvantages of Artificial Intelligence in eCommerce  While AI offers transformative benefits, businesses must address key challenges: Data Privacy and Security AI interprets data with the help of algorithms that may require human data, thus becoming an issue of privacy. Compliance with such regulations as GDPR and strict security measures must be adopted. Cost and Implementation However, cheaper solutions are available, and businesses need to look at initial investments, monthly charges, and possible profits. Scalability Check that your AI tool can manage traffic surges without showing decreased performance results. Customization Choose tools that are also customizable to meet today’s and tomorrow’s changes in your business. Human Oversight AI should complement work done by human beings, not supplant it as the last intervention. However, human opinion is still needed to monitor and manage complex queries and strategic choices.

title: M-Commerce: Stats, Examples, Trends, and the Future of Mobile Shopping
text: Summary More and more customers are shopping on their phones, and mobile transactions are increasing. All these changes point to a shift toward a mobile-first strategy that companies need to adjust to. For businesses to survive, it is time to invest in mobile commerce . By incorporating mobile shopping, not only will you meet customers’ expectations but also outrun your competition in a very dynamic market. The fast-paced digital world has significantly transformed shopping. Gone are the days when people had actually to go to a store or have a desktop computer. This became possible due to mobile commerce, or m-commerce, which refers to selling and purchasing goods and services via wireless handheld devices like tablets and smartphones. But what exactly makes m-commerce so important? M-commerce dominated the retail sector by 2023, making over 43% of total eCommerce sales . Furthermore, it is anticipated to increase to 44% by 2025, illustrating how important technology has become in shaping customer behavior. Mobile commerce is transforming retail in a world where convenience is king. This implies that staying ahead of this changing trend is necessary. Table of Contents Current Statistics Notable Examples of M-Commerce Emerging Trends in M-Commerce What’s Next for M-Commerce? Challenges and Considerations in M-Commerce   Current Statistics Let’s begin with the big picture: m-commerce has gone from an emerging trend to a global power player.  Currently, at least $2.07 trillion in m-commerce value happens globally (in 2024); this represents about 57% of all retail e-commerce sales. That means more than half of every online purchase worldwide occurs through a mobile. The numbers also portray an equally compelling story when zooming in on the U.S. Retail m-commerce sales, expected to reach a staggering $542.73 billion in 2024 . This shows that consumers are going for the convenience of mobile shopping, reshaping the retail landscape in real-time. ⇨  Consumer Behavior: Why Mobile Wins The shift toward mobile is more about preferences rather than just convenience.  For instance, 85% of shoppers opt for mobile apps over websites to purchase online.  Mobile apps don’t only engage the user base but convert it. In that case, mobile apps make the shopper 157 percent more effective than web sessions. Even the monetary implication is just as surprising.  The average order through a mobile application rings up to $102 versus $92 through a mobile site. Those few extra dollars might not seem like much but multiplied across tens of millions of transactions, it shows why businesses are doubling down on mobile-first strategies. When combining the above facts with consumer behavior, it is evident that m-commerce is not just a trend, but the future of retail, and business houses that adapt will thrive. Notable Examples of M-Commerce Regarding m-commerce, some brilliant brands and innovators have transformed online shopping.  Here are a few of these big players, emerging game-changers, and companies taking interesting stances on mobile-first tactics. Amazon’s mobile app is the epitome of convenience. One-click purchasing has transformed the checkout process, making impulse buying more effortless. Its personalized recommendations, tailored to your browsing and purchase history, make the shopping experience feel like it really “gets” you. Walmart’s mobile application takes friendly functionality to yet another level. From how easy it is to reorder household staples to streamlined mobile payment options quickly, every feature of the app works to save you time, whether it’s shopping in-store or online. In 2024, Temu, a Chinese e-commerce app, took the entire highlight when it became the most downloaded app on the Apple App Store, even before famous giants like TikTok and ChatGPT. As many of its users consider it a source of huge discounts for shopping, making it an emerging star of m-commerce. Starbucks has nailed the science of technology integration into customer convenience. Its mobile order and pay service allows users to avoid the line by placing their orders and paying before arriving, knowing that the coffee will be ready for them when they arrive. This system gives app users unparalleled ease, but it has been difficult for the company to reconcile this with the in-store experience, showing the difficulty of combining m-commerce with more traditional operations. Emerging Trends in M-Commerce As we head into 2025, m-commerce will become an unstoppable force in shopping.  Here’s a glimpse at some top trends reshaping how we shop from our smartphones: Mobile shopping apps are on track to dominate in 2025. In fact, over half of the U.S. shoppers use apps for purchases. Therefore, it is not surprising that consumers continue relying on them for browsing and buying. With this trend still in place, marketers should ensure that their mobile applications are well-tuned for a smooth and intuitive user experience . Buy Now, Pay Later, or BNPL services are on the surge and fever pitch during the shopping holiday season. With such changes in people’s preferred way of payment, consumers today enjoy flexible options of shopping now and paying later without worrying about the pressure of costs ahead. BNPL is expected to spread further in 2025, and more retailers will provide those options to attract budget-conscious shoppers. The distinction between shopping and entertainment is rapidly becoming more hazy due to social media platforms, particularly TikTok. Thanks to an integrated shopping feature, one can buy things from the apps while watching the video. This trend has transformed how consumers locate and buy products, turning social media into an immersive buying experience . Despite challenges like local app bans, eCommerce integration into social networks will keep growing, providing marketers access to customers where they spend most of their time. By 2025, around 60 percent of customers will have conducted at least one contactless payment monthly. This move towards safe, contactless payment methods indicates consumers’ desire to complete transactions quickly and quickly. Mobile wallet and tap-to-pay usage will continue to increase to accept contactless payments as they are more secure in completing transactions. What’s Next for M-Commerce? The future of m-commerce in the U.S. holds great opportunities. Mobile devices will continue to shape and influence retail sales, further transforming how customers shop and businesses interact with their audiences. Here are some m-commerce future trends to consider: Among the most important changes in the near future is the application of artificial intelligence to create highly customized shopping experiences . Imagine an AI that can recognize your preferences, predict your next wants, and alter the shopping experience. It will boost customer satisfaction and loyalty since shopping becomes enjoyable and quicker. Another exciting feature would be Augmented Reality (AR) , where customers could virtually try on a product to see how that particular furniture piece would look in the living room before even clicking the buy button. This will bridge the gap between online and offline, with a seamless customer experience, guiding more confident purchasing decisions. Challenges and Considerations in M-Commerce As mobile shopping grows, businesses and consumers alike face some critical challenges. There are two key areas to consider: The growing demand for shopping through mobile phones emphasizes the urgency to safeguard customer data. Business houses, therefore, need to take cyber threat protection for mobile transactions seriously. The focus should be on protection at every stage, from encryption to payment gateway. Each transaction has to be secured so that every consumer can be sure their personal details are being taken care of while making purchases on the move. Another force that shapes the mobile commerce landscape is changing regulation. Tightening data privacy laws in governments will create a business necessity for organizations to be better than their counterparts in terms of compliance with new rules that may range from how the data is collected and kept to even how apps can be delivered to users around the globe. Changes in trade policies may also affect which apps are available and, thus, the international reach of m-commerce companies. You can prevent your company from being caught off guard by staying updated on these changes.

title: 25 Ways to Boost eCommerce Sales
headings: 1. Optimize Website Design and User Experience
23. Launch Limited-Time Offers and Flash Sales
text: Summary Using a single strategy is not enough to increase your eCommerce sales; you need to take a multifaceted approach. For your customers to have a smooth, interesting, and customized purchasing experience, each of the 25 tactics we covered above is essential. The more you focus on developing relationships with your audience, refining your products, and staying up to date with trends, the more likely you are to achieve long-term success. Today, the fast-paced digital economy makes optimizing eCommerce sales more critical than ever.  As the U.S. eCommerce market continues to rise above $1.9 trillion in sales by 2029 , competition remains intense; standing out requires more than just having a sleek website. With that said, success in such a landscape demands strategic approaches and tactics to attract visitors and change them into loyal customers.  That’s where this guide comes in.  Our detailed blog focus is to equip you with effective strategies for raising your sales figures at online stores and succeeding in any saturated marketplace.  Let’s see what tactics will help bring your eCommerce business the extra edge to succeed. Table of Contents Optimize Website Design and User Experience Enhance Product Pages Implement Effective SEO Strategies Leverage Email Marketing Utilize Social Media Platforms Offer Multiple Payment Options Provide Excellent Customer Service Implement Retargeting Strategies Optimize for Mobile Users Utilize Influencer Partnerships Implement Upselling and Cross-selling Techniques Enhance Site Search Functionality Offer Free and Fast Shipping Create Compelling Content Marketing Utilize Customer Loyalty Programs Conduct A/B Testing Optimize Loading Speeds Implement Exit-Intent Popups Leverage User-Generated Content Utilize Analytics and Data Tracking Personalize the Shopping Experience Collaborate with Local Businesses Launch Limited-Time Offers and Flash Sales Focus on Visual Storytelling Expand into International Markets 1. Optimize Website Design and User Experience Making sure your website design is entirely responsive to mobile devices is crucial.  Websites are increasingly being seen and accessed on mobile devices; therefore, maintaining user engagement requires a mobile-friendly design. Reduce load times and enhance site navigation—nothing irritates users more than a website that is difficult to use and takes a long time to load. Navigation must also be streamlined for ease and quick access to anything your visitors desire. Load pages should be optimized so users can navigate your website more smoothly. Last, use clear and compelling calls to action that push visitors in your desired direction – toward purchase, a newsletter sign-up, whatever the case. Together, these ensure a seamless and enjoyable experience on your website. 2. Enhance Product Pages Start with top-notch photos and videos that showcase your products in action and from various perspectives to make your product pages stand out . As a result, customers will better understand what they are purchasing, increasing their confidence in the transaction. Developing compelling and thorough product descriptions is crucial in addition to providing eye-catching images; highlighting features, advantages, and any unique selling factors will assist buyers in making well-informed choices.  Finally, do not forget the social proof; showing customer reviews and ratings builds trust and give people a real-life experience of how the product performs, making your page more persuasive and relatable. 3. Implement Effective SEO Strategies Finding the terms your target audience is searching for requires thorough keyword research before implementing SEO methods. This means you can get the most relevant keywords, driving traffic to your site. Ensure that your meta titles and descriptions are optimized because they work to your advantage in rankings and click-through rates from search engines. Don’t neglect the power of schema markup – this simple tool helps search engines understand your content better. Often, this results in rich snippets that stand out on the page and can boost your visibility.  All these will set a solid foundation for improving your SEO and attracting more qualified visitors . 4. Leverage Email Marketing Build and segment a high-quality email list.  From this, you can send out emails to the correct groups of customers, increasing relevance and, therefore, engagement. After having the list, develop targeted, personal campaigns that resonate with each segment’s interests and needs, making your emails feel like a conversation rather than some generic promotion. Do not forget to set up automated abandoned cart reminders to re-engage the shoppers who, for whatever reason, walked away without completing the purchase, nudging them with a well-timed, compelling message that may convert into sales. Strategically focusing on these areas will help improve your email marketing results and get a more personal connection with your audience. 5. Utilize Social Media Platforms  It is important to understand which social media sites are most active for your target audience and engage with them there.  Whether it is Instagram, LinkedIn, or Twitter, each channel brings unique opportunities to reach customers directly. The user-generated content and testimonials not only build trust but also foster a sense of community. It makes things more authentic in the eyes of your target audience if they see real people praising your brand.  Thus, active participation and response to feedback create a more personalized experience that reinforces customer loyalty and drives engagement. 6. Offer Multiple Payment Options Multiple payment options should be necessary to make buying seamless and convenient for your customers. Offering several credit cards or more popular digital wallets like PayPal, Apple Pay, and Google Pay would make shopping easier. However, flexibility in payability is provided by enabling different forms of Buy Now, Pay Later options to attract customers who want more flexi-payability. Most importantly, your checkout process must be secure, easy, and hassle-free so that people will be confident in trusting your site and, thus, repeat business. The more options you offer, the more customers are likely to feel confident about buying, which increases the chances of converting. 7. Provide Excellent Customer Service Excellent customer service can work wonders to get an edge over the highly competitive market today.  This can also be achieved through live chat support, where customers may receive instant access to their questions anytime and as often as possible. A helpful section is one well-organized, elaborate FAQ that allows shoppers quick access to most of the common questions asked without reaching the support department. A hassle-free return and refund policy also creates a sense of security in customers’ minds that they can return if needed. These simple strategies build trust and foster customer loyalty that will bring repeat business and positive reviews. 8 . Implement Retargeting Strategies Retargeting is a robust reconnect strategy for visitors who have already shown interest in your brand.  You can remind those potential customers of your products or services as they browse other sites, keeping your brand fresh in their minds. Setting up targeted email campaigns can re-engage them directly by sending personalized content or offers right to their inbox. Offer special discounts or exclusive deals to returning customers. This will make the customers feel valued and want to complete the purchase.  Retargeting strategies also boost sales, besides building customer loyalty, as visitors may become long-term supporters. 9. Optimize for Mobile Users  Delivering a flawless purchasing experience in today’s fast-paced digital world requires optimizing for mobile customers. Ensure your website is mobile-friendly to preserve its functionality and style across all screen sizes. A simple checkout procedure is a way out because customers should be able to pay for their purchases fast, without unnecessary steps and distracting elements. Furthermore, consider creating a mobile app for your store. That can improve the user experience by providing them with more personalized features, push notifications, and quick access to products, making shopping easier for your customers while on the go. All of this will help in enhancing your conversion rates. 10 . Utilize Influencer Partnerships Collaborating with influencers in your niche can also be a great approach to increase brand awareness and reach. With such collaboration, you tap into their existing trust and following as long as the influencer’s values and target audience are aligned with yours. You can offer them an affiliate program as a bonus for them to sell your products. To maximize the impact, be sure to share their content on your own platforms, amplify the exposure, and build a sense of community around your brand. This kind of strategic partnership drives traffic and builds credibility and trust with potential customers. 11. Implement Upselling and Cross-selling Techniques Another method that is sure to boost sales is upselling and cross-selling. You could suggest related items on your product pages so the customer can look for others they would like to purchase. Offer a bundle discount when you sell items together. They will end up with more stuff for a cheaper price and increase their average order value. It can make the shopping experience more personal and relevant by having personalized product recommendations based on a customer’s browsing history or purchases. That can increase the possibility of further purchases. Upselling and cross-selling tactics drive more sales while improving the customer experience if you thoughtfully suggest the right products at the right time. 12 . Enhance Site Search Functionality To improve search functionality on your site, start with an intuitive search bar that provides autocomplete suggestions as a user types to make it easier and quicker for them to find what they want. Adding filters will help refine customers’ results by specific criteria, thereby improving their overall experience. Also, analyzing search data regularly will be necessary to establish patterns in what users are searching for. This will help you understand their preferences better and optimize the search function to ensure that your customers always have a smooth and efficient shopping experience. 13. Offer Free and Fast Shipping Free and rapid shipping is another powerful marketing tool that can significantly increase your sales.  Free shipping on all orders above a certain amount compels customers to spend more yet gives them added value sense. Be transparent about how long shipping takes and the costs involved—it helps not create confusion and fosters trust. Working with credible shipping companies can also result in on-time and secure delivery, impacting customer satisfaction directly. This combination creates a positive shopping experience that will increase sales, make repeat customers, and give a stronger brand reputation, placing you in a competitive market. 14 . Create Compelling Content Marketing To get creative content marketing, start by developing a blog where you could place valuable insights in the field and describe how your product can solve a given problem.  A blog helps to gain trust, create authority in the given domain, and better explain your offerings to customers. Follow this by enriching content with interesting videos or tutorials where you display certain product features or give some excellent tips to the customer. These kinds of content are perfect for drawing viewers in and offering experiential learning opportunities. Lastly are infographics and guides, which simplify difficult information into easily understood visuals so your audience can quickly grasp the main ideas. 15. Utilize Customer Loyalty Programs Customer loyalty is a good approach that should be adopted for customer retention and satisfaction. Set up a points reward system where each customer gains points with every purchase to redeem later in the form of discounts or exclusive products. Offering special discounts to regular customers will ensure they become more committed to your brand. For word-of-mouth referrals, always give your customers incentives, like adding points and rewarding every new customer they bring in. This approach not only increases the rate of customer loyalty but also instills in the minds of your audience a feeling of exclusiveness and appreciation, leading to higher engagement and sales later. 16 . Conduct A/B Testing A/B testing is the most effective method to optimize your marketing. Testing different versions of landing pages can tell you which is more responsive for your audiences. You can even experiment using different call-to-action (CTA) buttons, headlines, or images for your website. After discovering what makes it in with your visitors, data-driven decisions and implementations with the best strategies could be made through careful analysis of results. This will keep improving the user engagement and conversion rates for your content based on actual user feedback. 17. Optimize Loading Speeds  Improve the website functionality by improving the loading times . To do this, compress the photos on your website to make them smaller without sacrificing the quality so that they load faster. Another thing is to use browser caching, which means returning visitors don’t have to reload every element, speeding up their experience. You can also implement a Content Delivery Network or CDN, which spreads the content across multiple servers worldwide, making the load time for users irrespective of their location. Finally, reducing HTTP requests by making your website’s elements streamlined and optimized coding will further improve the speeds, creating a smoother and more rapid experience for your user. Combining these strategies will ensure your site loads quickly and efficiently, providing a better user experience overall. 18 . Implement Exit-Intent Popups  The exit-intent pop-up tool captures visitors’ attention, leaving your site with a power that cannot be underestimated. It allows you to give them some special discount, promotion, or even an exclusive deal when they hover over the exit button. It raises the possibility of making the last sale and helps to collect their email addresses for future marketing. Also, through their browse behavior, you could further display tailored product suggestions, thereby creating an experience they might go with all the way to purchase from, lest they leave your platform. 19. Leverage User-Generated Content Another excellent way to create trust and engagement with your customers is to encourage them to share their experiences in photos and reviews.  It not only provides real content for prospective buyers but also fosters a community surrounding your brand. You can show these user-generated photos and testimonials on product pages or other social media networks where customers use and enjoy your products. Run contests or campaigns that motivate people to create and share more content, with the chance of being featured or winning prizes. This will increase the volume of user-generated content, strengthen customer loyalty, and boost your brand’s visibility. 20 . Utilize Analytics and Data Tracking One of the best things you can do to maintain the pace in business is through analytics and tracking data to your advantage. Monitoring the flow of traffic going through your website and tracking the behavior of those using the site will give insight into how people interact on your site. Monitoring sales data helps businesses observe trends, understand customer preferences, or find growth opportunities. Armed with such knowledge, you make more intelligent decisions that advance your business, whether optimizing your site, refining your marketing strategy , or changing what you offer to better cater to customer needs. 21. Personalize the Shopping Experience To create a truly personalized shopping experience, use AI to offer product recommendations based on each customer’s preference and past behavior . One can think of location-based promotions or exclusive deals such that customers feel they are receiving something special just for them. Furthermore, analyzing actions taken by users allows email and SMS campaigns to be designed based on individual shopper interests, whether it’s reminding shoppers about items viewed or offering discounts on those products shoppers are most likely to buy. This is the kind of personalization that not only enhances the customer journey but also creates loyalty by making the shopper feel understood and appreciated. 22 . Collaborate with Local Businesses Partnering with local businesses is a significant game-changer for any brand, mainly when strengthening one’s connection with the community. Teaming with nearby brands for a joint promotion appealing to a shared customer base can do this. This isn’t only going to expand your reach but also build more trust as customers see that you are supporting local businesses. Offering in-store pick-up for customers in neighboring areas also makes shopping seamlessly convenient, allowing them to shop with you. These local partners are, therefore, examples of how you differentiate yourself and show that the brand is invested in the well-being of the area. 23. Launch Limited-Time Offers and Flash Sales One of the effective sales boosts can be made through limited-time offers and flash sales, as such an approach creates a feeling of urgency and scarcity and motivates customers to take action right away.  It can be promoted via email campaigns, social media, and attractive on-site banners, capturing attention and generating traffic.  This could make it worthwhile for you to get creative with your timing—seasonal promotions or event-based flash sales can be quite exciting and relevant, giving customers another reason to take advantage of the special offers.  With this, you can generate a sense of exclusivity and urgency that might drive you to more conversions. 24 . Focus on Visual Storytelling Visual storytelling is a proven way to get your audience hooked on your brand. This can be done through interactive or even shoppable videos.  The good thing about Instagram Stories and TikTok is that they allow you to create attention-grabbing fun posts about your products by emphasizing the most important points without being too dull and mundane.  Then, add customer stories via compelling images – real-life testimony, a glimpse behind the scenes, or user-generated content help increase authenticity and enhance trust for your audience with the blending of these visual elements creates an experience and drives action. 25. Expand into International Markets Expanding your business into international markets opens doors to many exciting growth opportunities. However, this also demands a cautious plan and its implementation. Begin with multi-currency support and multilingual capabilities in products to make the product offering more accessible to consumers from various regions. This helps build trust and creates a smoother shopping experience for international buyers. Simplify international shipping and duties, removing any barriers preventing customers from buying from you. Clear, affordable shipping can make a big difference in purchasing. Lastly, your marketing strategies should be adapted to cater to different cultural preferences. Understanding other regions’ local values and traditions will let you tailor your messaging to boost your global appeal and provide better results.

text: Summary Successful platforms are all about innovative, scalable, and customer-driven approaches. They succeed through cutting-edge innovations, seamless user experiences , and responses to changing needs. Explore the platforms this blog mentions for inspiration or shopping needs to see their standout features and strategies. Introduction eCommerce has grown exponentially to become one of the cornerstones of modern shopping. It has reshaped how people find, buy, and get their products. With consumers becoming more accustomed to digital convenience, global eCommerce sales are expected to surpass 8 trillion dollars , growing by a robust 39%. This steady growth shows an increasing dependence on online sites and the scope of business operations to succeed in this digital market. When you think about the various eCommerce sites in play today, identifying which aspects contribute to the success of the more successful ones helps businesses decide about resource allocation. This blog breaks down the leading websites that set the future course of eCommerce and their features that are transforming the way the eCommerce industry works. This page ranks the top 10 online shopping sites in the world by one metric: total monthly website visits, Semrush Traffic Analytics, July 2026. It then covers eleven more eCommerce websites that lead a category or a country. Every figure here carries its source and its period. Where a number could not be confirmed against a primary source, it is not on the page. That rule removed several familiar claims, including the market-size figure this page used to open with. A number with no date and no named source is decoration, not evidence. The ranking also has a real blind spot, and this page states it rather than hiding it. Web-visit panels do not count app traffic, which is why Taobao, Tmall, JD.com and Pinduoduo are absent. Below the ranking sit the same companies by disclosed revenue, the regional and category leaders, and what any of it changes for a store you actually run. If you are here to benchmark your own build, the must-have store features are a better starting point. Table of Contents Summary Introduction How this ranking is measured Top 10 online shopping sites in the world 1. Amazon 2. Temu 3. AliExpress 4. Walmart 5. eBay 6. Etsy 7. Rakuten 8. Shein 9. Coupang 10. Ozon Why the biggest sellers are missing from this list The same companies by disclosed revenue instead Regional and category leaders worth knowing What this means for your store People also ask Conclusion Frequently asked questions How this ranking is measured This ranking uses one metric: total monthly website visits, Semrush Traffic Analytics, July 2026. Every figure was read from the same panel, in the same month, one domain at a time. One company gets one flagship storefront domain. Amazon’s country sites are counted separately by Semrush, so they are not stacked into a single total. What is excluded and why Only shopping destinations qualify. Three kinds of site are kept out, and the rule is worth stating plainly because it changes the list. Commerce software. Shopify sells store software, not products. It is not a place a shopper buys a thing. Single-brand manufacturer stores. samsung.com drew 407.2M visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, more than Etsy. It is still one brand selling its own goods, and apple.com is out for the same reason. Food delivery. A restaurant delivery service answers a different question than this one. Naming the number you are excluding is what makes an inclusion rule credible. Samsung would sit sixth on visits. It is out because the rule says so, not because it is awkward. If you read this page before, Apple, Shopify and DoorDash are gone. That rule is why. Top 10 online shopping sites in the world Ranked by monthly website visits in July 2026, the top 10 online shopping sites in the world are Amazon, Temu, AliExpress, Walmart, eBay, Etsy, Rakuten, Shein, Coupang and Ozon. Every figure below comes from one source on one metric in one month: Semrush Traffic Analytics, total monthly website visits, July 2026. Nothing else is used to order this list. Rank Site Owner or parent Home market Monthly visits, Jul 2026 1 Amazon (amazon.com) Amazon.com, Inc. (Nasdaq AMZN) United States 2.42B 2 Temu (temu.com) PDD Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq PDD) China origin, United States is the largest market at 38.87% of visits 1.25B 3 AliExpress (aliexpress.com) Alibaba Group China, cross-border 699.81M 4 Walmart (walmart.com) Walmart Inc. (NYSE WMT) United States 562.88M 5 eBay (ebay.com) eBay Inc. (Nasdaq EBAY) United States, global 556.74M 6 Etsy (etsy.com) Etsy, Inc. (Nasdaq ETSY) United States, global 372.66M 7 Rakuten (rakuten.co.jp) Rakuten Group, Inc. (TSE 4755) Japan, 97.31% of visits 347.66M 8 Shein (shein.com) Shein Group, HQ Singapore, listed Hong Kong 00625 Global, China supply chain 321.71M 9 Coupang (coupang.com) Coupang, Inc. (NYSE CPNG) South Korea, 94.31% of visits 253.78M 10 Ozon (ozon.ru) Ozon Holdings Russia 230.94M Ranked by total monthly website visits, Semrush Traffic Analytics, July 2026, data updated 12 August 2026. One flagship domain per company. Web visits only, app traffic is not counted. For store owners Run a store? Benchmark it against these ten. Every shopper lands on your site with habits built on the sites above. Our free CRO audit shows where your store falls short of them on search, delivery promises, returns and mobile checkout. Get my free CRO audit See what to match and what to ignore Ozon takes tenth place on the metric, not on usefulness Ozon holds the tenth slot because the metric puts it there. It drew 230.94M monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics. Almost none of that audience is reachable by a US or EU brand. We are leaving it in anyway, because a ranking you edit for comfort is not a ranking. Quietly swapping in a friendlier name is what most pages on this query do. You cannot check a list that has been tidied for taste. Just outside the top 10 Flipkart and Mercado Libre are the two near-misses most likely to matter to you. Flipkart drew 224.37M monthly visits in July 2026, with 94.36% of them from India. Walmart has majority-owned Flipkart since 2018, so two rows in that table share a parent. Mercado Libre drew 221.18M visits in the same month and leads Brazil and Latin America. Both are more useful to most readers of this page than the tenth-placed site. Any plan that leans on a single one of them carries real marketplace dependency risk . Why Amazon’s country storefronts are counted separately Amazon.com’s 2.42B does not include amazon.de, amazon.in or amazon.co.uk. Semrush counts each country domain on its own, and so does this table. In July 2026 amazon.de drew 435.13M visits, amazon.in 299.59M and amazon.co.uk 276.46M. Amazon.fr had 174.16M, amazon.ca 170.97M and amazon.es 166.61M. Three of those would rank inside this top 10 by themselves. Stacking them into one row would make Amazon look bigger and the comparison worse. 1. Amazon The largest online store in the world, Amazon offers exceptional customer service and an amazing selection. What began as an online bookstore has evolved into a one-stop store for cloud computing services, apparel, electronics, and food. It is through features such as one-click ordering, fast delivery through Prime, and AI-driven recommendations that Amazon is thriving. The Amazon Marketplace is an access platform to millions of customers and is a superpower for eCommerce entrepreneurs. 2. Temu Temu is the second most-visited shopping site on earth, at 1.25B monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics. Its parent is PDD Holdings Inc., Nasdaq PDD, which also owns Pinduoduo. Temu began commercial operations in 2022, per PDD Holdings’ Form 20-F. Reaching half of Amazon’s web traffic inside four years is the fastest build on this page by a wide margin. The United States is its largest market at 38.87% of visits, and that is the part operators keep missing. For a US brand, Temu is not a China story. It is a price-anchor story. If your category has a cheap equivalent on Temu, your customers have already seen it. That does not mean you compete on price. It means your product page has to justify the gap. 3. AliExpress AliExpress is a well-known brand that enables you to purchase goods at a reasonable cost anywhere globally. It also offers exceptional cross-border trade since it links buyers and sellers from other nations, frequently directly from manufacturers. This makes it perfect for dropshipping and entering foreign markets because the firms can source goods at cheaper prices. Overall, AliExpress is a household name in international eCommerce because of the variety of products, cost-effectiveness, and shipping convenience. 4. Walmart Walmart has significantly marked eCommerce through seamless online and offline shopping integration. Known for its “Everyday Low Prices,” Walmart uses the extensive network of its physical stores to enhance digital offerings. The features like free curbside pickup, next-day delivery, and integration with Walmart+ have made it the favorite among value-conscious shoppers. Walmart’s marketplace opens up a wide consumer base for sellers, thus making them benefit from a household name, but with the trust intact. 5. eBay eBay is popular for its auction-style and peer-to-peer sales. Here, one can find a platform for both individuals and businesses. From rare collectibles to everyday things, eBay connects buyers and sellers worldwide. Its notable features include flexible pricing models, an auction or “Buy It Now,” strong seller tools, and a straightforward interface for small businesses. For eCommerce businesses, eBay is the go-to marketplace for reaching niche audiences and building loyal customer bases. 6. Etsy Etsy is an online go-to for artisans, crafters, and collectors. The marketplace focuses on individuality and handmade, vintage, and rare items. This allows a small business and independent creator to connect with an international audience with a passion for unique, one-of-a-kind items. For the eCommerce entrepreneur, Etsy has tools that help in branding, inventory management , and analytics to scale without losing authenticity. It also encourages a sense of community through its seller forums and offers guidance and support for navigating the world of online retail. 7. Rakuten Rakuten is Japan’s marketplace, and describing it as a cashback programme is a United States view of a Japanese company. Rakuten.co.jp drew 347.66M monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics. 97.31% of that traffic comes from Japan. It is the most domestically concentrated site in this top 10, and still the seventh most-visited shopping site in the world. Rakuten Group, Inc. trades in Tokyo as 4755. The marketplace sits alongside banking, mobile and travel businesses, and one loyalty currency runs across all of them. The lesson for an operator is not the points programme. It is that a single-country marketplace can outrank global brands on traffic, which is worth holding in mind when you compare top eCommerce platforms for a market entry. 8. Shein Shein has brought a storm to the fashion world by offering affordable fashion products while being driven by the trend. Their model creates designs and produces items directly based on real-time consumer information, ensuring whatever they make is in fashion. Its aggressive digital marketing, mainly through social influencers, has brought Shein to international stardom. Shein has drawn in younger audiences while maintaining customer loyalty by concentrating on direct-to-consumer sales and adopting a mobile-first approach. 9. Coupang Coupang is South Korea’s dominant shopping site, at 253.78M monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics. Coupang, Inc. trades on the NYSE as CPNG. 94.31% of that traffic comes from South Korea. It is the second most concentrated entry in this top 10 and still one of the largest shopping sites in the world. Coupang’s own fulfilment network is the reason it holds the market. Overnight delivery is the default expectation for Korean shoppers, not a paid upgrade. That matters outside Korea too. Delivery expectations set in one market do not stay there, and a two-day promise reads slow to a shopper used to next morning. 10. Ozon Ozon takes tenth place with 230.94M monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics. It is Russia’s largest marketplace and is operated by Ozon Holdings. For most readers of this page it is not a sales channel. Payments, logistics and sanctions rule it out for a US or EU brand. So why is it here? Because the metric puts it here, and the whole point of stating a metric is that you then follow it. Treat Ozon as a scale reference, not an opportunity. A regional marketplace can be enormous on traffic and irrelevant to your commercial plan. Why the biggest sellers are missing from this list The biggest sellers are missing because this ranking counts website visits, and Chinese commerce happens almost entirely inside apps. Taobao, Tmall, JD.com and Pinduoduo move enormous volumes of goods and barely register on a web panel. This is not a rounding error. It is the difference between looking like a regional player and being one of the largest retailers on earth. What the traffic numbers say about Taobao, Tmall and JD.com Taobao showed about 60.78M monthly web visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, at global rank 679. That is less web traffic than a mid-sized US retailer. The readings for jd.com at about 20.33M and tmall.com at about 18.25M are low confidence. Both came back as June figures rather than clean July ones, and Semrush’s China panel coverage is thin. Use those two numbers for one purpose only, which is to show the size of the gap. They are not JD’s audience and they are not Tmall’s. Pinduoduo has almost no consumer web storefront to measure at all. Why a web-visit panel cannot see app-first commerce A web-visit panel measures browser sessions, and the panels say so themselves. Wikipedia’s methodology note on its most-visited-websites list states that these rankings “do not account for app traffic”. Chinese shopping is app-first by default, so the panel is pointed at the wrong surface. The mobile commerce statistics behind that shift show the same pattern spreading well outside China. Taobao shows 60.78M monthly web visits. JD.com booked US$187.2B in net revenues in FY2025, per its investor release of 5 March 2026. Those two facts describe one market, and only one of them measures what people assume it measures. This limitation applies to the table above on this page. It ranks by web visits because that is the only metric available on the same basis for all ten sites. That same choice is why four of the largest sellers on earth are not in it. Read the ten as the most-visited shopping websites, not as the biggest sellers. No other page answering this query says that out loud. At least one makes it worse. It lists app users for one site beside web visits for another. Those are not the same measure. A ranking that admits what it cannot see is worth more than one that does not. That is the only reason to trust the ten above. The same companies by disclosed revenue instead This table switches metric completely. It reports company-disclosed figures from annual results and regulatory filings, not website visits. Read it as a second view, not a correction of the first. It is not comparable with the visit figures and it is not what the ranking on this page is based on. Company Figure Period Source Amazon Net sales US$716.9B FY2025 Amazon Form 10-K, SEC, filed February 2026 JD.com Net revenues US$187.2B FY2025 JD.com investor release, 5 March 2026 Walmart Global eCommerce sales US$150.4B FY2026 Walmart FY26 annual report, April 2026 eBay GMV US$79.6B FY2025 eBay Q4 and FY2025 results, February 2026 Mercado Libre GMV US$65B FY2025 MercadoLibre Q4 and FY2025 results PDD Holdings (Temu and Pinduoduo) Revenues US$61.75B FY2025 PDD Holdings Form 20-F, SEC Shein Net revenue US$41.8B FY2025 Disclosed in the Hong Kong listing process, reported 1 September 2026 Coupang Net revenues US$34.5B FY2025 Coupang Q4 2025 results, 26 February 2026 Company-reported figures from annual results and regulatory filings. Fiscal years differ by company. Net sales, net revenues and gross merchandise value are different measures and are not comparable with each other, or with the visit figures above. This table is not used to rank this list. What changes when you switch metric Two things. JD.com appears at all, having been absent from the visits table entirely. Temu’s parent, PDD Holdings, sits well down the order rather than second. Be careful reading straight down the Figure column. Net sales, net revenues and GMV are three different things, and stacking them into one league table is the error this page exists to avoid. The practical takeaway is simple. Traffic tells you where attention is, filings tell you where money is, and the two lists are not the same list. Traffic is not your problem Traffic shows where attention is. Your own data shows where you lose it. If your store gets visits but not orders, the leak is usually in search, product pages or checkout. We will find it, free. Audit my store Regional and category leaders worth knowing These sites are not in the global top 10 and none of them is close. They are here because each one owns a category or a market well enough to set customer expectations inside it. Read the group as category leaders, not as a continuation of the ranking. They are grouped by what they sell: big-box retail, home and pets, beauty, electronics, and resale. Where a company fact could not be confirmed against a primary source, this page describes what the site sells and stops there. That restraint is deliberate, and it is why some entries carry no numbers at all. Target Target embraced digital transformation, emphasizing customer convenience features, including app-based shopping, same-day delivery, and curbside pickup options, that make it stand out among the best in omnichannel retail. With a balance between affordable prices and trendy product lines, Target keeps appeal among various demographics. Target is an online retailer looking to increase sales and client loyalty using technology and customer-focused tactics. Wayfair Wayfair is far superior to the competition in terms of furnishings and interior design. Its extensive collection includes both high-end and low-cost styles. Its user-friendly interface and interactive features, like 3D room planners and augmented reality previews , let customers picture things in their homes. The delivery and assembly services offered by Wayfair guarantee prompt arrival and assist in eliminating the hassles involved in handling large objects. Chewy Chewy has changed the face of how pet owners shop for their pets. With its superb customer service, Chewy provides extra miles of personalized touch through handwritten cards and product suggestions that cater to each customer’s needs. The subscription model ensures regular delivery of pet essentials and allows pet owners to shop easily. Chewy’s customer-first strategy can be learned from these eCommerce businesses. Its proactive assistance, easy returns, and round-the-clock customer service show how building an emotional bond can result in enduring success and loyalty. Sephora The foundation of Sephora’s supremacy in the cosmetics sector is innovation. Their strong internet presence is complemented by an engaging mobile application and an excellent social media approach. Features like virtual try-ons and AI-driven skincare consultations help customers make the most informed decisions while purchasing from the comfort of their homes. In a way, Sephora exemplifies how technology can be woven with personalization for an eCommerce business . Its “Beauty Insider” loyalty program is another great example of how reward systems can encourage repeat purchases and create community among customers. StockX StockX is like a stock exchange for collectibles, streetwear, and footwear. Similar to buying and selling stocks, the site features a unique bidding system that allows buyers and sellers to negotiate at real-time prices. Also, every product sold on this platform is authenticated, bringing trust to its audience. By catering to a niche audience, this innovative approach for eCommerce proves that specialized platforms can find success by addressing specific customer passions. ThredUp ThredUp has become a market leader in used clothing with a growing consciousness about going green. It allows sellers to list their pre-worn clothing, giving a window to quality items for less price-conscious buyers. With increasing trends in circular economies, sustainability helps ThredUp compete against other secondhand sales. A clean interface and extensive catalog make their website accessible and desirable for an expansive audience, proving that second-hand also becomes chic, scalable, and desirable. Zappos Known as the destination of choice for shoes, Zappos is an industry leader in merging niche expertise with unbeatable customer service. This “WOW” philosophy shows through their lenient return policies, 24/7 customer support, and quick shipping. For any eCommerce business, Zappos offers a master class in building brand loyalty through focusing on customer satisfaction and specialization. Newegg For technology fanatics, Newegg is like a mine of gold. It features electronics and computer parts coupled with its gaming gear. The store has generated a devoted niche following for buying tech-related things, offering businesses an opportunity with seller programs, a focused audience, and marketing techniques such as daily deals. Its emphasis on product-depth information and reviews from experts is what has separated the company from most others selling in niche marketplaces. Best Buy One feature of this site that stands out is its smoothness between the online and in-store buying experience. The site lets consumers browse products online and have them shipped to their local Best Buy within hours, creating an eCommerce experience that brings a brick-and-mortar immediacy. For eCommerce brands, Best Buy is a model example of how to offer flexibility and convenience. Its value is added through its tech support services, especially the Geek Squad, which has further created loyal customers returning both for products and expertise. What this means for your store None of these sites is your competitor, and every one of them is your benchmark. Your customers arrive on your product page carrying habits built on Amazon, Temu and Coupang. Search that finds things. Delivery dates that are specific. Returns that are not a negotiation. Pages every shopper can use, which an ADA and WCAG accessibility audit will confirm. That is a build problem, not a marketing one. You cannot message your way past a checkout that takes six steps. If the checkout is the problem, a focused ecommerce website redesign will fix it faster than another campaign. Which expectations are actually worth matching Not all of them. Copying Amazon’s fulfilment promise on a US$5M catalogue will drain your margin long before it converts anyone. The ones worth matching are the cheap ones. Accurate stock counts, honest delivery windows, and a search box that finds your own products are configuration and data problems, not capital projects. A free CRO audit is a quick way to see which of these fixes your store is still missing. The ones worth ignoring are the ones funded by scale you do not have. Free returns on bulky goods is the usual trap. When the answer is your platform, not your team Sometimes the gap is not effort. If your platform cannot hold customer-specific pricing or ship a usable mobile checkout, no amount of tuning fixes it. Grocery and specialty food sellers hit this wall often, which is why we compared the leading ecommerce platforms for food and beverage brands . That is the point to work through the eCommerce platform selection factors properly, before anyone writes code. For most growing brands, that comparison starts with Shopify vs WooCommerce . Most replatforming regret starts with skipping that step. If the decision lands on a move, treat shopping cart migration as a data and URL problem first, and a design project second. Plan it in that order and you keep the rankings you already have. Want to build a store like these? If you are planning a store of your own, the platform you pick shapes everything above. Virtina builds on WooCommerce , Magento , BigCommerce and Shopify , and also delivers B2B ecommerce development . Choosing how customers pay? Read our guide to payment gateway service providers . Five-minute self check Score your store on five marketplace expectations Give your store one point for each line you can honestly tick. 1 Search that finds your own products Pass if your ten most common search terms return the right product first.2 Specific delivery dates Pass if the product page shows a real arrival window, not a vague range of business days.3 Returns that are not a negotiation Pass if the policy fits in three lines and is linked from every product page.4 A mobile checkout that works Pass if a first-time buyer can pay on a phone without creating an account.5 Accurate stock counts Pass if no customer can buy something you cannot ship. Scored below four? Send us your store URL and we will show you which fixes to make first. Score my store for free Which of these sounds like your store? Pick the closest match and we will point you to the right next step. My platform is the limit It cannot hold customer pricing or ship a usable mobile checkout. Plan the move before anyone writes code. Plan a replatform → My pages and checkout are the limit The platform is fine, but shoppers drop out between product page and payment. See redesign options → I am not sure what the limit is Get a free review of your store that shows where orders are leaking. Get the free CRO audit → People also ask Is Temu bigger than Amazon? No. Temu drew 1.25B monthly web visits in July 2026 against Amazon’s 2.42B, on Semrush Traffic Analytics. On money the gap is far wider. PDD Holdings, Temu’s parent, reported US$61.75B in FY2025 revenues in its SEC Form 20-F, against US$716.9B in net sales in Amazon’s FY2025 Form 10-K. Temu is much closer to Amazon on attention than on revenue. Is Amazon bigger than Alibaba? It depends which metric you use, and both answers are sourced. Amazon reported US$716.9B in net sales for FY2025 in its Form 10-K, several times Alibaba’s group revenue for its financial year ended 31 March 2026. Alibaba’s own Form 20-F states that Alibaba is the largest retail commerce business in the world by gross merchandise value. So Amazon leads on reported revenue and Alibaba claims the lead on GMV. Anyone giving you a single answer is picking a metric without telling you. Which is the number 1 online shopping site in the world? Amazon, on both metrics this page uses. Amazon.com drew 2.42B monthly visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, roughly double the second-placed site. Separately, Amazon reported US$716.9B in net sales for FY2025 in its Form 10-K. No other company on this page is close on either measure. One caveat: that visit figure counts amazon.com alone, not amazon.de, amazon.in or any other country storefront. What is the biggest online shopping site in China? Alibaba’s marketplaces, Taobao and Tmall, on the company’s own account. Alibaba’s Form 20-F states it is the largest retail commerce business in the world by gross merchandise value. JD.com is the largest of the Chinese players here by disclosed revenue, at US$187.2B for FY2025 in its investor release of 5 March 2026. None of them looks large on web traffic. Taobao showed about 60.78M monthly web visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, because Chinese shopping happens inside apps. Conclusion The honest answer to this question is a list plus a caveat. The list, by monthly web visits in July 2026, is Amazon, Temu, AliExpress, Walmart, eBay, Etsy, Rakuten, Shein, Coupang and Ozon. The caveat is that web panels cannot see app-first commerce. Four of the largest sellers on earth are missing from this ranking, and from every ranking built the same way. Most pages answering this query publish a number with no caveat, or a caveat with no number. Either one is easy on its own. Doing both is the actual work. Use the ranking for what it is good for. It tells you which platforms set the expectations your customers arrive with, which is a build and a fulfilment question for you, not a marketing one. Do not use it as a league table of retail size, because it is not one. This page is due for its next data refresh in March 2027, when these July 2026 figures will be old enough to say so. Frequently asked questions What metric ranks the sites on this page? One metric only: total monthly website visits, Semrush Traffic Analytics, July 2026, with the data last updated on 12 August 2026. Each domain was read from the same panel in the same month. No other measure is used to set the order. Why is Taobao not in the top 10? Because it is measured on the wrong surface. Taobao showed about 60.78M monthly web visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, while almost all of its actual shopping happens inside its app. Web-visit panels do not count app traffic, so Taobao, Tmall, JD.com and Pinduoduo are understated by every ranking of this type. Why were Apple, Shopify and DoorDash removed from this list? They fail a stated inclusion rule. This page counts shopping destinations only, so commerce software, single-brand manufacturer stores and food delivery are all out. The same rule keeps samsung.com out, and it drew 407.2M visits in July 2026 on Semrush Traffic Analytics, more than Etsy. Where do Flipkart and Mercado Libre rank? Eleventh and twelfth on the same metric. Flipkart drew 224.37M monthly visits in July 2026, with 94.36% from India, and it has been majority-owned by Walmart since 2018. Mercado Libre drew 221.18M in the same month across Brazil and Latin America. Is Shein a public company? Yes, since 1 September 2026. Shein listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under code 00625, having moved its headquarters to Singapore in 2022. It disclosed FY2025 net revenue of US$41.8B during that listing process. Is Ozon relevant to a US or EU brand? Almost certainly not as a sales channel. Ozon holds tenth place on the metric with 230.94M monthly visits in July 2026, but payments, logistics and sanctions rule it out for most Western brands. It stays in the table because the ranking follows the stated metric rather than convenience. Why is Amazon’s total not combined with amazon.de and amazon.in? Because the rule is one flagship domain per company, applied to everyone. Semrush counts country storefronts separately, and in July 2026 amazon.de drew 435.13M visits, amazon.in 299.59M and amazon.co.uk 276.46M. Three of those would rank inside this top 10 on their own. Building a store like these? Most stores on this list started on a platform and grew from there. Pick the one that fits your catalog, budget and growth plans, and see how our team can help you build on it. WooCommerce Flexible, open and fully yours on WordPress.
