title: eCommerce Stats Of The Year
headings: Top eCommerce Stats Of The Year
⇨ 2.71 Billion People Do Online Shopping In 2024
⇨ 20.1% Online Purchases Will Be Made In 2024
⇨ By 2024, the Global Online Retail Market Will Be Worth Over $6.3 Trillion
⇨ The Rate Of Cart Abandonment On Average, Is 70.19%
⇨ When Buying Stuff Online, Pretty Much Everyone (99%) Looks At Reviews.
⇨ Increase In Online Shopping Via Mobile Phones
⇨ Apple Pay Holds A 6.21% Market Share In Online Payments.
⇨ Businesses Without Mobile-Friendly Websites See 52% Less User Engagement.
text: Summary Keeping up with the recent eCommerce stats can help you craft innovative strategies and boost customer satisfaction, paving the way for your online business to grow and thrive. This blog contains the trending online shopping stats to help you make decisions that match online shoppers’ shifting preferences. You can use this data to develop a flexible and creative business strategy, stand out from your competitors, and establish a strong brand image. eCommerce has recently transformed marketing practices by encouraging positive customer shopping habits and brand interactions.  This change in the eCommerce marketplace has created a fast-paced and complex environment where businesses must upgrade themselves accordingly.  This blog will discuss the most recent eCommerce data and examine a wide range of statistics that will help you with your business or marketing plan, from market share and growth estimates to customer behavior, resulting in improved sales and profit. Table of Contents Key Components Of eCommerce Top eCommerce Stats Of The Year Customer Behavior Of Online Shoppers Mobile eCommerce Stats Key Components Of eCommerce There are certain fundamental key components in eCommerce that are essential for business success. Hence, businesses must know the tactics to use these components appropriately to meet their goals. ⇨   Customer Experience Businesses must provide seamless browsing and checkout processes for better customer experience.  For instance: Offering flexible ordering options to the buyers whether they want to order online or pick their products from the store. Adding features like product searches, responsive customer service, and easy website navigation. Ensuring consistent consumer experience on all digital channels. ⇨   Data Analytics Data analytics help eCommerce platforms gather substantial data about customer behavior in real time.  Companies can use this data to personalize and optimize their product offerings to strengthen business-customer relationships. ⇨   Digital Payments There are multiple digital payment options available that support eCommerce transactions and allow customers to place orders without any restrictions.  Hence, a company must include third-party payment and integration systems, including cryptocurrencies, credit cards, digital wallets like ApplePay, and other internet-based payment options. ⇨   Logistics An efficient logistics and supply chain ensures that the ordered products reach customers on time, fostering smoother operations and higher customer satisfaction.  Employing an orderly system, such as the drop-shipping model, wherein products go directly from suppliers to customers, increases delivery speed.  Incorporating IoT (Internet of Things) into manufacturing facilities further improves order accuracy and efficiency, ensuring that products are prepared and dispatched quickly. ⇨   Security A secure online store ensures safe transactions and protects sensitive customer information.  Businesses can safeguard financial and personal data using payment gateways, secure login methods, and secure socket layer (SSL) encryption. Top eCommerce Stats Of The Year To sell online, you must understand your target market, including its size, demographics, and expectations for success. You also need to know which technological platforms will be most beneficial to you.  Keeping up with eCommerce trends is crucial. It helps you figure out where to put your efforts, how to use your money, and how to expand your company. This knowledge impacts your choices about investing time and resources to grow your business. This knowledge significantly impacts your company’s future direction and success.  Let’s find some eCommerce stats for the year: ⇨   2.71 Billion People Do Online Shopping In 2024 By 2024, 33% of all consumers—2.71 billion individuals worldwide—will purchase online. With increased Internet users, experts expect 2.77 billion eCommerce users globally by 2025.  Source: Oberlo ⇨   20.1% Online Purchases Will Be Made In 2024 Online sales are projected to account for 22.6% of total purchases by 2027. The percentage of purchases completed online has increased by roughly 0.32% annually on average since 2021. Source: eMarketer , Oberlo ⇨   By 2024, the Global Online Retail Market Will Be Worth Over $6.3 Trillion Global eCommerce sales are expected to reach $8 trillion in 2027, rising 7.8% from 2024.  This growth rate is over double that of physical stores. This pattern indicates that eCommerce is becoming a more lucrative revenue generation for companies worldwide. Source:   eMarketer Customer Behavior Of Online Shoppers Let’s explore the amount of internet buyers and their purchasing habits. These insights will assist companies in developing informed plans to target consumers more effectively. ⇨   60% Of Purchases Begin Online Google, social media, and other online resources are the starting point for 63% of retail purchases. Furthermore, roughly 50% of customers who start their shopping in-store eventually look into online options. Source: Zippia ⇨   The Rate Of Cart Abandonment On Average, Is 70.19% Mobile users ditch their carts the most, about 85.65% of the time. Desktop users are just a little behind, abandoning carts 73.07% of the time. People buying jewelry and stuff for their homes and cars are the worst at leaving things in their online shopping carts. But folks shopping for groceries and gadgets tend to follow through more often. ⇨   When Buying Stuff Online, Pretty Much Everyone (99%) Looks At Reviews. Almost all shoppers (99%) check out what others say before buying online. Most of them (96%) also specifically look for bad reviews.  49% of consumers place equal faith in online reviews and personal recommendations from friends and family. This means that online reviews can make or break a product. Source: TrustPulse ⇨   Free Shipping Attracts 50.6% Of Online Shoppers The second most motivating factor for people to shop online is savings and coupons (39.3%). Furthermore, 33.2% of consumers believe the ease of returning things is another reason they shop online. Source: Oberlo Mobile eCommerce Stats Mobile commerce is growing due to smartphones’ widespread adoption and ease of use. According to statistics, mobile phones are the most widely used device for online shopping worldwide. Let’s examine some further data regarding mobile commerce. ⇨   Increase In Online Shopping Via Mobile Phones The majority of people rely on their smartphones every day. 91% of people use it whenever they want to make an online purchase, regardless of whether they have an Android, Apple, or other device.  Ensuring your website functions and looks great on mobile devices is almost as critical as ensuring your desktop purchasing experience is flawless. Source: RetailBoss ⇨   Apple Pay Holds A 6.21% Market Share In Online Payments. Apple Pay dominates the mobile wallet market but is a small fish in the bigger pond of online payments.  PayPal leads the market, handling 56.55% of online payments. Stripe comes in second, processing 20.94% of online transactions.  With a 4.19% market share and 3.26% percent of online payments, Authorize.net and Google Pay are ranked first and third behind Apple Pay. Source: Money Transfers ⇨   Businesses Without Mobile-Friendly Websites See 52% Less User Engagement. If your website, app, or product doesn’t adapt to mobile devices, you risk losing half your users.  You could also miss out on at least 25% of potential customers, given that mobile devices now generate over half of all internet traffic in the US. Source: Zippia

title: Direct-To-Consumer Explained: A Complete Guide
headings: The D2C model allows you to maintain larger profit margins by eliminating middlemen, reducing distribution and marketing costs, and allowing for greater pricing control and operational efficiency.
How To Start A D2C Business
Effective Strategies To Improve D2C Marketing Approach
⇨ Boost Your Credibility With Positive Reviews
text: Summary The Direct-to-Consumer movement is less of an industry trend and more of a shift in how customers and businesses engage with each other.  With D2C, customers can now fully experience more honesty and authenticity, while businesses can get a deep understanding of their market needs and customer preferences. Use these factors and the strategies mentioned above and tailor them according to your business needs and transform your marketing strategy to a profitable one. While third-party collaboration might offer some benefits to the retailers, it is not the sole factor in building a successful brand. Instead, you can go for Direct-to-consumer (DTC or D2C) if you want flexibility and independence without any third party getting in the way.  D2C allows companies to maintain end-to-end control over business operations and offer products at lower prices than brands using traditional retail business models. It also eliminates the need for mediators and fosters a strong brand-to-customer relationship. With the digital marketplace rapidly rising, it is the perfect time to launch a D2C brand that will succeed by setting itself apart from competitors instead of merging with them. Let’s find out more about D2C and its strategies. Table of Contents What Is A Direct-To-Consumer Approach? Benefits Of D2C Model Challenges With D2C Approach How To Start A D2C Business Effective Strategies To Improve D2C Marketing Approach What Is A Direct-To-Consumer Approach? Direct-to-consumer (D2C) marketing refers to a business model or approach where products are sold directly to customers without intermediaries.In traditional retail, items are passed via several mediators before being purchased by customers. The manufacturer is typically the point of origin, followed by the distributor, wholesaler, and retailer. On the other hand, D2C products are created, advertised, sold, and delivered directly from the company to the customer.While some businesses use their stores for direct sales, others prefer online platforms where they can connect directly with consumers through their eCommerce platforms. These platforms make shopping, purchasing, and brand engagement happen all in one place. Benefits Of D2C Model There are several reasons to choose a direct sales strategy.  Here are some of the benefits: Maximum Profit The D2C model allows you to maintain larger profit margins by eliminating middlemen, reducing distribution and marketing costs, and allowing for greater pricing control and operational efficiency.  The additional profit can be reinvested into the business to finance new product development or pay for last-mile delivery costs. Customer-Centric Approach D2C businesses benefit from having direct access to client opinions, tastes, and buying patterns, which help them accurately meet customer demands.  Using this essential data, they can improve the entire client journey, customize offerings, and improve products. Better Pricing Competitive pricing is the main reason many people purchase directly from brands, as it offers better value by eliminating retailer markups and intermediary costs.  Brands that sell directly to consumers (D2C) can set their prices without being constrained by the usual markups associated with traditional channels.  Due to their independence, they can develop and improve pricing strategies to suit their customers’ requirements and tastes. Speedy Marketing Process D2C brands have a significant edge in quickly getting their products on the market as they bypass traditional retail channels and directly respond to consumer demands, streamlining the production and distribution process.  This flexibility shortens the time it takes to develop a product and gives D2C firms more immediate control over their marketing and consumer connections. Challenges With D2C Approach Although D2C strategies offer numerous benefits, they also present distinct challenges.  It’s essential to consider these carefully when deciding the most suitable approach for your business. High Competition The emergence of D2C models has caused a significant change in business tactics in recent years.  These days, most consumer companies use D2C in some way, making it a fiercely competitive market that is particularly difficult for new businesses. Acquisition Cost Acquiring new customers can be a hefty expense for D2C businesses as it is challenging to gain consumer trust, especially when established brands already have a competitive advantage.  This hurdle often confronts newer or less recognized D2C brands aiming to build credibility.  Moreover, the necessity of substantially investing in marketing, advertising, and client acquisition can directly influence business profitability. How To Start A D2C Business Do you have a spark of inspiration for a product but need help determining where to begin?  Here are our top 7 tips to help you launch your idea successfully. Choose The Right Platform Select a platform that aligns with both your immediate needs and long-term ambitions. Consider how comfortable you are with managing a website and how much you’re willing to invest in your brand’s growth. Set Up Your Online Shop Get the essentials in place, such as your merchant account , payment processor, and shipping services. Take high-quality product photos and craft compelling descriptions. Your online shop should be organized and user-friendly for better customer engagement. Spread The Word Make sure people are updated about the product availability. Use social media, newsletters, paid ads, SEO, influencer partnerships, and customer referrals to attract attention and drive sales. Master The Logistics Smooth operational features that guarantee on-time delivery and cut expenses, such as effective shipping, careful packaging, and simplified inventory management, directly impact consumer satisfaction and business profitability.  Mastering these processes is essential for maintaining competitive edge and customer loyalty. Secure Financing Building a robust online presence requires time and investment. Strategize your funding options, whether using personal savings, seeking outside investors, or exploring innovative methods like cryptocurrency. Develop Your Brand Identity Determine what makes your brand unique. This includes your logo, style, tone, and overall attitude. Distinguishing yourself from the competition is critical, and can be done by fostering customer loyalty with personalized experiences, outstanding service, and transparent interactions. Effective Strategies To Improve D2C Marketing Approach Unlike traditional brands, D2C brands depend on solid marketing strategies. They prioritize top-of-the-funnel branding efforts to launch their products successfully and sustain growth over time.  Here are some key tactics that top DTC brands employ to design highly effective marketing campaigns. ⇨ Boost Your Credibility With Positive Reviews According to 98% of buyers , reviews are a crucial tool for decision-making when making purchases. This shows how critical reviews are for a successful business.  Positive reviews significantly affect new leads and first-time visitors to your website. Therefore, you must collect and share customer reviews on your website, social media, and other relevant platforms, as this helps boost your brand’s credibility. ⇨ Implement SEO Being present across all channels where prospects search for products is basic to building a successful direct-to-consumer brand.  This can be done quickly by incorporating SEO and PPC into your ad campaign. Start by identifying the search terms people use to find similar businesses or competitors. Then, you can use the mentioned words in your ad text and website content. ⇨ Chatbots Chatbots are essential as it is impossible to manually pay attention to and resolve customer queries at any time.  Chatbots can help provide an instant solution for your customers, regardless of the time. While a chatbot cannot replace human interaction’s effectiveness, it will fill the void and ensure that customers always get the help they need, even when your representatives are unavailable. ⇨ Have A Unique Selling Point Every business should develop a USP that can make them more competitive than the well-established competitors.  Giving consumers a solid reason to choose your brand is essential when selling goods to them directly, and that’s what a USP does to your brand.  Ensure that your brand has some strong USPs to offer such as excellent product quality, exceptional customer service, competitive pricing and a strong brand identity that resonates with your target audience.

title: 11 Best WooCommerce Payment Gateways
headings: What Is A WooCommerce Payment Gateway?
Tips To Pick The Best WooCommerce Payment Gateway
text: Summary WooCommerce payment gateways are essential to any WordPress-based online business. It’s a perfect solution to payment processing because customers can pay fast and easily for goods and services on a website. Consequently, you can significantly expand your activity globally and lower the percentage of abandoned carts on your WordPress website. Pay attention to providers who share your company’s growth objectives, essential features, and target market.  You can also use the tips and comparisons mentioned in this blog before subscribing to any eCommerce payment gateway . In today’s fast-paced eCommerce marketplace, optimizing the proper payment gateway for your WooCommerce website is essential.  An efficient payment gateway improves user experience and conversion rates, contributing to increased sales, while a problematic one can frustrate customers and leave a poor impression on your brand image. This is why faster checkout with a quick, secure, and easy-to-use payment gateway is essential to reducing cart abandonment for more profitability in your store. Let’s review some popular WooCommerce payment gateways and compare their features to see which will work best for your business. Looking for a wider comparison? See our guide to payment gateway service providers for fees, features and supported regions. Table of Contents What Is A WooCommerce Payment Gateway? Best WooCommerce Payment Gateways Options Tips To Pick The Best WooCommerce Payment Gateway What Is A WooCommerce Payment Gateway? For every store, WooCommerce offers four payment options: PayPal standard, Direct Bank Transfer, Check, and Cash on Delivery (COD). For the first three options, you don’t need to make an online payment, and for the fourth option, customers are redirected to PayPal. You must have a good and secure payment gateway to facilitate online payments for customers using your eCommerce business. Consider it the software version of a store’s point-of-sale system that securely transfers money from the customer’s account to yours. There are more than 80 WooCommerce payment extensions available that can be quickly installed, or you can get the WordPress payment plugin immediately.  The final step is integrating it into your platform with a few easy installations and settings that require little to no coding knowledge. WooCommerce Payments WooCommerce WooCommerce Payments is an integrated payment gateway that accepts major credit and debit cards and local payment options. It features a user-friendly interface and easily syncs with your WooCommerce store. WooPayments allows you to access your store’s dashboard to manage disputes, track cash flow, and collect payments. 2. Stripe Payments Stripe supports multiple payment methods, such as local payment choices, credit cards, and debit cards. Stripe’s ability to enable rapid payouts for qualified merchants is a significant benefit. This can be especially helpful for cash flow management, implying that businesses can have their money in their bank accounts in minutes. 3. Square Square is an outstanding WooCommerce payment gateway suitable for small and medium-sized businesses. Its mobile-friendly point-of-sale solution allows retailers to process debit and credit card payments with mobile devices. It also facilitates numerous ways of collecting in-person and online payments. 4. Authorize.net Businesses can accept various payment options using Authorize.net , including all major credit cards, gift cards, signature debit cards, and eChecks. It provides solid fraud protection to help detect, handle, and stop questionable and possibly fraudulent transactions. Authorize.net guarantees prompt access to funds by automatically depositing money into the user’s merchant bank account within a few days.  The checkout procedure is easy to use, and businesses can quickly streamline the payment process for clients by adding a Buy Now or Donate button to their website. 5. PayPal PayPal is a well-known and reliable payment method that works well with WooCommerce. It offers an efficient and safe payment management system for all types of eCommerce websites. It allows one to accept credit cards, debit cards, and payments from consumers’ PayPal accounts. All it takes is an email address and a bank account. PayPal helps business people easily take payments from clients online and in-store. Before allowing access, PayPal confirms the details to ensure the legitimate owner is creating the account. As a security measure for clients, PayPal also protects purchasers who do not receive what they requested. 6. Amazon Pay Amazon Pay allows your customers to make payments easily using their Amazon accounts.  Usually, all they require for validation is your password, email address, and an active Amazon account.  One significant advantage of Amazon Pay is that customers do not need to disclose any payment information on a third-party website. Customers can create and use an Amazon Pay account for free, with Amazon as an essential intermediary between them and the online retailer. 7. Apple Pay If you have a physical store for your WooCommerce store, using Apple Pay can further improve the consumer experience. This mobile payment system helps businesses that serve a mobile-dependent clientele by managing online and offline transactions. Apple Pay enables users to make purchases with only one click, much like Amazon Pay.  The cardholder data collection process no longer requires a payment form thanks to the direct gateway. 8 . Alipay Alipay is an excellent option for your WooCommerce payment gateway if you deal with a global customer base. Alipay prioritizes security and ensures that transactions are correctly processed. Their fraud prevention package includes 90-day payment protection and a 100% recovery guarantee against fraud. Furthermore, Alipay allows users to set up auto-debits for the following transactions and supports regular checkout/cart payments. 9. Skrill  Slice 1 By integrating an online wallet and payment gateway, Skrill allows company owners to accept payments via various channels, including cryptocurrencies. Skrill offers store owners a hosted payment gateway for all transaction management. You just need to include the payment button on your checkout page, and Skrill will take care of the rest. 10 . Braintree Braintree , a subsidiary of PayPal, operates independently in many respects.  Although it can initially seem similar to Stripe, Braintree primarily offers merchant accounts. It supports numerous payment options, such as credit and debit cards, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, etc. 11. Mollie Within a very short time, Mollie has become one of the fastest-growing payment systems due to its wide array of payment alternatives. It supports various payment methods, satiating customers’ preferences, such as PayPal, Apple Pay, Klarna, major credit cards, etc. One of its best qualities is its seamless payment experience; users may finish transactions without being sent to an additional page, guaranteeing a quick and easy checkout procedure. This integration contributes to maintaining a consistent brand experience and improving customer ease. Tips To Pick The Best WooCommerce Payment Gateway Several important factors are involved when choosing a WooCommerce payment gateway.  First, consider your target market.  Select regional-specific systems or global options like Visa and MasterCard based on their preferences. Consider transaction fees, which differ depending on the location and the mode of payment.  Compare gateways to see which offers the most value for money. Ensure the gateway complies with PCI (Payment card industry) standards to safeguard client information and foster confidence.  Furthermore, to improve your store’s operation and speed and guarantee a quick and easy payment procedure, search for features like support for mobile transactions, seamless integration, and choices for recurring billing.
