text: B2B eCommerce is growing significantly fast , and the trajectory for 2023 seems more promising than ever. More and more companies are now taking their B2B business to the online platform. Naturally, the B2B eCommerce development is also undergoing rapid changes as more companies flock to the online platform.  You must keep up with these changing B2B eCommerce trends to ensure the success of your online business, especially when it comes to B2B checkouts. Some of the prominent B2B eCommerce trends in 2023 are listed below. The list below will help you ensure that your B2B eCommerce store keeps up with the competition and generate adequate conversions and profits. Moreover, the eCommerce trends listed below can significantly impact the B2B checkout process. Hence, it is vital to understand the nuances in these trends and use them to optimize the B2B checkout process.  Significantly higher rate of mobile commerce adaptation A growing number of B2B marketplaces Customer experience prioritization AI integration for enhanced B2B shopping experience More prominent use of machine learning Sustainable B2B eCommerce Widespread use of blockchain technology Sunbscription-based B2B plans Simplify your website’s B2B eCommerce checkout process Let’s Discuss 20 Tips to Simplify and Optimize B2B eCommerce Transactions in 2023 As you can see, the B2B eCommerce trend is rapidly changing. 2023 is becoming one of the most promising years for B2B eCommerce. But, you can only benefit from the rapid changes in B2B eCommerce if you prepare yourself for it. The following tips can help you simplify and optimize your B2B eCommerce transaction in 2023 using the latest tools and trends.  1. Smoother Customer Experience In 2023, customer experience precedes everything else in B2B eCommerce. Your priority should be to ensure a smoother customer experience and make the purchase journey as easy as possible. In 2023, B2B buyers expect the same shopping convenience as a B2C customer. It means ensuring an intuitive interface that enables the customer to choose the desired product specification and easy checkouts.  2. Personalized Customer Experience In the past, many B2B eCommerce store owners could ignore personalization and still make reasonable profits. However, that is no longer the case. B2B customers can get personalized product suggestions and overall customer experience from other online B2B stores. If your online B2B store fails to rise to the occasion and deliver a personalized customer experience, you may lose customers to the competition. You can provide a more personalized B2B shopping experience by assessing past purchases and other relevant customer data.  3. Mobile Device Optimization The B2B buyer no longer sits by their desk searching for B2B suppliers on their computer. Even though the B2B purchase process is more complex as there maybe be multiple stakeholders and decision-makers. Nonetheless, the initial research for B2B suppliers can often happen on mobile devices.  It would be best to prepare your B2B business for this by optimizing your store for mobile viewing. It is also not uncommon for companies to complete their B2B purchases on mobile. Hence, optimizing your B2B eCommerce store for mobile devices would be best. Your site should load quickly on mobile devices without delays and be fully functional across multiple mobile devices. 4. AI Assistants and Chatbots In 2023, AI assistants and chatbots like ChatGPT are quickly gaining popularity everywhere, including B2B eCommerce. AI-based chatbots or shopping assistants can do more than answer generic questions of the customer.  Depending on how advanced your AI solution is, it can gather information from the customer and suggest the most relevant products. Moreover, AI can work around the clock to ensure you don’t miss valuable sales. Hire an expert to create a custom AI chatbot to effectively answer all customer queries on your B2B eCommerce store. 5. Utilize Social Media Platforms to Their Full Potential Social media platforms are no longer exclusively for targeting B2C customers. They are now one of the best places to find and target B2B buyers because they also need a solid social media presence. Social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, etc., let you engage with the B2B audience more organically.  If that doesn’t work, you can always use the advanced advertising capabilities of the platforms. Most social media platforms have advanced targeting capabilities to reach the relevant audience and market your B2B business. As a result, you can boost audience engagement, promote your B2B products, and boost brand awareness. 6. Ensure Superior Payment Flexibility It is common for customers to reach as far as the payment section and abandon the cart because their desired payment method is unavailable. Such situations are more common in B2B eCommerce because they typically involve various payment methods, including credit payments. Your B2B eCommerce store should have multiple payment methods, including credit card payments. PayPal, ACH, etc., are popular payment integration choices for your B2B store. Ideally, you need an expert to ensure a seamless payment gateway integration for your website and equip it with custom capabilities. Equip your B2B eCommerce store with superior payment flexibility with the help of an expert Schedule a Free Meeting 7. Detailed and Confusion-free Product Descriptions One of the primary differences between a B2C and B2B eCommerce store is their product descriptions. With B2B products, you must provide a detailed product description as the buyer has bulk requirements. Returning a product or refunding money can be challenging because of logistics and high order value.  Additionally, endless product descriptions can have the opposite impact on the customer. Consider using tables and other formats to convey the information to customers efficiently. Besides, you should also clearly communicate the pricing to speed up the purchase decision. 8. Flexible Shipping Options To keep in line with the convenience element of online B2B transactions, you must ensure flexible shipping options for your customers. The challenging part is that B2B buyers often have highly-specific shipping requirements . For example, many B2B buyers may require expedited shipping and international delivery. Your B2B eCommerce store should be able to keep up with these needs by offering multiple shipping options. Besides, you must ensure the timely delivery of your products as it helps you build trust and cultivate loyal customers.  9. Minimize Cart Abandonment With Checkout Optimization Minimizing cart abandonment should be a priority for any eCommerce store, whether B2B or B2C business. But the thing about many online B2B stores is that they tend to complicate the checkout process trying to stuff in all the order information. As a result, it often leads to lengthy checkout processes with multiple steps/pages.  Checkout optimization involves streamlining the whole process by simplifying it as much as possible. Doing so ensures an easy checkout with minimal steps and conveys all the relevant information to the buyer. Besides, you can implement a guest checkout to boost conversions and encourage one-time or first-time purchases. 10. Setup an Advanced ERP System Your B2B ecommerce store is incomplete without an advanced ERP system, and it stops your business from growing to its full potential. An advanced ERP system can help you streamline your B2B business in several ways.  An advanced ERP system can help you optimize various aspects of your B2B business, like order processing, and minimize errors. You can also consider using a customized ERP solution for your B2B business with the help of an expert like Virtina. 11. Avoid Stock-outs and Overstocking With a Seamless Inventory Management System Another crucial aspect that can decide the success of your B2B eCommerce store is an effective inventory management system. You must implement an effective inventory management system to track products from multiple manufacturers and wholesale suppliers. Having an effective inventory management system enables you to avoid overstocking and stock-outs. You can use custom software solutions to meet your unique inventory management needs. The expert team at Virtina can help you build a custom solution and even incorporate dropshipping capabilities into your B2B eCommerce store. 12. Track and Analyze Customer Behavior Via Data Analytics It is another vital element for running a successful B2B eCommerce store . It would be best to use data analytics for all online businesses regardless of what or to whom you sell the products. Data analytics is essential to understand what your business lacks and how you can improve your online B2B business.   Effective data analytics enables you to access valuable insights to understand user behavior better. You can use the data to better cater to the B2B customer needs and implement custom functionalities to your online store. Data analytics is vital in identifying customer pain points and optimizing your eCommerce strategy .Maximize the potential of your online B2B store by implementing custom functionalities with our team of experts Contact Us 13. Provide Tiered Pricing and Volume Discounts  Selling products in bulk often requires B2B businesses to provide tiered pricing and volume discounts to attract more customers. Implementing these capabilities to your B2B eCommerce store allows you to incentivize large volume purchases and encourages return customers.  An eCommerce expert like Virtina can help you set up customized tiered pricing for your B2B eCommerce store. We can help you implement unique features and functionalities to incentivize high-volume purchases and boost average order value. 14. Build Trust and Brand Credibility With Ratings and Reviews In 2023, every B2B customer expects your wholesale online store to have customer reviews and ratings. Ideally, your website must have separate ratings and reviews for individual products and suppliers/manufacturers.  Customer ratings and reviews enable B2B customers to make better purchase decisions. Moreover, they are also vital in keeping your customers engaged and conveying critical information about the items you sell. As a result, you can effectively build trust and boost brand credibility. 15. Provide Advanced Self-Service Capabilities Self-service capabilities like customer portals are another essential feature many B2B eCommerce store owners are still sleeping on. Most B2B customers prefer access to a personalized customer portal and other self-service capabilities.  Self-service capabilities like a personalized customer portal give your B2B customers more control. As a result, the customer can quickly re-order items, access their order history, and manage account information at their convenience. 16. Build Targeted Landing Pages for Products and Promotions If you aren’t already using targeted landing pages for your products and promotions, it is high time you did. There are several benefits to using targeted landing pages for your business, including their ability to boost conversions.  Your targeted landing pages should include a clear and compelling call to action that can effectively push your customers toward conversions. Moreover, creating dedicated landing pages for specific products/promotions simplifies the purchase process for customers. 17. Execute Digital Marketing Strategies and Retargeting Ads Digital marketing strategies are just as crucial to B2B eCommerce stores as to B2C online stores. Ensure that you invest your time and money into SEO and PPC campaigns to boost traffic to your online B2B store. It enables you to increase visibility and engagement, effectively enhancing your reach to a broader audience.  Additionally, you should ensure that you use retargeting ads to target customers/visitors that abandoned your website without making a purchase. It involves targeting customers with relevant ads, encouraging them to return to your B2B eCommerce store, and completing the purchase. 18. Invest in a Strong Security System Security is a primary concern in B2B transactions because the average order value is almost always high. The last thing you want to do is compromise your system security which could potentially put your customers at risk. With cyber-crimes and ransomware increasingly hitting online businesses, you must put your customers at ease and ensure secure online transactions.  Implementing a robust security system for your B2B eCommerce system enables you to protect sensitive customer data. Besides, a secure B2B eCommerce store can help you earn customer trust and build stronger relationships with them. We can help you build a fully secure B2B eCommerce store with multiple security measures to safeguard sensitive customer data. 19. Optimize B2B Site Speed and Performance One of the things that can quickly bring down your B2B eCommerce store is its slow loading speed. B2B customers will instantly navigate away from your site if it takes more than a few seconds to load. Moreover, slow site speed can significantly impact your SEO rankings, ultimately affecting your inbound traffic.  Similarly, you must closely monitor your B2B eCommerce store’s overall performance. Speed and performance optimization is a continuous and regular process. You must regularly assess your website’s speed and performance to ensure a seamless customer experience. It is significantly easier to accomplish this with the help of an eCommerce expert like Virtina. 20. Utilize Social Proof to Establish Brand Credibility  Social proof, such as customer testimonials, establishes brand credibility and boosts customer trust. Hence, having social proof like customer testimonials and highlighting industry awards are essential for running a successful B2B eCommerce business. Use social proof on your B2B eCommerce store to boost brand credibility Talk to Experts For instance, highlighting industry awards enables customers visiting your store to ensure that yours is a reputable brand. It effectively allows you to build trust with your target audience and encourage them to collaborate with your brand. 21. Personalized B2B eCommerce Checkout  Personalization involves customizing the shopping experience to the specific needs and preferences of individual B2B buyers. Personalized content, product recommendations, and pricing can be provided by utilizing customer data and insights, creating a more relevant and engaging experience. It helps build customer loyalty, increases conversion rates, and facilitates cross-selling or upselling opportunities. 22. Email Capture for Retargeting Users Email capture refers to collecting the email addresses of B2B customers during the checkout process. You can use email capture to build a B2B customer contacts database. The database is useful for marketing initiatives, such as sending transactional emails, promotional campaigns, order updates, or nurturing leads. More importantly, email capture helps establish direct customer communication channels and facilitates ongoing customer engagement. Try including SPF verification for successful delivery of emails and to prevent email spoofing and spam. 23. Optimize Your B2B eCommerce Checkout Design  The checkout design encompasses the visual and functional aspects of the B2B eCommerce checkout process. B2B store owners must ensure their checkout design is intuitive, efficient, and optimized for conversion.  You can accomplish this by identifying and minimizing friction elements, simplifying the checkout steps, and providing clear instructions. Additionally, you must ensure the checkout design is responsive across different devices, ensuring a seamless experience for buyers on desktops, tablets, and smartphones. Final Note – The Importance of a Perfect B2B Checkout Experience We can not stretch enough how critical the checkout experience is in your B2B eCommerce store. It enables you to boost conversion rates, enhance customer experience, minimize cart abandonment, and build customer trust. Overall, having an optimized B2B checkout process is not an option but a necessity. However, optimizing your B2B checkout can be challenging, considering its unique nature. text: Summary Dropshipping lets you sell products you never stock: a customer orders from your WooCommerce store, and a supplier ships the product directly to them. It is still a workable way to start an online store in 2026, but the economics changed. The US ended duty-free de minimis imports for all countries in August 2025, so cheap China-to-US shipping now carries duties and customs processing. The stores that do well now pick a focused niche, favor suppliers with US or EU stock, price in duties and shipping from day one, and build a brand customers remember. This guide walks through each step, from niche to first sale. Introduction We first wrote this guide in 2023, when the main questions were which plugin to use and which supplier had the most products. Those still matter, but they are no longer the hard part. The hard part in 2026 is margin. Import rules, shipping times and advertising costs decide whether a dropshipping store makes money. WooCommerce helps because it is free, flexible and lets you choose any supplier or plugin, but it also means you are responsible for setup, security and updates. Here is how to do it properly, including what WooCommerce offers, the steps to launch, the suppliers worth considering, and when it makes sense to bring in help. Table of Contents What is dropshipping, and how does it work with WooCommerce? Is dropshipping still worth it in 2026? How do you start a WooCommerce dropshipping store? Which dropshipping suppliers work with WooCommerce? Why is WooCommerce a good choice for dropshipping? What are the benefits and challenges of WooCommerce dropshipping? How do you market a WooCommerce dropshipping store? When should you bring in a WooCommerce developer? People also ask Conclusion What is dropshipping, and how does it work with WooCommerce? Dropshipping is a retail model where you sell products without holding inventory. You list products in your store, set your own prices, and pass each order to a supplier who ships it to the customer. Your profit is the difference between your price and what you pay the supplier, minus fees and marketing. 1. Customer orders Pays your price 2. Your Woo store Plugin sends order 3. Supplier ships Direct to customer 4. Delivered Tracking synced Tracking number returns to the order With WooCommerce, a dropshipping plugin connects your store to one or more suppliers. It imports products, keeps prices and stock in sync, sends orders to the supplier and brings tracking numbers back. If you are new to the platform, our overview of the major features of a WooCommerce website is a useful starting point. Is dropshipping still worth it in 2026? Yes, for the right products and the right supplier setup. What changed is the cost of the cheapest route. US imports now carry duties. Duty-free de minimis treatment ended for goods from China and Hong Kong in May 2025 and for all countries on 29 August 2025. Low-value parcels now go through customs and pay the duties that apply to the product and its origin. A federal law repeals de minimis permanently from July 2027. The EU added a duty on small parcels. Since 1 July 2026, e-commerce parcels under €150 pay a flat €3 customs duty per item type, on top of VAT. Customers expect faster delivery. Two-to-four-week shipping loses sales to stores that deliver in days. What this means in practice: calculate duties and shipping into your prices, test landed costs with real orders, and consider suppliers with warehouses in the countries you sell to. Rules and duty rates have changed several times since 2025, so check current rates for your products before you commit. Sources: US Customs and Border Protection and Federal Register notices on the suspension of de minimis (2025 to 2026), and the European Commission guidance on the temporary flat duty for low-value imports. How do you start a WooCommerce dropshipping store? These seven steps take you from idea to first order. For a detailed, technical walkthrough of the WooCommerce settings, see our step-by-step WooCommerce setup for dropshipping . 1 Pick a niche 2 Choose suppliers 3 Business basics 4 Build the store 5 Plugin + products 6 Price + ship 7 Test + launch From idea to first order, in seven steps Step 1: Pick a focused niche Choose a product category you understand, with enough demand and room for a margin after duties, shipping and advertising. Narrow niches, such as gear for one sport or products for one type of pet owner, are easier to brand and cheaper to advertise than general stores. Check demand with keyword tools and marketplace best-seller lists. Avoid heavy, fragile or regulated products at first. Look for products customers buy again, or that pair well with accessories. Step 2: Choose reliable suppliers Your supplier is your warehouse, your shipping department and part of your customer service. Order samples, check delivery times to your main markets, and ask about returns and damaged items before you list anything. Compare suppliers in the section below. Step 3: Set up the business basics Register your business, open a separate bank account, and find out where you need to collect sales tax. You also need clear shipping, returns and privacy policies before launch. Rules vary by country and state, so check with an accountant or local advisor. Step 4: Build your WooCommerce store Pick reliable WordPress hosting, install WooCommerce, and choose a fast, mobile-friendly theme. Keep the design simple so product pages load quickly. If you want a distinctive look, WooCommerce theme customization or custom WooCommerce development can help you stand out from other stores selling similar products. Moving from another platform? Our WooCommerce migration team can bring your products, customers and orders across. Step 5: Add a dropshipping plugin and import products Install the plugin that matches your supplier, then import a small, curated set of products. Rewrite titles and descriptions in your own words, use your own photos where you can, and set pricing rules. We compare the options in our guide to the best WooCommerce dropshipping plugins . Step 6: Set prices, shipping and returns Price every product on landed cost: supplier price, shipping, duties, payment fees and a share of advertising. Show realistic delivery times on the product page and at checkout, and make your returns process clear, including who pays return shipping. Illustrative example: where a $40 sale goes $14 $5 $3 $8 $8.50 Supplier $14 Shipping $5 Duties $3 Fees $1.50 Ads $8 Profit $8.50 Example figures only. Your costs depend on product, supplier, destination and duty rates. Step 7: Test, secure and launch Place test orders from start to finish, including a refund. Install security basics, back up the site, and keep plugins updated. Our WooCommerce security guide covers what to set up before you take real payments. Which dropshipping suppliers work with WooCommerce? Supplier What it is Cost to use Best for AliExpress Retail marketplace with a dropshipping center No membership fee; you pay per product Testing products cheaply Alibaba B2B wholesale marketplace Varies by supplier Bulk and private-label sourcing once products are proven CJdropshipping Sourcing, warehousing and fulfillment agent No membership fee; you pay for products and fulfillment Faster shipping and branded packaging Doba US supplier marketplace From $28.67 a month US-stocked products SaleHoo Directory of vetted suppliers plus a dropship app From $9 a month billed yearly, or lifetime plans Finding vetted suppliers on a budget Worldwide Brands Directory of certified wholesalers and dropshippers One-time membership fee Authorized US wholesalers Spocket US and EU supplier marketplace From $39.99 a month Fast US and EU delivery Syncee Marketplace of suppliers in the US, Canada, EU and Australia Free plan, paid tiers available Local and niche suppliers Checked on each supplier’s website in September 2026. Prices change often, so confirm before signing up. AliExpress The largest catalog and the easiest place to test products, with no membership fee. Shipping from China to the US now includes duties, so compare landed costs carefully and look for sellers with local warehouses. Alibaba Better suited to buying in bulk or creating your own branded products once you know what sells. It is a sourcing platform first, not a dropshipping service. CJdropshipping Sources, stores and ships products for you, with warehouses in several countries and options for custom packaging. A good next step once you have proven products. Doba, SaleHoo and Worldwide Brands These help you find suppliers with stock in the US. Doba is a marketplace with monthly plans, SaleHoo combines a vetted supplier directory with a dropship app, and Worldwide Brands is a long-running directory of certified wholesalers with a one-time fee. Spocket and Syncee Both focus on suppliers close to your customers, which means faster delivery and fewer duty surprises. Each has a WooCommerce plugin. Why is WooCommerce a good choice for dropshipping? You own the store and the data WooCommerce is free and open source. There is no platform fee on each sale, and you can move hosts or change suppliers without rebuilding. Any supplier, any plugin You are not limited to one app store. Most major dropshipping tools support WooCommerce, and you can combine suppliers in one store. Flexible and customizable You control design, checkout, pricing rules and content. When a plugin cannot do what you need, WooCommerce plugin development can fill the gap. Content and SEO on the same site WordPress makes it easy to publish buying guides and blog posts that bring in search traffic, which lowers your dependence on paid ads. A large community Thousands of extensions, tutorials and developers support WooCommerce, so help is easy to find. What are the benefits and challenges of WooCommerce dropshipping? Benefits Challenges Low startup cost, with no inventory to buy Lower margins after duties, shipping and ads Large product range without warehouse space Less control over product quality Quick to test new products Delivery times depend on your supplier Full control of design and pricing You handle hosting, updates and security Run it from anywhere Supplier stock-outs and price changes Most challenges shrink with better suppliers, careful pricing and regular maintenance. How do you market a WooCommerce dropshipping store? Make the store fast and trustworthy. Quick pages, clear policies, real contact details and genuine reviews convert better than flashy design. Create content that answers buyer questions. Buying guides and comparisons bring steady search traffic. Use social media and short video. Show products in use rather than supplier photos. Work with niche creators. Small, relevant influencers often beat large accounts on cost per sale. Offer smart incentives. Free shipping thresholds and bundles protect margin better than blanket discounts. Build an email list. Welcome offers, abandoned cart reminders and restock alerts turn one-time buyers into repeat customers. When should you bring in a WooCommerce developer? Many dropshipping stores start as a DIY project. It makes sense to get help when: You add several suppliers or systems. Connecting inventory, accounting or fulfillment tools is a job for WooCommerce integration . Plugins start conflicting or slowing the site. Ongoing WooCommerce support and maintenance keeps the store stable as you grow. You need custom features. Pricing rules, checkout changes or supplier logic that no plugin offers. You are scaling. Here are the main reasons to hire a WooCommerce developer once a store takes off. Our WooCommerce experts have built and supported stores for more than 14 years. You can hire a WooCommerce developer for a single task or ongoing work, or explore our full WooCommerce development services. People also ask How much does it cost to start a WooCommerce dropshipping store? WooCommerce itself is free. Expect to pay for hosting, a domain, a theme, a dropshipping plugin and sample orders, plus a budget for advertising. Many stores launch for a few hundred dollars before marketing. Is dropshipping legal? Yes. You need to register your business where required, collect sales tax where you have obligations, follow consumer protection rules and avoid selling counterfeit or restricted products. Can I dropship from China to the US in 2026? Yes, but every order now goes through customs and may carry duties, because duty-free de minimis treatment ended in August 2025. Many sellers now use suppliers with US warehouses. Conclusion WooCommerce is still one of the best platforms for dropshipping because you control the store, the suppliers and the costs. What has changed is the math: duties, shipping speed and advertising decide profit more than ever. Start with a focused niche, choose suppliers close to your customers, price in every cost, and test before you scale. If you want help building or growing your store, talk to our team . Frequently Asked Questions What is WooCommerce dropshipping? Selling products through a WooCommerce store without holding stock. A plugin sends each order to a supplier, who ships it directly to the customer. Which plugin do I need for WooCommerce dropshipping? It depends on your supplier. See our comparison of the best WooCommerce dropshipping plugins for current prices and features. How did the end of de minimis affect dropshipping? Since 29 August 2025, low-value parcels entering the US no longer arrive duty-free. Each order goes through customs and may pay duties, which raises costs for products shipped from overseas. How long does dropshipping delivery take? From local warehouses, usually a few days. From overseas, one to three weeks or more, depending on the supplier, shipping method and customs processing. Do I need a business license to dropship? In most places you need to register your business and may need a sales tax permit. Requirements vary by country and state, so check local rules.

Magento 2 one-step checkout lets online store owners let their customers complete the purchase with a single form. text: Enabling advanced subscription capabilities on a WooCommerce website is often difficult for businesses. Most businesses are busy determining what plugins to use and how they will impact their store. But what if we told you that this decision does not have to be so complicated? Below, we present the best WooCommerce subscription plugins for your online store. The article explains the salient features and capabilities you can add to your WooCommerce website with a subscription plugin integration. Find the ideal WooCommerce subscription plugin for your website Free Consultation Table of Contents What is WooCommerce Subscription? Role of WooCommerce Subscription Plugins for WooCommerce Website 20 Best WooCommerce Subscription Plugins Tips to Choose a WooCommerce Subscription Plugin for Your Website Wrapping up Best WooCommerce Subscription Plugins – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is WooCommerce Subscription? WooCommerce subscription involves setting up your online store to support automated or recurring payments. You can accomplish this by using a premium WooCommerce plugin or extension. The plugins allow you to sell products and services on your store via regular charges or subscription fees.  Your eCommerce customers can subscribe to a product or service via the automated payment method. The admin has the option to approve or deny subscriptions to the customers. After subscribing, users can log in to your WooCommerce website as a subscriber.  Typically, the subscriber login redirects the user to a product page. The user can change their role and access the paid website section after successful payment. The paid section could be exclusive content or a dashboard for accessing your services. Why Subscription Plugin? With the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin, you can easily generate recurring revenue from user payments. Sell subscription-based products and recurring services for a predetermined duration. Compatible with the PayPal Standard payment gateway. Convert your online store into a WooCommerce subscription store. Offer free trials of subscription-based products and services to your clients. You can cancel your WooCommerce subscription at any moment. Receive updated order notes, including explanations for missed recurring payments (Stripe and PayPal). When an order fails, the subscription status is placed on hold. When an order is canceled, any subscriptions are automatically canceled. Multistep setup for automatically configuring the Subscriptions WooCommerce plugin and its needs. Set up the WooCommerce Subscription plugin flows through the multistep form. Automatically produce subscription error logs based on logging criteria. Email notifications for subscription renewal orders. Types of WooCommerce Subscription Plugins for WooCommerce Website In short, the role of WooCommerce plugins is to enable store owners or admins to manage subscription (recurring) payments and related services. There are three types of subscriptions that you can implement on your eCommerce store. Product subscription Membership subscription Email subscription Product subscription enables you to offer recurring payment options for products you sell on your WooCommerce store at periodic intervals. Membership subscription allows customers to purchase a membership to access your products and services. Email subscription allows your customers or target audience to facilitate effective communication with your brand. It typically involves communications, such as major updates, newsletters, promos, and more.  Even if your website has an inferior subscription plugin, you can still upgrade it with a WooCommerce Subscriptions migration. The WooCommerce developers at Virtina can help you ensure a fast and efficient subscription migration. We can customize the WooCommerce subscription plugin to add tailor-made features to better manage your online business. How Do You Install A Woocommerce Subscription Plugin? In addition to constant income, subscription software enables you to bill consumers automatically. This saves you time while reducing payment errors and delays. Here’s how to create a WooCommerce subscription: 1. Select a subscription plugin. Advanced plugins for WooCommerce subscriptions are now accessible for businesses of any size. You can use native WooCommerce plugins or third-party applications available in your location. 2. Add a product and choose the subscription type. The process is simple and similar to adding standard products to WooCommerce. Navigate to WooCommerce > Products > Add Product. If you want the most basic model, choose Simple Subscription when selecting the type of subscription. To establish a more diverse subscription plan, use a variable subscription instead. 3. Include product pricing and additional information.   You can customize your membership costs, billing cycles, sign-up fees, trial duration, and more. 20 Best WooCommerce Subscription Plugins One of the advantages of using WooCommerce’s open-source platform for running your online business is access to numerous plugins. You can easily add subscription capabilities to your website by integrating a WooCommerce subscription plugin.  There are numerous plugins with unique features and functionalities that you can use on your WooCommerce store. Following is the list of the most efficient WooCommerce subscription plugins you can use for your online store in 2023. 1. WooCommerce Subscriptions It is arguably the most widely used WooCommerce subscription plugin today, and it is a native product from none other than WooCommerce itself. It is an ideal choice for your WooCommerce store because it offers unique features, including the ability to manage different subscriptions simultaneously. Besides that, the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin also lets you access functionalities, such as periodic billing and automatic invoice generation. That’s not all. You can access numerous other features and functionalities with the WooCommerce plugin. Some other attractive features of the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugins are listed below. Top Features and Benefits of Using WooCommerce Subscriptions by WooCommerce Automated rebilling for failed (subscription) payments Automatic subscription renewal notifications for customers Multiple subscription products for greater purchase flexibility Ability to choose subscription schedules for customers Support various subscriptions for a single customer 2. Subscriptions for WooCommerce WebToffee offers an advanced subscription plugin called Subscriptions for WooCommerce. It is another excellent WooCommerce subscription plugin to consider for your online store. You can easily use the plugin to set up and manage subscription/recurring payments on your WooCommerce store.  The WooCommerce plugin lets you handle your subscription billing needs without a complex setup. More importantly, you can use the plugin to set up subscriptions for physical and digital products. Following are some other attractive features of Subscriptions for the WooCommerce plugin. Top Features and Benefits of Using Subscriptions for WooCommerce Renewal synchronization support with option for prorate Multiple billing schedule support Create and manage discount coupons for recurring subscriptions Date synchronization for products Payment gateway compatibility with numerous merchants 3. Subscriptio With Subscriptio, you get a WooCommerce subscription plugin that lets users sell subscriptions. Another attractive aspect of this plugin is that it can easily enable recurring revenue schemes for your website.  It is an ideal WooCommerce subscription plugin for your business if you wish to sell eLearning packages. Of course, you can still use the plugin for selling online memberships, including for online magazines and other similar items. Some other features you can access with the WooCommerce plugin include the following.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Subscriptio Flexible billing cycles with multiple billing capabilities Automatic subscription renewals Variable product subscriptions support Advanced tools for creating and managing subscription lists Manage subscription trial period PayPal and Stripe compatibility Multiple subscription support with unlimited quantity Payment reminders for customers 4. YITH WooCommerce Subscription Another popular WooCommerce subscription plugin you can consider for your eCommerce store is the YITH WooCommerce Subscription plugin. It lets WooCommerce store owners create subscription products ranging from essential items to product articles.  You can download the YITH WooCommerce Subscription plugin for free from the WordPress store, but you can also use its premium version if necessary. With YITH, you can create unlimited subscriptions for your physical or digital products.  You can control sales volume, provide fixed membership plans for content distribution, and more. YITH even lets you set up a schedule for content distribution to your subscribers. Other attractive features of the YITH WooCommerce Subscription plugin include the following.  Top Features and Benefits of Using YITH WooCommerce Subscription Easy access to subscription information for customers. PayPal and Stripe payment compatible. Quick and easy subscription upgrade/downgrade. Multiple payment gateway support. Single transaction for various subscriptions. Pause Notification feature for users. Build a custom WooCommerce plugin for your online store Schedule a Meeting 5. WP Simple Pay (Stripe Payments) It is an excellent plugin for implementing a subscription option on your WooCommerce website using Stripe’s secure payment gateway. WP Simple Pay lets you facilitate recurring and one-time payments via Stripe. Zero coding is required to add the WooCommerce subscription capability to your website.  The plugin lets you create subscription plans for your business using nothing but your Stripe account. It allows you to design installment plans and specify the trial period and initial setup fees. Besides that, you can use the plugin to create custom form fields, collect data, and enable custom entries using dropdowns.  Top Features and Benefits of Using WP Simple Pay Non-card payment support Secure payments via Stripe’s ultra-secure servers Secure Customer Authentication – SCA support Mobile-optimized Subscription integration support Drag and drop builder for payment form customization Percentage or amount discounts to customers Multi-language and multi-currency support 6. SUMO Subscriptions  Another excellent WooCommerce subscription plugin you can use on your website is SUMO subscriptions by Fantastic Plugins. One of the specialties of the SUMO Subscriptions plugin is that it comes with several built-in payment gateways.  The plugin facilitates automatic renewals via PayPal and Stripe. You can create the variable and grouped product subscriptions using this WooCommerce subscription plugin. Apart from that, the plugin lets users set their subscription duration, renewal frequency, etc.  Top Features and Benefits of Using SUMO Subscriptions Free and paid trial support Built-in Stripe subscription and PayPal recurring payment capability Subscription renewal automation via SUMO Reward Point Gateway and Reward Points plugins Master log for accessing all transaction records Enable regular donations via SUMO Donations plugin 7. Paid Memberships Pro Unlike most WooCommerce subscription plugins discussed above, the Paid Memberships Pro plugin is exclusively for membership sites. It means you can’t use this plugin for physical or digital products. The company also offers several other plugins for networking, email marketing, and more that can work seamlessly with each other.  It is also worth noting that the plugin supports numerous add-ons and integrations. However, this WooCommerce subscription plugin works best for membership-based websites. Besides, Paid Membership Pro plugin offers many features to enhance your WooCommerce site capabilities. You can further enhance these capabilities via appropriate add-ons.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Paid Memberships Pro Set up special content access and pricing for members Multi-tiered membership support, including child account management for parents Design and content customization for member messages Member level and role synchronization Recurring and subscription payment support Integration support for PayPal, Stripe, 2Checkout, Braintree, and Authorize.Net Offline payment support Option for members to choose their desired payment option 8. WP Full Stripe You can significantly enhance the payment capabilities of your WooCommerce store using the WP Full Stripe plugin. The plugin lets you create subscriptions and send invoices to customers. Furthermore, it also supports the standard one-time purchases on your WooCommerce store. As the name suggests, the plugin uses Stripe’s secure API. No coding is necessary for using this WooCommerce subscription plugin on your online store. The plugin even lets you integrate pricing tables and receive donations through the WooCommerce website. Besides that, the plugin offers advanced payment and refund management capabilities for your online business.  Top Features and Benefits of Using WP Full Stripe Offer trials to users for a limited period Localized messages Custom form creation Optimize post-purchase experience Appearance customization Email notification for customers Recurring service support 9. Paid Member Subscriptions Another excellent WooCommerce subscription plugin for membership websites is the Paid Member Subscriptions plugin. With this WooCommerce subscription plugin, you can set explicit access to premium content on your website. The Paid Member Subscriptions plugin offers Elementor page builder integration for content restriction.  The plugin offers numerous features that enable WooCommerce store owners to manage memberships and payments better. After installation, you can organize subscriptions into different hierarchies. Furthermore, the plugin lets you offer customers free trials before choosing a subscription plan.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Paid Member Subscriptions Edit/delete user subscriptions Superior member management capabilities Shortcode support Free Trial/Sign Up for customers Recurring payment via PayPal Multiple subscription support Payment status and purchase information tracking CSV file export for subscriptions and memberships 10. WooCommerce Memberships Membership associations, eLearning sites, online magazines, and similar businesses can significantly benefit from WooCommerce Memberships plugin. The WooCommerce plugin provides superior access control for managing your content or products. Besides content restriction, the plugin lets you manually assign memberships and facilitate a complete member integration to your WooCommerce website.  Top Features and Benefits of Using WooCommerce Memberships Sell or assign memberships Advanced content access capability Drip Content feature to schedule access to your content Product viewing/purchasing restriction to members Provide member discounts to all or selected products or categories Member Area for accessing all membership-related information 11. AWeber Newsletter Subscription It is an ideal WooCommerce subscription plugin for your business if you want a specialized newsletter plugin. AWeber integration requires zero coding and instantly connects your email marketing with your WooCommerce store. Many online store owners use the specialized newsletter subscription plugin to grow their email audience and boost sales.  Top Features and Benefits of Using AWeber Newsletter Subscription Enable customers to sign up for the newsletter during the purchase Add users abandoning cart automatically to the AWeber account Apply product tags using tailored checkout rules Visitor attribute record for cart abandonments Widget for adding AWeber Web Form in the WooCommerce store 12. Minimum Periods for WooCommerce Subscriptions It is a unique WooCommerce subscription plugin that allows you to assign a minimum period for subscriptions. Besides, you can set custom payment terms for your subscription products using the Minimum Periods for the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin. The plugin requires customers to keep their subscriptions active for a minimum period before they can cancel the subscription.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Minimum Periods for WooCommerce Subscriptions Set a minimum period for your subscriptions It enables you to up-sell subscriptions before the customer cancels their new purchase Prevent accidental cancelation of subscriptions Automatically apply minimum periods for all your subscriptions, including future ones 13. Buy Once or Subscribe for WooCommerce Subscriptions You can use the Buy Once or Subscribe for WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin to enhance your site’s subscription capability. It allows you to offer all your existing products in your WooCommerce store for subscription purchases. The plugin is ideal for any business wanting to sell its stand-alone products using a subscription plan. Add custom capabilities to your WooCommerce subscription plugin Get a Custom Plugin Top Features and Benefits of Using Buy Once or Subscribe for WooCommerce Subscriptions Single-purchase and variable product subscription support Apply subscriptions to individual products, product pages, or categories Set subscription frequency from the admin panel Offer different discounts for each subscription frequency 14. Groups for WooCommerce Another popular WooCommerce subscription plugin for your membership-oriented website is Groups for WooCommerce. The plugin is one of the best for enabling and managing group memberships. It is also a robust access control solution that works seamlessly on WordPress and WooCommerce websites.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Groups for WooCommerce Group-based membership grants Automatic product-based group assignment to customers Ability to sell unlimited memberships Time-limited memberships 15. Bulk Table Editor Although not a dedicated plugin for managing WooCommerce subscriptions, the Bulk Table Editor is famous for its diverse capabilities. The plugin is an excellent choice for businesses that want to edit their subscriptions and products in bulk. Besides bulk editing your subscriptions, the plugin lets you quickly schedule sales, assign tags, edit prices, and more.   Top Features and Benefits of Using Bulk Table Editor Quick and convenient access to bulk functions Support recurring sales Hide prices and other variables Read and update aspects, such as SKU, description, and ID 16. It enables you to create fundraising campaigns with advanced capabilities. Donation for WooCommerce plugin allows you to create tailored donation campaigns to meet your organizational goals.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Donation For WooCommerce Support recurring donation payments on WooCommerce stores Support round-up donations Easy donation attribute configuration, including limits, amount types, etc Simultaneously run multiple fundraising campaigns 17. Kissmetrics Organizations must keep close track of their subscriptions, and Kissmetrics is one of the best plugins. The plugin works seamlessly with WooCommerce subscriptions and enhances its capability. Besides subscriptions, you get actionable insights on various aspects of your WooCommerce store. It enables you to build an advanced subscription system for your organization that works on par with the subscription capabilities in Amazon. Using this plugin, you can even implement a subscribe and save system similar to Amazon on your site.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Autoship Cloud Implement a Subscribe and Save setup Support multiple payment gateway integrations Automated inventory or stock syncing Advanced management tools for subscriptions (for users and admin) Access to additional marketing tools 19. Chargebee It is one of the most widely-used subscription management software in eCommerce. Chargebee enables subscription-based businesses to retain and grow their revenue with advanced capabilities. Some of the most attractive aspects of this WooCommerce subscription plugin include recurring billing and superior subscription management.  Top Features and Benefits of Using Chargebee Automated recurring payments Revenue analytics capability Superior subscription management Seamless integration with tech stack 20. PPWP (Password Protect WordPress) Pro PPWP Pro is another effective alternative to the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin. B2B eCommerce is a direct business-to-business (B2B) digital commerce. It is a broad term used to describe selling goods or services online to other businesses, including direct and indirect sales through one or more intermediaries. The main objective of B2B eCommerce is to help customers find what they want quickly, have a personalized shopping experience, and make educated purchasing decisions on time. B2B eCommerce: The Objectives Moving a B2B business online has the following simple goals. Wider customer reach Cost-effectiveness Save time Streamlined Process Enhance efficiency Drive revenue B2B eCommerce: Some Statistics Here are some B2B eCommerce statistics to give you a clear picture of its relevance.  Global B2B market has reached a whopping $12 trillion It comprises 13% of total B2B sales in the United States B2B market is over six times bigger than the B2C market Buyers are spending more online during and after the pandemic There is an average 45% jump in order values Businesses are adopting a digital-first approach for broader customer reach What does all this data indicate? Is it time to shift to the B2B eCommerce market ?  Virtina Says: Hell, yeah! Pull up your socks and get going! Learn more about the advantages of building a customized B2B eCommerce platform for your business Let’s Discuss Working of B2B eCommerce B2B differs drastically from B2C as a business model . B2B sells products and services to businesses, while B2C eCommerce sells products and services directly to consumers. B2B eCommerce involves more advanced techniques, such as cross-channel marketing and automation. In addition to its differences in approach, B2B vs B2C also differs in how it is done. Instead of selling directly to a customer, the transactions can happen through an online sales portal between manufacturers and wholesalers or wholesalers and retailers. Traditional B2B eCommerce involves intense manual sales and marketing processes. The key to making daily operations easier is through eCommerce automation.  eCommerce Automation: The Keystone The process has reduced the hassles of the manual running of B2B businesses. The sellers and buyers can meet on a single digital platform, place orders, and manage shipments – everything from the comforts of their mobile phones or computers. There is minimal chance of error, lower running costs, and improved efficacy. Moreover, there are better chances to connect with new suppliers and distributors.  Overall Advantages of eCommerce Automation Fully automated sales between businesses, suppliers, distributors Lowered infrastructure and overhead costs  Does not need intermediaries Improved growth prospects Mass market at scale reach 24/7 omnichannel branded presence  Enhanced partner relationships Augmented employee productivity Different Types of B2B eCommerce If you are in a B2B business, there are one or more categories that your company falls into. Let us have a look.  Manufacturers Manufacturing enterprises produce the products in bulk and then sell them to other manufacturers, suppliers, or wholesalers. Their products are brought in bulk and branded or resold directly by their buyers. If you are into manufacturing, you should equip yourself with tools to meet digital demands from buyers. Customized features in pricing, production schedule, or sizing while completing transactions act as an added advantage.  Wholesalers These traders buy goods in bulk either from manufacturers directly or from distributors. They then sell them at retail prices to their patrons. Buyer-oriented B2B marketplaces are the best options for wholesale companies to showcase their products to retailers and buyers. They can advertise their products at lower rates and efforts compared to traditional marketing tactics. Distributors Manufacturers often partner with distributors for marketing, packaging, selling, and shipping their products. An online partnership between the two businesses facilitates eCommerce fulfillment operations cost-effectively. They will be able to find suppliers, finalize deals, streamline the supply chain process, and ensure seamless customer satisfaction in less time. With good service, they can get established businesses to outsource the fulfillment process.  Business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) In this business model, B2B enterprises procure goods from manufacturers and wholesalers and sell directly to the customers. The business model needs a digital storefront that showcases detailed product catalogs and comprehensive descriptions that appeal to buyers.  The clients that B2B businesses deal with generally fall under the following broad categories.  Wholesalers Retailers Resellers Schools  NGOs Different Stages of a B2B Business Every business has its unique journey. And every industry and business size moves differently. But there are some typical overarching stages to every business. Let us take a close look at the different phases of this journey.  Startup This is the first and most challenging stage, where you decide to embark on your business. It is a phase of ideation, testing the market for feedback, making adjustments according to the market trends, and sales start to trickle in. You learn to estimate the minimum viable product, find the total addressable market (TAM), and start creating brand awareness. Keep in mind that your business venture solves a crisis and offers solutions. Growth This is a phase full of changes and can be cumbersome. You reimagine your processes, revisit systems, and optimize them to meet the growing market demands. You can start experimenting with marketing strategies and explore chances for possible partnerships. You will need to hire an experienced workforce and look for external funding. Build on the relationship with the suppliers to break even. Expansion In this stage, cash flow increases enough for you to consider development and diversifying distribution. This stage calls for hiring the best in the business talent, creating a better omnichannel customer experience, and tracking growth per quarter. It is the time to invest the resources wisely, make educated budgeting decisions, and keep the marketing share afloat among the competition. Maturity By this stage, you know where your business stands in terms of evolution. The sales sources become more apparent, and hiring new talent gets easy. It is now simpler to make business projections. You can consider diversifying your market, testing new products, investing in technology that aids your processes, and expanding marketing tactics.  Profitability By now, you are in charge. You can choose which way you want to go as a business owner. You can continue to grow in the same manner or branch out with different product offerings. You can think of innovative ways to change up your business and invest freely in technology. You can even plan to exit the business by selling at a profit, with a tidy sum squirreled away for your future. Top B2B eCommerce Platforms in 2023 The biggest challenge in B2B eCommerce, you ask? Yup! Finding the platform that fits you best! All eCommerce platforms are not created equal. Only some have the potential to create a wholesome B2B experience. Some platforms are designed specifically for the B2B business model, with the best-in-class customer experience and analytics capabilities. Your victory lies in selecting the one best suited for the needs and requirements of your business. Here’s the list of the top four B2B eCommerce platforms in 2023. Magento Magento platform has the best in-the-market credentials for enterprise-level businesses and suits all business sizes. It stands out for its powerful execution, custom pricing, dependable cloud-based performance, and efficient reporting and analytics tools. Magento offers users the ability to self-manage accounts, easy installation, minimal maintenance, and total value for money. Hire Magento expert developers for high-quality and stable B2B eCommerce websites. BigCommerce BigCommerce is the most integration–friendly platform , giving it the best customization capacities. It also features B2B-specific payment gateways, advanced shipping tools, a simple subscription and reordering structure, a quote builder, and easy integration with other ERPs and CRMs. WooCommerce Businesses love this open-source WordPress plugin for its rich eCommerce features. It is easy to create, launch, and manage a highly-customized eCommerce store on WooCommerce . B2B WooCommerce websites have access to the large WordPress support community and an immense collection of add-ons and extensions, and it offers excellent scalability and flexibility. Shopify Shopify store development is known for its customization capabilities. It is a cult favorite because it can process as many as 8000 orders per minute, integrates seamlessly with most ERP and CRM software, creates a great customer experience, and supports over 100 payment providers and global currencies. Hire a Shopify developer and proceed with advanced Shopify Plus if you have the budget. Confused about finding the right platform for your B2B eCommerce business? It allows you to sell more products to your customers without additional spending on marketing efforts. Here, we discuss the case of Product Bundles for WooCommerce, its benefits, and how you can set it up for your online store. Additionally, we explain how product bundles can help you boost your online sales and revenue without spending more money on marketing. Table of Contents What are WooCommerce Product Bundles? Increase Revenue With Discounts Ease of Bundling Different Products Provides Flexibility To Choose Increase Perceived Value Bundling the Right Products Increase the Average Order Value Wrapping Up What are WooCommerce Product Bundles? WooCommerce Product Bundle is an advanced capability that lets your eCommerce customers create and purchase a group of products. It allows you to group your simple and variable products and sell them together as a bundle.  You can use the WooCommerce Product Bundle feature for your subscription products too. Implementing the Product Bundle feature can help you encourage your customers to buy more from your WooCommerce store. In short, WooCommerce Product Bundles allow customers to group several products and sell them as a single package. This feature is especially effective if the per-piece price of the product in the bundle is lower than the original price of an individual product. Moreover, you can add even more capabilities to your plugin with custom WooCommerce development . It is an excellent way to encourage customers to buy more products from your WooCommerce store. Bundling products is a familiar concept to online businesses. Corporate giants like McDonald’s have tested this strategy in the real world with their famous happy meal offer. What are the Benefits of WooCommerce Product Bundles?  There are numerous benefits of using WooCommerce Product Bundles for your eCommerce business. Implementing a feature like product bundling allows you to significantly improve the quality of your customer interaction and shopping experience on your eCommerce website. Here are some of the most significant benefits of using WooCommerce Product Bundles in your eCommerce website. Effectively pitch your complementary products to the target audience. It helps you boost your inventory turnover ratio regardless of the product category. It helps significantly increase your website’s average transaction time using bundled products. Offer better customization capability to your eCommerce customers. Minimize your eCommerce store’s overhead and shipping expenses. Boost your eCommerce store’s average order value.  It helps in optimizing your inventory management and minimizing inventory waste. Do you want to learn how you can efficiently group items for your WooCommerce  Product Bundles? Get Advice From Experts How Do I Use the WooCommerce Product Bundle? The WooCommerce Product Bundle offers many capabilities which enable your eCommerce customers to mix and match products. You can use it on your simple and variable products. The simple products are the ones that have just a single SKU or do not have different variations.  As you can guess, the variable products are the ones that have more than one variation. For instance, you can sell different tea flavors on your eCommerce website, such as regular tea, chamomile tea, Etc.  The customer can create a bundle where they can add a different tea flavor and buy them all together. With WooCommerce Product Bundle, you get superior flexibility that lets you set up the bundle product option however you want. Here is how you can use the WooCommerce Product Bundle for your eCommerce store. Enable customers to bundle simple and variable products. Enable customers to create bundles with multiple same products. Set the type of variations the customers can add to the product bundle. Set the minimum or maximum quantity available for bundled products. Provide discounts for bulk quantity orders. Offer higher discounts to customers based on the number of items. Decide which individual item to show or hide from the customers. Select the layout of the bundle products or bundle product suggestions. Set up advanced shipping and pricing features for your WooCommerce Product Bundles. WooCommerce Product Bundles Plugin To implement the WooCommerce Product Bundle feature on your eCommerce store, you need to integrate an advanced plugin into your WooCommerce store. The good news is that you can easily find a plugin that fits your specific needs, thanks to the extensive availability of WooCommerce plugins. WooCommerce does not come with advanced product bundle features out of the box. However, you can still access basic product bundling features without a plugin. But as a WooCommerce store owner, you probably knew that already.  Integrating the WooCommerce plugin enables you to access advanced product bundle features and capabilities. Usually, all WooCommerce Product Bundles plugins have a similar set of features. However, you can find some great traits in most of these plugins.  We will discuss the best WooCommerce Product Bundle plugins as we proceed further. It is also crucial to note that if the integration doesn’t go right you may have to carry out a WooCommerce bug fix for your store. And if your website is not hosted on WooCommerce you can always try out our WooCommerce migration services and upgrade your online store. We can even provide you with a WooCommerce migration guide to help you through the process. Let’s look at how you can set up Product Bundles for your online store using WooCommerce’s in-built capabilities. How to Set Up WooCommerce Product Bundles With the Built-in Feature? Before we explain how you can set up WooCommerce Product Bundles on your website, you must ensure two things.  You must have a fully-functional WooCommerce store. You already have individual products added to your WooCommerce store.  You can only create product bundles using the existing products in your WooCommerce store. Assuming that both the conditions above are satisfied, you must follow the steps below to set up WooCommerce Product Bundles using in-built WooCommerce features . Step 1: Create a new Product (Bundle) To create WooCommerce Product Bundles, first, go to your WordPress dashboard. Once you reach the WordPress dashboard, follow the below steps to add new bundle products to your eCommerce store. Products → Add New Following the steps above allows you to add a new product. The new product is a different item from the products already in your store. You can then link other products in your store with the WooCommerce Product Bundles plugin.  After adding the relevant products, you can provide an appropriate name and description for the WooCommerce Product Bundle. Using words like “value pack” is advisable when providing the title and description for your WooCommerce Bundle Products. Step 2: Edit Product Information After adding a WooCommerce Product Bundle, you must provide the necessary product information. To do this, go to the “Product data” box, click on the drop-down menu, and select the “Grouped Product” option. Next, click on the “Linked Product” tab on the left of the “Product data” box. Use the “Grouped Product” field to add the products you want to enable the customer to include in their bundle. You can type in the product name, which will automatically appear in the Grouped Products field. The suggestion for adding bundle products only shows up if you already have the product in your store. Suppose you do not add the bundle products in your WooCommerce store and try typing the name. In that case, you will not get any return suggestions.  Step 3: Upload Images and Pick the Categories You can finish things by adding the necessary images for your WooCommerce Product Bundles. All you have to do is pick a product image and assign it to the appropriate product category. Creating a picture of all the products in the bundle is worth considering in a single file. On top of all this, WooCommerce Product Bundle options let you keep your bundle products in a different category. You can categorize and save your bundle products as bundles or grouped products, which makes bundling your products all the easier. After providing the necessary product data, uploading the images, and choosing the category, you may update or publish your product bundles. Step 4: Test Your WooCommerce Product Bundles At this point, your WooCommerce Product Bundles are all set to go, and all you have to do now is test them. You can ensure all your bundled products work by going to your eCommerce website’s front end. You should be able to find your bundled products and take a look at its product page. Once you reach the bundled product’s page, you can see that each item is listed along with its title and price. You can also see that your customers can choose the quantity or remove something from the bundle. Implementing WooCommerce Product Bundles like this treats each product as a separate item once it reaches the cart. The primary benefit is that your customers can speed up your WooCommerce store and  their shopping process and save money on orders.  Effectively bundle products for your eCommerce store with the help of our WooCommerce experts Learn More How to Provide Discounts for Your WooCommerce Product Bundles? When it comes to user-friendly tools to provide discounts for bundled products, your best bet is to go for a premium plugin. These plugins offer significantly better functionality, lacking in WooCommerce in-built tools. However, there is a way you can go about implementing discounts for your WooCommerce Bundle Products using in-built functionalities. Follow the steps below to provide discounts to your customers for bundled products using in-built WooCommerce capability. WooCommerce → Coupons → Add Coupon After following the above steps, you can create a coupon that works for your WooCommerce Product Bundles. Here you can also add a description for the coupon to be extra evident. When you scroll down, you can see a General tab in the “Coupon data” box. You can select the “Fixed cart discount” as the Discount type using the drop-down menu. The neat part about setting up your discount like this is that you can set expiration dates for the discounts or offer free shipping. Pro Tip: It is ideal to assess the popular and most convenient payment gateways to boost conversions as customers often tend to abandon cart if the desired payment method is unavailable. In the “Coupon data” box, you can also find the “Usage restriction” tab. Select the tab on the screen and add every item included in the bundle to the “Products field.” Doing so enables your WooCommerce store to offer discounts on any item in the bundled products to the shopping cart. One issue you may need help with such discount offers is that fixed discounts are applied to even low-cost items. You can avoid this by setting a minimum spend for accessing the discount code. You can set it up so that the discount is canceled if the customer removes one of the bundled products from the cart. It is also essential to have smooth functioning WooCommerce payment gateways to ensure a streamlined eCommerce transaction . This tiny discount coupon setup displays an error message if the customer tries to remove one of the bundled products. Although this is far from perfect, you can still get the job done using this method. The better option is to go for a premium WooCommerce Product Bundle plugin. One of the most significant downsides of implementing this discount coupon setup is that the discount is not automatically applied to the cart. The user has to type in the coupon code after adding the WooCommerce Product Bundle to their cart. How To Automatically Apply Discounts For Your WooCommerce Product Bundles? Using a premium plugin or extension is the best way to apply discounts automatically to your WooCommerce Product Bundles. There are numerous plugins you can choose for this job. But most online businesses find the extension WooCommerce Product Bundles as the best solution to apply automatic discounts for bundled products. The extension is not free; you must pay $49 to purchase it, but the subscription is valid for a year. You can easily cover this initial investment after completing your first few sales.
