text: Every year numerous online businesses choose WooCommerce to start the eCommerce journey . However, not everyone starts like this. Many online businesses make the mistake of rushing too fast into eCommerce that they either go for the cheapest or the easiest eCommerce platform to set up their online business. But later on, they realize that their existing eCommerce platform is not scalable enough or flexible enough, and so on. And then, they start the research to find the ideal eCommerce platform for the online business . In most cases, this search leads them to WooCommerce. If you are reading this article now, then the chances are that you also had a similar experience and are now considering WooCommerce migration services . Here we discuss the answer to every question you may have about WooCommerce migration and how you can execute it effectively. Table of Contents Methods to Migrate Your eCommerce Business to WooCommerce Migrating Your Data Manually WooCommerce Migration Using a Migration Tool Hiring a WooCommerce Expert Developer for Migration Migrating From Your Current eCommerce Platform to WooCommerce Magento to WooCommerce Migration BigCommerce to WooCommerce Migration Shopify to WooCommerce Migration OpenCart to WooCommerce Migration SquareSpace to WooCommerce Migration PrestaShop to WooCommerce Migration Other eCommerce Platform to WooCommerce Migration How to Migrate Your Existing WooCommerce Website Checklist For WooCommerce Migration WooCommerce Pre-migration Checklist WooCommerce Post-migration Checklist What are the Challenges in WooCommerce Migration? When do you Need WooCommerce Migration? WooCommerce Migration Project – Final Thoughts Methods to Migrate Your eCommerce Business to WooCommerce There are three ways you can migrate your website to the WooCommerce platform . But no matter which method you choose, you have to be extra careful because any mistake in the process could cost you your priceless business data.  Hence, it is essential that you follow the best practices and back up your data before beginning the migration process. Ensure that you carefully follow each step, so you don’t accidentally jeopardize your business data. The three methods you can migrate your website to the WooCommerce platform include the following. Manual WooCommerce migration WooCommerce migration using specialized tools WooCommerce migrations using expert migration services Migrating Your Data Manually One of the options you can consider if you are thinking of migrating your website to a WooCommerce platform is to do it manually. It is the least expensive way to migrate your website to the WooCommerce platform.  Although it is not an easy task to migrate a website by yourself, there is a silver lining. WooCoommerce offers a CSV product importer straight out of the box. The importer feature alone makes migrating to WooCommerce significantly easier for you. You would still need to ensure that your data is properly mapped. In theory, the WooCommerce migration process is pretty simple. It may even fool you into thinking that you can do it yourself. However, the reality of the situation could be a lot different.  You can also find the documentation for migrating products from your existing website to WooCommerce. But here is a quick rundown of the steps you must take to migrate your website to the WooCommerce platform. Step 1 Select the products you want to migrate to the WooCommerce site from your existing site and create a CSV file. Step 2 Import the products to WooCommerce after setting up the WordPress website and installing WooCommerce in it. WooCommerce Importer Tool You can access the WooCommerce Importer tool for importing all your products from the WordPress admin panel. You can find a section called Tools in the WordPress admin panel. Under the tool menu, you can find the Import option, which you must click on.  Now, you must click on the Run Importer button that you can find below the WooCommerce products option (CSV). To reiterate the steps, you need to take for importing products to WooCommerce, follow the steps given below. Tools → Import → Run Importer (Under WooCommerce Products (CSV)) At this point, you can select the necessary CSV file and run the WooCommerce Importer Tool and finish the process. And just like that, you can import all your products to your new WooCommerce website.  You can use the same process for importing the following details from your existing website. Orders Categories Custom fields Tags As we stated above, it may be simple enough on paper, but the actual process could be much more different. If you are not careful with the migration, you are likely to run into some roadblocks. Therefore, we would not advise you to attempt the WooCommerce migration alone if you have no previous or technical experience with the WooCommerce platform. Want to know how to migrate your store to WooCommerce using a migration tool? Talk to Our Experts WooCommerce Migration Using a Migration Tool A better way to accomplish successful WooCommerce migration is to use a migration tool. The good news is that several tools are available in the market that lets you migrate your business to a WooCommerce site. Most of these tools come with a default migration protocol. Some of the major advantages of using such tools include the following. No or zero downtime during the migration. Receive orders even during the import process. Keep your store functioning normally during the migration process. Below are some of the more popular WooCommerce migration tools you can use. LitExtension LitExtension is one of the best tools you can use for migrating your eCommerce store to the WooCommerce platform. Moreover, it only takes three simple steps to migrate your website to WooCommerce if you use LitExtension’s migration tool, which is as follows. Step 1 Download the LitExtension software and fill in the details of your eCommerce website. Step 2 Choose the data or information you want to migrate to the WooCommerce website. Step 3 Execute a free demo migration and immediately transfer all your site data. Cart2Cart Another excellent plugin or tool of choice for migrating to the WooCommerce platform is Cart2Cart. With zero downtime, you can use it to transfer all the data from your existing website to your new website on WooCommerce. The steps to move eCommerce data to the new WooCommerce platform is as follows. Step 1 Choose the migration source and pick WooCommerce as your target platform. Step 2 Choose the data or information you want to transfer, including the 301 redirects. Step 3 Run a free migration or directly proceed to full migration. WP All Import Many consider WP All Import the best tool for WooCommerce migration. Part of the reason why people feel this way about WP All Import is its drag-and-drop interface. It makes the migration process easier to use and understand. Listed below are some of the other functionalities of the WP All Import tool. Automatically detect every element in your WordPress site, including image galleries, custom fields, and even taxonomies. Import the necessary data to WordPress from a spreadsheet, CSV, or XML format and easily map the data using drag and drop. Full control over the data you update, enabling you to pick the data to be updated and the data that should remain untouched. Hiring a WooCommerce Expert Developer for Migration The safest and most effective way to migrate your eCommerce website to the WooCommerce platform is by hiring a WooCommerce developer . There are always risks associated with eCommerce migration, whether you do it manually by yourself or with the help of the advanced tools we discussed above. Hence, the safer approach is to seek the help of an expert like Virtina. We can help you execute even complicated migration processes without compromising the safety of your precious data. Moreover, a WooCommerce migration presents the perfect opportunity for you to revamp your website and equip it with new features and capabilities.  Virtina can help you build an entirely new WooCommerce store where you have complete control over your eCommerce business. Here are some of the major benefits you can get by hiring an expert like Virtina Reliable and error-free WooCommerce migration process Efficient migration and access to certified WooCommerce experts WooCommerce experts with in-depth knowledge of the eCommerce platform Ability to navigate through complications in the migration process Save valuable time and ensure data security Ability to set up your WooCommerce store with additional features and capabilities In short, an eCommerce expert like Virtina can help you migrate your website to the WooCommerce platform and improve it. There is no point in migrating your store to the WooCommerce platform if you don’t use the platform’s full potential. A WooCommerce expert like Virtina can help you realize the full potential of the WooCommerce platform. You can customize your store to align with your brand logo and colors. On top of that, you can implement complex integrations and set up additional features that were not possible on your previous website. The only downside of hiring a WooCommerce expert is that it can cost you a few extra bucks. But you can make up for it by completely revamping your eCommerce store and saving valuable time.  Moreover, suppose you try to execute WooCommerce migration yourself, and something goes wrong. In that case, you may spend even more money fixing it. Hence, we recommend you always hire a WooCommerce expert for your migration project if you do not have a strong knowledge of the WooCommerce platform. Migrating From Your Current eCommerce Platform to WooCommerce Typically a WooCommerce migration happens from an existing eCommerce platform to WooCommerce. There are several reasons why businesses may want to migrate their eCommerce website from their present eCommerce platform to WooCommerce.  One of the most common reasons begins migrations from the current eCommerce platform to WooCommerce is the need for flexibility. An open-source eCommerce platform like WooCommerce is significantly easier to manage and offers superior flexibility. We could go on and on about the various benefits of WooCommerce over other eCommerce platforms. So, here are the basic steps you need to know to migrate your website from some of the popular eCommerce platforms.  Do you want to migrate your existing eCommerce store to advanced WooCommerce platform? Hire a WooComerce Expert Magento to WooCommerce Migration Magento is one of the most powerful eCommerce platforms out there. However, managing your business on Magento requires technical knowledge , which is not always flexible like WooCommerce. The basic steps involved in migrating a website from Magento to WooCommerce using a tool like LifeExtension is as follows.  Step 1 Download the connector to your store’s root folder, choose Magento as your “Source Cart,” and enter your store’s URL. Step 2 Choose WooCommerce as the “Target Cart” and enter the URL for your WooCommerce store. Step 3 Choose the eCommerce data or entities you want to migrate, such as products, orders, customers, etc. Step 4 Execute the migration process using LiteExtension. (Run a demo migration first if necessary) BigCommerce to WooCommerce Migration BigCommerce is another popular eCommerce platform from where businesses migrate to WooCommerce. It is an easy-to-use and robust eCommerce platform with superior security features. However, it tends to run on the pricier side compared to WooCommerce. The steps you must follow for manual BigCommerce to WooCommerce migration are as follows. Step 1 Backup your eCommerce data The manual backup process for BigCommerce to WooCommerce migration is slightly complex and takes place in parts. Products and Product Images Go to your admin panel to migrate your product and images from BigCommerce to WooCommerce. Once you reach the admin panel, follow the steps listed below. Products → Export → [set bulk export settings] → Continue → Confirm → Export my products to a CSV File → Download Product File You must connect your eCommerce website to WebDAV to download the product images. After that, you can download the images via a drag-and-drop option. Customer Trace BigCommerce PCI compliance does not allow you to export a customer’s password. You can take the following steps to export your customer data from your eCommerce website.  Customers → Export → [Set Bulk Edit template] → Continue → Export my customers to a CSV file → Download my Customers file Orders Follow the steps below to export your order data from your Big Commerce website.  Orders → Export → [Set Default Template] → Continue → Export my orders to a CSV file → Download My Orders Step 2 Create a WooCommerce Storefront After backing up all the necessary data from the BiigCommerce store, you can proceed to create a WooCommerce storefront. Start by creating a WordPress-powered website with its hosting and domain name. Follows these steps after finishing the initial setup of the WooCommerce store.  Create new database → WordPress package upload → Edit config-sample.php and run installation script → WooCommerce plugin installation and configuration Step 3 Data Migration The final step in the BigCommerce to WooCommerce migration process is importing all the data to the new platform. You can import the data through a manual approach or use an importer tool, as discussed above. Follow the same steps we discussed in the case of Magento to WooCommerce migration to import data using an import tool. Shopify to WooCommerce Migration You can find several similar functionalities in the Shopify to WooCommerce eCommerce platforms. Hence, it is relatively easier to implement migration from Shopify to WooCommerce. Here also, you can take a manual approach or use a tool. Step 1 Shopify Apps Migration You can not directly migrate information from third-party plugins and applications from Shopify to WooCommerce.  However, you can tackle this limitation by analyzing your existing Shopify apps and finding the WooCommerce plugins having the same or similar functionalities.  It is best to seek the help of a WooCommerce expert like Virtina to accomplish this if you are not familiar with the WooCommerce platform. Step 2 Themes and Designs Unfortunately, your WooCommerce store can not use Shopify themes. Hence, you must design your new WooCommerce site from scratch if you migrate from Shopify. The good news is that WooCommerce’s open=-source platform offers you unlimited customization capability. With the help of an eCommerce expert like Virtina, you can make your website exactly how you envisioned it.  OpenCart to WooCommerce Migration The three standard migration methods apply to OpenCart to WooCommerce migration . Step 2 Input the Source and Target Cart information. Step 3 Choose your migration settings or preference. Step 4 Execute the migration process. Step 5 Check the results of your migration. You can easily conduct a simple migration from OpenCart to the WooCommerce platform using a migration tool LitExtension. However,  Seek the help of a certified expert like Virtina implement custom designs, features, and functionalities on your WooCommerce store. It can help you create unique capabilities that can better serve your customers. SquareSpace to WooCommerce Migration SquareSpace is a relatively new eCommerce platform. It offers built-in tools that help the design process simple for business organizations. However, it lacks the flexibility you get from WooCommerce and could be the number one reason for SquareSpace to WooCommerce migration. Step 1 Export Your SquareSpace Content To export your eCommerce information from your SquareSpace online store, follow the steps below.  Settings → Advances → [Set your import/export option] → Export → [Select the WordPress logo from the pop-up window] → Download You can’t export some elements in your website, such as product/album pages, product blocks, templates, Etc. However, you may download them separately in CSV format. Step 2 Import Your Content to WordPress To import the content you downloaded to your new WordPress website, follow the steps below after logging in to the WordPress Admin Panel. Tools → Import → [choose relevant platforms] → Install → [run the importer]  WordPress will automatically upload your exported file from SquareSpace and give you access to its import settings page. PrestaShop to WooCommerce Migration PrestaShop offers you an open-source CMS platform similar to WooCommerce. With PrestaShop, you can facilitate high traffic. But, it lacks the scalability level you get from the WooCommerce platform and access to out-of-the-box features. We do not recommend manually executing the PrestaShop to WooCommerce migration, as it can often lead to complications. Using a WooCommerce plugin like FG PrestaShop could significantly simplify the migration process. The eCommerce data you can migrate using the plugin include products (including product images), categories, tags, and CMS. Below are the simplified steps to migrate your website from PrestaShop to WooCommerce. Step 1 Back up the data from your PrestaShop website. Step 2 Build a website on WordPress. Step 3 Install WooCommerce and configure your desired settings. Step 4 Install the importer tool (FG PrestaShop) to the WooCommerce plugin. Step 5 Choose the data types you need and import them from PrestaShop to WooCommerce. Other eCommerce Platform to WooCommerce Migration The basic premise of migrating from any eCommerce platform remains the same. You have three methods of migrating your eCommerce store, which includes Manual migration Migration using a software solution Migration by eCommerce experts (recommended) However, the migration process can change depending on the complexities of migration, such as the incompatible nature between platforms. In most cases, it is best to seek the services of a certified WooCommerce expert like Virtna for your migration process.   Although the basic principle behind every migration process is the same, they are also unique in their ways. For example, online businesses could use different third-party applications or plugins to streamline their business operations. In many cases, custom or third-party solutions are not easy to migrate to new platforms. Sometimes, you may have to create customized solutions to meet your specific eCommerce needs, depending on your existing eCommerce CMS. Hence, it is always best to let an expert like Virtina take over your WooCommerce migration project. How to Migrate Your Existing WooCommerce Website In some cases, businesses may have to migrate their eCommerce store already on WooCommerce to a different WooCommerce website. There are mainly two reasons why an online business may want to do this, and they are as follows.  To move an eCommerce business to a different domain name To migrate products from one website to another The simplified steps for a WooCommerce to WooCommerce migration involve the following steps.  Tools → Export → [select entities/data you want to migrate] → Download Export → [obtain an XML file] You can always simplify the migration process by using a migration tool or plugin like WP Migrate for easy and convenient WooCommerce to WooCommerce migration. Here, we discuss the basic pre and post-migration checklist to ensure a seamless WooCommerce integration process for your business organization. Acquire the FTP Credentials It’s essential to have your FTP credentials with you before migrating to WooCommerce. The necessary FTP credentials for the migration include the following. Username. Password. Server ID and address. Port number. Backup Your eCommerce Data The worst thing that could happen in a WooCommerce migration process is losing all your precious eCommerce data. Always ensure to back up your eCommerce data to avoid this from happening. WooCommerce Post-migration Checklist Pre-migration checklist deals with the measures you need to take before the WooCommerce migration. In contrast, the post-migration checklist includes everything you need to do after the migration. DNS Entry Update Make sure to update the DNS entry soon after the migration process. If you don’t, your customers may get redirected to your old store. Test The New Store After the DNS update, you must check whether your new website or online store is working as it should. Check all the pages and functionalities before going live. Test External Links Ensure that all your old URLs point to the new one. Use the search and replace operation to redirect internal links and direct them to new ones to avoid server overload.   SEO Optimization The final item of the post-migration checklist is to optimize your SEO for the Google search engine. It also includes submitting your new site and ensuring that the search engine bots can easily crawl it. What are the Challenges in WooCommerce Migration? headings: Is Shopify Good for Web Development?
Know more about how Shopify can help power your eCommerce business
Still debating if to choose Shopify for your eCommerce business?
Why Choose Shopify for Your Website?
Still confused if and how to choose Shopify as your platform?
Why Choose Virtina for Your Shopify Needs?
Virtina can help set up an unparalleled eCommerce shopping experience for your clients powered by Shopify.
text: Introduction So, wondering, “what exactly is Shopify?” An easy-to-use eCommerce platform where anyone can set up a website to start selling their products easily – that is Shopify for you in a nutshell.  Shopify is a powerful eCommerce platform that allows you to set up and manage your online store. It’s also one of the easiest ways to build a website, so it’s well worth checking out if you’re looking for an alternative to WooCommerce or other popular platforms. We hope the details we furnish below help you get started with building your Shopify website ! The first obvious question to pop up in your mind would be: Can Shopify produce a good website? If done right, Shopify can create a perfect website with impeccable features. The Canadian platform helps businesses of all sizes through its online platforms –  Shopify and Shopify POS.  Since it is user-friendly, it has slowly emerged as one of the leading eCommerce platforms globally. It has extensive reach, expanding to 175 countries with hundreds of thousands of merchants using it. Well-known brands, including Tesla, Red Bull, and The Oatmeal, use Shopify to support their websites. Is Shopify Good for Web Development? Shopify is an excellent option for eCommerce . It gives merchants complete admin control. You can make it look and feel the way you like. Building a Website on Shopify If you want to build a website quickly and easily, Shopify is a great choice. If you want to host your own store, then Shopify is an excellent choice. And if all that isn’t enough…well, there are plenty of other benefits as well! Here’s what we’re talking about: You can use the same platform for eCommerce and non-eCommerce projects with no extra software or plugins (except maybe PayPal). You can use any theme from the hundreds of free ones available online. Shopify and eCommerce Shopify has had a significant impact on the eCommerce industry. The platform has made it easier for businesses to set up and manage online stores. Shopify is great for selling products because of its excellent customization capabilities. It is also favored for having complete admin controls. It offers users a customizable platform, an easy-to-use checkout process, and a wide range of features. Shopify has also helped to lower the barriers to entry for new businesses, making it easier for them to get started in the eCommerce industry. Know more about how Shopify can help power your eCommerce business Talk to Experts All this hype about Shopify is bound to naturally make you think: How much is it going to cost me? What exactly are my options? Shopify Plans – Comparison, Pricing Shopify is a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform — which means you cannot own a copy of the software but use it by paying a monthly or annual fee. Shopify packages are broadly classified into two – Shopify and Shopify Plus . Both have the same core offering concerning dashboards and eCommerce functionality. The main difference is that Shopify Plus offers more flexibility, support options, and access to a store’s underlying code. Let us get to know them in detail. Shopify Plus is the most expensive plan and the only one with unlimited pages, websites, and apps. However, this comes at a cost: $2,000 per month (with no discounts). If you want to use all three features at once—pages, websites, and apps—you’ll need to pay for Shopify Plus. Shopify Plans Currently, there are 4 Shopify plans you should be aware of differentiated based on the payment plan. Shopify plans are all pretty similar, but there are a few differences you should be aware of. Shopify Advanced is still expensive at $299 per month but has extensive features. If you have a large enterprise, you might as well choose this package. It has an inbuilt custom report builder, allows 15 staff accounts, and has the lowest transaction fees.  Shopify Plan is the middle man – charging $79 per month, it has enough features to cover most of the advanced company requirements. It enables professional reporting, five staff accounts, and better shipping discounts. Shopify Basic is the least expensive option by far in terms of the monthly fee: $29/month. It allows you to pull basic reports and gives two staff accounts. But if your business doesn’t need any extra services beyond what’s included with this plan (which includes custom domains), then there’s no reason not to go with it! Shopify Starter is the starter pack, as the name suggests. It gives you a feel of what the software is about and only costs about $5 per month. But if you already have a successful online eCommerce business but think it lacks functionality and support – don’t you worry! You have the option to migrate to Shopify from your existing platform . Shopify Migration If you need more scalability, security, a robust ecosystem, and easy product management for your store, we suggest you migrate to Shopify from your current platform. Shopify migration process includes: Importing data from other platforms (i.e., Google Analytics) Importing products, categories, and other data from your existing eCommerce platform Importing customers and orders from your existing eCommerce platform Importing product images, product variants, and product attributes Shopify only requires minimum developer assistance to maintain a store. It has a wide range of features, functionalities, add-ons, and apps. Shopify has uncomplicated security and hosting infrastructure. Do you need any more reasons to choose Shopify now?! We can tell you more! Still debating if to choose Shopify for your eCommerce business? Know More Why Choose Shopify for Your Website? Shopify offers users a wide range of features and benefits, making it a popular choice for those looking to build an online store. However, like any platform, Shopify has its advantages and disadvantages that you should be aware of before using it to build your eCommerce store. Advantages of Shopify Platform Ease of Use: One of the biggest advantages of Shopify is that it is extremely easy to use. Even if you have no prior experience with website development or design, you will be able to create a beautiful and functional online store using Shopify. The platform’s simple interface and drag-and-drop features make it easy to add products, customize your store’s design, and more. Affordable: Another great advantage of Shopify is that it is very reasonable. Three different pricing plans are available, all of which are reasonably priced. Plus, there are no transaction fees if you use Shopify Payments (the platform’s own payment processor). Lots of Features: Despite being very easy to use, Shopify is packed with features. Some of the most popular features include the ability to offer discounts, gift cards, and abandoned cart recovery. There is also a vast app store with over 2,000 apps that you can use to add even more functionality to your store. Excellent Support: If you ever run into any problems while using Shopify, you can rest assured knowing that their superb support team will be there to help you out. The support team is available 24/7 via phone, email, and live chat. Mobile-friendly: In today’s day and age, websites need to be mobile-friendly. Luckily, all Shopify themes are automatically responsive , meaning they will look great on all devices, from desktop computers to mobile phones. Scalability: Shopify is a very scalable platform, perfect for businesses expecting to grow their online presence in the future. As your business grows, you can easily upgrade your Shopify plan to accommodate your new needs. Limitations of Shopify Platform Limited Customization Options: Even though many great themes are available for Shopify stores, the overall customization options are still quite limited compared to other ecommerce platforms such as WooCommerce. This can be a bit restrictive for store owners who want complete control over their online store’s look and feel. Shopify Fees: While the monthly fees for using Shopify are relatively reasonable, additional “transaction fees” are charged on each sale made through your online store. These transaction fees can range from 2% to 0.5%, depending on which Shopify pricing plan you choose. Requires Some Technical Knowledge: Even though Shopify is designed to be easy to use, it still requires some basic technical knowledge to get the most out of it. For example, you’ll need to know how to use HTML and CSS to customize your online store’s look and feel. Limited Payment Options: Shopify currently only supports a limited number of payment options, which can be a problem for store owners who want to offer their customers more options. No Phone Support: One of the biggest disadvantages of using Shopify is that they do not offer phone support. This can be a problem if you run into any technical issues with your online store or have any questions that need to be answered quickly. Before making an educated decision, it is always best to compare the product you are going to pay for with their biggest competitor(s). That is what we have done for you – to make things easier for you! eCommerce Platforms Comparison Shopify Vs. WooCommerce Two platforms stand out above the rest when setting up an online store: Shopify and WooCommerce. Both platforms have unique benefits and drawbacks, so it’s essential to compare them side-by-side to see the best fit for your needs. Shopify is a turn-key eCommerce solution that lets you set up an online store in minutes. Shopify handles all of the technical aspects of running an online store, so you can focus on selling your products. WooCommerce is an open-source e-commerce WordPress plugin that turns your WordPress website into an eCommerce store. WooCommerce is an excellent option for businesses that already have a WordPress website and want to add eCommerce functionality. When comparing Shopify and WooCommerce, it’s essential to consider the following factors: Ease of Use: Shopify is designed to be easy to use, even for businesses with no technical experience. WooCommerce is a bit more complex but can be easily mastered with a little time and effort. Features: Shopify offers a wide range of features to help you run your online store, while WooCommerce is more customizable but has fewer built-in features. Pricing: Shopify’s pricing is subscription-based, while WooCommerce is a free plugin with optional paid extensions. Overall, Shopify is the better choice for businesses that want an easy-to-use platform with plenty of features. At the same time, WooCommerce is better suited for companies that need more customization and control. Still confused if and how to choose Shopify as your platform? We Can Help Now we can delve into how a Shopify development company aids in creating unique eCommerce websites. These are some of the services software engineering companies like Virtina can provide.  Shopify Development Plan A good Shopify development plan will take into account your budget, timeframe, and desired features. It is important to balance these three factors to ensure that your website is built successfully and within your budget. Shopify development services can vary depending on the size and complexity of your project. However, there are some basic services that all Shopify developers should provide. Shopify Development Services The process of developing a Shopify website can vary depending on the size and scope of the project. Shopify Website Consultation The first step is to consult with a Shopify development company like Virtina to discuss your project requirements. During this phase, the developer team will get to know your business and needs with multiple in-depth discussions with your representatives. This step is important to create a custom solution that meets your specific needs. Shopify Website Planning / Architecture Once the consultation phase is complete, our Shopify experts will create a plan for your project. This plan will detail the steps needed to complete your project successfully. Shopify Design Development The next step is to design the look and feel of your website – including building a custom website theme that fits your brand and style. It means creating the overall layout, choosing colors and font styles, and adding images and other visual elements. This phase aims to create a website that reflects your brand identity and provides a positive user experience. Shopify Theme Development Virtina’s Shopify Theme Development process involves a Shopify developer creating a custom theme for your website. We understand your business needs and goals, design a custom theme that meets those requirements, and code the theme to work with Shopify’s platform. Shopify Website Development After the design phase is complete, the development team will begin building the actual website. This process includes coding the site’s front end, setting up back-end functionality, and integrating Shopify’s eCommerce platform . Shopify Website Testing Once the website is built, it will need to be tested to ensure everything is working correctly. This step includes testing the functionality of the site, as well as the usability. Shopify Website Launch Once everything has been tested and is working correctly, your website will be launched and made live. You can then start selling products and processing orders through your Shopify store. Congratulations on launching your new Shopify website! Why Choose Virtina for Your Shopify Needs? Virtina is a Shopify expert in every sense of the word. We deal with every aspect of your website development.  Time: The time needed is entirely variable. It will depend on your customization needs, product requirements, and website size. But most projects follow a similar general timeline, and we promise the best and fastest services in the industry. Price: We offer the most reasonable pricing for Shopify in the U.S. market and globally. Pricing will depend on the complexity, duration, size of the team, and expertise applied to the project.  Resources: We are unlike any other generic agency in the market. We engineer your Shopify site to your satisfaction. We have been in the industry for years and have a unique, seasoned team that can work with you to produce astounding results.  Process: We have a transparent process. We sit down to understand your needs, discuss the ideas with you, form a strategy, and then deploy our best team. We focus on the project and provide periodic updates during all steps leading to completion.  If you need help with any phase of the development process, our team of Shopify experts at Virtina can assist you. Virtina can help set up an unparalleled eCommerce shopping experience for your clients powered by Shopify. text: Summary Choosing a gun store eCommerce platform in 2026 usually comes down to a firearms-friendly general platform (BigCommerce, WooCommerce or Adobe Commerce) and a firearms-specific platform such as Gearfire, AmmoReady or coreOUTDOOR. Shopify is a poor fit because Shopify Payments does not process firearm sales. Whatever you pick, the legal rules are the same: online firearm sales ship to a licensed dealer (FFL), where the buyer completes Form 4473 in person and passes a background check. Your platform’s job is to make that process smooth, not to replace it. 2026 shortlist at a glance Allows firearms: BigCommerce WooCommerce Adobe Commerce Gearfire, AmmoReady, coreOUTDOOR Check terms first: Shift4Shop Avoid for firearms: Shopify Introduction Selling firearms online is legal in the US, but few industries have as many moving parts, which is why picking the right gun store eCommerce platform matters so much. Payment processors can drop you, some platforms ban the category outright, and every sale has to be routed through a licensed dealer. We first published this guide in 2022 and have updated it for 2026. It corrects some common misunderstandings about online compliance, covers the two ATF proposals published in May 2026, and compares the platforms gun stores actually use today. Table of Contents What changed for online gun stores in 2026? How does an online gun sale actually work? Which eCommerce platforms allow firearms? BigCommerce WooCommerce Adobe Commerce (Magento) Firearms-specific platforms: Gearfire, AmmoReady, coreOUTDOOR Shift4Shop Can you sell guns on Shopify? Flxpoint, GunBroker and multichannel selling How do you take payments for firearms? Which gun store eCommerce platform should you choose? What changed for online gun stores in 2026? Three things matter most this year: ATF proposed shorter record retention. Since 2022, dealers have had to keep Forms 4473 and most acquisition and disposition records until they go out of business. A May 2026 proposed rule would cut that to 20 or 30 years. It is not final yet, so keep following the current rule. ATF proposed a revised Form 4473. A second May 2026 proposal would simplify the form, allow software to pre-fill more fields, and extend how long a completed form and background check stay valid. The buyer would still complete it in person at the dealer. Payments remain the biggest risk. Mainstream processors still restrict firearms, so a platform that locks you into its own payment service can put your store at risk. How does an online gun sale actually work? Many guides, including earlier versions of this one, suggest that Form 4473 can be built into an online checkout. It cannot. The form is completed at the receiving dealer’s premises, not at the point of sale. STEP 1 Order online Buyer pays on your site and picks a receiving FFL dealer. STEP 2 Ship to the FFL You ship to the dealer, never to the buyer’s home. STEP 3 4473 + NICS Buyer completes Form 4473 in person and the dealer runs the background check. STEP 4 Pickup If approved, the dealer transfers the firearm to the buyer. Electronic Forms 4473 are allowed, but only when completed in person at the dealer, as FastBound explains . What your store can automate is everything around the transfer: letting buyers choose a receiving FFL at checkout, collecting and verifying that dealer’s license, keeping firearms and accessories in separate shipments, and blocking items that cannot be sold into the buyer’s state. For the full process, see our guide on how to sell guns online . Which eCommerce platforms allow firearms? Here is how the main options compare for a US gun store in 2026. Always confirm current terms with the platform and your payment processor before you build. Platform Firearms allowed? Payments Best for BigCommerce Yes Choose a firearms-friendly gateway Hosted store with FFL apps WooCommerce Yes, self-hosted Any compatible gateway Full control and custom rules Adobe Commerce Yes, self-hosted Any compatible gateway Large catalogs and B2B Gearfire, AmmoReady, coreOUTDOOR Built for firearms Firearms merchant services offered Dealers wanting an all-in-one system Shift4Shop Historically yes Free plan requires Shift4 Payments Low-cost start, check terms Shopify Restricted Shopify Payments does not allow firearms Not recommended for guns BigCommerce BigCommerce allows legal firearm sales and does not charge transaction fees, which makes it the most popular hosted option for gun stores. You connect a firearms-friendly payment gateway of your choice. FFL checkout apps let buyers pick a receiving dealer and capture license details No platform lock-in on payments, unlike Shopify Hosted and managed , so you do not maintain servers Good for stores that want a hosted platform without the Shopify payment problem. See our BigCommerce development services . WooCommerce WooCommerce is self-hosted on WordPress, so there is no platform owner that can ban your category. You choose your hosting and payment processor, and you can build any compliance rule you need. FFL dealer selection plugins add a dealer picker to checkout Custom rules for state restrictions, age checks and split shipments Strong content and SEO through WordPress The trade-off is responsibility: you, or your agency, handle hosting, security and updates. See our WooCommerce development services . Adobe Commerce (Magento) Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento) is self-hosted or cloud-hosted and has no category restrictions of its own. It suits larger retailers and distributors with big catalogs, complex pricing or B2B accounts. It is the most powerful option here, and the most expensive to build and run. See our Magento development services . Firearms-specific platforms: Gearfire, AmmoReady, coreOUTDOOR These platforms are built only for the firearms industry, so FFL workflows, distributor feeds and firearms merchant services come ready to use. Gearfire . A platform founded by FFL dealers, offering eCommerce, point of sale and merchant services. AmmoReady . A firearms eCommerce platform with distributor integrations and automation for listings and pricing. coreOUTDOOR . An all-in-one system from Coreware covering storefront, point of sale, inventory and payments. The benefit is speed: much of the firearms-specific plumbing is already done. The trade-off is less design freedom and tighter dependence on one vendor. Ask each for current pricing, contract terms and how easily you can export your data if you leave. Shift4Shop Shift4Shop (formerly 3dcart) has historically accepted firearms retailers and offers a free plan for US merchants who process payments through Shift4. Because that plan ties you to one processor, confirm in writing that Shift4 will accept your firearms products before you launch. Can you sell guns on Shopify? Not for firearms, in practice. Shopify bans some firearm products outright, and Shopify Payments does not allow firearm sales at all . That forces you onto a third-party gateway, adds Shopify’s extra transaction fee, and leaves your store exposed to future policy changes. Shopify can work for accessory-only stores, such as apparel or cleaning supplies, but gun stores are safer on a platform they control. For a wider look at both platforms, see our Shopify vs WooCommerce comparison. Flxpoint, GunBroker and multichannel selling Flxpoint is not a storefront. It is an automation layer that syncs inventory, routes orders to distributors and pushes listings to channels such as GunBroker. Many gun stores pair it with BigCommerce or WooCommerce to sell a large distributor catalog without managing stock by hand. How do you take payments for firearms? Payment processing is the most common reason gun stores get shut down online. Before you choose a platform: Work with a processor that explicitly accepts firearms and ammunition Avoid platforms that force their own payment service Keep clear records of your FFL, age and state compliance, because underwriters will ask Have a backup processor ready Our guide to what underwriters check before approving a regulated store covers this in detail. Which gun store eCommerce platform should you choose? If you… Consider Want a hosted store and full payment choice BigCommerce Want full control, custom rules and strong content WooCommerce Run a large catalog, B2B or distribution Adobe Commerce Want firearms features out of the box Gearfire, AmmoReady or coreOUTDOOR Need the lowest possible start-up cost Shift4Shop, after confirming terms Need something built around your store? We design and build custom gun store websites on WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Magento. Read about our gun store eCommerce services . People also ask Can you sell guns online legally? Yes, in the US, as long as every firearm ships to a licensed dealer who completes the transfer, including Form 4473 and a background check, and you follow state laws. Can a customer fill out Form 4473 online? No. The buyer completes Form 4473 in person at the dealer that receives the firearm. Dealers may use an electronic version, but only on their premises. What is the best platform for a small gun shop? BigCommerce or a firearms-specific platform such as Gearfire is usually quickest. WooCommerce is a strong choice if you want full control and plan to grow content. Related firearms ecommerce guides This page compares the platforms. For the compliance and process side, read our guides on selling firearms online and how to sell guns online . Payments are the hardest part of a firearms store, so see how underwriters assess a regulated store in merchant account underwriting and compare gateways in our guide to high-risk payment processing . If you need a tailored build, we also cover custom ecommerce solutions for firearm and ammunition retailers . Conclusion The best gun store eCommerce platform in 2026 is one that allows firearms, lets you choose your payment processor, and makes FFL transfers easy for buyers. For most stores that means BigCommerce, WooCommerce or a firearms-specific platform. Shopify is best avoided for firearms. Keep an eye on the two ATF proposals from May 2026. If they become final, they will change how long dealers keep records and how Form 4473 is completed. If you want help choosing or building your store, talk to Virtina. This article is general information, not legal advice. Frequently Asked Questions How long must dealers keep Form 4473 records? Under the current rule, since 2022, dealers must keep Forms 4473 until they go out of business. A May 2026 ATF proposal would change this to 20 or 30 years, but it is not final. Can I ship a gun directly to a customer? No. Firearms bought online must ship to a licensed dealer (FFL) who completes the transfer with the buyer. Does Shopify allow gun sales? Shopify restricts firearms, and Shopify Payments does not allow firearm sales, so it is not recommended for gun stores. Do I need a special payment processor? Yes. Many mainstream processors restrict firearms. Use one that explicitly approves firearms and ammunition merchants. Our guide to high-risk payment processing explains how approval and underwriting work. Is BigCommerce or WooCommerce better for a gun store? BigCommerce is easier because it is hosted. WooCommerce gives more control and no platform owner can restrict your category. Both allow firearms.

text: Summary WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce and Shopify are still the four platforms most growing stores choose between in 2026. WooCommerce gives you the most ownership for the money, Shopify is the fastest to launch, Magento handles the most complex catalogs, and BigCommerce packs the most features into a hosted plan. This guide compares all four on pricing, features, performance, ease of use, scalability, customization, security and SEO, with 2026 pricing and store counts. It also adds two head-to-head sections: Magento vs Shopify and BigCommerce vs Shopify. Introduction If you’re running an eCommerce business, you’ve heard the names WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce and Shopify thrown around. But which one is right for you? Is WooCommerce better than Magento? Is BigCommerce better than Shopify? Finding the right ecommerce platform is like searching for the perfect series on Netflix. There are so many options, the reviews are endless, and nobody can pick the right one for you. Let us help you out a bit here. Table of Contents eCommerce and Platforms What Changed in 2026 WooCommerce Vs. Magento Vs. BigCommerce Vs. Shopify Comparison: An Introduction WooCommerce: The Popular Kid in Town Magento: Worth the Hype BigCommerce: Big Reputation Shopify: Simplified Business Comparison in Detail: Eight Commanding Factors Magento vs Shopify BigCommerce vs Shopify: Which Is Better in 2026? Virtina’s Verdict Final Takeaway Summing It Up Frequently Asked Questions eCommerce and Platforms In 2025, US online sales reached a record $1.234 trillion , up 5.4% from the year before and 23.1% of all US retail sales. With immense possibilities opening up in the eCommerce arena , finding the best platform for your eCommerce store is a pressing decision. Half your work is done once you make the right choice. With that in mind, we’ve put together a comprehensive guide to help you decide which platform will work best for your online store. In this article, we compare WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce and Shopify to lay out their pros and cons. If you sell groceries, beverages or specialty foods, also see our guide to food and beverage ecommerce platforms . What Changed in 2026 Shopify is a launch partner of Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), announced on 11 January 2026, which gives Shopify stores a head start with AI shopping agents. WooCommerce had no built-in UCP support as of August 2026, so stores that want to sell through AI agents need custom work. See how to make your eCommerce store agent-ready . BigCommerce renamed its plans on 1 June 2026. Standard, Plus, Pro and Enterprise are now Core, Growth, Scale and Performance, and a new Open Payment Provider Fee of 0.6% to 2.0% applies on self-serve plans that use a non-embedded payment gateway. Magento 2.4.9 was released on 12 May 2026, and Magento 2.4.6 left support on 11 August 2026. If you’re on an older version, read our Magento support cliff guide . WooCommerce Vs. Magento Vs. BigCommerce Vs. Shopify Comparison: An Introduction 1. WooCommerce is a free and open-source eCommerce platform built on WordPress. It is the most widely used eCommerce platform, with over 4 million live stores, and it sells physical and digital goods equally well. It suits small businesses as well as larger stores looking to scale. 2. Magento is a free and open-source eCommerce development platform , with a paid enterprise edition called Adobe Commerce. There are more than 100,000 live Magento stores in 2026 . It powers many large retailers and manufacturers and can be customized for almost any business model, though it needs experienced developers. 3. BigCommerce is an online store builder offering a cloud-based, multi-channel solution for growing businesses. It has the features you need to run a successful store, advanced B2B tools, and integrations that let you sell anywhere online. 4. Shopify provides merchants with everything they need to start selling online , including themes, apps and built-in payments through Shopify Payments. It stands out for its easy interface and quick setup. Now, let us get down to the nitty-gritty of each platform. WooCommerce: The Popular Kid in Town WooCommerce is the most popular eCommerce platform, and it adds an online store to your WordPress website. Built on WordPress, it supports thousands of extensions, so there are countless ways to customize your site. Some extensions let you sell products from marketplaces like Amazon or eBay, and a custom WooCommerce plugin can add almost any feature your store needs. WooCommerce has a simple interface for managing products, inventory and shipping, and there is no monthly platform fee. While the plugin is free, there are costs to set up and maintain your site. You’ll need a domain name and a hosting plan. Hosting quality has a big effect on speed and security when running your eCommerce business on WooCommerce . You’ll also need an SSL certificate so shoppers can pay securely, although many hosts now include one free. Premium extensions add features the core plugin doesn’t cover. What you spend depends on your needs, but WooCommerce remains affordable compared with other eCommerce platforms. One gap in 2026: WooCommerce has no built-in support yet for Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, so selling through AI shopping agents takes custom work. Also Read: Customizing WooCommerce: Developing Unique Themes and Extensions Salient Features of WooCommerce Platform Build your store with WordPress blocks and themes. Sell physical, digital, subscription and bookable products. Connect payment gateways such as WooPayments, PayPal, Stripe and Authorize.net. Easy to use if you know WordPress, with no coding needed for day-to-day tasks. Flexible costs with no platform subscription. You pay only for hosting and the extensions you choose. Advantages of Using WooCommerce Platform Easy interface Free WordPress plugin with access to the whole WordPress ecosystem Complete data control Access to thousands of store designs Rich in features High security when hosted and maintained well Makes SEO easy Fast loading speed on good hosting Disadvantages of Using WooCommerce Platform Additional costs for setting up and maintaining the site You need to buy a domain name and hosting plan Premium extensions add up No built-in UCP support yet for AI shopping agents Need help to build a WooCommerce store from the ground up? Let’s Discuss Magento: Worth the Hype Magento is a robust eCommerce platform that has become a favorite among developers and large businesses. It comes in two versions: Magento Open Source, which you can download and use for free, and Adobe Commerce, the paid edition. Magento offers a number of advanced features , great flexibility and a large community behind it. The latest release, Magento 2.4.9, arrived in May 2026. Magento offers a huge range of extensions and modules that let you tailor your website exactly the way you want. Its search is fast and accurate, so shoppers find products quickly. Magento websites also work well on mobile devices. That matters because most online shoppers browse on their phones, and mobile-friendly sites do better in Google search. A mobile-friendly site also helps with Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO), so you get more conversions from the same traffic. Magento supports customer segmentation and personalization. Segmentation groups customers by needs, preferences or behavior, and personalization uses that data to tailor the shopping experience to each group. Magento’s reporting tools show how your store is performing, so you can track sales, understand customer behavior and spot opportunities. It also integrates with Google Analytics. Built-in marketing and promotions features let you run discounts, loyalty offers, coupons, gift cards and campaigns. Magento’s checkout is flexible and supports multiple payment gateways, including PayPal, Stripe and Authorize.net. Also Read: A Guide to Optimizing Your Magento Store for Peak Performance Salient Features of Magento Platform Built-in eCommerce features to sell physical and digital products. A wide range of payment methods and gateways. Advanced B2B features in Adobe Commerce, including company accounts, quotes and custom pricing. An excellent catalog management system for large, complex catalogs. Multi-store, multi-language and multi-currency support from one admin. Strong shipping and fulfillment features. Advantages of Using Magento Platform Amazing flexibility Unique features other platforms lack Extensive community support Mobile-friendly, headless-ready storefronts Insane scalability Disadvantages of Using Magento Platform One of the most expensive to build and run Smaller, more specialized developer community Time-consuming setup process Needs powerful hosting Regular version upgrades to stay supported Looking for guidance to set up a Magento store that matches your vision? Learn More BigCommerce: Big Reputation BigCommerce is a leading SaaS eCommerce platform that helps online retailers of all sizes set up stores, manage inventory, grow sales and engage customers. It includes more features out of the box than most hosted platforms, with no transaction fees on its embedded payments. BigCommerce provides a variety of plans to suit your needs. In 2026 they are called Core, Growth, Scale and Performance. Even the entry plan includes unlimited products, coupons and discount codes, one-page checkout and real-time shipping rates. Every BigCommerce store includes a responsive storefront, PCI compliance, SEO tools and site reporting, so you can build your online presence with confidence. The BigCommerce App Marketplace offers hundreds of apps and integrations, from inventory and customer service tools to payment services such as Stripe and Braintree. You can add advanced features as your needs grow. BigCommerce also makes multi-channel selling easy. You can manage sales on Facebook, Instagram, Google, Amazon and other marketplaces from one back end. Also Read: Maximizing ROI with Custom BigCommerce Theme Development: Strategies for Success Salient Features of BigCommerce Platform Unlimited products: unlimited products and categories with flexible templates. Abandoned cart recovery: automatic emails when a shopper leaves items in the cart. One-page checkout: shoppers buy on a single page instead of several steps. Real-time shipping rates: live quotes from major carriers at checkout. BigCommerce integrations: hundreds of apps for marketing, ERP, payments and more. See how it compares with WooCommerce and Shopify . Selling on multiple channels: connect to Amazon, eBay, Walmart and other marketplaces. Selling in multiple languages: localized storefronts for international customers. Security: SSL, PCI compliance and a secure payment gateway included. Native B2B features: customer groups, price lists, quotes and bulk ordering. SEO tools: editable URLs, meta data and reporting to help pages rank. Show Me How Shopify: Simplified Business Shopify is a cloud-based SaaS selling platform with a wide range of themes and apps for building an online store. It supports many languages and currencies, and Shopify is one of the best eCommerce platforms for beginners because it’s easy to use, has a massive selection of templates and integrations, and includes strong marketing tools. Shopify stores shine because of the Shopify App Store, where free and paid apps make your store more functional and attractive. There is also a large selection of free and paid themes, so you can make your store look the way you want. Payments are simple. Shopify Payments accepts all major cards and wallets with no extra transaction fee, and Shopify POS lets you sell in person from the same admin. Shopify store development is popular because of low startup costs, an accessible interface and easily customizable themes. Hosting, security and software updates are handled for you, and you can sell unlimited products. In 2026, Shopify is also a launch partner of Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, which helps stores get found and sold through AI shopping agents. Quick to set up and use, even with zero technical know-how. Abandoned cart reminders to win back lost customers. Responsive themes that make startup and small business stores pop. Unlimited bandwidth and storage, which matters as you scale. Shopify POS for in-person sales. WooCommerce comes second, with strong performance for most business sizes as long as you choose the right hosting provider. BigCommerce handles high traffic loads easily and is next in line. We’ve covered how these platforms differ, from features and pricing to ease of use and scalability, plus the 2026 changes that matter. Use this as your go-to guide when you’re ready to decide. If you’re ready to get started with any of these platforms, talk to Virtina , or check out our other articles . Frequently Asked Questions What are eCommerce platforms? eCommerce platforms are software applications that let merchants sell online and shoppers buy. Shoppers use them to discover products, add them to a cart, pay and check out. Businesses use them to list, display, track and sell products and collect payments. How have eCommerce platforms evolved over the years? eCommerce started as mail and telephone ordering in the 1970s and 80s and grew into today’s online model: marketplaces like Amazon and Alibaba, and brand websites. In 2026, AI shopping agents in tools like ChatGPT and Google are the newest channel. What are the different types of eCommerce platforms? There are three main types: SaaS (software-as-a-service, like Shopify and BigCommerce), PaaS (platform-as-a-service), and on-premise or self-hosted platforms that you run with your own team (like WooCommerce and Magento Open Source). What important factors should I consider while choosing the right platform for my eCommerce website? We look at ten criteria: affordable pricing, strong security, SEO support, responsive design, omnichannel selling, integrations and plugins, tech support, scalability, customization and load speed. In 2026, add readiness for AI shopping agents. How do I set up an eCommerce platform for my company? Start by defining your business goals, then research and choose a platform. Work with the provider or an expert agency to set it up, then customize it with themes, plugins and integrations to match your goals. What is the need for different platforms for different business sizes? Requirements change with company size. Large companies need highly customizable, stable platforms that handle heavy traffic and payment volumes. Mid-size businesses need scalable, flexible options. Small businesses usually do best with a hosted platform that covers the basics. Can you bring out the differences between BigCommerce and WooCommerce? BigCommerce is a hosted platform that runs your whole store. WooCommerce is an open-source WordPress plugin that adds eCommerce to a WordPress site you host yourself. Both offer many templates and designs, but WooCommerce has the larger community and more control, while BigCommerce includes more features out of the box. How would Shopify compare to WooCommerce? Shopify has set monthly pricing and handles hosting for you. WooCommerce is free but comes with hosting, domain and security costs, and gives you full control. Shopify is simpler for start-ups, while WooCommerce suits stores that want flexibility and content-led SEO. Read our full Shopify vs WooCommerce guide. Could you list out the pros and cons of Magento and Shopify? If you compare Shopify vs. Magento, Shopify is the more affordable and easier option, with a polished app store. Magento offers more extensions, deeper customization and stronger B2B features, but you need developers to install and maintain them. Which is better of the two platforms – Magento or WooCommerce? WooCommerce is user-friendly and low-cost, and suits small to medium stores. Magento offers more performance and B2B depth for enterprises, at a steeper cost and with expert developers needed for customization. Read our full Magento vs WooCommerce guide. Is Shopify or BigCommerce cheaper in 2026? Their plans cost the same: $39, $105 and $399 a month, or $29, $79 and $299 billed yearly. Real costs differ through payment gateway fees, apps, and BigCommerce’s yearly sales thresholds. Is Magento still worth it in 2026? Yes, for large or complex B2B stores that need full control. Stores on Magento 2.4.6 or older should plan an upgrade to 2.4.9 or a replatform, because 2.4.6 left support on 11 August 2026. Which eCommerce platform is best for small businesses in 2026? Shopify is the easiest to launch. WooCommerce is the best value if you already use WordPress and want full control of your content and data. Which eCommerce platform is best for AI shopping agents? Shopify has the head start as a launch partner of Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol. WooCommerce and Magento stores can get ready with clean product data, schema and custom UCP work. Can I switch eCommerce platforms without losing SEO? Yes. A planned migration keeps your URLs or 301-redirects them, and moves products, customers and orders. Virtina has completed more than 2,500 eCommerce projects, including platform migrations. Virtina builds and supports stores on WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce and Shopify, which is why this comparison doesn’t push one platform for everyone.

The WooCommerce plugin has been downloaded 161,908,802 times so far from WordPress.org  WooCommerce powers approximately 3,876,748 websites the world over 40% of all the websites use WordPress WooCommerce leads with 23.43% of the total world market share 12.96% of eCommerce websites on the internet use WooCommerce WooCommerce plugin supports 66 languages With all these features comes a steep learning curve if you want to take advantage of everything you can do with it. Be aware of the best and worst of WooCommerce before you start.  Is WooCommerce the platform for your eCommerce store? Find Out More Advantages of WooCommerce 1. Free and Open Source WooCommerce is free and open source. You can download it right from the WordPress plugin directory and use it without charge. 2. Limitless Customization and Scalability WooCommerce is highly customizable . You can easily create your product catalog, calculate shipping costs, send a confirmation email after purchase, etc. It is also very scalable and has low shop costs. 3. High Security for Site and Payments WooCommerce is known for its security options. It is pretty hard to break into your site if used right. The platform also integrates payment options like Paypal, Stripe, and even COD to give your customers a faultless checkout experience. Easy Integration Another great thing about WooCommerce is that you can integrate it with almost any other service since it works on top of WordPress’ REST API. title: WordPress 6.0 Arturo: Leafing Through the Improved and Advanced Features

text: Have you guys heard the buzz lately? WordPress 6.0 “Arturo” is here and how! It is the new kid in town, the latest WordPress release. It is named after Arturo O’Farrill , the Grammy-winning jazz musician, known for his influence on Afro Cuban and contemporary Latin jazz. It was released to the public on 24 May 2022. If you are an expert in WordPress development , this very jazzy version is touted to help you unleash your creative spirits and aid in an intuitive site-building experience. The new version was realized through the contribution through enhancements and fixes from over 500 WordPress community members across 58 countries. Table of Contents WordPress as a Platform WordPress 6.0 “Arturo” How to Download Version 6.0? What is New in WordPress 6.0 Update? 1.Improved Performance 2.Enhanced Accessibility 3.Superior Writing Experience 4. Style Switching 5. Five New Template Choices 6. Integrated Patterns 7. Extra Design Tools 8. Easy List View 9. Block Locking Controls Things to Consider Before You Upgrade to WordPress 6.0 WordPress 6.0 – Final Note WordPress as a Platform WordPress is known to power more than 42% of the world’s websites and we don’t think they are going to slow down anytime soon! Josepha Haden Chomphosy, Executive Director of WordPress, reminisces that the new release is an example of the WordPress community’s commitment at tackling tough situations as a single unit. The version’s planned writing experience updates, enhanced block functionality, addition of intuitive style switcher etc. makes it a proud achievement for the company. WordPress 6.0 “Arturo” WordPress 6.0 is the second major release from the platform in 2022. It is armed with more than 1000 changes – both enhancements and bug fixes. We are sure this version would be a delight to work with for developers and business owners globally. The database version (db_version in wp_options) for version 6.0 is updated to 51917, and the Trac revision to 53445. How to Download Version 6.0? The new version can be downloaded automatically from the Dashboard > Updates menu in your site’s admin area or visit the release archive on the WordPress website. The step-by-step instructions to install and update the new version is available on the WordPress site under the “Updating WordPress” tab. What is New in WordPress 6.0 Update? Why is this version important for your business? Or is it relevant for you? Read on to find out. It is said to have more than 1000 delightful changes up its arsenal and we would be more than obliged to list out some of the most important ones for your reference and ease of use. So here we go! 1.Improved Performance This new release is focused on improving the performance of WordPress sites. There are several updates and enhancements that aid in the process. They cover a large range of areas including improved page speed and post load speed, caching, reducing query execution time, navigation menus and the like. 2.Enhanced Accessibility WordPress believes in fostering an inclusive community and has all kinds of users around the world. This fact makes accessibility an important part of the WordPress mission. WordPress has dedicated around 50 updates in the latest variant focusing just on accessibility of the platform. 3.Superior Writing Experience The latest version has writing enhancements meant for every purpose – be it creating a shiny new post or adding or deleting from the existing content. It helps you streamline your creative process with the below features. Tag clouds and social icons are more appealing with updated settings and controls For quick access to recent posts and pages, just type two open brackets `[[` Texts can be selected across multiple blocks for easy copy and paste Create customized buttons that retain their style customizations Preserve existing style changes when transforming blocks 4. Style Switching Try out new style variations in block themes. You get to switch the look and feel of your sitre within a single theme. In some cases, you can change both available settings and style options with just a few clicks of your mouse. You could change minute options like font weight and default color palette. 5. Five New Template Choices WordPress 6.0 has 5 new template options for block themes, namely, author, category, date, tag and taxonomy (Refer below picture for clarity). Content creators gain more flexibility with these additional changes. You can tailor these templates with the tools that exist in your kitty. The below options are added advantages of the new variant. The query blocks supports multiple author filtering, customer taxonomies and other customizations Discover new layout options with patterns and templates that the quick inserter shows to help you work faster during editing at the root or between blocks Cover block can display featured images Featured image sizing controls make getting results a cakewalk 6. Integrated Patterns Patterns are available in more locations like the quick inserter or while creating a new header or footer. If you are a block theme author, you can use `theme.json` to register patterns from the Pattern Directory. This will help you prioritize specific patterns that are most helpful to your theme users. 7. Extra Design Tools Each new WordPress release comes out with powerful and intuitive design tools and this one is no different. The additional features are below. The gap support functionality in the Gallery block can be used to create different looks, from adding spacing to removing spacing altogether between images Group block allows controlling of gaps, margins, typography, and more on a collection of blocks, at once Set the border to your liking with the new border controls The new color panel design saves space by showing all the options at a glance You get more creative color options with the color transparency levelsSwitch between stack, row, and group variations to position groups of blocks with more layout flexibility 8. Easy List View The new keyboard shortcuts enables users to the following. Select multiple blocks from the list view Modify blocks in bulk Drag and drop blocks within the list Easily open and close List View Expand to the current selection whenever they select a block 9. Block Locking Controls WordPress version 6.0 allows you to lock your blocks. You get to choose to disable the option for moving or removing a block, or both. This simplifies project handover quite a bit and allows clients to be creative without worrying about accidentally breaking something on their site. Things to Consider Before You Upgrade to WordPress 6.0 Run a backup of your site before you switch to the new version Make sure nothing is broken on your site before the upgrade Watch the brief overview and how-to videos on the site to understand the major features Join interactive learning sessions on the website for specific topics Developers can explore the field guide prior to execution Refer the WordPress 6.0 Release Notes for comprehensive information WordPress 6.0 – Final Note We would suggest that online store owners and administrators should upgrade to the newest version to take full advantage of the myriad stability, performance, and usability enhancements at the earliest possible time. WordPress content creators will be ecstatic about the new suite of features geared toward improving their designing and writing experiences.
