title: Top WooCommerce Payment Gateways for WordPress
headings: Why are Easy WooCommerce Payment  Methods Consequential for eCommerce?
Do you want to understand why payment gateways are essential for your eCommerce?
Are you looking to integrate an effective payment gateway into your WooCommerce website?
Trying to figure out which payment gateways work best for your business vertical?
How to Evaluate WooCommerce Payment Gateways?
If you feel overwhelmed by the overload of payment gateway choices, we can help customize them
How to Choose the Right WooCommerce Payment Gateway?
text: In today’s digital economy, having a seamless payment process is crucial for any eCommerce store’s success. Yet, for WordPress site owners using WooCommerce, finding the right payment gateway can be overwhelming as a variety of options are available, each with its own set of fees, features, and compatibility issues. A poorly chosen payment gateway not only risks cart abandonment but can also limit sales by excluding preferred payment options. Here, we discuss the top WooCommerce payment gateways for WordPress, comparing each to help you choose the best for your business needs. Whether you’re aiming to expand payment options, lower transaction fees, or ensure the highest security for your customers, this blog will help you. Simplify your decision-making process and equip your WooCommerce store with a payment gateway that drives conversions and customer satisfaction. Why are Easy WooCommerce Payment  Methods Consequential for eCommerce? With the massive hike in online shopping in the past few years and people’s affinity to shop online from the comforts of their homes, eCommerce has taken precedence over traditional retail stores. But with busy schedules, governing lives, the customers are more inclined to abandon their shopping cart at checkout if the payment process is too lengthy, complex, or tedious. Having multiple payment options is also significant as customers leave if they can’t find a way to pay. This phenomenon, called the abandonment of carts, has stumped many popular eCommerce stores. And this is where having a competent payment gateway integrated into your site becomes pertinent. What are Payment Gateways? A payment gateway is an internet-based service commonly incorporated with any eCommerce platform to make a secure channel for transactions. In a nutshell, it is the virtual form of credit or debit card reader. Payment gateways have helped several eCommerce businesses minimize the risk of fraudulent payments. The customer has to fill in basic details like credit or debit card number, expiry date, and CVV to make the payment. Do you want to understand why payment gateways are essential for your eCommerce? Ask Our Experts Why are Payment Gateways Important? The fundamental role of a payment gateway is to aid an easy peasy transaction process between you and your clients. Merchants need approval from a payment gateway to complete transactions and thereby obtain payments. The gateways act as channels through which funds get transferred among banks and financial institutions, supplementing financial transactions across the US economy.  Then there is the big question of secure transactions. No customer ever wants to buy products from a site that doesn’t offer fundamental data and transaction protection. You can instill trust in customers by integrating reputed payment gateways into your online store. Below are reasons that explain why payment gateways are critically essential for your eCommerce business.  1. Protection Against Fraudulent Payments Online transactions are sometimes also referred to as card-not-present payments. This setup payment model can create an opportunity for credit card fraud. Hackers or anyone with your stolen credit card information and personal data can utilize your card to purchase items. The credit card holder and their bank are often left in debt. Online payment gateways have a unique processor that checks the customer’s data via fraud scrubbing technology to prevent cybercrime. Secure payments will ensure customers continue shopping from your site and improve your brand reputation. 2. Accepts All Payment Methods One of the reasons consumers love shopping from eCommerce businesses is that online stores provide them great flexibility regarding when and how they can buy stuff. Payment gateway plugins enable your favorite online store to give you several alternative payment methods. These payment options range from credit cards to debit cards to UPI and net banking transactions. The wide range of choices makes it easier for business owners to satisfy the distinctive demand of their consumer base.  3. Easy Installation and Low Maintenance Since payment gateways are fully automatic plugins, they can be installed and maintained at budget-friendly costs. Most business owners can easily install them, requiring minimal or no coding knowledge. Furthermore, these gateways don’t require frequent maintenance. These gateways have scheduled updates. In addition to this, business owners receive notifications regarding any upgrades to their payment gateway software. 4. Seamless Checkouts The primary reason behind unsuccessful transactions or abandoned carts is a lengthy and slow checkout process. Customers desire a quick, hassle-free checkout to save time and effort. Numerous eCommerce businesses streamline their checkout functions by integrating an efficient payment gateway software. Not only does it provide a secure channel for transactions, but it also reduces the time taken for processing payments.  5. International Transactions You can universally represent your brand through payment gateways. Multiple payment processing plugins allow safe transactions in international currencies. Consequently, customers across the globe gain access to purchase products from your website. This option enables you to grow your eCommerce brand and boost your current sales. Are you looking to integrate an effective payment gateway into your WooCommerce website? We Can Help Top 20 Payment Gateways For WooCommerce WooCommerce is a specifically built eCommerce plugin for WordPress. The eCommerce platform offers its users many features and additional flexibility to add any number of plugins to grow their website. There are more than hundreds of payment gateway options to choose from. Here are the top 20 WooCommerce payment gateways for WordPress.  1. Stripe Launched in the year 2011, Stripe is an American-Irish best payment plugin that severs more than a million consumers. Their central business is to offer Application Programming Interface (APIs) and payment processing plugins to eCommerce merchants. The extension for WooCommerce is free, and the transaction fee is as low as 2.9%+0.30 per purchase. The Stripe WooCommerce extension charges 1% to your account for instant payments and 1% for international payments. Through Stripe, business owners can send invoices, ask for recurring subscriptions, combat fraud, etc. If a particular payment option isn’t available on Stripe, the merchants can utilize the Stripe API to integrate the payment method or customize the code themselves. Stripe makes the checkout process convenient for both business owners and customers.  2. Square Square is the ultimate WooCommerce payment gateway plugin for WordPress. This all-in-one gateway offers you an online payment portal, an in-person payment service, and a money manager. It also provides benefits like appointment scheduling, social media marketing, and a standard POS (point of sale) for traditional offline stores. Square is incredibly user-friendly as the merchant can set up the payment process in a few minutes without having any prior coding skills. Through Square, your eCommerce business can also accept money as membership fees and donations. You can choose from any subscription plan ranging from free, professional, performance, and premium. The premium plan offers a discounted transaction fee of 2.6%+$0.30, while the other three plans charge the standard transaction fee of 2.9%+$0.30. 3. Braintree Braintree is now under PayPal, but it still has some independence in design and offering features to its users. It uses a different interface than PayPal and is available for free. Additionally, its parent company is PayPal. So you can trust its security and reliability. It accepts credit card submissions and provides support for WooCommerce pre-orders and subscriptions. Braintree is considered an advanced and competitive version of PayPal. As for pricing, it charges the same standard transactional fee as other payment gateways, but an ACH direct debit payment costs 0.75% per transaction. 4. Authorize.net CIM Authoroize.net CIM WooCommerce extension is a popularly used payment gateway. Business owners benefit from the various features that this payment processing software offers. It accepts all major debit cards credit cards and efficiently handles tasks such as managing subscriptions, refunds, and pre-orders. Authorize.net CIM permits customers to save their payment details for the next purchase to simplify the transaction process further. Aside from the standard transactional fee, there is a $49 installing fee and a $25 subscription fee.  5. PayPal   Everyone is familiar with how to operate or use PayPal. It is one of the first payment gateways to be introduced online. Although it may not offer your high-tech features like the other payment gateways, it is significantly easy to use and install. This payment processing software comes in two different forms for WooCommerce: Standard PayPal Integration with WooCommerce and PayPal Checkout for WooCommerce. The first option provides a simple, secure channel by merging with the checkout process and adding a PayPal button. The latter offers a convenient opportunity for your consumers by letting them pay directly from the product page.  6. WooCommerce Payments As the name suggests, this payment gateway solution is developed and offered by WooCommerce. Since it is specifically designed for WooCommerce, it naturally caters to all payment processing needs of the eCommerce platform. WordPress dashboard performs the money management and the payment collection. The extension is free to install and charges the standard transaction fee. However, it charges 1% extra for cards issued outside the US. It comes with a dispute management center in the dashboard, and there is an additional $15 fee if consumers lose disputes, such as a chargeback.  7. RazorPay Founded in 2014, RazorPay has rapidly grown as one of India’s best payment gateway providers . It is a user-friendly software that can be easily integrated with your store and be instantly activated to start the transaction process. It provides instant settlements, in-depth insights, and reporting to help business owners make informed financial decisions. The remarkably designed checkout interface fast-tracks the process and tailors a pleasing shopping experience for the consumers.   8. PayU PayU is a Netherlands-based financial tech company founded in the year 2002. However, they launched their payment gateway service nine years later, and since then, it has expanded in 50 plus markets. Several eCommerce businesses from different countries use PayU to process payments. Examples of companies that use PayU are Zoho, Tally, and Shopmatic. It offers more than a hundred payment methods to your clients. Features like responsive designs, API reference, no-hassle integration, and more make PayU a desirable payment gateway for WooCommerce. 9. Amazon Pay This new payment gateway option has opened up many opportunities for enterprises and startups to grow their eCommerce brand. This Woocommerce payment plugin is distinct from others in that it enables consumers to check out from your store by using their Amazon account. It cuts down the unnecessary time taken to complete the checkout process. This ease of shopping will attract new and repeated customers to shop from your store. Moreover, potential customers are more likely to trust your brand if they connect to your store through Amazon. Your store will be safeguarded against any cybercrime under Amazon Pay’s fraud protection. 10. PayFast PayFast extension for WooCommerce enables you to process payments, including deposits, subscriptions, and pre-orders. PayFast stands out amongst its customers because it offers them more flexibility in putting down deposits, placing orders before time, and paying annually, monthly, or weekly. It charges different amounts of transaction fees depending on the amount of the selected payment method. PayFast redirects the consumers to your PayFast merchant account , where they are required to log in and complete the payment process. Once the payment is confirmed, PayFast handles the rest of the process. The consumer then gets redirected to your online store. 11. AfterPay True to its name, AfterPay lets your consumers buy items and pay for them over four interest-free installments. They charge zero application fees and don’t conduct external credit checks to show how much they value the customers. Over 26.7 million customers chose AfterPay as their payment gateway option while shopping online. AfterPay is also available in Europe, but it operates as ClearPay. It protects against fraud and chargebacks, and you can focus on expanding your business. Likewise, as a business owner, you too get paid upfront in a few days for all purchases made using AfterPay.  12. Eway Eway extension for WooCommerce allows your eCommerce business to directly accept credit card payments without redirecting your customer to a third-party site. The payment process from start to finish takes place on your site without the customer leaving. Eway also supports tokenization, which means it lets customers securely save their credit card details in the event they repurchase from your website. This payment gateway also supports other WooCommerce extensions, for example, WooCommerce Refunds API, WooCommerce subscriptions, WooCommerce Bookings, and WooCommerce Memberships. Besides being completely PCI Compliant, Eway also hosts real-time promotional flash sales for online stores. 13. Affirm Affirms offers your consumer a Buy Now Pay Later option that helps convert your potential consumers into frequent buyers. It removes the price barrier by allowing the consumers to pay later for their purchased items. It not only increases your order value but significantly helps your business to grow. They have partnered with approximately 102,000 eCommerce retailers and serve more than 8.7 million customers. The users make the payments in installments without additional compound interest or transactional fees.  14. Klarna Checkout It is a versatile payment gateway app that gives your consumer a top-notch checkout experience and accepts all well-known payment methods like Buy Now Pay Later, Direct Payments, Interest-free installments, and Financing. It has a consumer identification feature that aids in building a loyal client base and increasing your sales. They also offer to protect consumers’ sensitive data and take complete fraud or credit risk for eCommerce sellers. Klarna empowers the buyers by managing their purchases and gives them access to 24/7 customer service through the app. Shoppers are actively looking for eCommerce sites that offer Klarna checkout because customers widely trust the plugin. By integrating this extension to your eCommerce store, your business benefits from the same high reputation by getting heavy traffic on your site.  15. Viva Wallet Viva Wallet offers a robust payment solution. Business owners need to sign up with ViVa wallet to receive a free payment gateway, free debit Mastercard, and an IBAN-enabled local merchant account for their eCommerce business. This extension also streamlines the payment settlement process by settling the amount in your ViVa wallet the very next day. The payment acceptance fees can be set as low as zero percent. There are no hidden or monthly fees. This payment gateway is easy to install and inexpensive. Customers can choose from nine payment method options enabled by the merchants. These options include iDEAL, BitPay, EPS, Giropay, MULTIBANCO, BLIK & PayByLink, WeChat Pay, Sofort, and PayU. 16. Opayo Payment Suite It is an independent payment service provider that both retailers and consumers trust. It offers many payment solutions and incorporates PCI-DSS security into your eCommerce business. It has several fraud screening tools and permits merchants to customize mobile responsive payment pages to enhance shopper conversion and experience. The pricing plans start from £9.99 per month, excluding VAT, making it affordable for your business. The payment suite offers three impeccable payment gateways for your website: Opayo Form, Opayo Direct, and Opayo Pi. All three of these payment gateways are different in terms of their features. Merchants can decide which one to choose based on their individual business needs. 17. SnapScan This payment gateway allows your South African customers to quickly check out by scanning or tapping the credit card details stored on their phones. Customers save time during checkout and have a comfortable shopping experience with your online store. The payment app lets your customers scan the code without leaving your eCommerce site. With the help of SnapScan’s contemporary mobile-friendly design, your targeted audience is one click away from paying for the desired products. 18. Worldpay Worldpay is a highly recommended gateway plugin that allows consumers to pay via a secure, hosted credit card channel. It handles all the payment processes without requiring any SSL certificate. The customer is redirected to Worldpay to make the payment. Once the transaction ends, they get diverted to your website to continue shopping. Worldpay payment gateway services are available worldwide to all eCommerce businesses that need a direct, seamless payment processing extension. Another significant benefit is that Worldpay payment services come at comparatively affordable costs.  19. Mercado Pago Checkout  It is one of the most predominant payment gateways in seven Latin American countries: Argentina, Chile, Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, and Uruguay. It is designed to be built as the best checkout stage for your online store to fulfill your clients’ preferences. From reliable support to avant-garde security abilities, you can count on the Mercado Pago Checkout extension for WooCommerce for any business needs. It offers two types of Checkout:  Transparent Checkout lets you maintain your store’s identity during the process, and the buyer is not redirected to other websites to complete the payment process. Checkout Pro offers payments with PayPal (Brazil and Mexico), saved cards, account balance, and offline payment methods (OXXO, Boleto, etc.) 20. Mollie Mollie payment gateway is Europe’s fastest forehand payment processor. The Mollie for WooCommerce extension gives your customers access to many payment options like Apple Pay, Klarna, and PayPal. It furthermore consists of several local payment methods like SOFORT Banking, EPS, Cartes Bancaires, etc. In less than 15 minutes, you can set up Mollie in any language. This payment processor also provides a personalized mobile dashboard to access real-time data insights and generate quick payouts to maintain the business cash flow. Trying to figure out which payment gateways work best for your business vertical? Let’s Discuss How to Evaluate WooCommerce Payment Gateways? To select a suitable payment gateway for your company, you need to evaluate it on various parameters. Some of them are as below. 1. Payment Methods How many types of payment methods are supported by your payment gateways? What kind of payment methods does the payment gateway offer? These are essential questions you need to ask before selecting a payment gateway. Consumers need to choose from a wide range of options available to them. Most payment gateways allow renowned credit and debit cards like Visa, MasterCard, Amex, etc. With the technology changes, consumers switch from traditional card payments to other payment methods like Apple Pay and GooglePay. The more payment options your gateway offers, the more suitable it is for your business. 2. Pricing Every business has a budget constraint. You need to analyze if you are receiving satisfactory benefits for the amount you’re paying for the extension. One of the most vital criteria you need to consider is your eCommerce business’s total expense. The costs involved in using these payment gateways can be categorized as installing fees, monthly subscription fees, and standard transaction fees. You can choose an affordable payment gateway based on the volume and value of your daily transactions. Most payment gateways have a competitive standard payment transaction fee of 2.9%+$0.30. Please note that higher prices don’t always mean better performances. Try to look for cheaper alternatives with powerful features. 3. Security One thing you cannot compromise while installing your payment gateway is the security factor. Most consumers are hesitant to buy online because they fear online scams. As business owners, it is your responsibility to ensure that your consumer feels safe doing business with you. It is possible by integrating fraud detection and other screening tools into a payment gateway. Ensure that your extension is compliant with PCI-DSS to provide you and consumers with optimal protection against fraudulent payments and sensitive data leaks. 4. Consumer Support Any technical problems with the extension can cause damage to the buyer-seller relationship. While tech issues can happen sometimes, the payment gateway must offer you the highest level of consumer support to resolve them. 24/7 consumer support for 365 days is an outstanding feature in payment gateways. Monetary matters require immediate attention to ease the anxiety of the consumer and the seller. Popular payment gateway extensions for WooCommerce like Stripe, Braintree, and PayPal have excellent community and technical support to tackle any issues that may occur.  If you feel overwhelmed by the overload of payment gateway choices, we can help customize them Contact Us How to Choose the Right WooCommerce Payment Gateway? A simple payment gateway that accepts and processes payments is a safe bet. However, finding a payment gateway that goes above and beyond to satisfy all your criteria is a grueling task. You need to ensure that your payment gateway caters to your business needs, has robust security, accepts international payments, 24/7 consumers, and so on. The best WooCommerce payment gateway is the one that suits you and your eCommerce business’s needs. The above 20 payment gateways have individualistic advantages that benefit your website differently. Recognize your business needs and conduct meticulous research on each payment gateway to choose a suitable one for your business. FAQs Can you use multiple payment gateways for WooCommerce? There are two types of payment gateways sellers can offer to their consumers. The first option is a single payment gateway, and the second is multiple payment gateways. Integrating your eCommerce business to multiple payment gateways plugins can help you effectively facilitate business operations. What should I look for in WooCommerce payment gateways? There are several features you should consider while deciding on WooCommerce payment gateways. However, out of all the other factors, security, merchant onboarding, customer support and experience, international transaction acceptance, and payment methods are critical aspects to consider. How can Virtina help me? Professionals at Virtina have years of experience which makes them aware of the potential of different payment gateways. Virtina also provides services to WooCommerce. Therefore, we know what payment gateway extension works for eCommerce businesses. Talk to our experts to learn more. What are the different payment gateway charges? All payment gateways charge nominal fees for various transaction processes. Some provide it for free; some cost a little less, while some cost you excessive amounts. The payment gateway charges are software, transaction, maintenance, set up price, features, and services offered by the extension and business model. Does Amazon Pay offer more advantages than PayPal? Amazon Pay and PayPal have the same working model, but it offers a set of advantages that PayPal doesn’t. For example, during checkout, the customers are taken through PayPal’s site in the standard version, giving owners lesser control over the process. Amazon Pay is more streamlined that way. Customers do not leave the site during the checkout process. This option is only available with the PayPal Pro version, which is more expensive. What payment application does Authorize.Net use? Authorize.net is in partnership with PaymentCloud as their preferred payment application. The organization has offered Authorize.net’s services, scalability, and solutions to your eCommerce business. Curate a secure, seamless, and reliable payment experience for your consumers by using these abilities. What is PayPal Pro? It is one of the many versions of payment gateways offered by PayPal. This pro version utilizes the direct payment method and can manage everyday product sales. However, it lacks in processing recurring payments like subscriptions. It has a monthly fee of 35 dollars and the standard transaction fee of 2.9%+$0.30. What are some of the features of WooCommerce Payments? WooCommerce built it, so it is highly compatible with the eCommerce platform. Additionally, it perfectly integrates with other WooCommerce extensions like WooCommerce Subscriptions. It can accept payments in international currencies and gives you direct access to all costs through the WordPress Dashboard. How do I withdraw funds from WooCommerce? Users can withdraw their balance money by placing a request to the site administrator. Once the administrator approves the withdrawal request, the user gets the requested amount. To create a new withdrawal request, users need to navigate to My account > My Wallet > “Withdrawal” menu. Does WooCommerce accept a percentage of the sales profit? WooCommerce Payments does not charge any setup or monthly fees. Users pay 2.9% + $0.30 for each transaction made with credit or debit cards issued in the US. There’s an additional 1% fee for cards issued outside the United States. text: Shopify is one of the most prominently used eCommerce platforms worldwide. It holds a market share of over 23% in the United States alone. By introducing Shopify Plus, this eCommerce platform generated tremendous profits and got ahead of the competition. However, the question remains: which version of Shopify is the right choice for your business ? Choosing a suitable eCommerce platform is vital for your business. This article will walk you through an outline of features and differences between Shopify and Shopify Plus. It will help you understand the two versions better and select a suitable Shopify store development plan for your business . Table of Contents Shopify Vs. Shopify Vs.Shopify Plus – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Shopify Vs. Shopify Plus: Fundamentals Shopify Shopify is a beginner-friendly eCommerce platform for merchants to build their online stores and sell products. It also comes with Shopify POS (Point of Sale), allowing merchants to sell products in person. Shopify is a subscription-based service accessed by store owners through regular payments like any other eCommerce platform. Online retailers use many tools, and features to build an engaging web store and utilize the shopping cart solution to sell, ship, and manage their products.  Business owners employ various tools to customize their online store and create a tailormade, hassle-free shopping experience for their customers. Shopify also aids in increasing business profits by optimizing the return of investment (ROI). This plan is highly suitable for small and medium-sized businesses.  Shopify Plus Released in 2014, Shopify Plus is the latest version of this cloud-based SaaS eCommerce platform. It was launched to compete with other widely employed platforms like Magento and Volusion. Shopify Plus is a fully hosted eCommerce platform targeted to promote and manage large-scale businesses or enterprises. The eCommerce platform has integrated several advanced features into this plan to make it more pertinent for rapidly growing brands. Brands such as Fashion Nova, Nestle, Unilever, Pepsi, and other 5,700 plus websites use Shopify Plus. Its objective is to aid businesses in managing increased traffic, orders, inventory, and shipment. Furthermore, it offers remarkable features and tools to handle high-volume eCommerce businesses at affordable prices.  How Does Shopify Work? Whether you are using Shopify or Shopify Plus, it works in similar ways. The difference doesn’t lie in how they work but instead in what they can do. Shopify Plus is much more advanced than Shopify as it allows more customization and offers a broad range of abilities. The first step is to design your Shopify store. You can use the available themes or customize a new one, plan the website layout, and include your products on it. With a stable internet connection, you can build and design the appearance of your store in about an hour. Shopify allows you to sell your products in multiple places, for example, online marketplaces, brick-and-mortar places, pop-ups, etc. Users can efficiently manage their everyday store operations like inventory, shipping, and payments by utilizing Shopify tools.  This eCommerce platform has a robust security system as Shopify payments are PCI compliant. It protects sensitive customer information and provides safe payment options. Moreover, there is no need for a third-party app service as Shopify automatically accepts all primary payment methods. Looking for support to set up an eCommerce store on Shopify? Book an Appointment What Can You Sell on Shopify? You can sell an unlimited number of products or services on Shopify. You can sell absolutely anything on this enormous eCommerce platform, from physical products and services to memberships, lectures, or classes. What’s more?  Let’s look at the type of products you can sell on Shopify in depth. 1. Physical Products This category is self-explanatory. It refers to any tangible object manufactured by you or a third-party manufacturer. Examples include clothes, jewelry, candy, junk food, toiletries, personal care, and home needs. 2. Services or Consultations This segment refers to an action or a helpful activity offered to you. There is no exchange of physical goods. For instance, you are booking an online or in-person appointment with your hairdresser or buying a spa treatment.  3. Digital Products This classification refers to the intangible products you can offer your customers. It includes audio, videos, e-books, and so on. 4. Event Tickets You can use this eCommerce platform to sell tickets for various purposes, from traveling to workshops. Many artists have benefited tremendously by selling their event tickets on Shopify. 5. Memberships You can buy annual, monthly, or weekly subscriptions to render specific services or products. E.g., A gym owner can use Shopify to sell different types of gym memberships (Basic and Premium.) Moreover, they can also restrict members-only access to specific parts of the gym’s official website. 6. Product Rentals It is a combination of physical products and services. You can rent out tangible objects like costumes, props, or cars as a service to other people. 7. Lectures and Classes Professionals in the teaching or education industry use the Shopify platform to sell their lectures and classes. It can either be live sessions or pre-recorded lecture videos.  Apart from selling, Shopify also renders dropshipping services. For those unfamiliar with the term, dropshipping is a solution that permits merchants to sell a product without having inventory or shipping services. The solution can play out in two scenarios as shown below. Scenario One: As soon as you get the order from a customer, you purchase the product directly from the manufacturer or a wholesaler and ship it to the customer. Scenario Two: You forward the customer order to the supplier. It becomes their responsibility to ship the product safely to the customer and process the payment. After completing the order, you receive the difference between the price you charged for the product and the supplier’s product cost. Know in detail about the type of products you can sell on Shopify Click Here Comparison Between Shopify and Shopify Plus Online retailers are always in a dilemma choosing between Shopify and Shopify Plus. We present a comparative analysis between the two plans below to clarify any confusion you might have. Factors   Shopify Shopify Plus eCommerce features Access to multiple payment processing options (inclusive of Shopify Payments) Protection against credit card fraud  In-built discount pricing options and shipping labels Multichannel selling via social media apps, online marketplaces, offline stores, etc. Customizable tools to enhance consumer experience and look of the website It includes all features Shopify offers plus- Accepts huge volumes of up to 10,000 orders per minute Operates a multitude of websites from a single management dashboard Offers consumer-based pricing, which includes wholesale tiers for B2B businesses Customized shipping processes Utilizing AI tech to advance the look and feel of the store Pricing Costs about $29 to $299 per month Price isn’t publicized, and sellers have to request a quote. They charge based on a percentage of your store’s monthly revenue. The minimum monthly fee is $2000, while the maximum is $40,000. Suitable for Start-up companies Side-gig sellers Dropshipping Print-on-demand product sales All small and medium-sized firms Multichannel eCommerce businesses  Established enterprises  Large-scale businesses Any brand requiring volume-focused sales tools Merchants managing numerous wholesale websites or country-specific sites Multichannel eCommerce businesses with annual revenue of two million dollars or more. Customer Support Offers support via Email Chat Phone Offers all channels of support as Shopify.  Includes a skilled Launch Manager and a Merchant Success Manager   Still confused about choosing Shopify or ShopifyPlus? Call Our Experts Why Use Shopify or Shopify Plus? 1. User-friendly Shopify lets merchants sell their services or products with minimal configurations compared to other platforms. It is one of the most beginner-friendly and user-friendly eCommerce platforms in the marketplace. The platform comes integrated with an intuitive drag-and-drop editor, which allows store owners to edit the look of their site without any prior knowledge in coding. It makes Shopify a suitable alternative for beginners who want the complete package without any tech responsibilities related to development and hosting. If you want more control over customizations, you can change the site by coding. 2. Mobile-friendly Online stores or websites operate 24/7, and customers desire unlimited access anytime, anywhere. More consumers are migrating from traditional stores to online stores because it offers them a convenient shopping experience. Shopify ensures that your eCommerce business has a responsive mobile design. It attracts more customers, which ultimately increases your revenue. Business owners can also run their store by installing the Shopify app and logging in with their credentials. Furthermore, Shopify is compatible with both Android and iPhone devices. 3. Domain Name  You can personalize your store by using your domain name. Just connect it to Shopify through your store’s Admin Panel and start running your store. You can also buy a domain name from Shopify or a third-party provider. 4. Variety of Themes Themes play an integral role in attracting customers and enhancing your marketing strategies. Change the theme of your Shopify store according to the needs of your brand. Shopify offers 70 distinctive premium and free themes for your eCommerce business. All of them are compatible with products such as electronics, clothing, art, services, etc. Users can tweak these themes even without knowing HTML and CSS. 5. Payment Tools Shopify comes with a built-in payment tool called Shopify Payments, eliminating the need for a third-party payment integration app. It accepts all predominant payment methods and cards. Some examples include PayPal, Apple Pay, Venmo, and Amazon Pay. It also accepts alternative payment options like cryptocurrency. 6. Social Media Selling You can integrate your store with social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook to implement marketing campaigns to boost your sales. Social media has a broader reach than other platforms and will help you connect with a more comprehensive set of target audiences. Shopify allows you to sell through other channels like online marketplaces, pop-up shops, offline stores, etc. 7. SEO Tools SEO is the number one strategy to get more traffic to your website. Shopify has in-built SEO tools that automatically optimize your store’s content by adding auto-generated canonical tags on your site’s pages, preventing duplicate content from appearing in search engine results. Along with the tags, your store’s themes, robots.txt, and site map.xml files are also automatically generated. For further optimization, users are free to edit title tags, URLs for blog posts, product descriptions, meta descriptions, etc. 8. Superior Plugins Since Shopify is an extensively used platform, many third-party organizations or apps offer several plugins to cater to business needs. The eCommerce platform itself has a variety of indigenous plugins created to boost the functionality of your store. These plugins are either free or premium. 9. Customer Support Shopify offers customer support via emails, one-on-one chats, and phone calls to resolve any issues you might face. Additionally, Shopify Plus will provide a Launch Manager and Merchant Success Manager to aid your store operations. Apart from the 24/7 customer support, users can also access free tutorials, webinars, and online courses through Shopify Learn. It equips them with the necessary knowledge and skill to promote online sales. 10. Dropshipping Dropshipping is a profitable business model that requires minimum efforts and maximum profits. Shopify dropshipping enables you to sell products through a seller or manufacturer that manages the inventory and shipping process. You can start dropping in three simple steps: Building your eCommerce store, uploading your products, and launching your website. Finally, start advertising your dropshipping stores. Remember to connect with suppliers, wholesale retailers, and other manufacturers before launching your store. Shopify Vs. Shopify Plus: Key Differences In a nutshell, Shopify Plus has all features of the Shopify plan coupled with supplementary abilities to handle enterprises. Below are the key differences between the two programs to help users understand the platforms in detail. 1. Staff Accounts The Basic Shopify plan limits the number of staff accounts you can create for your eCommerce business. However, Shopify Plus permits you to create an unlimited number of staff accounts and enables advanced permission settings.  2. Additional Customer Support As mentioned in the comparative analysis, Shopify Plus offers you two dedicated store managers. The added customer support significantly helps store owners to manage their business. These Shopify Experts are available 24/7 to resolve any queries, help you set up the store, or simplify the migration process. 3. Shopify Apps Shopify Plus users get exclusive access to some Shopify applications that are not available to regular Shopify merchants. These apps are listed below. Launchpad It is helpful to pre-plan and automate product launches, sale campaigns, and flash sales for a particular event or day. After the completion of the event, you can undo all changes made. Shopify Flow An intuitive eCommerce app that lets you automate many office or administration processes and customer-facing tasks. You can select this app to store data or execute actions like sending reorder requests, tagging loyal consumers, inventory notifications, and much more. You can demand anything on this app without knowing any coding language. Script Editor Personalize your checkout process through script editor. Minimal coding is required to implement custom shipping, payment options, and discounts on products for buyers. Script Editor has contributed considerably to decreasing the number of abandoned carts. Wholesale Channel Shopify Plus is appropriate for large-scale businesses, and this app supports high volumeB2B sales. Bulk Account Inviter This app sends bulk invitations to customers to import them from another store or platform and to activate their customer accounts on your online store. Transporter App The app helps users import their products, data, and customer base into their Shopify store. Online eCommerce retailers can access and send customer records across various storefronts. Organization Management Enhance your standard Shopify admin by downloading the organization management app. It gives you the flexibility to operate as a central organization by managing tools affecting multiple stores at once. 4. More Control Over Theme Customization Liquid is Shopify’s theme language, and you can access it through the Shopify Plus plan. You are provided more flexibility and control over customizing themes from scratch. You can also tweak the backend at the code level for increased control. 5. API Integrations APIs are crucial in facilitating integrations with any third-party apps. Shopify Plus equips you with additional API resources exclusively used by Shopify Plus users. These API resources are: Multipass Login Stores owners with separate websites and stores can use this API resource. Users are redirected from the website to their Shopify store through a seamless login process.  GiftCard This is a type of alternative payment option. Each gift card comes with a unique code entered during the checkout stage. You can redeem the balance amount over multiple checkouts. User Store owners can retrieve information on any staff account through this API resource. 6. Wholesale Channel  Some consumers may wish to purchase from your rapidly growing store in bulk, and any enterprise-level eCommerce business should have the necessary arrangements to facilitate the wholesale order. Shopify Plan caters to this need by offering you a wholesale channel that lets you create a distinct, password-secured wholesale storefront. It means you can provide the same products at exclusive wholesale prices to buyers. This feature is handy for B2B eCommerce businesses.  7. Premium Access to Memberships Shopify Plus gives you access to premium memberships that a regular Shopify plan can’t offer. These memberships give you the exclusive opportunity to be a part of supportive Shopify Communities like: Shopify Plus Academy A self-guided training to comprehend fundamental topics to grow your business  Shopify Plus Community A vast community on Facebook where similar merchants who run high-volume businesses come together to discuss ideas and strategies. Shopify Plus Partner Program Get your hands on advanced technology unlimited access to solution partners and agencies. Get a chance to sneak peek into the future beta programs and modify the product roadmap of Shopify Plus. 8. Merchant Success Program Shopify Plus provides a Merchant Success Program that helps members make the most out of the platform. Whether you need assistance with third-party app integrations or operating this platform, the Merchant Success Manager guides you through this journey and ensures you reach your full potential. The team will also aid you in finding verified Shopify Plus Partners to keep up with events and industry trends. Shopify Plus as an Enterprise eCommerce Platform Operating an Enterprise-level eCommerce store can be financially draining. The ultimate advantage of Shopify plus is that it cuts down on opportunity costs. The eCommerce platform handles bugs, web development, order management, feature implantation, servers, file storage, bandwidth, and other maintenance responsibilities. It thereby frees up resources to be efficiently allocated to other processes. Merchants also get access to agile marketing tools curated to boost their sales. Shopify Plus has state-of-the-art plugins, extensions, and APIs that can take your company to the next level. Most of these features are easy to use for people with no coding skills. This plan also supports B2B eCommerce business.  Relatability and Support are two primary factors to consider before setting up shop on any eCommerce platform. Shopify Plus undergoes tests and is then updated according to the feedback and reviews from plenty of merchants. Continuous improvements ensure that the platform’s robust framework can handle increased traffic, orders, and shipping processes. Moreover, its popularity ensures that you have an external and internal support system. These are the few significant reasons why Shopify Plus is ideal for enterprise and large-scale firms. Do you want to migrate your Shopify eCommerce store to Shopify Plus? Call Us Now Should You Migrate to Shopify or Shopify Plus? The answer to this question largely depends on the size of the business you want to run. This article explains why Shopify is a competent option for small and medium-scale companies, while Shopify Plus is appropriate for enterprises. The two plans are the same in offering essential eCommerce functions and tools. The difference lies in the additional support, flexibility, and tools that Shopify Plus provides. Small businesses don’t require these complex abilities to run their store. Therefore, buying the Shopify Plan will only prove too expensive for them. You should migrate to Shopify Plus only if you own a large-scale firm.  Shopify Vs.Shopify Plus – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Is Shopify a legitimate and dependable platform for my business? Shopify is an established and renowned eCommerce platform used by leading companies worldwide. You can build your store and operate it without coding or designing skills. It equips your store with a plethora of powerful tools utilized to increase your profits and widen your reach.  Is Shopify a contemporary mobile-friendly platform? Shopify has successfully adapted to the functioning of the modern world by making its platform mobile-friendly. From store managers accessing their store through phones to customers using their mobile devices to shop from Shopify stores, with a stable internet connection, Shopify is accessible from anywhere.  Is there a limit to how many stores I can build with Shopify Plus? Shopify Plus offers you great flexibility regarding the number of stores you can build using this plan. It allows merchants to expand into B2B, D2C, and other types of business without spending a fortune. Furthermore, you can create up to ten stores by purchasing a Shopify Plus subscription. What are the primary differences between Shopify and Shopify Plus? A regular Shopify plan suits the needs of small or medium-scale businesses, while a Shopify Plus plan is tailored for large-scale or enterprise-level firms. The two programs also significantly differ in pricing, with the regular Shopify plan being cheaper than the Shopify Plus plan. Can I temporarily pause my subscription? Yes, you have the option to either temporarily pause your store for two days or shut it down completely. Shopify lets you halt your subscription by following a few simple steps. You can utilize the Shopify Admin dashboard to carry out this task. Please note that you cannot pause your subscription during the free trial period. What are the key benefits of Shopify Plus? Shopify Plus offers more themes, greater control over customizing the website’s look, personalized checkout processes, data-driven analytics reports, the ability to smoothly manage increased traffic, better customer support, and much more. There are many such benefits you can unlock by purchasing Shopify Plus. How Do I purchase a Shopify Plus plan? You can reach out to our team to know more about the process and resolve any related queries. What are the other pricing plans offered by Shopify? Shopify offers four pricing plans to merchants. The first is the Basic Shopify plan which starts from $29 per month; the second is the Shopify plan that starts from $79 per month. The third plan is the Advanced Shopify plan, which starts from $299 per month. Lastly, the Shopify Plus plan has a minimum subscription fee of $2000 per month. What is Shopify Lite? You can purchase Shopify lite for $9 per month and create a primary eCommerce store in less than 15 minutes. text: Global online sales are exploding, expected to hit $7.4 trillion by 2025.  Are you trying to make extra money online but need help knowing where to begin? Or do you have an eCommerce store? Meet SaaS eCommerce platforms! This latest wave of software-as-a-service (SaaS) eCommerce solutions enables you to create, run, and optimize an online store without the need to build costly in-house infrastructure and expertise. The platform’s cloud-based technological infrastructure will streamline everything from web hosting to payment processing to marketing tools. A unique SaaS provider will give you an excellent chance to go without any requirement of being tied to it, thus giving you enough room for business expansion. Let’s discuss the leading SaaS eCommerce platforms for 2024 so you can get your products online. Whether you’re a budding entrepreneur looking to launch your online platform and learn from the best or a business owner searching for the top platforms to enhance your shopping experience, this article is tailored to your needs. Table of Contents What is a SaaS eCommerce Platform? Benefits of SaaS eCommerce Platform Top SaaS eCommerce Platforms How to choose the appropriate SaaS eCommerce Platform for your business? Common challenges with SaaS eCommerce Platforms Future of SaaS eCommerce FAQs What is a SaaS eCommerce Platform? SaaS is an anagram for Software-as-a-Service. To elaborate, it is a software licensing and delivery model. Its primary objective is to license software to the users, accessible via the internet. SaaS eCommerce platforms are cloud-based systems accessible through any web browser.  The most significant benefit of SaaS platforms is that the system isn’t introduced on-premise or maintained by the client. Instead, your eCommerce platform runs on the hosted servers of the SaaS suppliers. Your third-party supplier takes care of the security, maintenance, and execution of several applications on their servers. Users can access licensed SaaS applications as per their subscription. They can purchase the subscription by paying a monthly fee. The fee amount will depend on the number of features and level of service or support the users wish to access. The licensing model gives complete flexibility to the merchants as they can have a secure and constant connection to their eCommerce store anytime, anywhere. The most prominent examples of SaaS eCommerce providers are BigCommerce and Shopify.  How is Saas eCommerce Business Going? Let us analyze it the way it is. Envision is the construction of a house. In the past, the procedure utilized land buying, sourcing materials, and recruiting a team of builders, electricians, and plumbers. It sounds exhausting, doesn’t it? In the SaaS ecommerce world, it’s like a house with everything already in place; you just have to move in. It handles the most crucial parts, such as hosting, security, features, and updates, and does so well. The best thing is that you can put your signature laugh on it, thus making it a one-of-a-kind for your brand. Here’s how it works: Select a SaaS Provider  Pick a platform that corresponds to your business requirements. Consider chief ecommerce functions, ability to adjust, and pricing type. Customize Your Store Take advantage of the online site’s built-in tools to sketch the store, place the products, and establish a payment gateway. Market Your Business  Use the marketing tools offered by the platform to capture customers and boost sales. Analyze and Optimize Most SaaS eCommerce platforms come with built-in analytics tools, allowing you to track key performance metrics and make data-driven decisions. For a deeper understanding of your workflows and efficiency, you can use value stream mapping to visualize and optimize your business processes, ensuring every step adds value and minimizes waste. Grow Your Business  With the platform scaling as your business grows, your business is always at its maximum potential to succeed. Need more features? Just upgrade your subscription. Learn more about the benefits of using Saas platforms from experts Let’s Talk Benefits of SaaS eCommerce Platforms SaaS eCommerce is the fastest and hassle-free way to launch a digital store because it is neither installed nor maintained by the owner. There is more than one benefit of using such platforms, and listed below are a few of them: 1. How much does it cost? SaaS eCommerce platforms are inexpensive and highly efficient solutions for business owners:  All merchants should make a fundamental investment in building their online store. Investing in a robust SaaS eCommerce framework will give them long-term benefits. You will save on cost, time and all the hassles of building the whole ecommerce solution. Also, SaaS platforms come with many features and plugins that are practically impossible for an individual merchant to make. These platforms already integrate basic features and offer many design options through theme files, thereby saving you time and money on design as well. 2. Maintenance As mentioned above, third-party service providers are responsible for the maintenance process. Merchants get to save on maintenance and development expenses that way. However, apart from the costs, it also lightens the workload of the store owners. As a customer of the third-party service provider, the business owner can rely on them to take care of mundane issues like fixing bugs, regular updates, maintaining the server’s functioning, and much more. It is particularly advantageous for businesses that need a strong IT team with enough experience in the eCommerce industry. Furthermore, SaaS updates are automatic, cutting additional costs and efforts. 3. Enhanced Security and PCI Compliance Due to the automatic update feature, your SaaS online store is continuously upgraded, protecting it against any cyber-attack. The internet has its downsides, and it is crucial to protect your store and your consumers from potential data leaks and hackers. SaaS system providers ensure that you fulfill all the PCI consistency guidelines so that you can protect your customer’s sensitive payment information. The system suppliers are liable to stay updated with any bug fixes or patches that impact the security of your store. Your loyal consumer base trusts your firm with personal data, and the information must stay protected from the increasing number of hacks.  4. Scalability A growing business requires a platform that will grow with them. SaaS eCommerce platforms are considerably more flexible than other platforms. It allows you to widen your consumer base, process more orders, and add complex features to the store. When your store expands, you can integrate new sales channels, increase server bandwidth to manage site traffic, etc. Remember that growing your company can be something other than rebranding or restructuring the base business model. It is realistic and efficient to incur such expenses frequently. Instead, it means adding new features that will help you increase profits. 5. Avant Garde Solutions The principal role of this platform is to supply developed and ready-to-go products, ultimately saving the buyer’s time and money. Most of the commodities offered are exceedingly customizable and straightforward to functionalize so that clients can design their dream platform at the snap of their fingers. While assembling an eCommerce stage may take months, utilizing those “Lego” arrangements will help you build the outcome a lot quicker. Moreover, store owners don’t need an IT team or an expert to run their store. They can leverage the user-friendly design interface to manage store operations. 6. Integration As beneficial as your eCommerce platforms are, it is ill-advised to run your entire business from a single system. Integrating your current eCommerce platform with other software like POS, 3PL, ERP, payment gateway, or other money-related software is crucial in boosting your business growth. It is convenient to have a SaaS eCommerce platform that can flawlessly integrate with other applications. Shopify provides you access to both CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) and HTML (Hypertext Markup Language), two programming languages that can be utilized to create content for the page. Also, this eCommerce platform eliminates the need to purchase a web hosting service or install additional software. Merchants can directly accept credits from Shopify, which means there is no need for a third-party app. The payment details are synced with the orders to make the payment process easier for all parties involved.  Features Social media selling tools like Facebook Messenger, Buyable Pins, and Facebook Shop Highly engaging and supportive community Multiple channels retailing – offline, online and social Beginner-friendly and user-friendly  No server maintenance costs  A plethora of theme options Economical – no free plan available, but a free trial is available  Integration with marketplaces like Amazon 3. Magento Magento is predominantly an open-source e-commerce platform written in PHP, but it also provides SaaS services. The platform is renowned for its groundbreaking solutions and features. It is highly customizable and lets users tailor their site’s layout and blocks seamlessly.   They can either use the existing themes or build one from scratch. However, a professional developer’s help is required to customize websites. Magento 2 and the latest improved versions give greater flexibility to the merchants to manage their stores. It is also the reason why many upcoming businesses have migrated to Magento. Magento Development Popular websites using the platform are Ford, Landrover, Nestle Nespresso Sugarfina, Helly Hansen, Adore Beauty, etc. Each year, Magento manages a gross total of $100 billion in merchandise volume. Approximately 20% or more online stores use Magento as their eCommerce platform. The self-hosted solutions make it significantly easy for store owners to manage their business. Nonetheless, you need a decent amount of experience in the industry or possess some relevant knowledge to use Magneto because of its advanced software and complex features. You could otherwise hire a professional to manage the store. That being said, this eCommerce site is best suited for an established, large-scale business model. Any investment in Magento will benefit your business in the long term.  Features Users can add and manage more than a thousand products  This site can handle tons of traffic Process massive orders In-built multilingual support Product bundles  Coupon Management A multitude of payment gateway alternatives  Inventory management and Newsletter management   Marketing tools and site management tools 4. Wix Wix is an SMB-accommodating site hosting and building platform with diverse abilities for making a sophisticated web-based store. This widely used SaaS ecommerce platform allows you to configure, build and manage your online store with the help of Wix Editor. After signing up, the users can gain access to Wix Editor, the website building tool for this platform. It offers a simple, intuitive drag and drop builder tool that permits you to add/eliminate feature graphics, change the website’s structure, write the site copy, and make other changes according to your business needs. You’ll also enjoy the benefits of having countless layouts and stock pictures to select from to make the process simpler. It has one-page sites for individuals who favor an essential, concise browsing experience. Moreover, it includes an impressive collection of free and paid templates to design your site and increase the customer’s mobile shopping experience. It has over 500 free mobile responsive designs to choose from, and you don’t need extensive coding experience to manage your store. Furthermore, the platform accepts a variety of primary payment gateways and methods with no additional commission.  Features Real-time push notifications and no maintenance charges  Lets users add highly efficient SEO tags on the website pages Continuous sync with Google Calendar  Abandoned cart recovery  Parallax 3D effects  Supports marketing tools like ShoutOut Email marketing  Reasonable premium plans and free forever plan Confused about choosing a SaaS platform to choose for your business? Contact Us How Do You Choose an Appropriate SaaS eCommerce Platform for Your Business?  With many exceptional SaaS eCommerce platforms in the market, merchants may feel perplexed and intimidated to choose one. An eCommerce business is essentially a simple online shopping store. However, many back-end operations and features make it a success. Examples of such elements are stocking, secure payment options, warehousing, inventory management, order processing, and much more. Most beginners and startups often commit the mistake of not selecting the right platform to build their store. To ensure you don’t duplicate the errors, below are some curated factors to help you make a suitable choice. 1. Business Objective Every business has unique needs, and identifying them will help business owners arrange their priorities. One should ponder over the below questions:  What should be my business size? Who is my target audience? How much capital can I invest in an eCommerce platform? Is the eCommerce platform scalable? Do I need prior software knowledge to use the SaaS eCommerce platform? The answer to these questions will help you determine your business objectives and accordingly handpick a few SaaS eCommerce platforms. 2. Design  Building an online store from scratch requires a lot of groundwork. The advantage of choosing SaaS eCommerce platforms is that you can have your store up and running in an hour or so. However, not all of them provide the same amount of convenience while designing and developing your store. A few SaaS eCommerce platforms require experience and knowledge in coding to customize extensions, themes, and the site’s layout. Make sure to select a SaaS eCommerce platform with an optimized and responsive mobile-friendly design. It will attract more customers and exponentially grow your business.  3. Budget  Different eCommerce platforms have other subscription plans. Nevertheless, most of them offer a basic or free trial plan to help you get a knack for how it works. Investing in any SaaS eCommerce platform is a long-term commitment, and that’s why you must meticulously research before making any purchases. Remember to include costs like maintenance fees, security fees, transaction fees, hosting expenses, consultant fees, and so on. Opt for a self-hosted SaaS eCommerce platform to cut down the costs of maintenance, management, and hosting services. 4. Self-hosted or Cloud-based  One of your primary tasks is to choose between a self-hosted eCommerce platform and a hosted/cloud-based platform for your business. Self-hosted platforms will run the site on your server and have complete control over maintenance and management. You will require some expertise in the technical and software areas to operate self-hosting sites such as WooCommerce and Magento. Pros of choosing them are: Complete creative control over your site You can build, manage, and design the location on your terms Independent functionality of your site Hosted eCommerce platforms are tropically cloud-based platforms and are beginner-friendly. You are limited to the software’s abilities to release features and add-ons. No prior technical knowledge is required to run your store on Wix, BigCommerce, and Shopify platforms. Pros of choosing them are: Merchant is not responsible for server maintenance and development An excellent option for non-technical users as it is beginner-friendly More affordable than self-hosted platforms Challenges Faced by SaaS eCommerce Platforms Challenges Faced by SaaS eCommerce Platforms  1.B2B Support Needs  SaaS eCommerce platforms are not ideally built for B2B eCommerce . Even though B2B has a similar model to B2C, distinctive differences entitle both business models to separate unique needs. B2B eCommerce sites need features like customer-specific pricing, wholesale pricing, discounts by quantities, different payment terms, etc. Therefore, B2B sellers will have to look for other alternatives.  2. Management of Complex Systems  eCommerce sites need advanced customized features to manage complex business operations. It is primarily for sizable eCommerce sites as they handle multiple marketplaces, manage warehousing, control inventory, international shipping, and so on. A basic SaaS eCommerce cannot manage such complex operations. Future of SaaS eCommerce Platforms The current pandemic and the technological improvements in the past decade have changed the retailing landscape and encouraged more businesses to shift to the eCommerce model. It is vital to invest in progressive SaaS eCommerce platforms to ensure that your business stays profitable and competitive. The merchants may never have complete control over the functionalities of SaaS-based eCommerce platforms, and that can be a blessing in disguise. It is a highly responsible task to build a platform that will immediately and efficiently cater to your needs, not to mention the advantage of community support the platform will now have. SaaS eCommerce platforms seem to be the future of online retailing, and it is a sign for the readers to switch to one today.  Struggling with managing your SaaS eCommerce platform? We Can Help Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS) What’s the critical difference between SaaS and eCommerce business? A SaaS business sells a service that can be accessed through paid subscriptions and probably receive recurring payments. It provides platforms for an eCommerce business to develop and grow. An eCommerce business sells a tangible product or a downloadable file, and the transaction happens through a website. How do you differentiate between Open source and SaaS platforms? SaaS platforms are built, maintained, and hosted by the provider on their servers and licensed to merchants for use. E.g., BigCommerce and Shopify. Open source platforms allow merchants to change, view and distribute the source code for personal purposes. It is developed collaboratively by the public, e.g., Magento and WooCommerce. What are the three different types of eCommerce businesses? Three leading types of e-Commerce businesses are Business-to-Business (B2B ) like Salesforce, AliExpress, Business-to-Consumer (B2C ) like Amazon, and Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) like eBay. SaaS ecommerce platforms like Shopify, WooCommerce, and Magneto are ideally used to run B2B and B2C eCommerce. Can I get technical support for Magento? Since Magento is a famous SaaS eCommerce platform, many professionals provide top-notch support services to business owners. Virtina has a team of highly qualified experts who have sufficient experience to offer a wide range of Magento services to grow your eCommerce business. For more information, feel free to contact Virtina. Are all eCommerce platforms SaaS-based? No, not all eCommerce platforms are SaaS-based. There are predominantly two other eCommerce platforms, PaaS (Platform-as-a-Service) and on-premises platforms. However, SaaS platforms like Magento, BigCommerce, WooCommerce are considerably used and favorably recommended out of the three options. How many SaaS eCommerce platforms does Virtina support? We can proudly say that we provide exceptional technical support and services to 13 SaaS eCommerce platforms. Apart from the top 4 SaaS platforms mentioned above, namely, BigCommerce, Shopify, Magento, and Wix, we are also skilled in Squarespace, 3D cart, Volusion, Vtex, OpenCart, WordPress, Odoo, and PrestaShop. What are some of the issues faced by SaaS eCommerce startup companies? Not all startups with SaaS experience success and profits. Some of them fail at the very beginning for several reasons. The preliminary reason is a lack of strategy. Other significant reasons include a weak business model, lack of an efficient management team, slow growth rate, and inadequate resource management.  Can a person host their eCommerce website? Yes, it is possible to host your eCommerce website, but it is not practical. To host one, you require physical servers, which takes a lot of money, technical expertise, time, and effort. So, unless you are a multinational eCommerce firm, this option isn’t recommended for your online store. Is Shopify profitable for small businesses? This SaaS-based eCommerce platform is highly recommended for small businesses. Firstly, it is user-friendly and beginner-friendly, so you don’t need additional technical support to run your store. It includes all tools required to run an eCommerce business and manage operations. These features cut down the costs needed to set up an online store.

text: Magento is a humungous eCommerce platform supported by developers all across the world. Its popularity is the leading reason people opt to use Magento for their online store . It is safer to use a platform supported by developers because of the 24/7 help and expertise. Magento is budget-friendly, and it is less time-consuming to maintain the website. After the Magento 2 release, everyone was impressed with the various features and tech improvements it had to offer. Slowly the community support towards Magento1 started decreasing. It is scarcely available now, which should motivate you to migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 . Another reason to migrate is that Magento 1 is almost extinct in the software world. Magento 2 fast tracks your journey to success with its impeccable performance and robust security. One con of this migration is that the restructuring of the Magento code restricts the owner from transferring themes and extensions from Magento 1 to Magento 2. Also, most of your data will be automatically assigned, but some of it will require manual assistance to transfer.
