Boost in Sales Higher Conversion Rate Diminishing Number of Abandoned Shopping Carts Conclusion – Migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 Magento 2 Migration – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Know more about the benefits of Migrating to Magento 2 Contact Us Reasons to Migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 Any reputable software will continue to evolve in fulfilling the changing needs of business owners and consumers. Magento 1 helped eCommerce businesses flourish back in the day, but its features and tech support became obsolete with time. Magento 2 is the brand new version released by Magento to tackle the requirements of contemporary eCommerce stores. Magento 2 overcomes the major drawbacks of Magento 1 and gives its users an unforgettable experience. Read below to discover 12 compelling reasons why you should migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 . 1. Enhanced Safety Magento 1 remains exposed to cyber-attacks and is significantly vulnerable to hackers, bots, bugs, etc. This is because the platform has stopped the production of security patches since June 2020. It means that your eCommerce store data is no longer safe. Sensitive information about your clients like their credit card details, personal home address, email password, and other data can be leaked and sold by hackers for profits.  Customers will refrain from purchasing anything from your store because it is risky to do business with you. Thus, along with a dip in sales, your brand reputation will also take a hit. Magento 2 has strong data encryption, and by upgrading, your site becomes secure from cybercrime, making your business reliable and trustworthy to consumers.  2. Seamless Updates One of the primary drawbacks of Magento 1 is that it is highly complicated to install updates of Magento extensions . Many businesses expend a lot of time and energy during this process. Moreover, your eCommerce store must be frequently updated to ensure the smooth functioning of the site. Magento 2 comes equipped with LESS, HTML5, and CSS3, making upgrading significantly easier. It has helped several merchants oversee their business and reap the benefits of the latest features. 3. Database Segmentation Magento 1 had a single database for admins, customers, and developers. It was an inefficient design as it failed to cater to their unique individual needs and led to database overload. However, Magento 2 has divided the database into three broad categories: product data, orders, and checkout. It eliminates the codependency needs between the three categories. For example, the admin panel overload will not hinder the consumer’s experience. Each segment works independently to avoid negatively impacting each other. 4. Mobile-friendly In 2021, eCommerce had a significant share in the market, and the statistics predicted eCommerce to advance in the future due to technological improvements and varying consumer buying behavior. The busy lifestyle of today’s customers prevents them from frequently going out and purchasing from offline stores. The convenience that online stores provide them is impeccable. For these reasons, store owners should ensure their website has a mobile-friendly UI design to attract more buyers and simplify store administration. Magento 2 has a responsive mobile design that fits any phone screen and tailors an engaging shopping experience for the patrons. 5. Modernized Tech Stack Magento 2 offers you updated versions of technology stacks. It enables more effortless deployment flexibility and customization . Magento 1 has outdated technology, and with the rapid conversion rate, there is little or no help available for this version. Naturally, no one would want to invest in an obsolete technology that would be  financially draining and time-consuming. Magento 2 has also updated the minimum versions of the tech stack; for instance, PHP 5.5 is the least supported. This is one of the primary reasons for migrating from Magento 1 to Magento 2. 6. Payment Gateway Payment Gateways are a crucial part of any eCommerce website development . Without the integration of safe payment gateways, shoppers won’t be able to buy from your store, which will result in zero profits. Moreover, the downside of the technology boom  is the increase of cybercrime. Businesses should protect their customers from online fraud and unsafe transactions. Magento 2 offers integration of secure payment gateways like Braintree and PayPal. The release of Magento 2.3.3 also provides enhancements to these central payment gateways.  7. Admin Interface It is strenuous handling routine  business operations irrespective of the company size. It is vital to keep track of the daily sales, consumer website engagement, inventory data, profits, and more. It would be easier for the store owners if all of the above tasks were accessible from a single panel. Magento 2 has a remarkable admin interface design that lets you customize features according to your preferences. This personalized admin panel makes it convenient for you to run your company by giving access to essential business information at your fingertips.  Furthermore, creating new products with the latest Magento 2 admin interface is hassle-free owing to four times faster product import features.   8. Improved Scalability and Performance Google considers several characteristics as ranking factors for mobile searches .  Advanced scalability and performance are examples of two such factors. The new and improved Magento 2 offers its users better performance through its state-of-the-art features. For example, PHP 7 support, built-in tools for picture compression, utilization of web application accelerators  like varnish caching, minimized and bundled Javascript that reduces irrelevant background browser operations on the client’s computer, etc. Additionally, Magento 2 can also process a comparatively massive number of orders than Magento 1. It means more customers can enjoy the benefits of your products! 9. Advanced Testing Abilities Running an eCommerce store is a full-time job. Developers have to go back and forth writing codes and correcting them for customization and updating features, designs, etc. As humans, we make mistakes, and the code may not come out perfect on the first try.  With Magento 2, developers can run trial programs to evaluate the efficiency of the code and accordingly make changes to it. It prevents any negative impacts on the core functionality of the website. Below mentioned are some tests included in the Magento 2 testing framework. Unit Tests Static Tests Performance Tests Integration Tests JavaScript Unit Tests Legacy and Migration Tests Developers save a lot of time and effort thanks to Magento 2’s advanced testing abilities. Migrate your Magento 1 store to Magento 2 Call Us Now 10. Modernized Checkout According to Optinmoster, 26% of buyers leave the website if the checkout process is complicated. Losing a significant number of shoppers solely due to the checkout process is an avoidable loss. By migrating to Magento 2, you can eliminate this disadvantage. Unlike Magento 1, which has a 6 step checkout process, Magento 2 has a simple two-step checkout process.  Furthermore, Magento 2 offers 38% faster checkout to consumers than  Magento 1. Buyers can create an account or opt for guest checkout to complete the transaction. 11. Caching Slow-loading websites are the leading cause of decreased consumer visits, bad SEO ranking, low sales, consumer likability, etc. One of the reasons people choose to buy online is because it is convenient and faster for them. They don’t have time to shop at the mall or wait for the website to load. Not only does the sluggish loading time frustrate them, but it also sets a negative precedent for your brand. Caching occurs when frequently used pages are stored to diminish the loading time. Magento 2 has in-built page caching to boost the loading time. The platform has also made changes to improve browser caching for static content. 12. Customization Magento 2 codebase is wholly restructured to enable everything relevant to a module filed under a single module’s directory.  The separation of presentation and business logic makes for easy customization and maintenance. So why are you waiting? Customize your store to fit your store’s and customers’ needs and increase your profits!  Consequences of Not Migrating to Magento 2 Launched in 2007, Magento 1 has helped countless people establish their businesses.  However, Magento 1 was only the stepping stone to success. As technology improved with time, a better and improved version of Magento 1 was released – Magento 2. This version incorporates all the features that Magento 1 lacked and is a much more sophisticated platform for modern eCommerce businesses.  So far, we have discussed the reasons to migrate from Magento1 to Magento 2, but what happens if you don’t make this switch? Well, read on to know what ensues if you opt to continue with Magento 1 version. 1. Extinction of Support Magento 1 support ended by June 2020, but you must know that by now. In his statement, Joe Ayyoub, the Director of Support Operations, said that Magento 2 offers superior cloud-hosted performance. They are committed to supporting merchants worldwide, so the time to migrate to Magento 2 is now. Magento has stopped releasing security patches for the earlier version from June 2020, and the third-party security patches are extremely unreliable. Refurbish your Magento store to accelerate performance Book Your Appointment 2. Breach in Security Since Magento 1 will not be updated by the company anymore, the old version will not be able to keep up with modern technology. The base code will get weaker as time passes and will make the software vulnerable to bots, hackers, and spam. It will be a daunting task to constantly protect your store from external attacks and maintain the smooth functioning of the store. Please note that you are jeopardizing the security of your eCommerce store and the consumer’s personal information. Any mishaps or leaks of customers’ or store’s data will ruin the brand reputation and integrity of the store.  3. Limited Restrictions The number of businesses migrating from Magento 1 to Magento 2 increases day by day. At  this rate, no developer would want to invest time, money, and effort into making extensions for an outdated version. Finding required extensions from reliable and trusted sellers will be an excruciatingly difficult task. Consequently, your stores will have restricted features and lag in performance if you choose to stay with Magento 1. 4. Staying Behind the Competition The trick to staying ahead of the curve is to remain equipped  with the latest technology and have updated knowledge of the recent innovations. Your competitors won’t hesitate to migrate to Magento 2 and take advantage of the countless features it has to offer. It helps them raise the standards of consumer experience and store performance. Ultimately, it expands their customer base as more and more consumers will choose their business over your brand. You will lag in the competition and market share because no buyer wants to shop from a brand that does not meet their needs. 5. No Professional Help Talented professionals and organizations will invest most of their resources and capital into providing support and services for Magento 2. It is where the eCommerce industry and money lie. Finding a skilled expert developer to aid you with your online store will become tough. Naturally, you will be on your own to solve any future technical issues, which is an unfeasible task for you.  These disadvantages highlight how crucial it is to switch to Magento 2.  Whether you like it or not, there is no other alternative than making these transitions. Time is of paramount importance in this case. All businesses around you have completed this change. When will you? How to Migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 Magento migration is not an easy, do-it-yourself activity. You will require some experts with ample experience and skill to help you finish the process. It requires hours of pre-planning before implementing any changes to protect your store data. Keeping these vital factors in mind, below are the steps to migrate from Magento 1 to 2: Step 1: Data Backup As mentioned before, Magento migration is a complex process, and if not carried out appropriately, it will lead to the loss of precious data. It will damage your business by causing heavy losses. Professionals will first back up your current website to ensure this doesn’t happen. Your product and customer data, meta tags, meta title, and description will stay intact during this process. Experts use cloud storage, external hard drives, or Zip Drive to back up this tremendous amount of information.  Step 2: Extension Migration The design of Magento code doesn’t permit the conversion of Magento 1 modules to Magento 2 modules. Therefore, the transfer of Magento 1 extensions to Magento 2 with identical features will require expertise. Luckily for you, developers have found an efficient solution for this. Most search and integrate extensions with the same attributes have new versions. If your requirements are not satisfied with the current extensions available in the market, you can ask the developer to customize an extension from scratch. The customized extensions are guaranteed to fit the needs of your business ideally, thereby improving the efficacy of your store. Step 3:  Theme Migration  It is impossible to convert Magento 1 theme to Magento 2 themes. Nevertheless, developers can resolve this obstacle through two main options. Option 1: Developers can use the customization abilities of Magento 2 to create and replicate Magento 1 themes. It will ensure that your current store is a replica of the previous Magento store. Customers won’t notice any changes to the store, and the familiarity factor will aid in retaining buyers. Option 2: You can customize a whole new theme with guidance from your developer. Maybe the old store’s design wasn’t gaining you any traction among the consumers, and this is the suitable time to change that. Rebrand the store design with several fresh features Magento 2 offers to attain your business goals . Step 4: Custom Migration Magento is an open-source platform which means your Magento 1 online store is running on a custom code. To migrate the same to your Magento 2 online store, skilled individuals commonly use a code migration toolkit to simplify the process. It reduces the time taken to finish the entire migration process. Step 5: Data Transfer The ultimate step is to transfer all data backed up in Step 1 to your Magento 2 store. Developers need to precisely transfer data and adjust it according to the structure of the new version. If your store was running on Magento 1.6 version, it’s easier for developers to transfer the data using a Data Migration toolkit. In other cases, developers create a custom plug-in to transfer the data. After completing this step, ask your developer to conduct thorough testing of your store to ensure he moved all the essential data to your current store and there are no bugs in the program. What are the Results of a Flawless Migration from Magento 1 to Magento 2? After serious research and feedback, all businesses have recorded some optimistic results. 1. Boost in Sales:  Magento 2 is powered by Elasticsearch, which makes the process of buying from your online store ten times easier.Consumers enjoy the comfort and convenience your store offers them. It attracts more shoppers to visit and buy from your store. Word of mouth is a powerful advertising tool. So when consumers share their pleasant experiences with others, it builds up your brand reputation. It also positively impacts brand awareness, which helps you increase your sales by expanding your target audience.  2 Higher Conversion Rate: All thanks to the responsive UI design Magento 2 offers, your new store will be mobile-friendly. Gen Z today uses their phones to carry out the simplest to the most complicated tasks. More people can therefore access your store through their smartphones. Also, it will increase the number of orders and simultaneously the conversion rate. It will also ultimately amplify your profit rates and take your business to new realms of success. 3. Diminishing Number of Abandoned Shopping Carts: Most consumers don’t complete the purchasing process and, for various reasons, leave at the final step. This phenomenon is known as abandoned shopping carts. One of the reasons this happens is the long and complicated checkout process. It frustrates the customers, and they end up leaving your store without buying anything. Magento 2 delivers a faster and smoother two-step checkout process, increasing purchases made by the buyers. Remember to be patient throughout the process because re-platforming is a complicated process, and it will take a few days to switch to the latest version completely. You can look for pocket-friendly options to migrate from Magento 1 to Magento 2 in the market. Is Magento 2 an appropriate option for startups? No prior technical expertise is required to operate your store on Magento 2. The user-friendly design makes it easier for store owners to access store features without training. text: eCommerce has taken a giant step forward in the 21st Century. The unprecedented pandemic presented an unexpected opportunity for ecommerce businesses to grow and thrive. While most assume that the ecommerce marketplace is predominantly limited to B2C (business-to-consumer) firms, that is not the case. B2B (business-to-business) companies also hold a significant share in the eCommerce marketplace. From 2021 to 2028, the global B2B eCommerce market presence is expected to expand at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 18.7% . It is currently estimated that 73% of millennials are involved in the B2B buying process . This blog is a comprehensive guide on B2B eCommerce marketplaces and how you can open and customize your B2B eCommerce marketplace on the WooCommerce platform. Table of Contents What is B2B eCommerce? B2B eCommerce for WooCommerce Benefits of Choosing WooCommerce for B2B eCommerce Marketplace Compatible With Other Technology Robust Platform Additional Support Agile Features Easy-to-use Safe from Public View SEO-friendly Flexibility Customization of B2B eCommerce Platform Pros of Choosing WooCommerce for Your Customized B2B Marketplace Management of Unique Process Personalizing Checkout Process LOB Integrations Increase Conversion Rates and Decrease Bounce Rates Boost SEO for Your Business After Sales Services Wider Consumer Base Getting Ahead of Competition Why Opt for WooCommerce to Create a B2B Marketplace? Customer Needs Customized Platform Long Term Relationship Inventory Consumer Buying Behavior How Do You Build a WooCommerce Custom B2B eCommerce Marketplace? Set up B2B Prices Customize the Visibility Settings of Your B2B and B2C Customers Create Separate User Accounts for Your B2B Buyers To Summarize Customization of B2B eCommerce Marketplace on WooCommerce – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is B2B eCommerce?  The B2B marketplace brings together many B2B buyers and sellers on a single website to fulfill transactions. B2B enables payments between businesses. Hence it is imperative that the experience of B2B marketplaces meet the supply and purchasing needs of the market. The B2B marketplaces can be global, offering various products, the same products, or different products with similar features. B2B eCommerce for WooCommerce WooCommerce is an exceptional open-source eCommerce platform from WordPress. The plugin is free, and it offers fundamental eCommerce devices, namely, shopping baskets, payment gateways, items pages, order management dashboards, and landing pages. Nonetheless, you have to cover additional expenses for advanced augmentations to make your site attractive and productive. The best thing about WooCommerce is that it is backed by a reputable brand and subsequently has various extensions and themes. This platform currently powers about 42% of the online stores in the digital marketplace. You can choose from over 4900 WooCommerce extensions, both free and paid. These extensions are designed to support eCommerce factors. Besides themes offered by the official store, people in business can find many attractive themes from third-party developers to bring their websites to life. Thanks to this platform’s flexibility and deep relationship with WordPress, launching and managing an online store with WooCommerce is easy. Planning to start a thriving B2B business? Chat With Us Benefits of Choosing WooCommerce for B2B eCommerce Marketplace WooCommerce is the fastest-growing platform in the market that provides users with a wide range of benefits. Now that you are aware of its popularity, have you stopped to think about what makes WooCommerce so prominent? Why should you choose WooCommerce? What are the benefits of applying WooCommerce to your website? Find the answers to these questions below. 1. Compatible With Other Technology The primary aim of your website is to create a seamless user experience. However, delivering a remarkable B2B experience is a daunting task. It requires a lot of adjustments, like the addition of new extensions and technologies. WooCommerce is exceptionally versatile and lets business owners integrate the latest technologies like CRM, ERP, and OMS into the website. It enhances the user experience and makes your website efficient. Frequent integration and syncing of these systems also help the managers gather crucial data and leverage it to streamline their business. Whether a third-party app or a distinctive software, WooCommerce will easily integrate it to give you maximum benefits.  2. Robust Platform Nothing is 100% perfect, and as long as there are solutions to fix it, it will be alright. Similarly, no matter how well you complete WooCommerce’s coding and software testing, people are bound to find faults and bugs once it is out in the world. WooCommerce guarantees that many B2B business owners use the same features in myriad combinations. It means they have already identified the bugs and reported all issues. The information allows WooCommerce to work on them, provide solutions and make the software flawless. 3. Additional Support The problem with using small or less popular platforms is that it lacks community support. WordPress has an enormous community, and since WooCommerce was built for WordPress, you can benefit from the same community when needed. Technical experts and community forums have answers to all your problems. Get the specialized help you need by using this eCommerce platform. 4. Agile Features WooCommerce is a sophisticated eCommerce platform that offers its users a variety of agile features. B2B businesses need the support of platforms to build their site. One of the advantages of opting for WooCommerce over other platforms is that it comes with a range of pre-built features so that the managers don’t have to pay for fundamental features. Some of them are listed below: Addition of unlimited products/services, categories, sub-categories, and filters Receive notifications of a new order Configure the tax settings for stores, including different prices for different countries or products. Safe payment gateways through Apruve, credit card, PayPal, debit card, etc. It also provides secure offline payment options, for instance, cash on delivery, cheque, and invoice. Display visually represented sales, profits, marketplace trends, and so on. B2B customers can shop products by adding them to the cart, processing checkout, and paying through online or offline mediums. 5. Easy-to-use If you handle all business operations yourself without any prior background in tech, things will seem complicated. That is why you need an easy platform to understand and use. WooCommere is designed for usage by both beginners and experts. You don’t require programming knowledge to open up a B2B business on this eCommerce platform. Nonetheless, you will need professional help for future updates like adding new features/extensions, changing themes, improving the security of your site, etc.  6. Safe from Public View  Everything on the internet is easily accessible to the public if not cleverly hidden. Consumers can view your website and know your wholesale rates, disrupting the retail chain and causing massive losses. Therefore, you must protect your website from the general audience. You can add plugins to your B2B WooCommerce site since it is a compatible platform. It will help you hide confidential information from the public view or hide your entire online store. 7. SEO-friendly Since WooCommerce is built on WordPress , you can benefit from the superior SEO capabilities of WordPress and the support of an accomplished content management team. You can add external plugins like Yoast, All in One SEO Pack, etc., to boost the overall SEO of your website. Furthermore, you can choose from available WordPress plugins to increase brand awareness among other businesses. 8. Flexibility WooCommerce is an open-source platform that provides flexibility to developers. You have the option to customize current plugins or build them from scratch. WooCommerce allows users access to digital products, physical products, subscriptions, and customized themes. Startups or eCommerce beginners can carry out various store operations with prior technical or coding knowledge. You can easily categorize the products, set the sales price, write indivisible product descriptions, and so on. Talk to our experts to know the additional benefits of choosing WooCommerce Contact Now Customization of B2B eCommerce Platform  Lastly, one of the leading benefits of choosing WooCommerce for your eCommerce business is that it allows you to customize your store. With its handy features, you can navigate the platform and design the store as per your liking. It is a misconception that B2B sites don’t need as much effort as B2C sites and that B2B customers should be treated the same as B2C customers .  Using a generic website layout might seem like an intelligent way to save time and money, but it can lead to long-term losses. A personalized platform will cater to the specific needs of your business and the distinctive process to encourage your company’s growth. It will prove to be a significant asset for your online store. Pros of Choosing WooCommerce for Your Customized B2B Marketplace 1. Management of Unique Process  All eCommerce businesses, regardless of D2C, B2C, or B2B, have unique processes to complete purchases. Each function of the store should be carried out in a particular way. For instance, a thorough background check of the customer before buying an item or checking a consumer’s credit card details before authorizing bulk order purchases. These functions are essential for the smooth operating of the B2B eCommerce platform. Most shelf eCommerce solutions are ineffective when it comes to precise operations. When you are customizing your website, you can modify it to support the execution of these processes and contribute to the success of your business. 2. Personalizing Checkout Process  The checking-out process is perhaps the most crucial part of your business. Buyers add or discard items at this stage, and consumers must buy most of the items in their carts to increase profits. Some customers prefer buyer-specific pricing, ACH payments, and well-designed carts, while others prefer purchase limit approvals, contract purchasing, etc. Mundane eCommerce products are not equipped to handle the burden of these requests, and this is where customizing comes into the picture. You can build a highly consumer-centric checkout process to fit the specific requirements of your business. This step will directly influence the sale of your products. 3. LOB Integrations  Line-of-business (LOB) applications act as a support system to your online store. WooCommerce has in-built free or paid extensions and features that will help build your site. However, it is not enough to want a B2B site to be the best in business. An eCommerce platform like WooCommerce can be easily integrated with various LOB for the optimal functioning of the B2B site.  A customized eCommerce interface empowers you to ensure seamless integration between the frameworks, and the stage is custom-fitted to your business cycles. A flawless integration can be significantly advantageous to your eCommerce business and is only conceivable through customization. It comprises automated fulfillment, analytics of consumer online purchasing behavior, real-time inventory data, automating customer-specific pricing, and other advancements. 4. Increase Conversion Rates and Decrease Bounce Rates The aim of customizing your B2B online store is to create an unforgettable impression on the buyer. If buyers have a pleasant experience shopping from your website, they will naturally return for future orders. Eventually, it will create customer loyalty and a robust consumer community for your brand. The conversion rates will start showing a steady increase. Therefore, it is critical to customize your eCommerce store for consumer satisfaction. Customization also allows you to efficiently design the website’s layout to view crucial data and easily search for supplies they wish to buy. It helps in reducing buying friction and bounce rate. 5. Boost SEO for Your Business As mentioned before, primary packages, products, and marketing alone will not aid you in earning top ranks. The eCommerce platforms include generic SEO features and marketing schemes, but a customized platform includes target-specific SEO techniques which will boost your business. What works for other B2B sites might not work for your B2B store. That is why business owners should invest in customized SEO solutions which ensure that their site is accurately tailored to become search engine friendly.  6. After Sales Services A sale helps a company make profits, but after-sales service allows the company to build a brand reputation. Most companies fail to realize that their duty doesn’t stop or is restricted to handling purchases. They are also responsible for assisting the customers after buying the product or services.  Client loyalty and satisfaction also depend on how well you treat a buyer after making the purchase. A custom WooCommerce B2B marketplace allows the customer to track their orders , invoices, quotes, membership applications, get customer service, and so on. The happier they are with the after-sales services, the more likely they will purchase from your store again. 7. Wider Consumer Base Word of mouth remains one of the leading advertising and awareness-spreading methods. If a consumer has a considerably satisfactory experience with your store, he will most likely recommend your store in his business circles. A growing reputation will bring a whole new set of customers for your B2B eCommerce Marketplace. All this makes customization the key to building an impeccable user experience.  You can do it by studying your target audience and modifying the site based on consumer trends and preferences. It will guide you in gaining more consumers leading to higher sales which ultimately ushers in enhanced profits for your business.  8. Getting Ahead of Competition A B2B marketplace faces the same level of competition as a B2C marketplace. To convince users to buy from your eCommerce store, you need to offer them something exceptional from other sites. Customizing your website according to the needs and desires of your buyers will help you stand out amidst the ruthless competition in the marketplace. Personalization will attract more shoppers and help you build customer loyalty. Need to customize your WooCommerce B2B platform? Get in Touch Why Opt for WooCommerce to Create a B2B Marketplace? There are several other eCommerce platforms available on the internet. The million-dollar question is why you should choose WooCommerce to create your B2B eCommerce marketplace. What makes it unique? We have compiled the reasons for your understanding. 1. Customer Needs A business should have consumer-centric goals if it wants to succeed in the future. For this, they should understand their target audience’s needs, wants, and desires. Making a B2B marketplace on WooCommerce permits you to discern your B2B purchasers’ needs accurately. 2. Customized Platform You can offer them a personalized platform built from scratch that includes everything like the relevant product details, shipment information, easy navigation of the website, effectively designed checkout process, etc. Personalization will improve the user experience and business. 3. Long Term Relationship Your B2B eCommerce marketplace should have a strong client community to propagate a consumer loyalty culture for your firm. A customized platform enhances purchase satisfaction, leading to improved customer loyalty. It will help you build a long-term relationship with your patrons and be profitable. 4. Inventory Warehousing and inventory are significantly expensive and require a large workforce to manage. To reduce your company’s expenses, you can eliminate the need for stock or warehousing. WooCommerce allows you to utilize smart shipments from the related supplier to fulfill the buyer’s order. 5. Consumer Buying Behavior Understanding the psychology behind the consumer’s mind is essential. It allows us to answer questions like what do consumers like? How often do they purchase a particular product? How many times do they order in a year/month/week? Studying these patterns will help you comprehend the consumer buying behavior of your B2B online store, which will give you valuable insights into B2B marketplace trends, buyer preferences, and so on. How Do You Build a WooCommerce Custom B2B eCommerce Marketplace? Below are three simple steps to develop your B2B store. Step 1: Set up B2B Prices If you have a B2C store, it is best to combine it with your B2B online store in the long term. After integrating both online marketplaces, you can move on to finalize new product prices for your B2B customers. The logic behind this is to make the product and price reversely proportional, which means the higher the order volume, the lower the price. It is also the thumb rule for wholesale stores to prompt their patrons to buy in bulk from their store. To assign different prices to different customer strata, you must first give them particular roles. Role allocation could be done with the help of any plugin that is accessible to you. To make your store more flexible, you can add custom roles that enable you to create a complex pricing structure and numerous pricing tiers. The pricing could be based on user behavior, product, quantity, category, and global percentage discounts. Step 2: Customize the Visibility Settings of Your B2B and B2C Customers After deciding prices for your B2B store, you will need to determine which consumers can view the prices. If your B2C customers are exposed to the wholesale rates, it will hit your business profits. Some products will only gain you profits if sold in bulk rather than individually. To prevent this, you can customize the visibility settings to hide the view of products, prices, and more from your B2C or B2B customers. Another reason to customize these settings is to manage two different target audiences and sell products. For example, your B2C marketplace could sell clothing while your B2B marketplace could sell tech products. Step 3: Create Separate User Accounts for Your B2B Buyers Discounts are necessary to attract B2B consumers. For wholesale deals to be accessible, your WooCommerce B2B patrons should be signed up for a wholesale customer account. You can assign them the role of the site administrator. Customizing this process can be done in two ways: Make the wholesale customer role the default setting for a few accounts by navigating to Settings > General and changing the New User Default Role.  To add another client or change a current client’s role, navigate to the Users tab of the WordPress dashboard and choose their account from the dropdown. Scroll down to the role and select Wholesale Customer. Creating a B2B online website need not necessarily end with just three steps. After setting up the basics of the store, you can focus on other aspects like website layout, integration of various software to carry out specific processes, streamlining the checking out system, and more. There are multiple areas you could explore to make your store your own. A customized store leaves a mark on the buyer’s minds and encourages them to return for more business. Also, there might be plugins that your eCommerce business might need to function smoothly. You can visit the WooCommerce plugin marketplace listings to find those that suit your needs. In most cases, it is ideal to contact a WooCommerce expert to help you identify the plugins you need and modify them or create an entirely new one to match your objectives. Are you planning to set up a WooCommerce B2B website? Let’s Discuss To Summarize Whether a firm is a startup, an established company, or is classified as a small business, sooner or later, even the most fundamental operations will need to evolve. Technology is advancing rapidly, and humanity can barely keep up. Only the stores that adapt to and integrate the latest technological advancements survive the competition. Your B2B eCommerce marketplace must be equipped with state-of-the-art features to be ranked number one in the industry. To understand the process, systems, and features of your business needs, you must comprehend your business model, target audience, and business goals.  Based on your consumer requirements and the company’s growth, you can customize your B2B site. Customization is the essential requirement of your business and consumers. It ensures the steady advancement of your store, higher profits, buyer satisfaction, consumer loyalty, increased sales, a broader client base, and more. Unlike any other platform, WooCommerce allows the software to adjust according to your business. Through customization, managers and business owners obtain several benefits: user experiences, custom sales reports, pricing features, responsive design, unique products, and other business applications. Recognize the need in your B2B eCommerce marketplace and deliver it through customization. Customization of B2B eCommerce Marketplace on WooCommerce – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is the difference between a B2B eCommerce store and a regular eCommerce store? A regular eCommerce store is generalized to meet the requirements of the mass target audience. However, a B2B eCommerce store is tailored to fit the needs of specific buyers and give them a personalized experience. Is WooCommerce a flexible platform? Yes, WooCommerce has high technical flexibility. This allows your B2B website to shape business activities like customer pricing, registration forms for different business types, VAT or other forms of tax validations, tax support and exemption, user community support, wholesale order form, quote requests, custom checkout process, etc. How is WooCommerce B2B the best solution for you? WooCommerce is a secure, reliable, and robust platform for all B2B eCommerce marketplaces. It can manage products and their variants without compromising performance quality. Can you build custom catalogs in WooCommerce? You can create custom catalogs in WooCommerce. It has an inbuilt category and tag hierarchy feature that lets sellers customize catalogs. Is there any additional support available for WooCommerce? Since WooCommerce is widely used by businesses worldwide, it has a robust community that provides expert help. How does customization of the B2B marketplace lead to recurring purchases by consumers? To attract recurring customers, you need to make the process of reordering seamless and effortless. This is only possible through a customized user experience. Showing order history, reorder list notification, and payment information makes the process convenient for the buyers. Can I protect my B2B website from specific users? Customizing your B2B online store will hide your store and restrict access to specific users. For this, you need to implement consumer login and customer accounts by using the features available on the platform. What is a maximum or minimum order quantity? Since you run a wholesale B2B store, you need to sell a minimum number of items in bulk to earn profits. You can set a minimum or maximum limit to a particular item a buyer can buy through customization. What custom payment methods can the store owners create? WooCommerce allows store owners to create custom payment methods to streamline their business. They offer three custom payment methods: Net 30, Net 60, and Net 90. What do you mean by WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace? WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace (WCFM Marketplace) is a free open-end multi-vendor marketplace plugin powered by WooCommerce and available on WordPress. It helps you build your custom B2B eCommerce marketplace. The interface consists of a list of features that help increase your organic traffic and manage your on-site SEO more effortlessly.  The all-in-one SEO plugin manages many on-page SEO features such as canonical URLs, SEO redirects, internal linking, enhanced site indexing, identifying duplicate content, and advanced, rich snippets. Its capabilities will help you outrank your competitors in no time.  The plugin helps remove duplicate content and display rich snippets for each page on Google. The community edition of the plugin costs 319, and the Enterprise edition costs 619.  20. Merchants can use an extended list of customer attributes for setting rules. You can also give product X for free on purchase of product Y. Schedule and send discount emails and notifications. You can load product images later, improve page rendering, and optimize images. Improving the performance reduces bounce rate and encourages visitors to browse the site.  Enable JS bundling, Minify HTML and CSS, Merge CSS and JS, and much more. You can reduce the size of the product’s thumbnails without affecting their quality. Furthermore, you can apply code optimizations to ensure faster content delivery. The community version of the plugin costs 259, and the Enterprise version costs 559. 22. Banner Slider by Amasty Create beautiful sliders to highlight your offers, showcase products, and exhibit pictures. The sliders help to attract attention to the special offers. In fact, on the home page, you can highlight sliders with many animation effects.  Create clickable banners, place them in any area, and add several images in one slider. Merchants can auto-resize and lazy load images for better speed. You can even resize images for smartphones. Plus, set up separate views for mobile and desktop. The community version of the plugin costs 139, and the Enterprise version costs 429.  23. Magento Image Gallery by Magenest The extension lets every merchant create a simple gallery of rich and high-quality images. Merchants can easily set the status, name, filter function, and thumbnail picture for each photo gallery from the backend.  Plus, you can resize the images to optimize performance.  Besides uploading images, the extension also lets you insert information into the bottom area of every image in the gallery. Merchants can also control the movement of images in the gallery – horizontal or vertical scroll.  The community edition is free to download, but the Enterprise edition will cost $69. 24. Image Gallery by MageAnts Image gallery is another top extension to manage and sort all your media files on the site. This plugin can do everything from labeling the files to displaying them in a structured manner on the page. The plugin also lets admins optimize the images for responsiveness and faster load time.  Reduce the size of the images, add borders, watermarks, and other details to enhance your image. Display the photos anywhere on the site, from the product pages to the home page. The plugin costs $49 for the community edition and $128 for the Enterprise edition.  25. Image Gallery by MageArray Merchants get the ability to publish photo albums of products, events, and more. You can display and categorize all the multimedia into different categories and pages. The plugin allows the visitors to open the images in a large view in the form of a popup.  The extension lets you add, arrange, label the images, and add alt attributes to improve the SEO strength of the product pages. The extension enables you to space the pictures and arrange them in a grid. The thumbnail image would be a high-resolution picture that doesn’t compromise quality. title: A Detailed Insight on the Road to DTC for B2B Brands
headings: What Did the Landscape Look Like?
Managing Direct-to-customer (DTC) and Your Relationships With Other Businesses
Challenges in Attaining a Streamlined Direct-to-customer (DTC) Model
text: Manufacturers, who had traditionally only sold to other businesses, slowly embraced the Direct to Consumer (DTC) model. The high returns, better relationships, buyer loyalty, customer support, and other benefits have made them look outside the legacy model in place. For this reason, many manufacturers, at some point, will establish a full-blown online store. More manufacturers may adopt the eCommerce ecosystem and the other technologies in its periphery. This will help them realize operational excellence and optimum digital experience. Their future roadmap will integrate a wide range of digital solutions on various levels. The idea is to realize a successful DTC model. Table of Contents What Did the Landscape Look Like? What is Direct-to-customer (DTC)? Managing Direct-to-customer (DTC) and Your Relationships With Other Businesses Top Benefits of Embracing Direct-to-customer (DTC) 360 Degree Analytics Improve Customer Relationships Profit Margin Faster to Market Quality Control Content and Branding Omnichannel Increased Sales and Revenue More trials Customer Support Availability Promotions and Influencers Challenges in Attaining a Streamlined Direct-to-customer (DTC) Model Personalization Content User Experience Automation Logistics Mobile-first Customers Prefer Direct-to-customer (DTC) Best Industries for Direct-to-customer (DTC) Wrapping Up What Did the Landscape Look Like? Accessibility wasn’t always an option, but the ongoing digital transformation has made it possible to reach everyone anywhere. Unlike 15 years ago when acquiring an end-customer in another state seemed impossible, now you can sell straight to that buyer and that too seamlessly.  Sure there will be territories where DTC isn’t feasible, and in those areas, you can rely on distributors, wholesalers, and agents. If your product doesn’t reach a remote location in Africa, then going through an intermediary isn’t all that bad. But, keep in mind, D2C is one of the best ways to diversify your manufacturing business. The shift from B2B to DTC won’t be easy, but it’s worth every bit of serious consideration. There are plenty of concerns, and today we’ll focus on all the aspects that help create a thriving and profitable DTC model. What is Direct-to-customer (DTC)? Direct to customer is when a business decides to skip the intermediary and sell directly to the customer. Manufacturers don’t sell to other businesses, such as wholesalers or distributors. Instead, they go straight to the end customer. Manufacturers can engage and interact with the customers through the following. The official website Dedicated native apps The store on marketplaces Social media platforms  Manufacturers are slowly deviating from their standard distributor networks. They aren’t relying solely on the standard distribution channels. They want to expand beyond the realms of selling to other businesses. They want to improve their profit margins through higher-margin direct sales. Selling straight to the customer helps to do that.  Selling models like Buy Online, Pickup in Store (BOPUS), Customize Online, Pickup in Store (COPUS), and Manufacture online, Pickup in Store (MOPUS) are assisting brands in reaching their consumers directly. Having an omnichannel presence helps to connect with them anywhere and anytime. Managing Direct-to-customer (DTC) and Your Relationships With Other Businesses You can find ways to build a DTC strategy without breaking your relationship with distributors and wholesalers. You don’t want to upset your business partners. Do not try to sell a product directly to customers in territories where you already have a contract with other businesses.  Trying to do so may come in violation of the terms of your contract. Also, it’s unethical to break the trust of other businesses. If it was established that they would be the only ones operating in that territory, you might have to find a way to stay away from that region until the contract expires. In some regions, manufacturers choose to sell. However, they don’t slash the prices to anything less than what other businesses are displaying at that time. A product that costs $200 from one of your distributors cannot get priced at even $198 on your online store. You may have to rely on other ways to tempt customers, like extended warranty, free accessories, etc. Top Benefits of Embracing Direct-to-customer (DTC) 1. 360 Degree Analytics A close connection with end consumers will help the brand create better offerings. Now armed with all the behavioral, transactional, and demographic data, the brand will understand its customers better. Earlier, they did not have this valuable data since they were dealing with another business.  It was always the next business that ended up interacting with the customers. Manufacturers can now leverage pivotal, real-time data to understand buyer behavior, business performance, and product demands. The data helps to make informed decisions. Adopting DTC means manufacturers prevent overstocking and forecast better.  Advanced analytical tools, such as Customer Data Platform, help businesses compile and analyze data to succeed in their DTC venture. You get the feedback straight from the end-user. This helps scale and perfect your services and products without relying on any middleman. Better insights lead to better strategies, promotions, and communication. 2. Improve Customer Relationships Knowing more about your customers helps to create the right discounts, promotions, messaging, and recommendations. With DTC, manufacturers aren’t relying on speculation or hearsay from another business. Instead, they analyze and incorporate the rich data, collected straight from the customer in their next marketing campaign.  When brands start to show relevant ads and promotions, more customers will come onboard and complete purchases. This improves your relationships with customers, increases sales, and improves customer loyalty. Customers no longer see generic ads, instead they see personalized messages, more relevant to their unique needs.   3. Profit Margin By eliminating the middleman, you get rid of entities that cut into your profit. When selling goods to other businesses, you set the price in such a way that they can mark it up and make some profit. In essence, you have to factor their profits as well. These businesses limit your profit margin, something you can navigate by heading straight to end-users.  A product costs you $10, you sell it to another business for $15 and they sell it to a customer for $25. You make a profit of $5, but by cutting out the intermediary, you can make a profit of $15. The DTC model also lets you offer bigger discounts, due to a higher profit margin. So, you can sell it for $20 as well. Better discounts could possibly create more conversions. 4. Faster to Market From inception to release, it’ll take much less time to launch a product in the market. No need to tie up with other businesses or convince them to buy your new product. You won’t have to worry about third-party retailers not accepting your new product due to its no sales history. Conceive it and launch it yourself   Let the customer decide the fate of your new item. Manufacturers can release a new innovative product on a smaller scale. Plus, it helps you to understand what customers think about the product. Collect that feedback, make appropriate adjustments, and relaunch a perfected product. 5. Quality Control Selling straight to the end consumer ensures the quality of your product, pricing, and packaging – in sync with your standards. You get to control the condition in which customers receive the product, something you couldn’t do while going through other entities. Get more visibility into how the product gets packed, shipped, and delivered.  Sometimes third-parties damage the goods. But, they ship the product to the buyer nonetheless. The buyer receives a faulty product and blames it on the manufacturer. Thus, your reputation goes for a toss for no fault of your own. Manufacturers don’t need to depend on their distributors and retail partners to ensure quality. They can take complete control over production, stocking, logistics, and sales. 6. Content and Branding Going DTC, brands get to control and manage the messaging, experience, and reputation of their brand. Third-Party retailers and other businesses can dilute your branding. Selling through other businesses means your message will be far less impactful.  You get complete control over every touchpoint that your customers interact with. If this wasn’t the case, the wholesalers and third-party retailers would control the brand perception. Plus, they may even find it hard to sell your products, due to knowing much less. Let’s be honest, no one knows a product like the manufacturer.  Manufacturers can effectively communicate on the differential aspects of their inventory that can be of benefit to customers. They can present the unique value proposition of their brand and products, something that other businesses fail to identify and convey. 7. Omnichannel Your buyers can browse across any channels, purchase from any of them,  and even return a product on any of the channels. Brands can access customers anywhere they want. The interconnected ecosystem lets you track and engage with customers anywhere.  Plus, the collected data from different channels gives you better insights into how buyers interact with your brand. Brands can give their buyers a seamless and consistent experience. Buyers get the convenience to buy anywhere and you get to deliver an integrated experience.  7. Increased Sales and Revenue More insight into your customers leads to offerings that interest them and lead to more sales. Plus, you get the flexibility to cross-sell and upsell products. This allows you build a robust and deep relationship with your consumers. A better relationship leads to more loyalty, which results in more sales and revenue.  DTC marketing provides you with good insight into customer data. Use the customer data to understand customer behavior. Know their shopping habits and other browsing behavior to encourage more conversions. An increase in conversions will undoubtedly result in more revenue and profits. All as a result of understanding your buyers better via DTC. 9. More trials Going straight to customers means you get to try products faster. You are no longer going through any intermediaries. Any inefficiency in their ecosystem or supply chain will not affect your time introducing a product or service into the market. You take charge of the product and ensure it reaches the customers.  Plus, collect feedback and revise your product. No need to rely on distributors. When customers interact with you, they leave hints and reviews that stay with you. Use this data to improve your offerings. Plus, you get to use the mailing list to retarget them at a later date. You’ll know who they are, where they live, and how to contact them. Test new products far more quickly and often due to the direct contact with consumers. Eliminate any risk by testing the products with consumers first – before selling them to a distributor or wholesalers for other territories.  10. Customer Support  Buyers get direct access to your support team. They don’t have to speak to an intermediary who coordinates with you. Customers reach out to you straight on an eCommerce site or your retail store. When selling on third-party stores, their teams try to resolve the issues, and if it doesn’t help, they ultimately reach out to the manufacturer.  The loss of time and lack of immediate response leads to customer dissatisfaction. Also, these intermediaries have a team who knows very little about the products. Relaying and communicating with brand experts is more accurate and comprehensive than third-party distributors. The in-house team will give you more freedom to nurture relations, handle returns, replacements, queries, and refunds. 11. Availability Your brand can be continually accessible to customers compared to other businesses that may or may not operate 24/7. You can be available for your customers to ensure any issues get sorted and resolved immediately. If the customer had to reach out to another business, the likelihood of getting a resolution is low.  Plus, they may need to get in touch with you to resolve the issue in some instances. Now, you get to take the problem head-on and be there for the end-user. No more disgruntled customers who avoid your brand due to a bad experience with another retailer. Serve them better and serve them sooner. 12. Promotions and Influencers Manufacturers can introduce products to their global clients, and they need not reserve a high budget on ads for gaining customer attention. The promotions and deals in place suffice to generate customer interest to draw them to your site. Plus, you have a high chance of turning your customers into brand advocates and influencers with DTC. They will spread your message and advocate your brand by word of mouth. Why? Because they had a great time interacting with you. You were able to create a top-tier user experience for your buyers. Something that other businesses fail to do. Challenges in Attaining a Streamlined Direct-to-customer (DTC) Model 1. Personalization Adjust your communication, marketing campaigns, and other offers to suit the buyer persona. Send emails and newsletters personalized to a customer’s demographic and behavioral data. When a customer views relevant offers, more suited to their needs, they get tempted to engage and purchase from you.  Adjust the message, tone, type of content, vouchers, and more to what the specific customer wants. Even the product recommendations must match the buyer’s interests. If possible, go as far as displaying payment options and logistics providers in sync with your buyer’s interests.  2. Content Informative content that tells the buyer everything they need to know about the products and more. From certifications to product specifications, cover everything to create the best clarity around your products and brand. Having a content strategy optimized for search engines to draw more organic visitors.  Spec sheets, brochures, certifications, images, videos, infographics and much more play a pivotal role in attracting and retaining visitors. Visitors evaluate every little detail before buying a product. Optimize the content on your eCommerce site. Captivating and educational content plays a key role in nurturing buyer relationships as well.  3. User Experience A direct connection isn’t enough till you provide an adequate user experience or shopping experience. This may mean more convenience, somewhere on par with Amazon to tempt them to shop more from your portal. Plus, better speed, navigation, and information accessibility. In essence, a frictionless experience.  All this helps ensure your customers get what they want faster and more easily. Help your customers locate products, contact info, and other details as soon as they land on your store. Plus, offer the best performance on your website to avoid any abandonment due to delays. Also, perform mobile optimization to help users access the site from smartphones. 4. Automation Integrate high-end automation tools to speed your backend processes. This helps you move operations faster and serve customers sooner. With fewer errors, bottlenecks, and delays, you will see better efficiencies in your organizations for a D2C model. Use Accounting, order management,  Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and other software to handle your internal processes.  Rely on sophisticated systems to eliminate errors and other redundancies. Every entity, such as orders, tax, sales, logistics, etc., get processed and streamlined with absolute precision. Your workforce can focus on business management activities, marketing, customer acquisition, and customer support. They don’t need to worry about handling data manually. 5. Logistics Improve the way you handle shipping. If you are selling straight to consumers, then any delays or damaged goods can lead to future losses, lawsuits, bad image, and much more. Manufacturers need to reduce bottlenecks and streamline processes in their supply chain. Use dropshipping to get the order out as soon as possible.  Always be in the know-how about orders. Ensure you show the correct quantity to avoid out-of-stock situations and ship out orders correctly. Don’t mix up any orders and handle the labeling more precisely.  Try to incorporate a robust Return management system to handle all the returns seamlessly. Keep tabs on carrier rates and their shipping policies to save on delivery charges.  Have an automated system to refund the amount for the returned orders. Consumers want the ease of handling returns online. Implement real-time tracking, so they don’t need to reach out to customer support for minute-by-minute updates on their orders. 6. Mobile-first Consumers are more reliant on their phones for researching and buying products. They need to develop new-age strategies to fit their marketing and other development around smartphones. This might mean having a mobile-friendly website or a native mobile app. Sometimes even popping up for local searches can also make a difference to your business.  A mobile-first approach can enable brands to engage with buyers better. Many of your buyers are more likely to discover a social media post on their phone. Nowadays, creating eye-catching posts is easier than ever—you can create with Picsart or similar apps. Augmented Reality (AR) is another reason mobile shopping is growing so much. You can start directing ads and other communication towards consumers on mobile devices. Customers Prefer Direct-to-customer (DTC) In the recent past, customers too preferred to buy products directly from online brands. Many online shoppers have lost trust in other businesses due to counterfeit products. They aren’t willing to commit and put their faith in another brand for discounts and vouchers, only to end up with a defective product.  Customers prefer to browse the high-quality products on the manufacturer’s websites, knowing that if anything goes wrong, they’ll be able to go straight to the manufacturer. There is no need to go through vendors and other businesses that may or may not relay the concerns to the manufacturer.  The peace of mind when dealing with a manufacturer trumps everything else. Sometimes, even the convenience of buying a product from another vendor on a marketplace like Amazon or Etsy doesn’t seem lucrative. Manufacturers can capitalize on this trend to attract more buyers to their online stores. Best Industries for Direct-to-customer (DTC) Fashion and clothing, sports goods, home decor, cosmetics, and small electronic accessories, are some industries that can easily go direct to customers. These brands control the user experience, increase profit margins, and collect first-party shopper data. They get to bypass the middlemen and sell straight to consumers.  The use of Subscription models, rich content, Augmented Reality, chatbots, and Virtual Reality has made it easier for consumers to shop and get a better understanding of goods.  Brands in these industries have proper tools and integrations to engage with their consumers personally. Wrapping Up Brands can now connect, engage, and relate to their buyers personally using all the new-age tools and technologies. Through DTC,  brands get to ditch the long and winding supply chain. They can use eCommerce and other channels to communicate and sell their products to the end-users.  Brands are already on their way to building direct sales channels. The minimal customer acquisition costs, ability to build long-lasting relationships, and other benefits make them adopt D2C. Brands now have proper tools and integrations to engage with their consumers personally.

title: The Ultimate Guide on Customer Data Platform (CDP)
headings: What is a Customer Data Platform (CDP)?
Top Highlights of Customer Data Platform
Why is Customer Data Platform Superior to Customer Relationship Management?
text: Organizations have been using analytics to influence many marketing decisions in their ecosystem. But, very often, the data they use is unreliable and doesn’t give a holistic picture of the buyer. There’s not much you can do with the incomplete data . As a result, the marketing campaign fails to take off, and you get measly returns.  Other times, the collected data gets corrupted or misplaced. Else, the data stays confined to a single channel. Businesses fail to identify the unique needs and interests of their buyer demographic. The systems and solutions in place don’t give a 360° understanding of their target audience.  That is why you need a Customer Data Platform or CDP. CDP helps to deliver a unique and unified view into your customers’ minds and needs. This helps to gain a comprehensive understanding of your target audience. Thus, CDP helps brands create a more personalized campaign that is more suited to the buyer’s expectations.  Not only that, organizations can create a unified profile of their customers and target them on any channel. CDP helps merchants utilize zero, first, and third party data . This helps them comprehend their customers,  personalize their offerings, and improve buyer relationships. Let’s look at all this in more detail. Table of Contents What is a Customer Data Platform (CDP)? Top Highlights of Customer Data Platform Omnichannel Holistic 360° Data Unified Customer Database Proper Data Extensive Analysis Usability Data Compliance Sharing Automated Procedures Top Benefits for eCommerce Businesses Better Decisions Hyper Personalization Remove Data Silos Buyer Relationships New Territories Campaign Optimization Increase Sales, Revenue, and Profits What is Customer Relationship Management (CRM)? Why is Customer Data Platform Superior to Customer Relationship Management? Data Limitations Creates Silos Unstructured Lacks Holistic Analysis More Manual Security Wrapping Up What is a Customer Data Platform (CDP)? Customer Data Platform is a system that helps an organization create a persistent, unified, and holistic customer database. It aggregates and organizes buyer data from a range of touchpoints. CDPs compile and arrange real-time data into individual customer profiles. The profiles are accessible from a central interface.  CDP builds and integrates data from first, second, and third-party sources. CDP mainly uses three types of data about its buyers, and these are: Behavioral data Demographic data Transactional data The use of all this data empowers you with the relevant and actionable customer insights your business needs to create better and longer-lasting relationships with the customers. Implementing a CDP often requires robust data integration and management, which can be effectively achieved through professional data engineering consulting services. The Artificial Intelligence in CDPs help the company reap more benefits or higher returns in their investment. They do this by acquiring a better understanding of a customer – a 360-degree understanding. Structured, sorted, and clean data Deliver personalization Build buyer demographics Campaign optimization and learning Unify zero and first-party data Real-time data processing AI-driven automated processes Demographic, psychographic data with behavioral identifiers Ready-made workflows Top Highlights of Customer Data Platform 1. Omnichannel Businesses get to collect data from all touchpoints – offline channels and Digital Channels, ensuring seamless integration with a lead management system for efficient marketing workflows. The true omnichannel capability of CDP helps brands collect, clean, and access customer data from any channel. Plus, businesses get to deliver personalized communication on any channel to improve buyer relationships and the results of their marketing campaigns.  2. Holistic 360° Data CDP visualizes and collects data through individual user profiles, thereby creating a 360° view of the customer. CDP helps to collect Behavioral Data, Transactional Data, and Demographic Data. The focus on every aspect helps to derive a complete picture of the consumer.  3. Unified Customer Database Eliminates inconsistent data that gets pulled from multiple online and offline touchpoints. Customer Data Platform helps to create a reliable and unified single view of the customer. No more collecting data from various internal systems. The centralisation facilitated by data integration ensures easy access on one single platform. Create a Unified customer profile of the data obtained from every Customer Touchpoint. A Single Customer Profile that holds data of Customer Interactions from a Variety Of Sources. Enhance data collection efficiency by enabling users to scan QR code across touchpoints. 4. Proper Data Data in dated softwares and systems can often get misplaced and corrupted. Relying on unreliable data leads to wrong decisions that drain money, time and effort. Plus the marketing campaign goes for a toss. With Customer Data Platform, all the data gets correctly sorted, cleaned, and stored. Businesses access and use the best data for decision making.  Customer Data Platform has the ability to create an Accurate Customer Profile and store granular first-party and third-party data. CDP collects information from existing systems and databases. It will then structure, standardize, and normalize the data into sensible information.  Transactional data – order history Behavioral data – website or app usage or responses to messages User data – age, gender or contact data Psychographic data – emotions, attitudes or beliefs 5. Extensive Analysis Customer Data Platform helps to breakdown and analyze the customer data in real-time. CDPs help to gain insights, identify gaps, tap into high‑value territories, and use high-quality data to predict a customer’s future steps. The evolved algorithm within the CDP collects more accurate and actionable insights than any other data extraction and storage tool. CDP helps to understand customer behavior better.  6. Usability Customer Data Platforms organize and store data more effectively. As such, any immediate use is more likely, than when corporations end up using a CRM. Crm requires more effort to set things up. Plus, setting-up and maintaining a CDP doesn’t require technical expertise. The in-built tools are more than capable of handling the data, thereby minimizing the human effort.  7. Data Compliance Customer data platforms support data insight requests and data portability. Merchants can easily demonstrate the responsible use of customer data. They can show an extensive breakdown of how they collect and use data. Thus, merchants don’t need to concern themselves with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and other regulations. Plus, you can easily erase any personally identifiable information.   8. Sharing Customer Data Platform can easily interconnect with any existing systems in your ecosystem. CDP can forward and share data with any system that needs it. The way the platform stores and structures the data makes it easy for anyone to pass the information further, without any corruption or data loss. Share data with the Marketing Teams without any friction.  9. Automated Procedures The automated workflow within the CDP helps to extract and collect second-party and third-party data along with first-party data. This minimizes human intervention and speeds up backend processes, improves productivity, and helps businesses utilize their resources more efficiently. Top Benefits for eCommerce Businesses 1. Better Decisions With CDP, business owners get improved, impactful, and data-driven decision making. Instead of following a random and misleading approach that relies on ambiguous data, business owners will now use rich, informative, and cleaner data to make their decisions. Useful data leads to better decisions and profitable campaigns, than generic data. 2. Hyper Personalization Intuitive data collected from the Customer Data Platform helps to deliver communication, offers, and promotions in sync with buyer interests. Otherwise, business owners would have had to rely on weak data that heavily compromises their buyer communication. Plus, they aren’t able to provide personalized experiences.  With CDP, merchants get a granular understanding of every buyer, which helps to create more personalized campaigns. Merchants can easily persuade and tempt customers to click, view, engage, stay, and complete a purchase. Buyers spend more time due to finding information that connects with their unique preferences.  3. Remove Data Silos With Customer Data Platform, merchants get to consolidate all their customer data on one hub. Plus, all the departments and officials within the company can  easily exchange and forward information. You can exchange info between various personnels in your company, without the need for manual intervention.   All key people within the company will be in the loop. They’ll have complete know-how about customers from anywhere in the world. The ability to access data situated on a single platform, makes it easier to coordinate and collaborate internally. Get fast and seamless access from a single interface from anywhere. 4. Buyer Relationships Sending more relevant communication to the right buyer at the right time and right place, creates more interest, and improves the likelihood of them interacting with the store. Whereas, sending generic promotional offers and messages, not aligned with their interests widens the gap.  They’d much rather associate with businesses that understand and embrace their problems, budget, interests, and other needs, than work with a company that is not in the same headspace. Buyers are more likely to revisit, if they find products and solutions more tailor-made for their profile.  5. New Territories The ability to tap into data about buyers can help businesses enter new territories. Merchants can utilize the collected data to get deeper insights into a community from a particular geography. The next buyer from that zone will give you even more data, and so on.  An umbrella buyer from a region that records high rainfall, tells the brand that similar buyers in the region may have the same set of needs. Brands can recommend umbrellas, raincoats, boots, and other accessories, either through offline or online channels. The point being, even a small amount of valuable data helps businesses capture more customers from territories that were otherwise alien to them.  6. Campaign Optimization Real-time learning from a marketing campaign, helps to modify and adjust the campaign midway. View how users interact and respond to the campaign. Study the efficiency and outcome daily. CDP helps to offer insights for solving problems such as high advertising spendings or content mismatch for the targeted audience. Businesses can learn and improve their efforts midway.  7. Increase Sales, Revenue, and Profits Data-driven decisions are more likely to succeed, as it is closer to what customers want. The use of specific data gives you more insight into a customer’s mind, and that helps to customize information for their exact requirements. When they view info that appeals to them, they’re more likely to take action.  The more this persists, and the more persuasive and personalized your communication gets, the more interested buyers will feel with your brand. After a while, they’ll only be invested with you to the extent where no other brand will even seem like an option. This leads to an increase in your Customer lifetime value. Thereby, increasing sales, revenue and profits. What is Customer Relationship Management (CRM)? Customer Relationship Management is a cohesive system that collects and stores vital data of your prospects and customers. But, most modern CRM solutions have certain inherent limitations that restrict them from providing ample returns to a business. CRMs are mainly built for customer-facing reps, like salespersons and customer support staff. CRM data will give you a client’s name, their history of interactions with the customer support team, and tickets they’ve filed (among many other things). On the other hand, CDP will show specific steps taken by the customer since engaging with your company, from where they found you to how they behave with your product. The absence of AI and predictive capabilities in CRM makes it more dated. Plus, it lacks integral features to collect, clean, and handle pivotal data. It does a terrible job of organizing and sorting data. CDP, on the other hand, with all the built-in features, will responsibly handle the data of every customer across multiple touchpoints.  Businesses need to utilize the customer’s behavior to outrank the competition. Using customer demographics and other random data from a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software alone will not win you the eCommerce race. CRM can help you manage buyer relationships but comes up short when it comes to handling buyer data.  The legacy system features in CRM mean businesses need to rely on multiple systems in the learning curve, alongside all the integration cost, dependency on development, time for implementation, and other drawbacks that can create frictions and failure points – merchants can utilize CDP. Why is Customer Data Platform Superior to Customer Relationship Management? 1. Data Limitations CRM is more suitable for storing and preserving limited information about your buyer base. CRM doesn’t do a very good job of analyzing, deriving insights, and detecting patterns in huge chunks of data. CRM is incapable of handling a proliferation of data. 2. Creates Silos The inability to forward information is probably one of the biggest bottlenecks in a CRM system. CRM is mainly closeted data, that stays limited to a section. CRM doesn’t relay data as effectively as CDP does. You can’t seamlessly share and transfer information between different departments. As such, information requested by an employee doesn’t reach him instantly.  3. Unstructured CRM, mislabels and loses data often. The data within the CRM can be spread out over different folders, making it difficult for a user to obtain the info quickly. It also provides a very broad and sometimes inaccurate behavior analysis. CRM fails to get the specifics about customers right, as such, businesses can’t draw a correct inference.  4. Lacks Holistic Analysis  CRM lacks proper Analytics Capabilities.
