Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.Single Line Text * Email * Single Line TextSubmit A better approach would be to select a software engineering company like Viritna with in-depth knowledge and experience in multiple eCommerce platforms to strategize, design, develop and support your eCommerce site while letting your marketing team do what they do best – marketing. 7. Wrong Platform Following the example of the car rally, to win the race, you must select the engine that meets the “needs of the road.” Seeing as the engine is the most important component of the car, choosing the wrong one could be disastrous. The same is the case for the eCommerce platform, and the wrong one could end up doing more harm than good. According to the two most popular technology tracking websites Datanyze and BuildWith, there are approximately 500+ eCommerce platforms available for businesses to choose from. So how do you choose from this sea of eCommerce platforms, the ideal one for your business? The 20 points below are all the factors that your business should consider while selecting the ideal eCommerce platform, beyond the decisions like SaaS vs. self-hosted vs. headless vs. decoupled. As‌ ‌you‌ ‌can‌ ‌see,‌ ‌choosing‌ ‌the‌ ‌right‌ ‌platform‌ ‌for‌ ‌your‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌business‌ ‌can‌ ‌be‌ ‌a‌ ‌very‌ ‌challenging‌ ‌task.‌ ‌From‌ ‌cost‌ ‌of‌ ‌ownership‌ ‌to‌ ‌Upfront‌ ‌Implementation‌ ‌Costs,‌ ‌you‌ ‌need‌ ‌to‌ ‌factor‌ ‌every‌ ‌single‌ ‌facet‌ ‌before‌ ‌finalizing‌ ‌the‌ ‌right‌ ‌platform.‌ ‌Not‌ ‌every‌ ‌platform‌ ‌is‌ ‌fit‌ ‌for‌ ‌your‌ ‌unique‌ ‌business.‌ ‌An‌ ‌experienced‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌development‌ ‌company‌ ‌like‌ ‌Virtina‌ ‌with‌ ‌expertise,‌ ‌certified‌ ‌partnerships‌ ‌in‌ ‌multiple‌ ‌platforms,‌ ‌and‌ ‌an‌ ‌unbiased‌ ‌approach‌ ‌to‌ ‌platform‌ ‌selection‌ ‌can‌ ‌help‌ ‌you‌ ‌figure‌ ‌out‌ ‌the‌ ‌right‌ ‌platform‌ ‌for‌ ‌your‌ ‌business.‌ Need help in selecting a platform? Let’s have a word! Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.Single Line Text * Email * Single Line TextSubmit 8. Weak Implementation or Build Process An engineering project must be approached like an engineering project and nothing less. You need to put in the same effort and precision that you’d put into an engineering project. Treating your eCommerce site as a JAW (Just Another Website) often leads to catastrophic project failure. A well laid out implementation plan should have clearly defined phases shown below. Discovery Planning Platform Selection Design Development Migration Support Optimization  The phases should have iterations built to accommodate flexibility and learning while reducing the risk of cost and time. Ideally, it’d also balance the scope creep while keeping the costs and timelines in check. Depending‌ ‌on‌ ‌the‌ ‌client,‌ ‌budget,‌ ‌timeline,‌ ‌and‌ ‌other‌ ‌preferences,‌ ‌either‌ ‌an‌ ‌Adaptive‌ ‌Hybrid‌ ‌or‌ ‌Adaptive‌ ‌Agile‌ ‌Implementation‌ ‌(Agile‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌approach)‌ ‌can‌ ‌be‌ ‌used.‌ Adaptive Hybrid Implementation Process Adaptive Agile Implementation Process 9. Build, They Will “NOT” Come Let’s assume that you did manage to create the best eCommerce store for your business for a minute. What next? Do you just sit and wait to get an enormous spike in traffic and conversions? If you intend to get into the eCommerce business with such assumptions, let me stop you from doing so. Just‌ ‌because‌ ‌you‌ ‌have‌ ‌built‌ ‌the‌ ‌best‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌store‌ ‌does‌ ‌not‌ ‌mean‌ ‌that‌ ‌your‌ ‌online‌ ‌sales‌ ‌will‌ ‌sky-rocket.‌ ‌‌You‌ ‌have‌ ‌to‌ ‌invest‌ ‌in‌ ‌organic‌ ‌reach,‌ ‌such‌ ‌as,‌ ‌content‌ ‌marketing,‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌Search‌ ‌Engine‌ ‌Optimization‌ ‌(SEO),‌ ‌in‌ ‌paid‌ ‌marketing,‌ ‌abd‌ ‌other‌ ‌digital‌ ‌marketing‌ ‌strategies‌ ‌to‌ ‌reach‌ ‌your‌ ‌eCommerce‌ ‌store’s‌ ‌full‌ ‌potential.‌  With the right marketing team (remember the driving team), the right channels for the target customer demographics, the right content, and the right marketing tool, you can attract the optimum number of visitors to your site. At Virtina, our core focus is on building the ideal engine (eCommerce store), and we rely upon a few selected marketing partners whom we may recommend (at least two) if you are ever in need of one. 10. Absence of Continuous Improvement When it comes to eCommerce, you can implement “continuous improvement” through 3 different but mutually related optimization techniques. a. Content Optimization The goal is to optimize the content for organic reach and SEO using techniques and tools focusing on keywords, search engine rank positions (SERPs). You can even make use of the latest strategies like content commerce and content marketing. b. title: The Indispensable Role of eCommerce SEO in Digital Marketing
headings: What is SEO or Search Engine Optimization?
Why Do Brands Need eCommerce SEO and What Are the Benefits?
Meta Tags and Schema HTML Tags
text: Have you ever wondered, when upon typing something on Google – why a particular result ranks above the other? Well, this has everything to do with SEO. Correctly done, SEO has the power to position your eCommerce website or brand at the top. 93% of online experiences begin with a search engine – Search Engine Journal When it comes to Digital Marketing – SEO is believed to be the most integral part of it. A properly executed SEO strategy has the power to rank a website on the first page of SERP. The popular perception is that consumers make up their minds within the first two pages of the search results, which warrants the need for an SEO overhaul of your eCommerce website.  Not only that, but SEO assisted marketing activities are also likely to be more impactful. If you’ve made up your mind about digital marketing, then you can’t do the same without SEO. What is SEO or Search Engine Optimization? SEO or Search Engine Optimization is the practice of optimizing content to be discovered through a search engine’s organic search results. SEO is about helping your target audience find your business from among thousands of other companies online. Nowadays, even the idea of Content Commerce on an eCommerce website is invalidated without being backed by an adequately done eCommerce SEO. So, get to it and start an eCommerce SEO campaign – because having an eCommerce site is not enough. The same needs to be revised with eCommerce SEO to make it more effective. How Does eCommerce SEO Work? eCommerce SEO works by indicating to search engines that a piece of content is the best result for the search phrase entered on it. eCommerce SEO is, therefore, used to optimize the content for better visibility. All search engines have the same goal – show the best, most relevant results to their users. Google’s algorithm works by assessing a piece of content on E-A-T (Expertise – Authoritativeness and Trustworthiness) . If your content meets these standards – then it’ll rank higher on SERP. As such, if you want more traffic to any of the web pages, you need to mold your eCommerce SEO around the search engine’s algorithm. This may even come to include revisiting pages that lack proper content and editing them. The same pages mustn’t fail to show up on top on every SERP. Mobile-friendliness can become another contributing factor. Google gives preference to pages that are optimized for mobile. As such, you don’t want a desktop version of a page to load on mobile. The best part – eCommerce SEO actions can be adjusted as the search landscape, indexing, meta tags and other variable rules change from time to time. Not only this, but it is entirely possible to develop a personalized eCommerce SEO strategy for a company.  Why Do Brands Need eCommerce SEO and What Are the Benefits? eCommerce SEO services are needed to increase sales, lift engagement, increase revenue, and improve profits. Here are some of the other reasons why brands are committed to pursuing SEO. Brand Awareness The clout of eCommerce SEO is such that it can propel your brand to the top of SERP if done meticulously. Being on the first page means more eyes on your brand – which in-turn means more visibility . Every search term that results in your company getting to the top – will elevate awareness around your brand. The higher you show in search results, the higher the brand popularity will be for your target audience. Suddenly your brand will be recognized a lot more due to it featuring at the top quite often. Brand Credibility Ranking higher on the search page continually elevates your brand value. People start to recognize your company as the top brand on that particular topic. What that brings is credibility – which comes from a place where people have faith and trust in your brand . Once Google starts to position your brand at the top – know that you are already on the road to becoming the industry leader. Showing up more on a SERP around a particular phrase gives you the relative dominance you seek. It establishes your brand as the alpha. Accessing New Demographic eCommerce SEO creates more opportunities. Due to ranking higher on SERP and other local directories, your brand is discovered faster and across more territories. Global SEO allows for the brand to shine the world over. This ability enables brands to acquire more customers and that, too, while keeping the customer acquisition costs low. More Leads Now that you have more prominent visibility, more people can access your content and discover your page. Due to which, the likelihood of leads is higher. Higher traffic to any of the pages means from a given sample size; means more people are likely to drop an inquiry for a chance to communicate on a later date or even subscribe to your newsletters – thereby leading to more leads. Quality Traffic Accurately done eCommerce SEO, will increase the traffic to your web pages from the buyer persona that matters to you. In other words, a lot of the visitors will be the target audience , not uninterested and irrelevant traffic that has no desire to transact with your company. SEO delivers qualified visitors to your web pages. Less traffic from undesirable segments also lessens the sales team’s time and effort, as they attend to prospect leads only. Compared to a time when they’d have to weed through all the junk leads and unrelated calls – before they could close a minimal amount of leads in a day. High Conversion Rates When more traffic from the concerned segment or target audience starts flowing to the web pages – the chances of conversions get elevated . This has to do with the visitor arriving at the exact information or assistance that he was seeking. When the visitor finds what they were looking for, the engagement time on the eCommerce site goes up. As a result of the brand’s knowledge on the subject matter – the visitor will likely spend more time and give improved retention rates to the eCommerce website. Now that their impression about the company is sky high – they’ve made up their mind to collaborate with you, which is nothing but another conversion. Runs 24/7 Round the clock impact is generated when making investments in eCommerce SEO. Offline marketing (Billboards) is only visible at a particular time of the day and out of reach if you do not pass by it. Whereas eCommerce SEO has no time limit – when done right, companies reap consistent rewards of SEO. eCommerce SEO fuelled relevant content is available 24/7. When a user searches for something related to your industry – there is a chance that your web page will be the first one they see – at any time of the day. Users can conveniently search for something, without the need to drag themselves to a seminar, expo, trade show, etc. Affordable PPC (Pay Per Click) costs a ton, and you run the risk of emptying your cash reserves for close to no returns. On top of that, as soon as you stop spending money, the profits end right there. Now, eCommerce SEO is not the same. With eCommerce SEO, some of the work done can be lifelong – once you establish yourself at the top of the SERP – you may find yourself sitting there forever. The best part, eCommerce SEO is economical . All you’d need is an eCommerce SEO specialist and you are on your way to earning enough revenue and profits. The ROI on SEO is way higher than on any digital marketing activity – the cost-effective measures within SEO is what makes it the top strategy to capture any KPI. Various eCommerce SEO Services Here are all the potential tactics you can try within SEO. All of it or sometimes even some of it will lead to better positioning on SERP and other benefits. Content Content forms the backbone of your eCommerce website; thus, it needs the best eCommerce SEO care. An extensive SEO process revises the website and backlink content – by aligning it with what your buyer persona is searching for. Such a revision will improve the chances of the content getting triggered whenever someone searches for anything related to it. A content analysis on an eCommerce website will come to include – Checking for duplicate content, copywriting articles, blog posts, or any other social media content. Besides this, you’d also need guest blog content creation to fortify your content ecosystem. Keywords A comprehensive analysis of keywords is necessary to yield better results from the SEO campaign. An extensive eCommerce SEO process detects special, relevant, and high-volume keywords . The keywords are crucial to attracting your target audience. Also, the content mentioned above would be worthless without a vigorous Keyword strategy integrated into it. Beyond this, the keyword analysis would aim for Rank checking of keywords and predictive keywords. URL Optimization On the eCommerce website, you’d want the URLs to follow a consistent and logical structure. It also won’t do any harm if you started adding different categories in the URL. The role of “sub-folders” helps Google establish whether some pages come under a specific category or folder. Such a minuscule change gives Google more understanding about each page in that category. Besides this, redirect any old URL to new pages – get forwarded to the most relevant page. Initiate “301 redirects” to preserve all the “link juice” and ensure that all the historical links continue to work in your favor. Use URL mapping to identify and insert targeted keywords to the URL structure of various landing pages. Implement Canonical tags to establish the “master page” and to make it simple for crawlers to render and index a page. Sitemaps Sitemaps contain the URLs you want the crawlers to visit. Hence, these sitemaps need to be up to date and complete. Create a sitemap that includes a well-organized list of links to all the vital pages of the eCommerce website. Utilize Google Search Console for this purpose. A comprehensive analysis of XML sitemaps is necessary to eliminate errors and ensure that search engines are processing the website as intended. Head over to the “Sitemaps” feature in Google Search Console – to double-check that your sitemap is all good. If possible, use a plugin (Yoast SEO) to dynamically create and update the XML sitemap as the site evolves. Link Analysis The last thing an eCommerce website wants is to end up with broken links . Invalid links disrupt the user experience and make the site look suspicious to the visitor – which then leads to abandonment and elevates the bounce rates. Links that either don’t lead to the desired content or redirect to a “404 page” – needs to be fixed. Insert enough internal links to other pages on the website – which then helps Google to learn more about the website. Even backlinks from other trusted websites help to improve the credibility of the site in Google’s eyes. Increasing quality backlinks will elevate the website’s ranking. Backlinks are critical to domain authority and ranking. A good quality backlink from a trusted and authoritative website will significantly improve the way Google perceives your website. Quality backlinks are anything that directs to valuable content on your website. Image Optimization Use the right keywords for both the image name as well as the alt tag. Alt attributes tell SEO crawlers about the content within the image. Aside from this, ensure that the pictures do not take too long to load. Compress the images – use an image optimizer like Tiny PNG, Kraken, etc. to ensure that the image size is reduced while retaining the image quality. Use lazyload to delay the image-loading till the same is exposed to the user. If none of this gets the job done, take a shot at Content Delivery Network (CDN) . A CDN will host all the images and media files on its server – so when a user tries to access the page, the CDN closest to his location will load the images. CDN is especially useful when your eCommerce website receives global traffic. Competitor Analysis In this analysis, you’d understand how your competitors are performing and what factors contribute to their success. This process helps a company to grasp which specific keywords and links may be useful for optimization. Take a step back and assess the overall industry and your competitors, and what the search landscape looks like. Look at the competitor’s domain rating, Ahrefs rank, referring domains, featured snippets and then organic traffic and keywords. Identify the competitors, evaluate their keyword difficulty, look for keyword opportunities, dig into their backlink profile, examine site structure (overall UX), and finally learn about their social media tactics. Once done, produce a comprehensive competitor intelligence report based on your findings. Meta Tags and Schema HTML Tags When it comes to meta tags – write a unique title tag for each page. Keep it short, but descriptive. Avoid generic and vague titles or descriptions. Make sure to create something click-worthy, try to match search intent, and include the target keyword where it makes sense. Fix all the Meta title errors and meta description errors. Analyze and fix – missing, duplicated, too long, or too short meta tags. When it comes to Schema tags – Add Schema markup to your HTML to improve the way your page is displayed in SERPs. It is possible to add rich snippets – both a star rating and a publication date – to a search result. Allegedly, search results with extensive rich snippets will have a better click-through rate (CTR) – as it makes the search result seem more informative. Events, videos, FAQs, recipe, etc. are all added as Schema Markups. Google Ecosystem Use the Google AdWords and a range of other keyword research tools to see which keywords are most valuable to gain traction online. Use Google Analytics to learn more about your visitors. Monitor the organic search traffic sources to see what keywords people are using to find your eCommerce website in SERP. Use Google Search Console Management to monitor and manage your eCommerce website’s presence in search results. Google search console is also used to identify and manage duplicate content. Use Google’s Keyword Planner to identify the most relevant keywords for your brand. Crawling & Robots.txt A robots.txt file lives at the root of the website. Robots.txt is a plain text file that follows the Robots Exclusion Standard. A robots.txt file consists of one or more rules. Each rule blocks or gives access for a crawler to a specified file path on that website. It is essential to do a crawl analysis; such an analysis will often tell you when a given web page is correctly marked as non-index by a tag in the header. By doing so, web-spiders will crawl it, but not add it to the list of indexed pages. Information Architecture Information architecture focuses on whether people can find the content they’re looking for on any eCommerce website. The overall architecture will include navigation, page type, page structure, wireframes, content, and more. Whatever work is done on the eCommerce site must not compromise the overall UX and provide adequate help to the customers in their journey on the site. Mobile Responsiveness Always start with mobile-first and then expand to desktop. When a website is responsive, it delivers the best user experience – since its layout adapts to the type of device being used to view the site. Google gives priority to mobile-friendly websites. Use Google’s mobile-friendliness test, Pingdom, or GTMetrix to see how your eCommerce website holds up on mobile devices. Popular eCommerce SEO Tools Here’s a list of the most popular tools that most SEO specialists would use to gain a higher advantage of competitors. SEMRush SEMRush is the fan-favorite in the SEO community. The tool scans the website rankings, sees changes and new ranking opportunities as well. It lets you understand the website’s search data and traffic and compare keywords and domains. The On-Page SEO Checker allows easy monitoring of website rankings. Besides this, it shows suggestions on how to improve the website’s performance. SEMRush is of great support since it lets you see your competitor’s top keywords and reveals pages on their site that generate the most organic traffic. Ahrefs Ahrefs is another widely used SEO tool. Using Ahrefs, you can easily optimize your website, analyze your competitors, and study what your customers are searching for. Besides this, learn from your industry’s top-performing content and track your ranking progress. From content marketers to global multinational brands, everyone turns to Ahrefs to grow their search traffic. The tool is capable of highlighting the website parts that require improvements to ensure the best ranking possible. Moz Another popular SEO tool is Moz. Moz is a great tool for site audits and crawls, rank tracking, backlink analysis and keyword research. It offers a suite of solutions for all your SEO needs. Moz is one of the most greatest and effective tools to gather great insights and then improve them. The Moz Toolbar allows merchants to extract great insights and metrics about each page of their eCommerce store. UberSuggest and Answer the Public Both of these are popular keyword tracking tools that help to identify relevant, accurate, and high volume keywords. Key-in the target keyword and the tools would show a great set of similar keywords. Answer the Public lists a plethora of questions in who, what, why and how format. This allows marketers to go straight into the minds of their consumers. Aside from this, it also offers comparisons and other related keywords. Even Ubersuggest allows a comprehensive keyword overview and shows the CPC and SEO difficulty of each keyword. Google Keyword Planner Google Keyword Planner allows users to research and analyze the list of keywords with their search volumes. Using this tool, marketers can find new keyword ideas relevant to their product, service, and target audience. Keyword Planner also shows historical statistics such as search volume data for all keywords. This insight helps you to decide how to use the keywords in your campaigns. Google Search Console Google Search Console is a free platform for anyone with an eCommerce site to monitor how Google scans their website and optimize its organic presence. Using this, you can understand how Google sees your pages. Further, from this, you are also alerted about issues on your site. Also, you can submit sitemaps and individual URLs for crawling. Google Analytics Use this tool to track and acquire reports about website traffic. Google Analytics is used to track website activity such as session duration, pages per session, bounce rate, etc. of the traffic that comes to the site. Beyond this, you can also gather information about the source of the traffic. It can be integrated with Google Ads, to create and review online campaigns by tracking landing page quality and conversions. WooRank WooRank is another tool that offers the user actionable insights. Such insghts help him to optimize the website and marketing efforts. WooRank has an instant SEO Checker and SEO Audit Tool. The tool also helps to generate customizable website reports. Aside from this, you can also perform a side-by-side analysis to unravel the competitor’s keywords & strategy. Further from this – find new keywords, track rankings, local positions, rivals, and changes to search results. SpyFu SpyFu, which was earlier a PPC based tool has been revamped and turned into an SEO centric tool. SpyFu lets you learn more about your competitor’s SEO tricks and avoid their mistakes – so you can avoid them in your SEO strategy. It allows you to track your SEO rankings on Google, Bing, and Yahoo. Beyond this, it lets you study competitors’ keywords, organizes your keywords into groups, and allows you to trace any website’s ranking for a keyword. DeepCrawl Deepcrawl is another useful tool that offers the best granular and comprehensive cloud-based web-crawling technologies and solutions. DeepCrawl allows for multi-domain monitoring, custom dashboards and easy management of global content. Outside of this, it offers on-page SEO recommendations, Google Analytics integration and backlink tracking on both desktop and mobile. Summary When a lot of the techniques mentioned above are effective and return desirable results – it’s often the collective work of all these methods working in tandem that generates the best results for the site. For example, a hreflang tag tells Google which language you are using on a specific page so that it can serve the results in that language. On some occasions, not having the same can diminish user experience and lower the ranking on search engines – as your target audience doesn’t land on the most appropriate version of the web page.  The security (HTTPS and SSL) on the page will affect the way users view your site. On transaction sites, the lack of adequate security measures can see a detrimental effect on the conversions. Even the domain age is believed to have a slight impact on the ranking of your web page on SERP. Beyond this, having enough quality backlinks links is equally vital to establish your authority on search pages. Headers (H1, H2) also play a crucial role in ranking, as they not only help format and structure the content but also affect the SEO. Any of this that falls out of place can elevate the bounce rates considerably. All of the above reasons show you the true worth of eCommerce SEO and why the same can’t be overlooked if you wish to initiate a digital marketing campaign. Whether you’re working independently or with an online marketing mentor , continuous work on search engine optimization is what will ultimately bring stupendous success in digital marketing.

title: Content Commerce: Bringing the Best of Two Worlds for Your Business
headings: How to Create Useful Content for Your Customers?
Content Commerce Strategy for Your Business
text: What is Content Commerce? You might have heard the term content commerce being thrown around for some time now. Despite the term being new, it’s not hard to guess what it is, is it? Even for someone who is new to the eCommerce circle can speculate it’s a combination of content and commerce. But, is it really a new concept? Hasn’t both content and commerce coexisted for ages already? So how is this concept in any way new? The fact is, although content commerce has been used for ages by many industries, it was never really defined. Now, to answer the question, content commerce can simply be defined as the right combination of content and commerce that helps you sell more. But, that would be the shorter definition. Content commerce involves making use of captivating content that can complement your products (that is, the commerce part). And unlike other marketing methods, bluffing can only get you so far; you need quality products that compliment your content. Is Content Important? If someone thinks content is not important or that it can’t have a significant enough impact on the business, then he or she’s ill-informed, to say the least. Consumers are always looking for reliable and worthy content to help them make the right buying decisions. Great content has always lured consumers into buying the right product for them. content can help you put your products in different perspectives and bring into light the products’ different sides to your customers that they may have otherwise missed. The content itself can be anything from a blog to vlog to an entire magazine (if you can afford it). content commerce can be split into two, depending on how you look at it. One is content-driven commerce, and the other is commerce-driven content. Don’t let the similarity in the names fool you; one is quite distinctive from the other. Content-driven Commerce Did you know that the Benetton Group owns the Colors magazine? Yes, the same Benetton as United Colors of Benetton (UCB) . And the much-loved lifestyle magazine The Red Bulletin is published by Red Bull Media House . This is not the first time corporate giants like UCB and Red Bull are making use of the print media or content to market their products. So what makes these corporate giants turn to print media while they can clearly afford any type of marketing strategy ? The answer is quite simple; the traditional approach to advertising does not yield the desired results anymore. We live in a time when our whole day is filled with advertisements, and there is no getting away from it. You see them in the movies, on your YouTube, on social media, on Spotify, and even in between games. The only kind of ads that people want to watch now is no ads. The user is virtually drowning in an ocean of advertisements. It doesn’t stop there either. Traditional advertising is tiresome work; it requires you to pay close attention to the details and often brings unrewarding results despite your best efforts. By the end of the day, you end up feeling you have done tedious work, which brought in zero results. This is where content commerce comes into the picture and turns the tables. Content-driven commerce involves employing captivating and useful content to build a brand narrative through which you can peak consumer interest and lead to conversions. Unlike traditional advertising strategies, content marketing actually connects with the audience and helps them in the process. Helpful content has a more positive effect on users than discounts.  However, if you think you can bluff your way into making your customers buy more, you’d be wrong. The content has to align with the needs of your customer, and your products must align with the content you create. A failure to do so will inevitably result in the failure of your marketing strategy as well. Commerce-driven Content If content-driven commerce is one side of the content commerce coin, the commerce-driven content is its flip-side. Both are an integral part of the same system but never the same. In content-driven commerce, we saw giant manufacturing brands moving to the publishing media. But, in commerce-driven content, it’s the other way around, which is to say publishers market products for other companies, for a price of course. Commerce-driven content makes use of everything from ebooks, music, videos, pictures, and so on. This could be in the form of advertisement, partnership, affiliate programs, or even influencer marketing. It shouldn’t come as a surprise to you when I say that this is not new either. Magazines and newspapers have been doing this for ages now. Magazines, especially well-established ones, have a profound effect on their readers and can easily influence their shopping habits. Just like you can’t bluff about how good your product you can’t give unreliable info to your readers either. When it comes to publishing media, the main challenge is to monetize their content without compromising its editorial integrity. So how do publishers market a product without compromising the editorial integrity?  The trick is to create and present your content in such a way that it genuinely helps your customers highlighting the various advantages of the product. Now, this does not mean that you get to exaggerate about the product. 76% of respondents said ads in general were either very exaggerated or somewhat exaggerated –  Lab42 The truth is that the readers actually expect the writer to tell them where they can buy the product that you wrote about. And that is how content commerce helps both you and the customer. As far as marketing goes, this is by far the most transparent method out there which engages with the audience. How to Create Useful Content for Your Customers? The most important thing you should keep in mind when dealing with a content-intense eCommerce store is that you always use the relevant content to connect well with your consumers. Try to figure out and address the pain-points of your customers using the content on your eCommerce store. No one wants to spend their time reading or listening to something that is not relevant to them. Let’s take the example of an online fashion store, what could be the best content that’s useful for the customers in this case? The content should focus on season-friendly clothing, provide insight into the latest fashion trends, and even add celebrity looks. You could publish content that draws inspiration from the pop-culture and market the products accordingly. If you can pitch it right then, there is practically no limit to what you can sell to your customers. Similarly, you can make use of even more engaging mediums like videos or vlogs t0 attract new customers. The more interesting and helpful your content, the more attention it’ll get, and get you more traffic and sales. However, it is equally essential not to under-deliver on your promises or oversell your product. If you make claims on your content that your product is incapable of delivering, it’ll inevitably backfire sooner or later. It is also desirable to find out what form of content your target audience prefers depending on the target audience: their age, needs, and the type of content they prefer to follow. Let it be videos or pictures or blogs, try publishing content in different formats, and find the right one that works for your business. Once you have figured out your customers’ preference and taste, content marketing becomes a lot easier, and you will be able to get the best results from it. Content Commerce Strategy for Your Business It is clear that the ideal content commerce strategy for an eCommerce store is content-driven commerce. Content puts up a facade on advertising and presents the audience with a less intrusive form of communication. At a time when every form of advertisement is loathed by the audience, content commerce could be your only viable solution. Although content-driven commerce is the ideal strategy for an eCommerce store, it doesn’t necessarily mean that you have to stick to just that. You can employ both strategies simultaneously to get the best results for your business. You can collaborate with publishing media to market your products through affiliate marketing.  Summary Content commerce offers an effective way to communicate with your target audience. It can help you market your products as well as boost the conversion rate. But, like any good thing, it does not come easy. Combining content and commerce is no cakewalk; it is easier said than done. It doesn’t matter if you are integrating content into commerce or the other way around as both require you to pay attention to the details. There are two things that are fundamental to create a successful content commerce strategy. The first thing is the product (obviously). It doesn’t matter how good your bluffing skills are; an inferior product can only get you so far. Content commerce does help you create a facade over the products, but it can not, however, change it. The product has to be high quality and worthy enough to be suggested to the readers or consumers. The second element, as you might have already guessed, is the authentic content. Readers are looking for content that can help them, and they are looking for products that fit their needs. The content should align with the needs of the reader or customer, and the product should align with the content as well, which brings us back to the first fundamental factor- the product. If done right, content commerce will benefit not just you but also your customers. Your customers get helpful content that can help them choose genuine products that fit their specific needs. And for an eCommerce business, you get to market your products to the right audience, without shoving another advertisement to their face. By the end of the day, content commerce enables both you and your customers to come out as winners.

title: The eCommerce Integrated Learning Management System (LMS) for an Innovative eLearning Experience
headings: What is Learning Management System (LMS) and What should it include?
Top Benefits of eLearning for Owners
Top Benefits of eLearning for Tutors
Top Benefits of eLearning for Students
Top Benefits of eLearning for Course Creators
How Can Virtina Help with the Learning Management System for a Better eLearning Experience?
Selection of Learning Management System (LMS) Isn’t a Simple Task
text: The age of online classes has been picking up momentum lately. The idea of attending lectures or training from the comfort of your home has persuaded many educational institutions and businesses to invest in Virtual Classrooms . The learners now value Quality Education + Convenience . This led to numerous coaching academies and businesses starting – eLearning. eLearning makes it possible to cater to individual needs and vastly improve the learning methodologies. The recent COVID-19 disruption and the possibility of other pandemics further cemented the importance of online learning. Physical classes are unable to navigate these difficult situations with ease. Such institutions find it hard to cope with these challenges. The on-going digital transformation and the upcoming 5G networking standard will further increase the urge for online classes. The constant lag and bandwidth issues during online streaming sessions will become a thing of the past. All the above reasons warranted an immediate upgrade to eLearning & this was made possible via the Learning Management System (LMS) . What is Learning Management System (LMS) and What should it include? Learning Management System (LMS) is an eCommerce application for the administration, documentation, tracking, reporting, and delivery of educational courses and training programs. Depending on the needs of the organization, an LMS will come to include a plethora of features and functionalities. Some of the indispensable possibilities required within an LMS are listed below. A clean & easy to use interface for both administrators and learners. Low implementation and life-cycle costs – easy course registration and management. Compatibility with mobile devices. Gamification elements to reward, rank and increase retention of learners. Powerful safety features to ensure the data stays secure and corruption-free. Data extraction to get insights that’ll improve, regulate and refine learning. High level of automation – with very little LMS administration support. Top Benefits of eLearning for Owners Let’s go through all the benefits that institutions and businesses gain by implementing an effective Learning Management System (LMS). Scalability Accommodating new users, course material, or any other kind of expansion will not become an issue with LMS. The ability to integrate more requirements with ease is what makes LMS such a preferred learning tool. A proper LMS will support your organization as it grows. It is not restricted to the preliminary model and can upgrade to include any new development. Now, take your company to unimaginable heights with an evolving LMS. Recurring Revenue The Subscription model of online courses ensures a steady stream of revenue. The course content stays online. New users will buy the course content, across a lifetime for as long as it is relevant and informative. Some go as far as creating the content once and selling it forever – without adding any extra value. LMS is a system where the uploaded study materials can be purchased on and on. Under the renewal model, users stick around – hence the flow of funds never stops. Reduce Costs Offline classes collect hefty expenses . The expenses come to include rents, utility bills, labor, and other miscellaneous costs. But, when you take these classes online, you’d mitigate these charges to a great extent. All the study material is now digitized, saving you enormous money. The need to print out thousands of copies of notes, booklets, training guides, and other paperwork becomes redundant. Top Benefits of eLearning for Tutors Ease of Teaching Tutors can now take these classes from a place that is suitable and convenient for them. There is no need to pull themselves to a coaching center every day. The online interface helps even to record endless hours of classes in a stretch and upload all of it in one shot. The plethora of features and functionalities further simplifies the teaching standards. Also, they can schedule a live session at a time that is convenient for them. Analytics The inbuilt analytic tools also helps the trainers to pinpoint areas within the course that need more polishing. The tools help with monitoring the performance of students. The same tools help to identify struggling learners. Aside from detecting modules that need a little bit of fine-tuning. With sophisticated reporting, it becomes possible to craft unique strategies for a learner. On top of that, measure the impact of your learning programs. Doing so, your company gains a ton of intricate details to polish and restructure the courses.Gathering data helps to make informed decisions. The use of analytics helps to create personalized assessments and learning materials. LMS also allows companies to track progress. The progress helps to identify areas that need further improvement in real-time. Advanced Tools The wide array of features and functionalities create an engaging and interactive learning experience for users. Such features also make it possible to improve the delivery of subject matter to learners. They, too, find it easy to comprehend complicated info. Peer collaboration is also possible – via chats and discussion forums. The use of charts, graphs, 3D modeling, and other engaging tools ensures there is no drop in the Quality of learning. Use captivating animations to put your point across. Thereby conveying the subject matter better and enhancing the impact of your training. The High production value of LMS courses increases retention and engagement. Automation A lot of manual chores like grading, assessments, roll-call, and other miscellaneous time-consuming tasks can be left to LMS. As a result, teachers focus on the needs of learners and on improving the curriculum standards. The automation makes it possible to give feedback immediately. This is due to the inbuilt mechanism which reviews coursework in a matter of seconds. With eLearning, it’s quick and easy to pull all the measurable data. Gather information like course completion, engagement numbers, time log, and more directly from the LMS. Top Benefits of eLearning for Students Besides the apparent reduction in time as learners no longer need to shuffle between coaching centers and their home – there’s a wide list of other benefits of eLearning. Continuity In a scenario, where your offline classrooms are affected by any disruption – the faculty and students remain confined and vulnerable. But such an event can be circumvented if eLearning is in place. Natural calamities can strike and make it difficult to reach such places. Virtual classrooms happen from anywhere in the world. Learners have the convenience to adjust the classes according to their schedule. Learners get to drive the course at their own pace. Due to which learners no longer need to expose themselves to outside threats. Convenience When the classes shift online, the learners no longer need to drag themselves to their academies every day at a fixed time. In fact, with eLearning, students get to figure out a learning schedule that is convenient for them. In the earlier scenario, learners would need to attend the classes at a particular time slot. But, eLearning can be adjusted around their schedule. Pre-recorded online sessions allow students the opportunity even to attend skipped or missed classes. Finance Running back and forth between the institution and the home is exhausting and expensive. Learners would have to bear the transportation costs . The costs would come in the form of fuel costs, ticket charges, or any other commuting expense. Thereby costing the individual hefty charges on top of what they’d be paying for their classes anyways. But, with eLearning, they no longer need to worry about this issue. Fewer Distractions In your personal space, you are less likely to encounter unknown elements and other irrelevant people. A familiar environment means learners stay more calm and relaxed while learning. A soothing learning experience is conducive to knowledge retention and a better understanding of concepts. It allows the learners to submerge themselves in the curriculum without worrying about surrounding interference. Top Benefits of eLearning for Course Creators There are many resources available for those who are new to eLearning course creation. These handy benefits provide creators a unique way to create a beneficial course. Such courses, then help learners succeed, and stay accountable for their training.  Microlearning The new way to deliver a packed, informative, and productive learning experience. What we have come to know as short and sweet can be accomplished. LMS allows course creators to squeeze all the vital content into one neat and crisp package. When course creators make the course and its modules – right to the point, they’re able to keep the attention of their candidates for longer. Also, learners are more likely to opt for such a course knowing that they’d have a qualification and necessary knowledge sooner. Course Builder Course creators can easily create and sell courses. The ability to drag and drop within a course builder allows them to develop multi-layered courses easily. Not just that, but course creators get to reuse their content – making it easy to spin-up new courses. Aside from this, deliver quizzes, award certificates, manage learners, download reports, and much more. All you need to do- set the price, choose the pricing model, and publish it on top of the ability to interact with learners. Multi-language The ability to build courses in any language lets course creators penetrate new regions and access other demographics. When your course creation interface gives support for many languages – it becomes easy to change the language used in any part of your site. Such an LMS will optimize the user experience by localizing the process and put an end to geographical boundaries. Learners can easily switch between languages – at the click of a button. As a result, you shorten implementation times and increase user adoption. Gamification Multimedia and other interactive elements make it possible to simplify course content. Such features assist in delivering a better teaching experience. With the help of this, content creators can set a better and stronger narrative around their syllabus. The use of rich animation will also improve engagement and increase retention times. Content Management Content management is another useful and necessary component. CMS supports the latest international standards (SCORM and Tin Can/xAPI) for eLearning. Beyond this, the management system allows upload of documents, videos exams & links to web content hosted elsewhere. How Can Virtina Help with the Learning Management System for a Better eLearning Experience? Here’s everything that the eCommerce experts at Virtina can do to assist you in implementing an Learning Management System (LMS). Omnichannel LMS makes it possible to give a consistent experience across all touchpoints. It is easy to deploy the training on multiple sites. Ensure uniformity in learning and the delivery of messages across several locations. Learners can access info from anywhere.
