title: Why Retailers Can No Longer Afford to Ignore eCommerce?
headings: Challenges Faced by Retail Store Owners
Lack of Analytics or Insight to Assess Business Performance
Difficulty in Hiring and Retaining Employees
How Can Retailers Stay on Top of Their Game?
Point of Sale: The Importance, Challenges, and Capabilities
text: Customers nowadays demand effortless and convenient shopping experiences. They no longer bother to go from shop to shop looking for a pair of pants (or anything for that matter). In fact, the consumers are actually willing to pay more for the convenience the eCommerce platform offers them. After the pandemic hit, eCommerce is perhaps the only sector that actually managed to strive while others struggle to survive. Retailers are in destitute because of the COVID-19 situation. They have nowhere to turn to as the shops are forced to close down. However, the retailers who had an online presence were saved by their eCommerce store. Even before the pandemic, buyers spend most of their time in the digital world. They continuously switch from one device to another – explore, search, and choose an item on desktop and then buy it from a brick and mortar outlet. By creating digital storefronts, retailers can support their venture both online and offline. When this is done in a unified fashion it becomes the omnichannel way. They’d be able to give consumers a personalized, low-cost, and reliable solution on all touchpoints. It’s high time that you step away from single-channel Commerce. eCommerce unlocks a new revenue stream for your business . It lets you sell and ship to the other side of the world if you want to. You can further make your business more accessible by launching mobile apps for your store. The best thing, however, is that you can centralize your business and control all of them from a single place. Challenges Faced by Retail Store Owners Now, more than ever, the retail store owners find it hard to compete and survive. The pandemic has proved beyond all doubt that the future is the hands of eCommerce. The legacy solutions in place have restricted their growth and capped the conversions to a great extent. They are finding it hard to build a competitive advantage, deliver a level of service that enhances brand reputation. They are unable to offer compelling-unique experiences that improve customer satisfaction. Retail store owners today run the risk of being ejected from the race. They are going up against a much more advanced form of business which is eCommerce and its omnichannel alternatives . Further from the above – retailers face the following critical challenges in their industry. Unforeseen Pandemic The COVID-19 pandemic affected all us: neither man nor business was spared from it. We saw an unprecedented reduction in footfall, labor shortages, and fulfillment issues. The traditional business was destabilized, and those who didn’t have a backup like an eCommerce store suffered the worst. Operating on a Single Channel There is only so much growth potential for a single-channel retailer, and most store owners fail even to reach that. Following a single-channel system implies that there is little to no room for growth. eCommerce, on the other hand, has practically unlimited growth potential. No Real-time Inventory Visibility A business with multiple retail stores cannot access the available stock. Rely on CSV’s and spreadsheets to coordinate, tally, and track all the available units. Some depend on guesswork and estimation – leading to a high margin of error. Response Time The response time to the customers is miserable when it comes to physical stores (especially post-purchase). Stores find it hard to interact with their buyers and answer queries during peak time. Post-purchase service is even worse when it comes to conventional stores. Customer grievances and feedback are rarely addressed in a conventional store. Additionally, the inability of the workforce and tools to operate 24/7 left only a small and ineffective window for communication. Lack of Analytics or Insight to Assess Business Performance When it comes to conventional stores, it is almost impossible to get valuable insights. This includes conversions, consumer habits, industry trends, friction areas, abandonment reasons, what appeals to the masses, and so on. Factoring in these can affect the customer journey and they can never be accurately found for a conventional store. Difficulty in Hiring and Retaining Employees Your employees are always looking to learn the best and latest practices in the industry to keep themselves updated and relevant. A conventional brick and mortar store may fail to live up to the expectation of your employees. How Can Retailers Stay on Top of Their Game? The above list of challenges may seem daunting at first – but believe it or not, it is quite simple to mitigate the same to gain absolute dominance in your industry. So, what is this magic solution to all your problems, you ask? The answer is eCommerce; however, getting your business online simply wouldn’t do. You need to build a functionally superior, easy to use eCommerce store that can connect to your customers. And for doing that, you need a well experienced and tech-savvy eCommerce partner like Virtina. Now, let’s take a look at what an eCommerce store can contribute to your business. A full-fledged no-nonsense eCommerce store is the answer to not losing sales during an unpredictable crisis. Having a robust eCommerce store fulfills many things. But, most importantly, it keeps your business up and running during any unprecedented events like a pandemic.With an eCommerce store, while most businesses can’t even open for business, yours will be able to fulfill orders. You can make use of features like no-contact home delivery, curbside pickup, lockers, pick-up from the nearest store, and so on. The point is – eCommerce stays immune and grants conventional retail stores the power to sell as the buyers can still access your digital storefront. Adopt an omnichannel model for your business. This lets retailers diversify and have a presence on multiple platforms. The omnichannel approach removes the boundaries between different sales and marketing channels. As a result, eCommerce unifies and integrates the whole operation.It also means that your store is open for business in your physical store, on the internet, and even on social media. A multi-spoke approach that can capture engagement and conversions from any channel. You can even improve your brand’s visibility and awareness by displaying your inventory on multiple channels. Automating could be the ultimate upgrade you can get from shifting your business to the eCommerce platform. You can easily control, audit, and manage your business with the help of automation.Also, automating frees you from many manual chores. Your staff can focus on collecting leads and building new marketing strategies. Tedious and time-consuming chores that are prone to errors will be left to the software. Use a good ERP, CRM, and inventory management solution to improve the business practices. The use of AI and AI-assisted programs are being employed in businesses of all types. To make the most out of AI, you need a digital presence for your presence. AI can be seen even in chatbots, comment sections for feedback, forums, social media, and other tools help to enhance customer relationships. With an AI, it is easier to keep in touch with your consumers, and they feel more appreciated for the quick response. On top of that, the business has created a  fluid-seamless communication line  to interact with its target audience. The lack of analytics or insights means the owners do not really know in which direction their business is heading. Whereas having  detailed insights  about the various elements of your business helps to steer the company in the right direction. Access to key info, like orders, demographics, and so on helps to create personalized offers and improve cross or up-selling as well. Use tools like Google Analytics, Tableau, HotJar, and more to generate more data about your company. You may even incorporate this assessment into your marketing strategy for more impactful results. In the IoT (Internet of Things) age, relying on medieval practices will hurt your chances to hire candidates. The first thing anyone does before considering to work for a company is to check the companies credibility online, they check for their website, their reviews, and even LinkedIn. Even a lack of social media presence can cause displeasure & create delays in hiring. More Capabilities for Retailers If you are still not convinced about taking your business online, consider this: eCommerce lets you improve operations, reduce costs, scale better, make it easier to acquire customers and expand to other territories. Let’s take a look at the factors that enable eCommerce to achieve this. Point of Sale At some point, every retailer must need robust POS software to help take their business online. Most such omnipresent brands need software that will import stock from your physical store to your digital shop.Beyond this, it updates the order status to a customer. POS helps with analytics to give businesses a handy overview of their data points so they can make more well-informed decisions. The analytics also helps to forecast inventory levels so you don’t end up overstocking or understocking.It also centralizes purchasing and enables you to view buyer habits with detailed customer profiles. You can track stock levels, manage reward programs, and finally simplify the multi-location ordering process. You can even use LightSpeed, QuickBooks, CounterPoint, Shopkeep ,and more to manage sales accounts. Payment Solutions Retailers are often restricted by the number of payment solutions they have access to. In the age of digital wallets & lightning-fast transactions, the idea of cash & Check payments are slowly disappearing.eCommerce offers merchants the ability to accept payments in multiple ways. This enables a faster & more secure way to pay online. It also enables you to offer instant discounts & cashback that tempt more B2C buyers to opt for online shopping over offline.PayPal, Stripe, Square, Amazon, and more facilitate transactions and deliver a smart, safe and simplified gateway to conduct the same. You can also introduce recurring billing via memberships which helps to improve the residual revenue of the company. Support Post-sales support is weak when it comes to conventional stores, which is the principal reason why retailers are unable to foster customer relationships and improve loyalty. During and after the sale, retailers fail to give adequate support for the sold goods.Retailers need to collaborate with customers more proactively through the entire customer journey. However, even with the best performance, conventional stores fail to give the desired level of service to the customers. For such reasons, you’d need chat bots, direct messaging, feedback forms, forums, testimonials, ratings, and more. An eCommerce store and social media presence enables just that. Content Commerce As an ordinary retailer, offline marketing, and some in-store product launches is all you’d rely on to improve the visibility of your store. But, eCommerce offers you a plethora of options that can help you get noticed by your targeted audience. Apart from the age-old practice of digital marketing, you can also employ the latest and best practices in the industry.The power of Content commerce is often underestimated – content fueled with accurate SEO will elevate your presence more holistically. It’ll also make sure that your website has a higher ranking, which means that you’ll be among the first to be listed by search engines like google.Higher ranking; means more awareness around your brand; thus, more people would discover you faster with less effort. You may even throw in visual contents (images and videos) to enrich the way you showcase your products. Add VR/AR to the mix, and you’d offer a more elaborate and bedazzling way to view your SKU’s. Catalogs, posters, brochures, flyers are a thing of the past. eCommerce lists every product, certification, manual you hold in an easy to access & readable format virtually. Point of Sale: The Importance, Challenges, and Capabilities POS or Point of Sales refers to the time at which a transaction is made from the customer to the store owner or merchant. The POS system has been around since the beginning of business transactions, and it was nothing more than written receipts. But, times have changed, and so has the way we conduct business. Now, we have electronic POS solutions, and almost all retailers prefer this over the conventional ink and paper system. POS solutions not only make the work easier and accurate for the businesses but also allows the retailer to collect precious sales data. The most basic POS system that is used by a physical retail store could consist of a cash register and software that collects the sales data. Its capability can be boosted by adding additional hardware, such as barcode scanners, card readers, etc. to the system.Retailers make a plethora of mistakes and face some severe challenges in selecting the right POS Solution for their business. Let’s run through all the POS challenges for retailers. Lack of Understanding Not knowing which POS is the best fit for their business size proves costly in the long run. Such businesses often opt for a POS that is in demand or comes recommended by a specialist. Having a vague understanding of the POS, they pick the one that doesn’t align with their business requirements. Prioritizing Price Putting budget over necessity is also risky when sorting the right POS for your company. Businesses trade value for cost-effective POS solutions. This results in them buying the cheapest POS around – economical it may be, but it is certainly not going to fulfill the POS tasks. Mobile Compatibility Companies can’t afford to lose the on-the-road aspect of monitoring your business. Mobile compatibility makes it easier for you to access your business. If your POS supports mobile monitoring of every aspect of your business, then you’re all set to work on the go. Security A breach can severely compromise your business. The only way to avoid this is to pick a POS solution that offers the highest-grade security of your confidential data. The customer information and other sensitive payment details cannot be compromised. Reporting Advanced reporting helps to gather intuitive and informative insights about your business performance. It tells the owners about how well the business is faring. Use this data to make informed decisions about your company. Once you understand customer habits and create personalized offers it is easier to target them. Quality POS systems integrated with your eCommerce store and retail locations need to be error-free 24/7. Anything that triggers an issue can create lapses in order values and inventory between 2 touchpoints. The overall POS quality should sync everything as cleanly as possible. However, the POS system can reach its full potential only when it is used for an eCommerce store. The POS system makes your business almost perfect when used in combination with eCommerce. The reason for it is that a lot more functionalities or capabilities can be added to it. Some of them are listed below. Track and Analyze The ability to track the inventory levels along with the sales. They also help you figure out the gross revenues, profit margins, sales pattern , and the list of data that just keeps going. Evaluate the Store The accumulated data from the POS can be used to analyze your eCommerce store and increase its profitability. It can also help you figure out the shortcomings in your sales and inventory process. Sync and Track It has everything you need to sync and track your inventory . It enables you to be on top of your game regardless of whether you are running your business online, in-person, or both. Flexibility It is perhaps the biggest advantage of POS. They can accept all major credit and debit payments. This lets your customer choose which mode of payment that suits him or her, ensuring a smooth shopping experience. Security It is a primary concern to many consumers and maintaining the privacy of your consumers is a primary concern for a business. POS lets you have this peace of mind by ensuring the safety of sensitive info of you and your customers. Loyalty Program It is the number one way to earn brownie points from your customers. The POS system gives you valuable insight into how much your customers spend and lets you offer a reward that’s best suited for the customer. Summary The fact is that the retail market can no longer afford to depend solely on the conventional brick and mortar store. The threat from the unprecedented COVID-19 situation made this very clear to the retail store owners. all your competition has already entered the digital landscape.The cost of refusing to turn to online trading can more than just hurt the retail business. The key to the success & growth of your business lies in embracing eCommerce.Of course, when running an omnichannel model, the physical interactions will run parallel – only that now it will be complemented with an online presence. Selling online will mitigate a small business owner’s exposure to risky changes in the market.Setting a storefront on the internet may have seemed overwhelming in the past, but today, it only takes a matter of days to get online. Talk to one of the eCommerce experts in Virtina, and we’ll guide you all the way.

title: Why Manufacturers and B2B Brands Must Shift to eCommerce?
headings: The Urgency of Manufacturers and B2B Brands to Go Online
The M2 Factor: Millennials and Mobile Phones
Role of eCommerce in the SMART Manufacturing Era
How Has eCommerce Become Synonymous to Existence Today?
Why Should Manufacturers and B2B Brands Expand to B2B and D2C?
What Makes Manufacturers and B2B eCommerce Unique?
Importance of Content on a Manufacturer and B2B eCommerce Store
text: From the time of its inception, the manufacturers and B2B brands have stuck to their traditional approach to business. They deal with bulk quantity products, and the transactions are almost always made with regular customers. If you think about it, not much has changed in the functioning of a Manufacturers or B2B brands. Even though the technology around it has grown by leaps and bounds, it remained unmoved. But, the time has finally come for the manufacturers and B2B brands to step up their game and shift to a more efficient platform – eCommerce. The eCommerce market value of B2B business is a mind-boggling $14.9 Trillion! That is more than six times that of the B2C market. Not to take your B2B business online now would be foolhardy, and the numbers can vouch for it. More than half the manufacturers don’t have an eCommerce store. The earlier you get into the eCommerce platform, the better it is for your business. This will not only ensure that you have less competition but boosts the number of potential customers as well. The Urgency of Manufacturers and B2B Brands to Go Online The traditional way of doing business is slowly but surely becoming obsolete. The eCommerce platform has long since started substituting the conventional way of B2B commerce. We are now entering a new SMART manufacturing era, and the transition has already begun . The B2B business can no longer thrive on the conventional platform. The manufacturers & B2B brands were forced to face this harsh reality when the Pandemic hit. There is not a single business that did not feel its effect on their business.  The Pandemic and eCommerce The COVID-19 / coronavirus pandemic made it clear that traditional businesses are not prepared for an unprecedented crisis, at least not by themselves. It showed us the importance of omnichannel selling, and how eCommerce can help you stay ahead of your competition. While once consumers used to look to eCommerce for convenience it is much more than that now. eCommerce gave them safety for the consumers as well as the store owners, which is the biggest challenge that the store owners are struggling with during the pandemic. If you are still choosing not to take your B2B business online now, you are intentionally putting your business at risk. And even if by some chance your business makes it out of this pandemic safely, how sure can you be that your business will survive another unprecedented crisis like this? The M2 Factor: Millennials and Mobile Phones Today, most of the workforce in a company are millennials. One of the reasons why the traditional way of selling has worked out as far as it has is because of the older generation of workers. They fit into the system very well which was in perfect harmony with each other in the past. But, that is not the case anymore, millennials do not go around calling different suppliers for the right product. Instead, they do their research online and find the product best suited for their purpose. 70% of B2B searches happen on mobile devices. Millennials work on the go, when a requirement comes up, the millennials lookup for the relevant products on his/her phone. If your B2B business does not have an eCommerce presence, it could mean that the buyer may not even consider your company as a potential supplier. Disintermediation B2B business has a much more complicated and structured buying process than that of a simple B2C one. There are Procurement Officers employed by your customers whose job it is to find the best product for their requirements. The decision is made only after considering the price, value for money, quality, and other such factors. Your customers are always on the lookout for ways to cut their costs, and it is more relevant than ever now. The buyers realize that disintermediation is the key to cutting costs without compromising on the quality. With the intermediaries removed from the equation, you can sell at a price favorable for yourself and your customers. Lack of Digital Transformation The biggest challenge for a manufacturer or B2B brand is the error by humans, and they can often lead to a marginal loss. Automation is the only viable solution to this problem. Any part of the production that does not require a human’s touch, Manufacturers are trying to bring a minimal error scenario by automation. This further urges manufacturers & B2B brands to adopt digital transformation and smart manufacturing. Amazonization With its immense success, Amazon is a brand that has proved time, and again that eCommerce is the present and the future. Amazon is not just an eCommerce giant anymore. With their in-house products & world-class logistics, they’ve revolutionized eCommerce. Amazon is now spreading its wings to the B2B wholesale sector as well. It is evident that if B2B companies need to stay relevant, they need to go digital now! Logistics and Accounting The manufacturers and B2B brands handle the logistics and account for bulk quantities of products. We are talking about a massive amount of products here. It is a monstrous task, but eCommerce companies often enjoy the convenience of automating these processes, whereas manufacturers and B2B brands have to struggle to get their affairs in order. Role of eCommerce in the SMART Manufacturing Era eCommerce is arguably the only systematic way that is powerful and flexible enough to embrace the new changes in the SMART manufacturing era. The traditional way of selling simply cannot match up with the SMART manufacturing era that’s always evolving. Its characteristic features like agility, connectedness, lead generation, design thinking, experiential buyer journey, and millennials (talent/buyers) let it adapt to the latest changes in the manufacturing industry. These characteristics act as the pillars that enable eCommerce to support the ever-changing manufacturer requirements. If the characteristics are the pillars that support the eCommerce manufacturing era the eCommerce features are the base on which these pillars stand. Some of the major features offered by eCommerce in the SMART manufacturing era are the following. 1. User-Experience The user experience can be the deciding factor of any sales, let it be physical or eCommerce. However, in an eCommerce store, the user experience can be enhanced, modified, and changed entirely to suit the needs of the user. This gives eCommerce an unprecedented level of flexibility over conventional stores. 2. Consumerization Consumerization focuses on reorganizing the products and service designs to be consumer-centric. The conventional way of doing this is to follow an organization-oriented offering (B2B). Whereas, consumerization opens up possibilities like D2C (Direct to Consumer). 3. MRP/ERP Systems MRP or Materials Requirements Planning is an organizational system used by most manufacturers now. It enables you to plan, schedule, and control the materials used in the manufacture. ERP or Enterprise Resource Planning is a system derived from MRP and enables B2B brands (Non-manufacturers) to make use of the capabilities of MRP. 4. Complete 24/7 Availability An eCommerce store is open for business 24/7 and throughout the year. Your customers can shop online at any given time of the day. There is no worry about the shop being closed and the store owner doesn’t have to worry about losing any business. 5. Self-service No one enjoys being dependent on anyone or anything. And this is true when it comes to making a purchase. Which explains why Self-service is so popular today. eCommerce lets you be your own boss while making a purchase, it gives you the freedom to choose and even compare multiple products together. 6. Digital Marketing Marketing using massive billboards is a thing of the past, now, all marketing is carried out on the digital platform. Digital marketing lets your customers view products, compare them and buy it with just a few clicks.  7. Content Marketing Content Marketing makes use of relevant, helpful, and quality content that helps customers understand more about the product and how to use it. eCommerce lets you employ the latest practices like content marketing to raise awareness and also helps the procurement officers to make a well-informed decision. 8. Global Outreach An eCommerce presence means that you are not bound by the geographical limitations as that of a physical store. Your store is available and accessible from anywhere on the globe. This global outreach can be further enhanced using digital/content marketing.  9. Direct To Consumer (D2C or DTC) Direct to Consumer, as the names suggest selling your products directly to your consumers. This would mean excluding the middlemen like the retailers, wholesalers, and any third parties. As a company who has worked with numerous D2C companies, Virtina can guide you to build an eCommerce store with D2C capabilities. 10. Automated Logistics and Accounting eCommerce companies often enjoy the convenience of automating the logistics & accounting processes. The inventory data can also be integrated into your eCommerce store which is automatically updated. Furthermore, eCommerce even enables you to file your tax returns without having to go through the tedious task of documentation and cross-checking. 11. Omni-channel (O2O) Omni-channel selling refers to being able to sell your products through different channels (Online & Offline) to different customer pools (B2B, B2C, & D2C). The new O2O strategy involves finding the consumers online and bridging them to the physical stores to collect their purchases. 12. Blockchain-based Loyalty Programs Loyalty programs are the way you can ensure that your company has a reliable customer pool that you can count on. The blockchain loyalty programs are the best in the industry right now, which enables the customers to accumulate their reward points and the best part is that it never expires. How Has eCommerce Become Synonymous to Existence Today?  One thing that the pandemic made clear for manufacturers and B2B brands is that they can no longer ignore their eCommerce possibilities. Unless you don’t want your B2B business to survive even through the tough times like the pandemic, it is inevitable that you take your B2B business online. The best example that proves this is the food and beverage wholesale industry. The F&B wholesale business took the worst hit during the pandemic. The COVID-19 closed down all public places, no restaurants, bars, or pubs. And this left the wholesale F&B business in a ditch. With no backup plan or whatsoever, they were thrown into a battle for survival, and the fact that their products are perishable goods only made it worse. It is at this point that they realized the only pragmatic way to save their business is through eCommerce. eCommerce is perhaps the only way to run your business even under extreme conditions like a lockdown or any unprecedented events for that matter. eCommerce is no longer about the convenience of the consumers but a necessity. It is about the very existence of the customer as well as the seller. The pandemic has bought out this necessity to exist, and the manufacturers and B2B brands can no longer turn their heads on this fact. More than half the manufacturers either do not have an online presence or have a weak eCommerce site! In other words, more than half the manufacturers and B2B brands had nothing to save them from the pandemic. Why Should Manufacturers and B2B Brands Expand to B2B and D2C? The most obvious answer to this question would be omnichannel selling. It lets you sell to multiple customer pools (B2B, B2B, and D2C) through different channels (online and offline). This makes room for more revenue to be accumulated from your business. But, it doesn’t stop there; the omnichannel capability of your business gives your business flexibility that is unparalleled. It is the lack of this flexibility that caused many companies to go down without being able to put up a fight during the COVID-19 pandemic. When most of the shops closed down due to the pandemic crisis, it was almost as if the B2B/wholesale market vanished overnight. One of the best examples of this can be seen in the food and beverages wholesale market when the government was forced to shut down restaurants, hotels, and pubs. The uncertainty and panic which rose from it are of unprecedented proportion. Of course, there was no way of predicting that such a crisis would hit us. Now that we have had to learn it the hard way, it is only natural that you expand your business to the B2B & D2C spectrums. The total absence of face to face interaction during the pandemic is likely the reason behind the success of eCommerce. Innovative solutions like “No Contact Delivery” not only reassured the customers but encouraged them to embrace the eCommerce way. Apart from this, disintermediation is another seductive aspect of the eCommerce business. It allows you to lower the price of products by taking out the intermediaries and thereby offering a better deal to your customers. Direct to Customer or D2C/DTC is the ultimate strategy for virtually complete disintermediation. In a D2C/DTC business, you are selling directly to your end customer. This means that you can get a better understanding of your client’s needs and gives you absolute control over the brand. The best thing, however, is that you are faster on the market as products can be quickly developed and tested on a D2C business model. As far as the consumer is concerned, shopping becomes a whole lot easier for him/her. Especially at times like this, when social distancing is uncompromisable for the safety of you and your family. You can leverage the best practices like “Click and Collect” for your D2C business. “Click and Collect” further reduces the need for unnecessary physical interaction. It lets you buy products online and collect them from a local facility. The “Click and Collect” feature makes your customer’s shopping much more convenient. You no longer have to stand in a long line of people or walk around the supermarket looking through the never-ending aisle of products that you may or may not need. This significantly reduces the number of people you come in contact with, and in turn, helps your customers stay safe through the Pandemic. When it comes to eCommerce, you have the freedom and flexibility to choose between B2B, B2C, D2C, or even run them altogether if need be. All you need is a reliable eCommerce partner. The B2B, B2C, and D2C businesses have their unique features, and your eCommerce partner needs to be aware of them. The better understanding your eCommerce partner has over the different spectrums, the more accurate your eCommerce store will be for your business. For example, if you are running a store with both B2B and B2C clientele, then you’d want to display individual pricing for customers belonging to the respective groups. An eCommerce company like Virtina, who has broad experience working on eCommerce regardless of the type of business. Let it be B2B, B2C or D2C. Our experts can make sure that you have everything you’d need on your eCommerce store and more. What Makes Manufacturers and B2B eCommerce Unique? The manufacturer and B2B eCommerce is unique from the rest. The first and most evident contrast with conventional eCommerce being the sheer quantity of products. Manufacturers and B2B brands deal with a bulk amount of products, which means it requires immense logistic capabilities as well as a strong workforce. But, the differences don’t stop there. The entire buying process is drastically different from a typical B2C one. Procurement officers make the B2B buying decisions. They follow a specific set of processes before eventually reaching a buying decision. The procurement officers are switching suppliers , and they no longer turn to your old Yellow Pages. The B2B buying cycle involves a detailed analysis of the requirement where every aspect is considered to make a well-informed decision. With the right content and quality products and fair pricing, manufacturers and B2B brands can easily come on top of the list. 83% willing to pay higher prices if the supplier has excellent eCommerce and customer portal capabilities. The long consideration journey is perhaps the most significant of the B2B business for both the buyer as well as the seller. The consideration phase is done way before any direct contact is made, and it is your chance to make a good impression on the buyers with quality content and accurate product descriptions. Now, these men (procurement officers) have insulated themselves from most marketing gimmicks, and hence providing quality products with precise description is probably the best way to go about it. B2B Buyer Persona The key to being successful at any business is to give your customers what they are craving for, the same holds true for the B2B business as well. The B2B buyer persona is the hypothetical persona of your B2B buyer. By building a B2B buyer persona, you get valuable insight into what the buyer wants and doesn’t want from his products. You get a better understanding of his/her pinpoint and what can be done to remedy it. By building a B2B buyer persona, you are trying to understand what makes them tick? You dive into their personality, their values, their lifestyles, and needs. Once the B2B buyer persona is defined, it can guide you to optimize the customer’s buying experience. This also lets you match the right kind of messages and offers to your customers. As an eCommerce company with years of experience working for the B2B industry, Virtina can help you draw an accurate B2B Buyer persona for your business. Our experts can optimize your website to suit the needs of the B2B buyer persona and effectively boost your sales in the process.  Importance of Content on a Manufacturer and B2B eCommerce Store As I’ve mentioned earlier, the B2B buying cycle and B2B buying process are drastically different from the B2C. And one thing is clear before a product is bought by the Procurement Officers they conduct thorough research on the product before purchase. And what better and convenient way to research than on the internet? 94% of customers in the B2B market research online before they ever buy a product. Procurement officers go through your content with utmost precision and attention even before they even get into direct contact with you. So in a way, the content on your eCommerce store could make or break your deal. The more in-depth and specific your content is, the easier it is to convert your potential customers to buyers. But, how exactly do you make use of the content on your website? There are three stages of content utilization shown below. With conventional marketing little to no results, many businesses are also turning to Content Commerce. Content Commerce can simply be defined as the right combination of content and commerce that helps you sell more. But, that would be the shorter definition. Content Commerce involves making use of captivating content that can complement your products (i.e., the commerce part). It allows businesses both new opportunities and existing ones to establish relationships with these distributors, increasing sales while decreasing costs associated with increased efficiency! Why should manufacturers and B2B Brands Shift to omnichannel eCommerce? With the help of Omnichannel eCommerce, B2B companies can adopt communications that will put their customer in a position to be satisfied. They would engage customers at different points during this process by using voice or social media, for example – depending on what is most convenient and best suited towards engaging with them as they see fit. It’s essential not only to carry context forward throughout someone’s journey but also to keep up an ongoing conversation, so those who want more information don’t go thirsty! How is eCommerce in Manufacturing a Game Changer? Manufacturing has always been about pursuing new technology, but it’s time to start thinking outside of our traditional boundaries. As product-focused organizations move into customer-centricity and embrace eCommerce to improve their business efficiency, manufacturers are looking for digital solutions like these that can facilitate change within themselves and society at large–a shift that will be necessary if we want manufacturing jobs in this country again! title: How to Migrate Your Subscriptions to WooCommerce?
headings: What Does the WooCommerce Migration Involve?
WooCommerce Subscriptions Migration – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
text: Often, an eCommerce platform finds it hard to support your subscription program. It becomes a struggle to manage your subscriptions. But, you don’t need to stick around and optimize a difficult platform. All you need to do is transfer all the running and active subscriptions to WooCommerce . Once done, your subscription program will become easier to manage and regulate. Let’s read on to find out more. WooCommerce Subscriptions – Highlights When Do You Need Migration? Why WooCommerce Subscription? WooCommerce Subscription Migration Challenges WooCommerce Subscription Migration – Workflow Migrating WooCommerce Subscriptions – Infographic What Virtina Does? What Does the WooCommerce Migration Involve? Final Thoughts – WooCommerce Subscriptions WooCommerce Subscriptions – Highlights WooCommerce too, allows its store owners to conduct subscription-based selling. Store owners can get consistent revenue for their online business. To start the same, it uses the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin. With the help of WooCommerce Subscriptions, you can manage products for repeat payments. Such payments will give long lasting revenue. Furthermore, owners can track, manage and analyze their subscription program. Use the WooCommerce Subscription plugin to manage your subscriptions best. The plugin supports a variety of subscriptions. The best part, it offers support for both physical or virtual products and services. Store owners can create these subscriptions for a weekly, monthly, or annual basis. Beyond this, it offers the ability to add sign-up fees, offer free trials, and set end dates. Depend only on WooCommerce Subscriptions. It is the best way to track, manage, adjust and scale your subscription program. Currently, the plugin costs  $199/annum. The premium version of the plugin offers full updates and support. Owners will receive the following benefits. Several schedules and support from 25+ payment gateways for auto payments. Also supports manual renewal payments through any WooCommerce Payment Gateway. Provides auto rebilling on failed subscription payments. Give the control to the subscribers – ability to upgrade/downgrade or take free trials. Built-in renewal notifications and automatic emails to act as reminders. Detailed reports to keep track of everything. Get WooCommerce Variable Subscription. Also, get WooCommerce monthly subscription.  When Do You Need Migration? Many eCommerce platforms do not meet or scale according to the owner’s expectations. This may be because the platform does not provide the necessary functionalities. Some of these eCommerce platforms become outdated and stop providing any value.Often eCommerce store owners wish to escape an outdated selling setup. Sometimes they find themselves worrying about the complexity of their legacy platform. All they would want is an opportunity to move the entire website to another platform. A platform that is easier to manage, more secure, and more future-proof.In such a scenario, owners choose to migrate to another platform. The process of migration is intricate and often leads to loss of data. All the entities get transferred to the new platform. Owners can’t afford to rush their migration. They’d need to pay attention and avoid any premature actions. The last thing you’d want is data corrupting or data loss.Preserve the entities. Then, keep their relations in order when moving from the source store to the target store. On top of that, you need to take care to ensure zero feature loss during your migration project.Beyond this, preserve SEO URLs & create 301 redirects where need be. Carry out the whole process without any downtime. Safeguard all the personalization settings, reviews and ratings. Migrate the reward points and keep the unique order IDs of each subscription in the new platform.  Why WooCommerce Subscription? eCommerce store owners allow customers to automate product purchases. They set this weekly, monthly, or annual intervals. Due to this, customers don’t need to keep ordering the same set of products, through a manual process. It’s a great way to streamline and simplify repeat purchases.  The subscription is valid for a product or group of products. It acts as a future agreement between purchasers and merchants. Some store owners even allow modifications to certain variables of the eligible products. For this customers don’t need to take a new subscription. But some owners aren’t as flexible. They lock the subscriptions and don’t let customers change it midway. All the recipient needs to do is – set the time, duration, quantity, and other variables. Once the billing gets done, transactions carried out, the products start getting delivered. The subscribers sit back and await the product’s arrival – with no need to renew the subscription. Plus, you’d get the following benefits with a subscription program on WooCommerce. Loyal customers who’d stay for longer – increase the lifetime value. Recurring opportunity to promote miscellaneous products. Consistent revenue with minimal sales efforts – residual revenue. Get steady and predictable sales. Free your marketing and sales team  to focus on new potential customers. Boosts customer engagement. WooCommerce Subscription Migration Challenges Migrating a subscription is problematic. On top of that, a subscription stays linked to a product, customer, payment gateway, and a group of orders. As such, migrating it gets even more difficult. Not to mention the risk of corrupting the data.You need to ensure that the migration subscription gets carried out with utmost diligence. Owners must look to avoid all the common migration pitfalls. They could also miss transferring all the pending orders. Owners could also lose customer history, which could impact their business. To avoid this, it’s essential to take a complete backup of all the data. Understand how you have mapped the fields. Once done, confirm and test the data to ensure things are in place.Each of the subscribers are running on various forms of subscriptions. May be even with varying auto-renewal times and end dates. Far more important, is the payment information linked to their bank accounts. The link is what makes the auto-renewal possible. Thus, at no point should the migration process deduct any payment from the customer. Nor, should it trigger an extra subscription on top of the pre-existing on. Outside of this, you may face some issues with supporting apps, and few pages might break. Your site ranking could also take a hit on search engines.  WooCommerce Subscription Migration – Workflow The entire migration exercise is not an overnight one-step procedure. There isn’t a workable swift solution to move all your subscriptions in one-shot. Instead, it is a mammoth task that gets carried out in careful steps. The last thing you want is to make a mess of your subscription data. Here’s the chain of events that take place. 1. Discovery An early call and support from a WooCommerce subscription specialist. We get into the crux of your requirements. This helps us to conduct a holistic analysis. From there on, we work to create an optimal subscription migration strategy for your site. 2. Plugin Installation We install and set up WooCommerce, and WooCommerce Subscriptions. We will also install any other supporting plugins if needed. Furthermore, we compile customer data and payment data into a CSV sheet. During this stage, we capture the right subscription and payment information. 3. Migration We import your customers, products, and orders. We also import the meta information onto the new subscription module. During this stage, we’ll carry-over all your pre-paid subscriptions. Furthermore, we’ll ensure a secure transfer of the entire customer data. Our experts ensure that all the data gets mapped in the right way. 4. Testing and Delivery Our diligent quality assurance team gets to work. They probe and inspect the work to ensure glitch-free results. The effort in this stage ensures your site has 99.9% uptime. You don’t face any interruptions on your subscriptions. Further, from this, we’ll do all the necessary order counts. 5. Support We stick around to make sure you have all the help you need with your subscriptions. Once our experts have completed the work, your subscription would work as normal. Subscribers would get to manage, edit, skip, update, and add-to existing orders themselves. Migrating WooCommerce Subscriptions – Infographic What Virtina Does? The WooCommerce experts at Virtina will perform a safe migration of your subscription plan. On top of that, they do so without losing any recurrent revenue. Our best migration practices ensure a hassle-free migration of subscriptions. Don’t worry about messing up your subscriptions or payments We have the experience of having migrated large websites. A lot of these websites contained thousands of orders, customers and subscriptions with different payment methods ( Stripe , PayPal etc.). Furthermore, they also add varying taxes and Autoship intervals. But, our subscription specialists managed to move everything, without any loss. Our migration workflow is meticulous and straightforward. Thus, all the current subscribers and active  subscriptions get migrated without any issues. Your users won’t notice any discrepancies. Other than the short downtime while replicating the changes onto your live site.  Our Dedicated Migration Specialists will handle the entire process from start to finish. They make every effort to ensure that your migration is swift and successful. Our experts take special care to the following. Migrating automated recurring profiles (for PayPal, or Stripe) from another system. While migrating, we do NOT create any subscriptions. Nor do we create any extra charges. We use the “Subscription CSV” file, which includes the unique transaction IDs as well. We only start a manual workflow to import a subscription that wasn’t  transferred. In other words, all recurring subscriptions we import are real, and active subscriptions. These subscriptions are the ones already present in the payment gateway.  At Virtina, we do everything from – helping with CSV formatting, and fixing broken renewals. We also deal with any issues with incorrect subscriptions. Besides, importing, and syncing subscribers with their membership plan. Once done, we import all the subscriptions to the WooCommerce site. What Does the WooCommerce Migration Involve? Often, you get subscription projects that involve the use of only one payment gateway. This didn’t need us to do a lot with regards to moving the critical payment details.All we needed to do was make use of the tokens on the merchant end and the tokens sitting on the customer side. The use of tokens, meant, we could retrieve the billing information. The billing info connects to the recurring payments. The payments stay stored on the servers of the Payment processor.Since, the tokens are the same regardless of the platform or technology in use. All we had to do was capture the tokens in the database of the old eCommerce site. From there, link them with the customers and then insert them into the new WooCommerce site. Once in place, they behaved like tokens that generated there in the first place. Once that was in place, all the payment options added through the old site showed up in their profiles. Not only that, but all the renewals also continued to go through without any interruption. Final Thoughts – WooCommerce Subscriptions The migration experts at Virtina are your best bet to move your subscription program. We will transfer every entity of your subscription program. Our experts can help migrate the customers, products, orders and much more. In fact, we will also help to keep the relationship between every entity.  Virtina has, in the past, carried out the task of migrating WooCommerce subscriptions. A whole lot of them consisted of a vast number of users with different renewal times and products. Yet, the Woo Experts managed to transfer everything to the WooCommerce store. Virtina is the pioneer in any Subscription related matter. The Woo experts at Virtina are the ideal choice for your Subscription migration. Our experts will help you save time, money, and effort. They all take the fastest process and give the lowest error rate. WooCommerce Subscriptions Migration – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) What is the cost of migrating my subscriptions to WooCommerce? Since no two subscription programs are the same, it’s hard to offer fixed costs for their migration. Our cost tends to be more personalized. The complexity and size of your subscription program will decide the price. We will evaluate your subscription program, review the number of entities before submitting a final affordable quote. Can I migrate all the entities from my subscription to WooCommerce? Yes, you may migrate as many entities as you want from your subscription program on another eCommerce platform to WooCommerce. Our migration procedures allow you to transfer products, subscription Intervals, categories, customers, orders, and much more. Furthermore, we also map all the entities correctly in the new subscription on WooCommerce. How long will it take to migrate my subscriptions? The extent of time it takes will depend on the complexity and size of your subscription program. Subscriptions with multiple variations, orders, customers, payment, and other parameters take longer to migrate. We will give you a time estimate after analyzing your subscription model. Nonetheless, we promise to forward all the deliverables before the due date. Will I lose any data during the migration process? No. Our WooCommerce migration experts are well-versed in migrating subscriptions. They move all the data securely and that too without any data loss or corruption. Our experts follow best practices and take absolute precautions during the migration process. All the data will be safe, we’ll ensure the continuity of data, and if anything were to go wrong, we are quite capable of recovering the data. Will the migration affect the customers on my online store? No. Your customers will be able to access and modify their subscriptions as usual. Your online store won’t go offline during the migration process. Our developers will do all the work on your new subscription program on the backend, giving you adequate time to customize the settings, test your subscriptions, and train your team. Why not a Native Mobile App?
How to Make Your WordPress Mobile-friendly?
Tips to Optimize WordPress for Mobile Devices – Infographic
text: The epicenter of eCommerce is no longer desktop – it is mobile devices. Internet users are not tethered to their laptop screens – which is why your website shouldn’t be either. The rise in smartphone shopping has made it vital to adjust your business plans around smaller screen devices. Google would go on to penalize brands that don’t optimize their websites. They recommend websites be responsive to improve their SERP. Mobile-friendly websites are the “IT” in today’s age. Your Desktop only mindset will deplete your company’s earnings. 61% of users are unlikely to return to a mobile site they had trouble with – Google Companies are therefore leaning towards mobile browsing , so much so that they’d create a mobile version of WordPress before creating an equivalent for Desktop. All these efforts are a testament to the rise in mobile commerce. Not only that, but owners have also started monitoring their site page speeds on Google PageSpeed Insights to get an overview over how the search engine processes the page speed on mobile. The objective is to reduce friction & make the sales cycle on mobile as fluid as possible. What is Mobile Optimization? Mobile optimization is the process of adjusting your website content, in such a manner that users who access the site from devices other than a desktop are able to get an experience customized to that particular device. Visitors on mobile devices must also get an engaging & user-friendly experience on the website. The website should be flexible & therefore not compromise the site quality on mobile devices. Not simply, compressing, shrink the size of the pages & slightly rearranging the content, but designing an entire experience for smaller screens. An optimized site delivers bigger navigation buttons, reformatted content, and optimized images that will appear when the site detects that the user is browsing on a Smartphone. Such a site will ultimately drive mobile conversions . Why is Mobile Optimization Important? Users today are more likely to browse and shop on mobile screens – gravitating towards small screen devices is more convenience than anything. Smartphones are the preferred platform to fulfil all the shopping requirements. We live in a multi-screen world. In such a scenario, optimizing your WordPress site takes paramount importance. As a competitive business, you need to take your message to your target audience – engage with them on the platform of their choice. Do not take it for granted, that your customers will access your site via desktop; if the mobile experience fails their expectations. They’ll never return to your website & turn to your rival instead. You want your site to generate traffic. But once a visitor gets there, you want their experience to be positive. Having a website that’s ready for mobile use will improve your visitor’s experience & increase the customer lifetime value . Mobile Friendliness of Your WordPress Site To know if your WordPress site meets the mobile standards, head over to the mobile-friendless test page and enter your website to determine whether your site is smartphone friendly. This test is a sure-shot way to find out if your website will deliver quality mobile experience to your visitors or will it come up short. Simply, input your site’s URL, & it will tell you if there’s anything wrong with your site’s mobile optimization. Beyond this, website owners can even analyze their site on SEMRush . SEMRush will check the site for mobile compatibility & will pick up any other problems that are hurting the Google rankings. Things like slow page loading, broken links, pages where Google crawlers are unable to reach & other potential SEO issues. Else, turn to the section under Google Search Console. The section called “Mobile usability,” under “Search Traffic” will help you to learn more about your site’s elements – whether they are too close, font size, font face & other issues. Why not a Native Mobile App? A native mobile app is just more bloatware on your customer’s phone and will likely go unused for a very long time. Eventually, they’d uninstall the app, which will mean absolute cut-off from your brand.  There are already enough apps on your phone & it goes without saying on your buyer’s phone as well. So, if it doesn’t serve a higher purpose or solve multiple things, it is not likely to get downloaded. Here are some scenarios in which a native app makes sense. Developing a Rich-interactive experience which cannot be substituted by a responsive website. Existing web technology limits the ability to showcase your brand’s full potential. An established brand, that’d no doubt get thousands of downloads. But this isn’t the case with your brand. You, on the other hand, want the website for a whole lot of different reasons. You need SEO to attract visitors to your site. You want to facilitate the easiest way to social-share your website content. Your target audience won’t need to access your site offline There is a good chance that, in the majority of cases, a mobile website is the best path to hit the above objectives. And even if you do decide to go for an app, it will have to be complemented with a high-quality mobile-optimized website. How to Make Your WordPress Mobile-friendly? Here are all the different techniques to make your WordPress site mobile-friendly. 1. Make Sure to Optimize Images Images delay the page load times & make it difficult to adjust a page for mobile devices. For that matter, we’d have to address the image problem as well. Thankfully since WP 4.4, the CMS serves the smallest image using an HTML attribute. You could even optimize such images prior to uploading them – save them in a web format that reduces the load on pages & uses images in their optimal size. Ultimately you’d want the images to load in a fraction of a second & not forever.  Use Image Optimizers – these are the tools that create the best balance between resolution & dimension. They help to compress the image size & improve the page load times. Try Tiny PNG, EWWW Image Optimizer, & Kraken to optimize images. Minimize elaborate graphics! 2. Avoid Full Screen Pop-ups On desktop it may make sense – but on mobile they same can be a tad bit annoying. Since touch controls make it hard to get rid of them on smaller screens. If you are really in need of expanding your sales database; use banners, links or place CTA’s inside content. Even a sign-up form placed aesthetically in the right place can work wonders & solve the same purpose. The use of CSS or JavaScript will disable them on mobile devices & only limit them to users browsing on Desktop. Otherwise opt for mobile-friendly WordPress pop-up plugins.  3. Incorporate a Responsive Theme The responsive theme adapts the content to any device & not just a desktop. With a responsive theme – you wouldn’t need to run a separate mobile site, alongside the traditional desktop one. As the responsive themes will adjust to all screen sizes. Now, most of the themes in the WordPress directory are responsive. However, if you wish to retain the current theme, & optimize it somehow; either DIY via tutorials or turn to a WordPress designer who’d make the theme responsive.  With a responsive theme, every user on mobile/otherwise can access the same site. No need, to update/modify multiple versions for the same purpose – this conserves, time, resources & funds.  4. Utilize Google’s Accelerated Mobile Pages Google’s Accelerated Mobile Pages is a new kind of HTML mark-up that makes your pages quick to load in Google’s search results. Google’s AMP’s are lightning fast and mobile compatible. Use the official plugin (AMP for WP) to set up AMP for your website pages. All you need to do is activate the AMP plugin. From there onwards, your site starts serving AMP content to mobile visitors from Google. Also, you can add some styling options to these pages with the use of other plugins. Even the SEO of your site isn’t affected – as most plugins add rel=”canonical” tags to your AMP content, to avoid duplication. Most users prefer to click on sites marked with the AMP designation.  5. Make Use of Plugins The availability of plugins is another asset of WordPress, which makes the admin’s job so much easier. One of these plugins possesses the capability to turn your website mobile-friendly. No need to try & make sense of any technical coding. A simple plugin can make the website responsive, without having to zoom-in or scroll left-right when trying to sweep the page.  With one click, your mobile theme is activated. Further customizations, like changing the colors & creating custom menus are also likely via these plugins.  Try WordPress Mobile Pack, WP Touch, WP Mobile Edition, WP Mobile Detector, JetPack & more to provide a simple way to optimize the site for mobile. Beyond this, Gravity Forms & Contact Form 7 plugins create responsive forms that resize with the browser window. 6. Create a Textual Balance In addition to lowering the graphic load from all the web pages, it is also important to set the textual content in order. On mobile screens, the lack of space means the text will flow to the next line – thereby taking up too much space. Therefore minimizing text is equally important, as it could increase the scroll and make it exhausting to scroll through the whole content. Often visitors miss out on important details (CTA buttons, links, offers) due to it being placed way down on the page.  Keep what is needed and reduce the frill. This way, users consume what they need to make an informed purchase – without wasting time on redundant paragraphs.  7. Bring a Balanced Menu In the mobile world, menu’s play a very important role. Thus, find a way to display these menus correctly. Visitors need to be able navigate from one section to another – which is facilitated by the use of a balanced, well designed menu. On mobile the browsing pattern is slightly different from Desktop in the sense that, users here are only looking for relevant data. They’d probably not want secondary & miscellaneous content to waste their time. Stick to useful content in the top-half. Maybe opt for a Hamburger menu .  This includes product details, company description, contact info, certifications & other valuable content. Create a mobile specific menu that fulfils user needs & adjusts well on smaller screens. 8. Use Reliable Web Hosting To improve the likelihood of conversions – you’d need a proper host. A second faster loading will make a significant difference to your revenue & profits. Try as much to reduce the server response time & improve site performance considerably. In some instances, you don’t even need to mess with the cache. Just switch to a more credible provider and see the difference. Many store owners have seen a significant improvement in their uptime and load times . No further optimization needed! Tips to Optimize WordPress for Mobile Devices – Infographic Conclusion With scores of people using mobile devices for various reasons, it’d be senseless to think that they’d opt for Desktop to view your site. The fact that their daily browsing is already happening on a mobile device means they’d likely access your website on the same as well. Hence, it is essential to cater to the audience lurking on mobile devices . These folks run their entire digital activities on mobile devices. Thus, your brand must find a way to create a superior, responsive & mobile-friendly site.   By optimizing your site for mobile devices, you create another sales avenue . The crowd that is mobile-oriented will generate sales on phones, the other group that prefers Desktop will use that for shopping & the ones that are open to using both will use either. If your WordPress site isn’t already responsive and suffers from other issues on mobile devices, then get in touch with the certified, highly-experienced, and astute eCommerce experts – Virtina. We’ll ensure that your site functions at its very best on mobile devices.

title: WordPress for eCommerce: Security Enhancements in 2020
text: WordPress was mainly a content-rich platform, that wasn’t intended for eCommerce. It is one of the most powerful & flexible Content Management Systems (CMS). Over the years, with the help of eCommerce plugins, WordPress was given selling capabilities. So, if you are already high on content, all you’d have to do is download a free eCommerce plugin & acquire the power to sell online. But, every eCommerce store runs into security risks, which is why WordPress too needs proper security measures to keep sensitive data safe.   The vulnerabilities on your website can be exploited to gain access to the vital data. A potential breach will not only see you lose data, but it’d also risk some form of a lawsuit from the customers. 41% of WP sites are hacked due to security flaws on the hosting platform – WPWhiteSecurity The WordPress code being open source means unauthorized access is likely. But, it’s not all that bad, as we can, in various ways, prevent such an attack & safeguard your store. Why is WordPress Safety Important? A hacked WordPress site can cause critical damage to your business sales, revenue, profits & reputation. Hackers can steal user information, passwords, install malicious software, & even distribute malware to users. Worst, you may find yourself paying the hackers to regain access to your website. If you are running an enterprise-level business, then you need to be extra vigilant about such threats. Come what may, the business owners cannot allow lapses in their WordPress security. What Compromises WordPress Safety? The WordPress core is entirely secure in itself, yet plenty of WordPress websites are hacked every year & easily exploited by malicious users. A lot of it comes down to the recklessness of the webmaster.  Let’s look at some everyday things that WordPress site owners do that diminishes its security: Have weak administrator passwords & other login requirements Themes & Plugins that are not updated often – making it insecure The internet connection itself is compromised & greatly exposes your WordPress store Poor Hosting environment with an insecure host control panel The computer causing interference as it was pre-loaded with malware Using outdated technologies like PHP 5 over PHP 7 Various WordPress Attacks Let’s list some frequent attacks that can gravely compromise the quality of your WordPress site –   SQL injection – This is the oldest technique in the book, where a hacker manipulates the MySQL database & gains access to the admin panel. To access the database, hackers use a form page/input field. Backdoor Attack – This one is a little more advanced, where a hacker will bypass security encryption to gain access to the WordPress site. Once they control the whole system on the hosting servers, it’ll compromise the multiple sites hosted on the same server.  To prevent this, use two-factor authentication, restrict admin access, & unauthorized execution of PHP files. Pharma Hacks – These are also referred to as Blackhat SEO Spam & compromise the site to the extent where it stays like that for months. The spam that appears is generally about Viagra, Nexium, or any other Pharma drug. Use a secure hosting provider to prevent this kind of mishap. Brute-Force Attack – Hackers use an automated script to run a trial & error style of hacking on your WordPress site.  Malicious users attempt several times & end up on the right combination of username/password. Brute-Force capitalizes on websites with weak passwords. Despite the difficulty, hackers use context/research to guesstimate the correct credentials. Cross-Site Scripting – A malicious script is injected into a plugin. A compromised extension can be used to pass this code onto the site. The prime objective is to grab cookies, session data, or rewrite HTML on a page. Hackers even run JavaScript codes for redirecting to suspicious websites.   DDOS – Distributed Denial of Service is used to create a large volume of requests, to slow down the server & cause it to crash. The biggest problem with such attacks is it creates considerable downtime for your site – something that’d last even days. It is otherwise harmless & most sites can easily handle this. Invest in some premium web hosting providers to prevent any DDOS.   Remote File Inclusion (RFI) Exploits – RFI is the most common threat to any WordPress site. The PHP that makes up your WordPress site is exploited to close this attack. Via this hackers access various files, including the “wp-config.php” file that is used for WordPress installation. To prevent this, save the file paths with an ID in a secure database.  WordPress Security Measures Let’s list the several precautions that every store owner must take to secure their WordPress site. Core Software – Most websites get hacked because the core WordPress software wasn’t updated on time. Now, let’s be honest here, WordPress doesn’t just release an update for the heck of it.  The update is meant to tell the world that the earlier version is obsolete & it’s time for an upgrade. Not updating on time – leaves your website vulnerable to interference. It takes only a couple of clicks to update WordPress – may even turn on Auto Update.With Auto Update, you are promptly updated to the next version. The WordPress team identifies & addresses security issues with each update. On your side, all you need to do is apply this update at the earliest – before your site gets defaced! Hosting – Hosting is another major problem. Always use a Hosting company that is compatible with an eCommerce website. With this, you’d be offered your own hosting plan rather than a shared one which increases the safety of your site. The web-server level security is the most vital aspect, something that is the responsibility of the Hosting provider. There are various kinds of hosting options – Shared, Dedicated, VPS, Cloud & managed. When it comes to eCommerce stores, always opt for Dedicated Servers .   SSL certificates – Besides, a web host your eCommerce site needs additional security features like SSL/TLS certificates. SSL certificates, or HTTPS, ensure that the data that is transferred is secure & encrypted. SSL encrypts data between the website & the browser.SSL makes it harder on those sniffing to steal information. SSL certificate is used to provide an extra layer of support from the usual HTTP for all the transactions that occur on your eCommerce site. The Padlock sign next to website addresses is the SSL – it’ll cost around $80-100/year. Login Credentials – Store owners make it a lot easier on hackers when they use weak passwords. Believe it or not, the most common hacking attempts are using stolen passwords. Do this on the WordPress admin side, FTP accounts, database, hosting & email address .  Often the inability to remember hard passwords is what tempts them to use “12345,” “ABCD” “Admin” or their names. In such instances, you can use an encrypted password manager. Even consider adding a security question to your WordPress login screen.WordPress does a good job, by automatically generating secure/strong passwords. All you have to do is enforce these passwords. Also never store your FTP passwords in plaintext. May be avoid FTP altogether and opt for SFTP , which ensures no text passwords/file data is ever transferred.  PCI Compliance – PCI stands for Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard. The use of PCI will protect customer’s information while they pay with a debit or credit card. However, this isn’t applicable on stores/buyers that don’t use the above mode of payment. PCI encrypts cardholder data across open & public networks. Beyond this, it also tracks & monitors all access to network resources & cardholder data. The cardholder’s data is accessed on a need-to-know basis.  Security Plugins – Use one of these to protect your site from security threats & attacks. Plugins like WordFence & Sucuri are the best gatekeepers for your store. You could also opt for a free security plugin, but it’d only give you limited functionalities.  Such plugins keep track of everything that happens on your website – from installing a firewall, managing anti-malware & checking for spam. Beyond this, they look for failed login attempts; Audit logs, file integrity monitoring, locking down sensitive areas & much more. Update Plugins – Archaic plugins are a potential gateway for a malicious file. Despite the abundance of plugins and all the extra possibilities they bring to an eCommerce store – there lies a good amount of threat from not updating them on time. Plugins are in fact the most common ways for a hacker to gain access to your site. Despite the vulnerabilities of the plugin getting patched up by the plugin developer, the site owners did not bother to update the plugins.  Ignoring updates puts their businesses at risk! All the updates are meant to serve a specific purpose. Therefore do not overlook these best practices. Use the latest version of WordPress themes & plugins – and only install extensions from reliable sources.  Limit Login – Malicious users to intend to gain access will not stop at anything. They make numerous attempts to enter your site. Thus, it is important that you download a plugin that restricts the number of failed attempts. This will act as another security layer for your site. Latest PHP – Since WordPress is entirely made out of PHP, it is important to always use the latest version of PHP. All the bugs & security issues are sorted on every update. WordPress sites running on version 7.0 or below will have no security support. 57% of WordPress users are still using PHP version 5.6 or below – WordPress Consult your developers and upgrade to the latest version at the earliest. There is no reason to use a dated-compromised PHP for your site.  It is also advised to remove the current version of WordPress – knowing the version tells the hackers about its vulnerabilities. 2 Factor Authentication – A 2 step process, that requires you to login via username & password combo, plus another level of verification via an app/device. Install a plugin for this purpose & activate the same. Google Authenticator is an excellent plugin to achieve this purpose. Upon successful password entry, you need to access the app. Open the authenticator app & enter the OTP from there into the Login Terminal of your WordPress site. 2 Factor Authentication is one of the most reliable ways to prevent a Brute-Force attack .  Conclusion If your business is running on WordPress, then you can’t overlook the security aspect of the same. Your brand relies on this to generate leads, conversions, revenue & profit. A disfigured/crashed site will ultimately cancel your earnings – besides affecting your reputation. Hence, take WordPress security measurements & implement the above-mentioned security best practices. Your WordPress site is only as secure as you make it out to be. Don’t be reckless – use strong passwords, update periodically, use reliable hosting to protect your WordPress site. Beyond this, if you’d like an expert to handle your WordPress website’s security concerns, then speak to the tech-savvy WordPress professionals in Virtina.
