title: Importance of Product Images For Your eCommerce Store
text: A scenario where anyone must rely on descriptions and a wavering imagination to visualize the product would lead to displeasure when the product doesn’t match their unrealistic expectations.Back in the days, tele-callers would find it hard to convince you to invest in an item. Such was the apprehension that no consumer would book a product without referring to a catalog. Why, because the catalog held relevant imagery.Even face to face, people find it hard to convey the features of something. Let’s accept it; humans are incapable of reading minds; therefore, they will need some visual element to grasp the exact product. “Picture is worth a thousand words.” Giving your customers supportive images to ease their shopping experience and make your store more reliable for future purchases.The images that get uploaded must satisfy a whole host of other conditions as well. Whether it connects with the products being sold, appeals to your audience, the page load times, types, dimensions and so on.Once added and optimized well, these images can boost the traffic and improve the retention rates; which will then no doubt translate into higher conversion rates for your webstore.No matter what, don’t leave the images out. Factor these useful graphic elements to elevate the overall status of your store and edge out the competition.  Need for Media Images are helpful to the overall narrative on the webpage. Besides, adding gloss, they assist viewers with the decision-making process. A 360o photography of your SKU’s will give a better insight to the visitor.So, why leave them out. Embed these and boost your site’s power of luring and retaining customers. Images bring that X-factor on your site , which quotes, texts and paragraphs could never deliver.Pictures captivate people and engage them for longer. Precisely, what you want to conquer in this modern era of eCommerce evolution, images will reinforce the worth of a product and improve the likelihood of conversions.The most artistic traits of your product; like the craftsmanship on shoes, designer bags, fashionable garments and so on, need to be highlighted in rich detail and images accomplish this goal with remarkable accuracy. Your business can depend on them to give adequate sales. Optimizing the Images Images make up a substantial percentage of the total content on a webpage. Hence, it’s also paramount that you adjust the optimization of these elements on the webpage, right after inserting them.Reduce the weight and not the quality of the image. For the sake of bringing the lowest file size, don’t lower the details in the picture; some of which could be essential in assisting the consumer.Reducing an image to a tiny fraction of its original size is an approach that often leads to a severe amount of visual depreciation. A blurred image gives off all the wrong vibes and immediately tempts the visitor to look elsewhere.On an image-rich website, you will also need to be aware to keep request sizes down. As a faster loading time will improve your user’s willingness to stay on the page. So, don’t waste their precious bandwidth with oversized, unoptimized images. Use image optimizers for web and improve the loading speeds.With a good chunk of traffic on any webstore coming from mobile and tablets, the crowd there expects faster loading times and pleasant navigation w.r.t images. Any delay will lead to disappointment; which will make them desert your site forever. Best Practices How you go about the optimization on your website is equally important, there are many ways to perform the same; here’s listing a few approaches that you can take to arrive at the best output: File Types – JPEG is best for product images as they allow for the display of millions of colors and allows you to adjust the file size. PNG – 8 allows only 256 colors whereas PNG-24 allows millions of colors and is best to use when image quality is more important than file size.GIF’s also allows only 256 colors and is the best option when it comes to displaying animated stuff without taking up a lot of size. Can be used for small thumbnails, icons, and logos. File size – Keep the image file size small to improve conversions, as each image must load when you visit a webpage, thus the overall time to finish rendering the page is affected. Larger images take up more space on the server, take longer to load thus breaking the performance of your site. Naming  – Image names must be kept as precise as possible to assist the search engines in discovering your content. Change the names to be more descriptive, explanatory, to the point so that the search bots can detect what the image is showing. Random numbers and vague symbols will not direct the search results towards your webpage. Use straightforward labeling to help the search bots discover your pictures. ​ Alt Tags – Alt tags are descriptions given to an image within your website’s code. The image content is essentially written into the code. These tags come in handy for visually impaired people as the assistive tech will read the description out loud,In case of loading issues, this line of code will notify the browser what’s supposed to be there, which will help the SEO crawlers to determine the stuff within the image. Sitemaps – Search engine web crawlers will find it easy to navigate your site more intelligently when there is a map for all your site’s content. For any image embedded, use location, Title, Description, and Caption. Use SEO tools to add your images to a sitemap automatically. Thumbnails – The goal is to get the thumbnail images to load, whether on the product page or as a recommended product at checkout for Cross-Selling. In a scenario where these enticing visual elements take time to load; you stand to lose plenty of sales. A/B Testing – Never accept a single kind/type for any of the graphics on your site. Bring about changes from time to time to test various formats, sizes, dimensions, and quality; before you finalize the one that best suits your purpose. Experiment to find the best settings for each page. CDN – Content Delivery Networks are a go-to option for brands that wish to host images and media files to elevate your page load speeds and solve bandwidth issues. Especially if you get global traffic and your image servers are located away from where your traffic originates. Trends The fads for embedding media elements have evolved dramatically over the years. There are no creative boundaries that’d prevent an artist from sharing the content in a clear and visually stimulating manner. Be it infographics or meta images; creators are trying it all.As such, graphic designers are trying different formats and ways in which their idea can be presented to the audience; Ultimately, you want their recognition to improve the chances of order completion.Let’s look at some of the latest trends that the visitors will find visually speaking: Cinemagraph – Still photographs in which a minor and repeated movement occurs. One element within the image is static, while the rest of it moves to create an effect that can leave your readers awestruck. Use them effectively, to bring your pictures to life and to leave a better impact on users. Contemporary companies around the world use this on websites, banner ads, social media accounts and email campaigns to advertise, tell stories, and create an immersive experience. Indexical – Use such images in your visual storytelling and make the webpage more attractive to the visitor. Images that evoke specific emotions without the need to detail anything in-depth. Using kittens and puppies to convey happiness or using a tragic shot to express loss and negativity. Progress GIF’s – A great way to include a GIF and make it interesting for your consumers. A unique way to present your products, in which you get to see the progress of how something has changed or developed.Making it very useful to showcase the initial and final designs; be it in fashion, jewelry, footwear, and even automobiles. Daze your audience and give the message you wish to send. Tools When it comes to Image optimization, there is no shortage of image optimizer tools. Every known resource on the internet claims to bring the right balance of speed and quality.Thus, you need a comprehensive understanding to evaluate the ones that best serve the above purpose. A tool that varies the dimension but heavily compromises the quality or gives a high-resolution image that will eat all the bandwidth; causing slow page loads and leads to abandonment.Here’s listing some of the well-renowned tools that can help you to manage images effectively: – Kraken – An Image compression tool that lets you upload files in bulk and optimizes them for the lowest file size to accelerate your website. A robust ultra-fast compressor with the best-in-class algorithms to save your bandwidth, storage space and improve the website’s load times.Run your images through Kraken and witness the drastic drop in image sizes. Optimize pictures from within your applications using the fully-featured and easy-to-use API. EWWW Image Optimizer Cloud – Will automatically optimize the new images and already uploaded images; optionally convert your images to the best file format. Get to choose between pixel perfect or high compression options that are visually lossless.With EWWW you are not limited by file size, get intelligent conversion options (JPG, PNG, etc.), no charges on uncompressed images and attain secure communication with top SSL encryption. ShortPixel – An image optimization and compression API plus WordPress plugin that helps to improve your website performance; where the resultant smaller images don’t suffer from a diminished quality, comes with both lossy and lossless optimization.Provides batch optimization, quick backups, and uses powerful algorithms to with less bandwidth usage to give super-fast websites. Install to your WordPress dashboard and get started. TinyPNG – Using smart lossy compression to reduce the overall size of your PNG images. A very selective process that targets the number of colors in the image; barely any loss in quality but brings aboutUsing intelligent techniques to analyze the best possible JPEG encoding for your images. Even comes with its Photoshop version to scale, preview and save compressed PNG and JPEG images. Conclusion Once you have optimized your images to ensure the best performance on your eCommerce site; the traffic to your site will immediately start rolling. The hits, Click Through rates, retention times and conversions will follow. Use WordPress image optimizer plugins, that compress and optimize images externally on their servers. Which in turn, will reduce the load on your site or rely on vector images for faster loading. Beyond this, remove any unnecessary image data or rely on a photo editing software to accomplish the job.Use web fonts instead of placing text within images, use lossy compression where possible and save images as “optimized for web” in tools such as Photoshop. Witness your site becoming more search engine friendly, as the algorithm starts detecting your images better; leading to a higher ranking on Google .Format the visual statements to prevent your site from slowing down the experience of the keen visitors on the site. title: Traditional, Decoupled, Headless eCommerce: An Introduction
text: Solutions must at the end of the day offer elegance, a term that is often overlooked in the eCommerce space — a desire to bring convenience for the admin and a seamless session for the end user. The result must blend agility, efficiency, and adaptability on the entire interface. To be able to differentiate and compete at the highest level, top brands wanted the best breed of architectural performance. They wanted an architecture that serves the purpose of high organic traffic, increased sales, and thus better revenue — integrating content management and eCommerce platforms. The Early Days of eCommerce In the early days, all enterprise eCommerce platforms were designed to run on computer browsers that the majority of the audience used. Other touchpoints like mobile, social media, and wearable tech weren’t considered as a sales source or didn’t exist at all. All brands created their product pages with vast manually-coded HTML to achieve the desired result. It worked nonetheless, since the sales volumes were low. Though it couldn’t last the test of the evolving landscape. With more digital devices emerging, the need to recognize the broader picture arose. More and more businesses started to adapt their eCommerce stores with other channels. They made the shift towards sophisticated solutions to support larger inventory sizes and maximize revenue. The dated solutions (monolithic model) that existed were effective when you had minimal digital touchpoints. For the service providers nowadays highlighting their brand across several devices is the norm. Thus they need a more customer-centric commerce platform, powered by API’s. Hence, a headless solution or headless commerce makes more sense. A trend seen in recent years is the dwindling demand of the traditional eCommerce model . Since, there is a need for higher performance, cost, efficiency, and results. As a result, API-first Headless eCommerce is gaining momentum. Store owners desire to start their eCommerce business on a headless eCommerce platform. Traditional Commerce Traditional Commerce aka a monolithic model; the front and backend are not separated. This gives the business owner a rigid solution built with a pre-determined frontend. It requires any frontend change to reflect on the backend as well. The backend is where the website design and customization applications got stored. In Traditional Commerce (monolithic CMS) the editors are writing and publishing on the backend of the same system that your visitors are viewing. In Traditional Commerce, simple tweaks on the frontend need changes on the back-end code as well. Since, both are reliant on each other, this may mean shutting down or redeploying the entire site. Thus, you can’t make changes in real time, resulting in time wastage. If the back-end experiences any errors, performance issues, or requires maintenance, then it may cause downtime on the live site. Traditional eCommerce websites don’t adjust to changes very well, which limits the ability of the business to respond to market opportunities. Traditional Commerce offers templates that look and appear the same in presentation and feel. While setting this up may seem effortless, on the customer side it is very generic. This then results in higher bounce rates and cart abandonment issues due to the cookie-cutter feel on the page . A rich and captivating online experience that a visitor hopes to find, takes a beating. Something that repels customers and waives the faith of superior brands towards traditional eCommerce. Customization is the biggest concern in a full stack eCommerce architecture and it becomes difficult to maintain, like in a multi-touchpoint scenario. It also restricts the type of content that one can post, such as videos and rich imagery. Since most companies try separate commerce solutions, this creates silos which cannot be supplemented; something that’d result in inconsistent behavior. Over time this manifests into a high risk of failure. The downside of slow go-to-market timelines and high development costs in traditional commerce setup drifted many brands and made them look elsewhere to better connect with their audience. Traditional Commerce Summary Store Content and digital assets in a database Content gets created on a Content management backend. Publishers and designers can create and apply design schemas. Frontend displays published content on HTML pages. Benefits of Traditional Commerce Traditional CMS (Content Management System) is ideal for blogs, personal sites, and basic company sites. These sites don’t need any massive changes.  It is easy to develop, manage, and publish text-based content. The design is also simplified within a traditional CMS platform, with built-in themes and standard templates. Includes a frontend that can be edited and customized as and when needed. A summary of what the traditional model is made up of: Decoupled Commerce Decoupled CMS (Content Management System) contains headless commerce, making headless a subset of decoupled commerce. A decoupled CMS is “headless” and then some, meaning it gives you all the benefits of Headless CMS. In a Decoupled scenario, the back-end gets used for content creation and storage. The frontend gets used for consuming data and presenting it to the user through some interface. In a decoupled CMS, the two systems stay housed away from each other. It is also known as a Hybrid Headless CMS whereby your content gets managed in a distance. Yet it comes equipped with frontend tools like templates in case you ever want to use them. Also, like in the case of a traditional CMS, the backend and frontend are not tied. A scenario that sees changes made on one side to not reflect on the other side. Decoupled is also known as the best of both worlds, where you have “chopped off” the head, yet you haven’t detached the head from the “body.” In a headless architecture after preparing the content via the editorial tools you’d need an API call to publish it. It assumes the frontend developer team will be able to handle the content with the set of tools. Whereas in a decoupled architecture due to the availability of templates, the content management becomes easier since you could  start somewhere. A decoupled CMS is therefore looked at as being more proactive, since it prepares content and pushes it out . In contrast, a headless system is more reactive since it waits back for some process to ask for it. Decoupled has content management, storage backends, and delivers content from the database through a web service or API. The crucial difference between the Headless system and Decoupled architecture is in the presentation layer. Unlike decoupled, headless doesn’t  have a defined presentation environment. Decoupled Commerce Summary Content and digital assets are found stored in a database. Content is created on a Content management backend. An API that connects the content management backend, with the frontend. A default, content publishing frontend. Benefits of Decoupled Commerce In a decoupled environment you can use WYSIWYG editing, get content previews and other content publishing tools, something that you are robbed of in headless CMS. Decoupled CMS is the best of both worlds: you have templates to work with like in a traditional CMS you get the flexibility of a headless implementation. Future-proofs your website implementation, since the user interface side is more resilient in the face of change A summary of what the decoupled model is made up of: Headless Commerce Earlier sites were only a source of content but have recently ventured into retailing. With the Headless approach they could sync the same content with the commerce engine without the need to redevelop the whole site. Disconnect the frontend from the backend, chop it off – hence “headless.” The Headless CMS architecture is one of the most prominent concepts when it comes to developing eCommerce sites. Headless Commerce separates the backend from the user interface but connects the two through a set of web services. In essence, decouple the frontend presentation layer from the backend. “Headless” concept came to the surface when eCommerce over multiple points (Omnichannel) became a growing concern. In the past, eCommerce was performed on Desktop; as a result, both front and backend were coupled, and the sales were quite simple. Headless Commerce is something in which the content is separated from the logic and functional layer , making it a viable solution for many businesses looking to prioritize content going ahead. Push content into the frontend isolated from the management environment. Focus resources on customer interactions without worrying about impacting critical systems such as payment processing or product databases. Unlike traditional Commerce, the headless solution allows store owners to do just that. Take the headless approach and simplify the management of your eCommerce store.   With headless Commerce you can manage the content and deliver it to any channel , something that the traditional CMS (Content Management System) couldn’t support, giving us the flexibility of content, custom code, the editing interface and templates in a single environment. Traditional eCommerce limited the ability to change sites at whim.  Now, since we need to display content across several devices, the traditional CMS became unsupportive, and the need to design a new form of CMS took hold, something that wouldn’t influence the style or manner in which you present the content. If the front and backend are tied (full stack), any change executed on the frontend will affect the backend as well which then costs time, money and introduces risk. Headless Commerce only focuses on providing content through its API (Application Programming Interface). The API makes the content available, independent of the channel and device. Write your website or mobile apps using any programming language; in the process lending higher scalability to your eCommerce business. The customer touch points are anything that the customer interacts with, to achieve some purpose on a given site. The touchpoints could be the apps, the screen, forms, voice interfaces and so on, that visitors use to interact with your business. Headless Commerce architecture is something that realizes the need for CMS with eCommerce and allows for both to co-exist without any conflict. In other words, you can decouple the frontend customer touch points from the backend operational systems that we use to run the business. You can connect the eCommerce platform to additional tools like ERPs, PIMs, and perform other integrations via APIs. So, keep your existing content but still expand your eCommerce offerings without disrupting the entire business. Plus, with headless Commerce you’d reduce the time to market as well. Headless Commerce Summary Content and digital assets are found stored in a database. Content gets created on a Content management backend. Headless API connects the content management backend to any touchpoint Froontend development becomes much easier and frontend experiences become better Connect to any publishing frontend, enabling owners to have the frontend technology of their choice. Benefits of Headless Commerce Headless CMS architecture lets you integrate with any system, without any significant redevelopment. With UX being the clear focus for any brand going ahead, you want to invest in Headless architecture as it helps you to deliver a rich User Experience. Only replace the components of the architecture or the system that need any replacing, letting you have a more tailored development of pieces. With a clear divide between customer concerns and system concerns, you can focus on the underperforming / performing resources. Run promotions on the site without a full system reconfiguration. Compartmentalizing different functions of your commerce environment ensures that risks associated with one API remain isolated, preventing impact on other systems. Platform upgrades, performance fixes, applying new functionalities, integrations, and the addition of new features take less time in Headless CMS architecture; because of the openness of the architecture. Businesses relying on heavy content, visually stimulating rich media, personalized content and are continually upgrading or going through a series of changes can implement “Headless.” The ability to make changes fast, measure the impact of those changes, and then optimize the site based on those results, the sort of experiments critical in winning customers. A summary of what the headless model is made up of: Conclusion Content pages and data don’t oppose each other and are certainly not mutually exclusive, we just need to find a way to mesh them together, and that is how “headless” emerged. The headless approach has become quite popular in the recent past for building an eCommerce store. The Headless CMS became a major shift from the monolithic CMS. The headless architecture utilizes the power and functional maturity of both. In headless Commerce by detaching the frontend and backend, then allowing them to communicate via API enables changes to be made on either side (even in parallel) without being blocked by each other. Decouple the eCommerce platform from the presentation layer, so businesses can use any CMS they like. In Headless eCommerce, frontend developers can make the necessary frontend changes, and backend developers don’t need to fret over these changes breaking the backend rules and logic. Now, make a change to some part of the frontend and leave the backend components alone. Headless eCommerce creates a true separation of the frontend and backend.  Meanwhile, merchants can focus on conversion optimization, without upsetting developers, proving to be a big win. Performing A/B tests is far more flexible, enabling the brands to learn which version creates more traffic and drives higher conversion. All this is possible through the Headless Commerce approach. In fact, the headless Commerce approach gives you the ability to run tests even during peak seasons. The main advantage of a system  headless commerce is it gives you the liberty to run tests even during peak seasons – no need to shut down the website. Work with your internal team to test user flows and find the ideal conversion funnels for successful results. Decoupled CMS uses templates and tools seen with traditional CMS, many of these tools are not available in headless CMS. But, a headless platform will allow more control over how the content appears on each type of device. The Headless eCommerce solution cannot present the content to the end user on its own. Decoupled Commerce can maneuver this challenge with ease. The Headless Commerce system is “API only, UI anything” making it possible to present the content to any device. It isn’t limited by a predetermined user interface. The traditional CMS architecture made it difficult to use content management solutions to their full potential. Due to the backend and frontend; which slowed down innovation. Get in touch with the experts at Virtina and we’ll help you figure out the best architecture for your business model. Our eCommerce developers can also develop headless Commerce for your eCommerce store. We can help you to figure out which architecture works the best for your business model. title: eCommerce ADA Compliance in 2026: What Store Owners Need to Know (Checklist Included)
headings: Why are online stores being sued over accessibility?
What does the ADA require from an online store?
What about the new DOJ rule?
Should you follow WCAG 2.1 or WCAG 2.2?
Do you need to comply if you sell to Europe?
Can an accessibility widget make your store compliant?
How do you audit your store for accessibility?
Is my online store legally required to be ADA compliant?
Does a small store need to worry?
Does accessibility help SEO and sales?
text: Summary If you sell online in the US, website accessibility is no longer a nice-to-have. More than 5,000 digital accessibility lawsuits were filed in 2025, and nearly 70% of them targeted eCommerce stores. Most of those stores were not big brands. There is still no official ADA rule for private websites, but courts expect WCAG 2.1 or 2.2 Level AA. Overlays and widgets do not get you there. A proper audit and fix plan does, and it tends to lift conversions too. Introduction More than 1 in 4 US adults, over 70 million people, report having a disability, according to the CDC . That includes people who are blind or have low vision, people who cannot use a mouse, people who are deaf or hard of hearing, and people with cognitive or learning disabilities. Many of them shop online every day using screen readers, keyboards, voice control or zoom. When a product image has no description, a size selector cannot be reached by keyboard, or a checkout error is shown only in red, they cannot buy. They leave, and some of them sue. This guide explains what the law expects from an online store in 2026, which standard to follow, and what to fix first, with a practical checklist. Table of Contents Why are online stores being sued over accessibility? What does the ADA require from an online store? Should you follow WCAG 2.1 or WCAG 2.2? Do you need to comply if you sell to Europe? Can an accessibility widget make your store compliant? The 2026 eCommerce accessibility checklist How do you audit your store for accessibility? Why are online stores being sued over accessibility? Because the numbers make it a steady business for plaintiffs’ firms. The 2025 lawsuit data shows where the risk sits: More than 5,000 digital accessibility lawsuits were filed in 2025 eCommerce accounted for nearly 70% of ADA website lawsuits 64% of defendants had annual revenue under $25 million 1,427 lawsuits targeted companies that had already been sued before New York, Florida and California see the most filings Being small does not keep you off the radar, and settling once does not end the risk if the site stays inaccessible. What does the ADA require from an online store? Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act bans discrimination by “places of public accommodation”. The law was written in 1990, before online shopping existed, so it never mentions websites. Courts have filled the gap. Most now treat an online store as covered, especially when it is connected to a physical business. In 2019 the US Supreme Court declined to hear Domino’s appeal of a Ninth Circuit ruling that its website and app had to be accessible. The Department of Justice has never published a technical rule for private business websites, and its Title III rulemaking is now paused. In practice, plaintiffs, judges and settlements all point to the same benchmark: the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) at Level AA. What about the new DOJ rule? In 2024 the DOJ issued a rule under Title II of the ADA requiring WCAG 2.1 AA. It covers state and local government websites, not private stores, and its deadlines were extended in April 2026 to April 2027 for large entities and April 2028 for smaller ones. It still matters to you, because it confirms WCAG 2.1 AA as the standard regulators expect. Should you follow WCAG 2.1 or WCAG 2.2? Follow WCAG 2.2 Level AA. It includes everything in 2.1, so meeting it covers both. WCAG is built on four principles: content must be perceivable, operable, understandable and robust enough to work with assistive technology. WCAG 2.1 AA . The level most lawsuits, settlements and government rules reference today. WCAG 2.2 AA . Published in October 2023, it adds nine new criteria. Several matter for stores, such as larger tap targets, keyboard focus that is not hidden by sticky headers, and logins that do not rely on memory puzzles. Do you need to comply if you sell to Europe? Yes, if you sell to consumers in the EU. The European Accessibility Act (EAA) has applied since June 28, 2025. It covers eCommerce services offered to consumers in the EU, wherever the seller is based. Microenterprises with fewer than 10 employees and under EUR 2 million in turnover are exempt from most requirements. The practical standard is WCAG 2.1 AA, with WCAG 2.2 AA the safer target. If you ship to the EU, a US-only view of compliance is not enough. Can an accessibility widget make your store compliant? No. Overlays and one-line plugins promise instant compliance, but they do not deliver it. In 2025 the Federal Trade Commission ordered overlay vendor accessiBe to pay $1 million for claiming its AI tool could make any website WCAG compliant. Lawsuits against stores that use these widgets continued throughout 2025, often more than 100 a month. A widget can be a helpful extra. It cannot fix missing alt text, broken keyboard navigation or an inaccessible checkout. Those need to be fixed in the theme and code. The 2026 eCommerce accessibility checklist This checklist is organised by the parts of a store where lawsuits usually start, not by WCAG rule numbers. Navigation and keyboard access Every menu, filter, button and link works with the keyboard alone (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys) A visible focus outline shows where the user is, and it is never hidden behind a sticky header or chat widget (WCAG 2.2) A “Skip to main content” link appears first on every page Mega menus and dropdowns open and close by keyboard, and Escape closes them Product images and media Every product image has alt text that describes the product, such as colour, style and key detail, not the file name Decorative images have empty alt text so screen readers skip them Product videos have captions, and videos with important visual information have a transcript or audio description Nothing auto-plays sound, and carousels can be paused Product pages Size, colour and variant selectors are real form controls with labels, not coloured boxes with no name Price, stock status and sale price are read out correctly by screen readers “Add to cart” confirms the action in a way screen readers announce Size charts and zoomable images work without a mouse Cart, checkout and account Every form field has a visible label, not just placeholder text Required fields say “required” in text, not only with an asterisk or colour Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, next to the field, and are announced to screen readers Customers are not asked to re-enter information they already gave in the same checkout (WCAG 2.2) Login does not rely on puzzles or memorising codes, and allows password managers and paste (WCAG 2.2) Payment, shipping and coupon steps work end to end by keyboard and with a screen reader Colour, text and layout Text contrast is at least 4.5:1, and 3:1 for large text, buttons and form borders Colour is never the only signal, for example for sale prices, errors or stock status Pages still work when zoomed to 200% and on narrow screens without sideways scrolling Tap targets are at least 24 by 24 pixels, or spaced so they are easy to hit (WCAG 2.2) Structure and content One H1 per page, and headings follow a logical order Links say where they go (“View shipping policy”, not “Click here”) Tables such as size charts use proper header cells The page language is set, so screen readers pronounce content correctly Pop-ups and third-party tools Newsletter pop-ups, cookie banners and modals can be closed by keyboard, and focus returns to where the user was Review widgets, chat tools, payment fields and embedded maps are tested too. You are responsible for them on your site PDFs such as catalogues and size guides are accessible, or the same content is available as a web page Policy and ongoing checks Publish an accessibility statement with a way to report problems Re-test after every theme update, plugin install or redesign Keep a record of audits and fixes. It shows good faith if a demand letter arrives How do you audit your store for accessibility? A useful audit combines three kinds of testing: 1. Automated scan . Tools like WAVE, axe or Lighthouse catch missing alt text, contrast failures and missing labels quickly. They find roughly a third of real issues, so they are a starting point, not a verdict. 2. Manual keyboard and screen reader testing . Someone walks through the real buying journey, from home page to order confirmation, using only a keyboard and then NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver. This is where checkout and variant problems show up. 3. A prioritised fix plan . Issues are ranked by how badly they block a purchase, fixed in the theme, templates and plugins, then re-tested. Our ADA and WCAG accessibility audit covers all three, and our engineers fix what we find in your code. Start with the pages that make money: product pages, cart and checkout. A redesign is also the cheapest time to get accessibility right, because building it into a new theme costs far less than retrofitting later. See our eCommerce website redesign services if you are planning one. People also ask Is my online store legally required to be ADA compliant? The ADA does not name websites, but most US courts treat online stores as covered, and thousands of stores are sued every year. Following WCAG 2.1 or 2.2 AA is the accepted way to reduce that risk. Does a small store need to worry? Yes. In 2025, 64% of defendants had revenue under $25 million. Plaintiffs’ firms often target smaller stores because they are less likely to have been audited. Does accessibility help SEO and sales? Usually, yes. Clear headings, descriptive alt text, readable contrast and simple forms help search engines and every shopper, not only people using assistive technology. Conclusion Accessibility is now a basic requirement for selling online. The legal risk is real, especially for small and mid-sized stores, and the fix is not a widget. It is a store built and tested so that everyone can find a product, choose a size and check out. Accessible stores are usually better stores. Clear labels, readable contrast, simple forms and fast keyboard paths help every shopper, and they tend to lift conversions and search visibility along the way. If you are not sure where your store stands, get an ADA and WCAG accessibility audit from Virtina . We audit WooCommerce, Shopify, BigCommerce and Magento stores against WCAG 2.2 AA and fix what we find in the code, not with an overlay. Frequently Asked Questions Which version of WCAG should my store follow? Aim for WCAG 2.2 Level AA. It includes all of WCAG 2.1 AA, which is what most lawsuits and regulations reference today. Will an accessibility plugin or overlay make my site compliant? No. Overlays cannot fix problems in your theme and code, and stores using them are still sued. The FTC fined one overlay vendor $1 million in 2025 for claiming otherwise. Does the European Accessibility Act apply to US stores? Yes, if you sell to consumers in the EU. It applies to eCommerce services offered in the EU wherever the business is based, unless you qualify as a microenterprise. How often should I check my store for accessibility? Run a full audit at least once a year, and re-test key pages after any theme update, new plugin or redesign. Is this article legal advice? No. It is general information about accessibility requirements. Speak to a qualified lawyer about your specific situation.

title: Why Choose Magento For Your Ecommerce Website
text: Arriving at an eCommerce platform is always a major annoyance for any brand, with a plethora of options sitting out there, even an exhausting brainstorming session, is not enough to select the one, that best suits all your business requirements.Amidst this confusion a name that pops up often is Magento – widely regarded as a giant and the top choice for many brands when it comes to eCommerce platforms.Its availability as an open source and commerce edition makes it easy for businesses to either opt for the one that is free and easily modifiable or go for the premium one that comes pre-packed with all the advanced functionalities.However, both these editions have one thing in common, that is their source code can be customized easily by any developer to suit your business, which makes this selection flexible.But, why is it that merchants worldwide are leaning towards Magento, is it the robust platform backed by an expert community or is just clever marketing by the brand to showcase itself as the most reliable option for any upcoming or established company.In this blog, we’ll skim through some of the top reasons why Magento is featured continuously in industry trends, with the largest market share and is believed to run more than 250,000 stores online. What sets it apart from the rivals and what features help Magento dominate the space, even a decade later.Here’s listing the top reasons why any seller on cyberspace, should get in touch with a Magento development company and consider migrating or setting up their stores on Magento: Open Source The principal advantage of running an open source platform is it’s free and can be easily managed and developed by anyone around the world. Invest as much as you need and vary the support as per the size of your business.You get complete control over the design and functionality of the site, relying on a community of notable developers and web commerce experts that have been playing this field for a very long time, and can prove to be the guide you need. Get the top info on any Magento development services here.Install and create the plug-ins you need to run your store. Now you don’t need to depend on those heavy-duty webstore extensions; create the one that syncs perfectly to your webshop.A unique identity of Magento that separates it from the competition is the numerous customizations allowed on your shopping cart. Performance Magento website can easily handle your store requirements regardless of the nature of your business and alongside that gives the option to add numerous items to a single import. Its catalog management features include multiple categories and dynamic product attributes.It stays stable even when handling huge transaction volumes. Even with a diverse range of businesses, it remains steady. Which then implies that Magento’s performance is unaffected even when handling heavy traffic during peak times.The Commerce Edition of Magento offers full page caching, thereby helping the page load times significantly. Besides this, it includes features to optimize and automate indexing tasks thus elevating the overall performance of your store. Scalability Large business or a small start-up, there is potential for every kind of company in Magento; due to the flexibility of Magento, it quickly adapts to your store’s requirements.Whatever is the nature of your business, once your store is up and running, you can at any time scale the store with some simple back-end work.More extensive business won’t have any issues coping with a higher inventory of 1000+ products. Common issues that they face is slow site speeds and periodic crashes, something that can be easily neutralized in Magento.If that is not enough the access to Magento marketplace gives you enough extensions to scale your site and expand further. Reducing the response time, improving the product checkout time, catalog browsing, and the addition of new features have helped stores on Magento to boost their productivity.Enhancements that will always deliver the best performance for your site, to ensure you can accelerate and future proof your eCommerce business. Community Support Magento has huge online support in an ever-growing community of professionals who contribute selflessly to discussion boards; which is something that stands out as a significant plus for this platform compared to all the other portals that sit out there.The 24/7 availability of astute eCommerce developers, contributors, and innovators in this community, puts any rookie merchant in a perfect space to initiate any project or further enhance the current one.Discuss, consult, give feedback, enquire and solve all your Magento worries. Tips, tricks, and support is what this is all about. All this is creating a network of enthusiasts sharing and coming together for a common cause on how to better their Magento webshop.A sole purpose to help other developers share ideas, discuss updates and help one another solve technical and support issues. Manageable Magento lets you manage multiple stores from one admin panel, using a single magneto installation you can manage your store’s billing, mass product updates, inventory, customer records, etc. which saves you a lot of time and effort when it comes to online sales.You can easily capture the customers buying journey and even coordinate with them during the process; this enables the possibility of delivering a more bespoke experience to the customer.It also comes with plenty of currency features, multiple languages, international support; especially in Magento Commerce Edition by virtue of being the premium version.Thus, you get the advantage of full support from the Magento team and customer service, then there are the shipping and order management functionalities.Besides this, the store owners get a full set of extensions, making it even easier to optimize the store and make it more robust and if that’s not enough your Magento Store is also mobile friendly, every magneto store now supports responsive design by default.Customers can easily access their site from any device, thus, utilizing mobile commerce will no longer be an issue for any merchant; since you get the finest viewing across all devices with ease. Extensions The vast number of extensions that are available on the Magento marketplace simplify the store experience for any merchant, providing the services that you will need to connect better with your audience.Improve the eCommerce solutions and your online presence with numerous extensions that make tasks like accounting, logistics, payment, inventory and search features; more seamless. Run any of these in the back end and witness the load on your developers come down.The ability to easily integrate your store with any number of extensions, 3rd Party applications in Facebook, eBay, PayPal, Quickbook , WordPress and so much more to optimize your store is what makes Magento vastly superior to any other platform. Advanced SEO Gaining traffic for any online company is essential to their survival, and these days the search engine is one of the most effective ways to achieve the best returns on your massive investments. Drawing online traffic or support marketing strategies to your site will not be a cumbersome task.Magento is equipped with powerful tools that make the SEO job easy. These built-in SEO features allow your online store to be indexed in a manner that will boost the incoming traffic to your site.Within Magento, you will access prime tools that let you automatically create URL’s, tags and descriptions with relevant keywords; something that will help to drive inbound traffic. If that was not enough, within Magento, you have access to tools to boost conversions too. Security A breach of security on your store is a common occurrence, where someone attempts to slide into your admin panel, leaving your entire inventory vulnerable and this could jeopardize your business.Now, with two-factor authentication in place, the overall threat to your store has been suppressed by a great deal. Any random entry would need verification before committing any changes, which secures your site. Fast WAF and DDoS Services give the additional security blanket to prevent any attack.The payment concerns that emerge can be easily circumvented since Magento Commerce comes with Payment Application Data Security Standard, secured payment bridges and credit card tokenization which makes this edition more reliable.Implementing SSL security and a dedicated IP can also be easily achieved on Magento. Websites running on Magento are quite safe; thus, data infringement from an outside source will not be a concern. Modular Architecture The PHP framework of Magento allows any business to thrive, which means that the platform can complement your company regardless of what you sell.Instead of running on a large application, Magento is supported by small modules that give it the vital fuel with a specific set of functionalities, which allows the ability to enable and disable one of the modules at will.Configure any of the modules to target a specific area, this way you create a unique code which will help to extend some functionality without interfering with the core code. This helps to customize the store to suit your business ethics.So, in Magento what you get is a PHP framework that converts to form a full-fledged, fully functional and dynamic eCommerce web shopping cart. The modular elements of this platform enable you to retain the robust back end while altering the front-end to give users the best experience . Hosting Unlike Volusion and Shopify, the hosting of your business will not be a concern on Magento. Select the hosting solution of your choice, opt for an economic one or go with a premium package with full 24/7 customer support.The ability to pick one that suits your requirements or the one that suits your budget is what places Magento above all its rivals. Besides this, it also supports an effortless transition to any other hosting service.With some fully hosted eCommerce platforms where you get locked to the platform and in case of a switch find yourself going through the ordeal of transferring your entire database to another website; which is not the case with Magento.When it is time to migrate your store, there are no restrictions on where you could host your store.So, there you have it folks; hire an expert Magento Developer or entrust the astute minds sitting at Virtina to render a custom Magento platform for your company. title: Ecommerce : Why User Experience Matters and How to Do it Right
headings: How do you go about it?
text: Customers aren’t a transitional trend that fluctuates every season; they are omnipresent. However, despite that presence, their willingness to visit your site is dependent on an indispensable, integral element and that is user experience. If you can deliver the same, then you stand to acquire more customers with ease, at the same time retaining the previous group, leading to a set of loyal repeat clique.In the absence of such a streamlined interface, visitors look for other outlets that offer the same product, resulting in your competition eating into your sales. Here’s a quote from the man who started it all. “Focusing on the customer makes the company more resilient” – Jeff Bezos Stay intact on this principle, and your webshop with absolute certainty will receive the highest  organic traffic , that then converts into orders. Revenue will now soar above and beyond your expectations.Customer loyalty is based out of experiences they share with a certain brand; thus, an investment in the same will increase customer lifetime value. A wrong turn and your reputation could dwindle.In the age of people populating the internet, any downside to a site will spread soon and cause further damage, with the added challenge of your competitors innovating constantly. Sometimes lowering the rates just doesn’t cut it.In this piece, we’ll run through some of the factors that make or break customer experiences for any brand. Stay intact on this principle, and your webshop with absolute certainty will receive the highest organic traffic , that then converts into orders. Revenue will now soar above and beyond your expectations.Customer loyalty is based out of experiences they share with a certain brand; thus, an investment in the same will increase customer lifetime value. A wrong turn and your reputation could dwindle.In the age of people populating the internet, any downside to a site will spread soon and cause further damage, with the added challenge of your competitors innovating constantly. Sometimes lowering the rates just doesn’t cut it.In this piece, we’ll run through some of the factors that make or break customer experiences for any brand. Why does it matter? Regardless of your business model, you are at the end of the day dealing with people, hence whatever is your agenda try and make this your fundamental point.When customers seek a specific commodity, they don’t just look for discounts and bundled deals; it’s not always savings. Your ability to help them arrive at the desired item sooner will also be determinantal in their decision-making process.Your brand should be set around your customer’s priorities and not around your business goals. A move that will see an outcome that favors the customer and in turn favors you.Customers must form the backbone of your company from the get-go. Focus on their needs, and you will have the lead in your field in no time.You are relying on them to generate profits, then why not customize the site to their liking. Let their preferences shape your business. Once you allow this, the customer satisfaction will grow, and they will likely be back for more.Besides word of mouth and further free endorsements you’ll receive on the back end, without spending a dollar from your side. Stick to this model for continued benefits. A deviation from the same could result in customers investing in alternatives, resulting in the viewership dwindling, and no visitors means no orders.Take your time and devise a plan that draws the maximum crowd. Of course, shipping times, discounts, availability and a whole bunch of other variables will become a contributing factor, but at least from your side, you have addressed the prime issue of scaling the site to your customer’s liking. How do you go about it? Connect with your customers through all the available touch points and then deliver the brand experience they desire. Emphasize a more personalized shopping experience.Gain valuable insights that will help you to retrieve what your user-base is thinking at any given moment. Since you are about to outline the e-business around your customers, it’s vital that you use a channel to collect that info.What your demographic wants, how do they want it, when do they want it more, are just some of the questions you’ll need to address to get an understanding of your customer’s desires.Accessibility is of prime importance these days. If they can reach out to you and express their concerns, a significant portion of the work is handled.Retailers and brands are no longer just a source of shopping; they are engaging with their consumers through their purchase journeys. The focus has shifted to building customer relationships.Let them come to you. Listen to what customers have to say and implement the same accordingly. One of these days, a suggestion will prove to be the biggest breakthrough for your business.Let’s look at some of the ways in which you can boost your site via customer opinions: Social Media – Activity on social media plays a crucial role. Giving a forum to voice their opinions will help you to make adequate changes sooner, before your peers, and as it is half of the world exists on it. So, go ahead and interact with your Facebook and Twitter audience. Surveys – Get out there and conduct periodic surveys to assess the ground game. It may be online, or just a more casual one on one chat on the road, that’ll help you to decipher your audience even better. Chatbots – A communication tool, that will instantly resolve any customer query in one shot. Incorporate this into your website. If done correctly any grievance, doubt or feedback can be raised in a matter of seconds. What all could be done? When it comes to improving user experience , there are a lot many things that you can implement. Some of these integrations are important and can’t be compromised, regardless of the nature of your business.Use of certain elements will gain your customer’s trust, and anything along these lines will tempt them to place an order; furthering your sales objective. A negative impression can send things downhill.The way you interact with your audience is what dictates customer experience; this could be direct communication via messages or through the vast set of features on your site. They all give out some impression about your brand.Here are some of the things you can do lift the quality of your website: Images – Relevant product images of suitable sizes are an absolute must in every eCommerce website. Consumers do not get to touch any item; therefore, the need to reinforce the credibility of every product is even more. Detailed supportive high-resolution images will serve this purpose and give every visitor an additional reference point they need, to examine the product. Videos – Images are good, but an even better way of presenting a product is Videos. Use them to demonstrate the worth of anything in your catalog effectively. Testimonials – Let your customers leave feedback, a compliment will reassure your growth and criticism will cause you to introspect and look beyond the pre-existing model and redefine your site. AI / AU – The future of eCommerce will be made of this. Give your visitors the store experience, and another step closer to your products capability. The option to view this product in their surrounding will see them preferring your store for most purchases. A/B Testing – Test multiple versions to know which one compliments your business the best. A comprehensive analysis done with numbers, heat maps to track clicks, session times, visitor tracking and other such useful statistics to arrive at the best converting version. Layout – Create a platform that allows visitors to navigate without any hassle. Do not overcrowd any section, keep promotions minimum, avoid unwanted pop-ups and overuse of jargon. Use essential info and improve overall usability and visual appeal. Loading – The inclusion of numerous elements will often slow the website down . Prevent this from happening by regularly testing the site. Even a lag of 2 secs will make a customer consider other options. Security – If you are at any point dealing in confidential information, then investing in a premium software, would do you some good. Reckless coding and absence of essential tools will compromise sensitive customer data, a situation that is an instant kill for any business. Compatibility – Multiple touchpoints ( Omnichannel ) means your site should be optimized to each of them. Any anomaly will immediately send a negative impression, enough to make your customers look elsewhere. Ensure your website is synced to all devices. Content – Find a way to feature this in any form – Blogs, Case Studies, White Papers or some thesis to certify the work done so far. A little self-endorsement on your site goes a long way and gives the visitors an opportunity to familiarize themselves with your brand even better. Transparency – If there is anything that ruins a business more than the lack of funds, then it is false advertisement. Stay true to your core skillset and only mention marvels you can solve. Be honest about your infrastructure; this will help to build better customer sentiments. Effects A satisfied customer will be more inclined to come again, but this time he might bring with him more people, his network of acquaintances.How did this happen, all he did was pass the positive vibes from your site to his immediate peers, and this drew them to the site; leading to additional revenue for your business.Free marketing from customers is what businesses thrive on, you give them the best experience, and they will sort your promotions with word of mouth.Customers leave a profound impact on your business; hence it is paramount that we set the standards around them. Measure your performance consistently, to see if you are on the right track. Conclusion Create a compelling experience like none other. Cultivate that sense of belonging, every time a prospect arrives on your site.Remember, to take initiatives from your end to remodel the site now and then. Do not wait for a lousy experience to realize the need for changes.Conduct regular testing at the back end, which would immediately raise red flags from the developers, something that’d help you to identify the problem areas ASAP, from your side and get to work on them. Monitor 24×7 and ensure a critical scenario doesn’t arise ever.Understand your customer’s pain points, make an honest effort to resolve them. A lot of these concerns can be easily managed via some instant chat up.Focusing on customer experience will help you to improve the business KPI’s. High Bounce rates and dismal conversions will be a thing of the past, once you make the customer experience epicenter of your business plans.Win your customers at every front. Once you have sorted many of the issues and created an interface that promotes perfect harmony with your customers, it’ll see the best form of customers retention. The companies that excel in enhancing customer experience will last the test of times. Stay open to making changes, from customer suggestions. Magento Open Source Vs Magento Commerce: How To Decide?
text: Magento, by virtue of being the most popular, easy to install, open-source platform, powers one in every four e-commerce stores. But one of the biggest dilemma’s retailers face is when opting between Magento Open Source Edition (Magento Community Edition) and Magento Commerce Edition (Magento Enterprise Edition).Here we are trying to make your job a lot easier by listing out why you should choose each edition. We are going to summarize the differences and similarities between the two and the pros and cons of each edition so that you can effortlessly arrive at a conclusion. Magento Open Source Edition This edition of Magento platform is open-source and freely available to download. Since it is open-source, it has higher levels of customization and is apt for small-scale businesses not requiring huge investments. It is easy to customize as per whim, has a full-page cache solution and is suitable for a startup store. In addition, anyone can utilize the Magento Extension Marketplace to enhance the site’s functionality and expand their store. Magento Commerce Edition This Magento edition is premium and is a paid platform. It has an array of inbuilt customization and advanced features which makes it the best choice for leading enterprises. The edition gives its customers the added advantage of the Magento team support and customer service through mail and phone. The package comes with exclusive product enhancements, security updates, and unique features. Similarities These two major Magento editions are alike in quite a few features.Some of the salient common features are: Both are open-sourced Both are part of the Magento ecosystem They have the same core features Have access to Magento Connect – the Magento Extension Marketplace Supports use of web server’s API to incorporate with various databases Differences The significant differences between the two editions pertaining to the key features are : 1.Pricing Magento Open Source is free of cost with a free download option. With Magento Commerce, you need to pay for the advanced features as well as for implementation. The price will be about $22,000 per year for around 1 Million revenue.  2. Security Features Magento open-source is not PCI compliant and does not feature some of the major security features like credit card tokenization or highly secured payment bridges. But the more transactions you do overtime, you would be able to circumvent the PCI compliance issue.On the contrary, Magento Commerce has extra security via PA-DSS (Payment Application Data Security Standard), which makes the edition more payment reliable. 3. Performance Magento Open Source edition is fast, but when used for businesses requiring more modules, it won’t suffice. Addition of  Magento extensions to enhance features is possible, but it is generally not recommended by experts. Meanwhile, Magento Commerce performs better when it comes to high-end functionality businesses. 4. Functionality Both the editions have the same core.Magento Open Source has all the base features required to start a brand new Magento store.It has all the required essential features like: Integrated Checkout, Payment, and Shipping – Added payment sources for greater flexibility Mobile Optimized Shopping – Optimal viewing across an array of devices Global Selling – Transactions possible in multiple countries, currencies, using worldwide shipping providers Catalog Management – Creation of rich content across various products: simple, configurable, bundled, and customized Extended Functionality via App Marketplace – Possible to add capabilities and connectors using the Magento Extensions Marketplace for a nominal fee Instant Purchase – Presenting customers with a faster checkout Site Search – Aided by Elasticsearch, which delivers high-quality search results that help augment conversion rates Magento Enterprise would suit those businesses needing additional functionalities, as it comes packaged with multiple useful features in addition to the above Open Source edition features, such as: Account Manager – Dedicated account manager to oversee overall relationships Technical Support – 24/7 technical support with an actual person Access to Quick Design-Build Express Packages – Express packages offered by Certified Magento Partners, offer quick-launch, low-cost implementation solutions for start-up enterprises. Customer Loyalty System – Built-in tools for enabling reward points, gift registries, wish lists, and exclusive private sales events. Content Staging, Merging and Preview – Create, schedule, and review site changes faster and more accurately with built-in staging and preview features. Business Intelligence Dashboards – Analyze customer buying trends with advanced reporting tools and over 100 ready-to-use reports. Integrated B2B Functionality – Advanced B2B capabilities like quoting, custom catalogs, and company accounts. Advanced Marketing Tools – Create custom promotions and merchandising tactics for customer groups. WYSIWYG Page Builder – Includes a built-in enhanced content management system (CMS) with a drag and drop interface. Visual Merchandising – Enables merchants to organize products on catalog pages dramatically faster and easier. Sort by most popular sales items and more with a single click of the mouse. Optimized Cloud Commerce for Magento – A cloud environment that is optimized for Magento, so there is one less thing to manage when rolling out a new online store. Global Availability- Easily deploy shopping sites across the globe. Cloud availability SLA up to 99.99% – SLA covers availability of servers and supporting services. Fast Page Loading with Content Delivery Network (CDN) – Content Delivery Network (CDN) is always-on and ready to handle any traffic during peak times (including Black Friday and Christmas). Faster page loading performance for users, enabling increased sales conversion rates , SEO, and a reduced website bounce rate. Performance Monitoring Tools – Get real-time data about your site’s performance with application performance monitoring (APM) . Enhanced Security with Fast WAF and DDoS Services – Protects the store with advanced security. PCI Compliant – A security standard intended to ensure that the sellers can securely accept, store, process and transmit a customer’s card details, which in turn prevents frauds, guarantees trust, leading to sales and improved conversions. Easy Deployment – Get to market faster with pre-integrated Magento cloud services. Streamlined Updates and Testing – Immediately benefit from continuous infrastructure upgrades, performance enhancements, and patches. There are some more additional out-of-the-box features, namely: Advanced ACL Private sales, events and invitations Customer segmentation Advanced segmentation with targeted offerings CMS+ Automated email marketing reminders Assisted shopping Full page caching Recurring payments Customer attributes SOLR search RMA functionality Persistent shopping cart Minimum advertised price Return management authorization Price and promotion permission Enhanced catalog and content management system Call center software with assisted shopping Staged merging and rollback of content Version control Content hierarchy Banners Publication restrictions 5. Magento Support Magento Open Source edition is quite easy to install and operate and hence does not require a round-the-clock support team. In case you need to customize your platform, you can hire an external expert agency to perform the task for you.Magento Commerce, by virtue of being a premium edition, has the added advantage of full support from the Magento team and customer service.Our Recommendations on Both the EditionsOpen Source edition is loaded with all the essential features required for a standard to mid-range start-up business. The highlight is that the edition is free and can be downloaded even by a layman. It would be more than enough to handle small to medium business transaction volumes. Hence, if you intend to find an economical, decent performing, feature-rich shopping cart solution , this edition would be your best practical choice. It is light on the wallet if you are not keen on making a substantial initial investment on platforms.The Enterprise edition is a premium edition from Magento. It is an extremely powerful, fast performing tool, laden with a plethora of features which can competently support higher segment of businesses. If your business deals with a 6-figure revenue and you are looking for a platform which can take your e-commerce store to the next level, Magento Enterprise edition is the first choice you should go for owing to its increased scalability and functionality.There are multiple differences between the two platforms. But if you ask us, when it comes to customer engagement, data security and performance, Magento Enterprise Edition seems to have the upper hand. Summary You need to take into consideration the plans for your business as well as prospective business growth projections and business goals while you make the final platform choice. You can weigh in the costing and benefits to your brand during the selection process. Still confused, on which edition to choose for your business expansion?. Talk to Us (888) 478-4799

title: Sales Tax Extensions For Volusion Store
text: Taxes are misery for the one collecting as much as it is for the one paying. The constant overhauling makes it challenging to keep track of changes. New regulations are framed every week, keeping in mind a nations overall economic state. The repercussions are always on this small component that then fluctuates so much that it becomes difficult on the average eCommerce guy to monitor the daily updates. Plus, these are inescapable, if you are making money you are due on taxes at some point. As the saying goes “Two things in life are certain: Death and Taxes.” Institutions earn a good amount of money and as such become susceptible to these deductions. Also, the framework that governs major businesses is far more complex than what a civilian must deal with. Ecommerce Tax Ecommerce had acquired its own distinct identity as soon as it gained momentum in the early nineties, as such at some point this domain was heading towards its own specific tax laws, that’d govern it in years to come. Ecommerce tax is a certain percentage that is fixed to be deducted from the final order before the shipping charges are applied. During the payment process, you’d often come across this element. Once the payment is sorted, the entire sales tax is forwarded to the state governments tax coffer. What complicates the matter even further, some of these states don’t settle for a common tax, therefore as per the new reforms every state is entitled to a little cut, regardless of whether you are based in that state or not. Quill Law In 1992, Quill Corp vs. North Dakota ruling prevented any state from collecting sales tax on any retail purchase, if the business in question did not have a physical presence in the concerned state. The whole litigation was initiated by North Dakota who wished to avail a certain amount from Quill Corporation that by then had established itself as a major seller of licensed computer software and stationary. Despite not having a presence in North Dakota and being a Delaware based company, it could sell to anyone in the state and not incur any state taxes. Quill conducted any marketing via pamphlets, brochures and national periodicals, and as such was considered to not have a nexus, the outcome therefore was ruled in favor of Quill. If the ruling had favored State of North Dakota, Quill would have to pay up back taxes from the last three years. Meanwhile, the brick and mortar stores continued to pay taxes , for every state where they had a physical presence. Which then led to a strong resentment as it found the unfair advantage bestowed on eCommerce merchants to be unethical and a drawback for them. Kill Quill Initiated in the late nineties, was a collective effort from all the states to extract tax from sellers, conducting business with the residents of that state. Wayfair along with Overstock.com , Newegg , and Systemax were challenged by South Dakota in 2016. Systemax obliged, Wayfair protested, which by then had established itself as the seller of domestic goods. A South Dakota vs Wayfair hearing was ruled in favor of South Dakota. States are now free to pursue sales tax from businesses. Everything changed on June 22nd, 2018. All the 46 States that had suffered heavily (lost nearly $13 billion), up until then, realized the biggest relief when the Supreme Court overturned the Quill law, considering the previous judgement of 1992 to be “unsound and incorrect”. Now, eCommerce businesses regardless of where they originate will have to cough up state tax, if they are currently trading in that state. Also, as per the recent change if your revenue in any state exceeds $100,000 or 200 transactions then you’d be considered to have a Nexus , known as “Economic Nexus” and you will become eligible to pay taxes. This is called the economic threshold of that state. The new tax law applies to every merchant who has an online eCommerce store, whether it’s through a privately-owned website or through a third-party vendor such as Amazon. If you surpass a state’s economic threshold for total revenue or the total number of orders, you are required to register, collect and remit sales tax henceforth. You could be selling on Amazon Marketplace and still find yourself paying the income tax for the state where your customers are based. Deduct the same from the buyers and remit it to the respective state. title: Why Conversion Rate Optimization is Vital for eCommerce Success
headings: How do you go about it?
text: New tools emerged in the market in the first half of the last decade that enabled internet marketers to experiment with their website layout and content variations to determine which design, text, template, offers, or images work the best. This sort of optimization accelerated further in the latter half with the introduction of Google Website Optimizer. Sit back and read on, as we take you in the most awe-inspiring journey of leads to subscribers to sales. The process by which a business increases the percentage of website visitors who convert on available offers. Turn the guest visitors into loyal buyers. The small changes made will now translate to major conversions, furthering more revenue. What is Conversion Rate? The KPI that evaluates the performance of your site and the percentage of users that visited the website and did something productive that benefited your business. The conversion rate can also be defined as the percentage of visitors who complete a goal, as set by the site owner. It’s all about keeping those visitors, getting them to click on more pages and eventually make the conversion. If website sales or lead generation activities don’t provide a healthy ROI, your business is doomed. Across multiple platforms, varied demographics, segmented or product wise. Whichever is your reference point to draw an in-depth inference of your customer pattern, it should all culminate into one thing, and that is to help you to penetrate your customer’s mindset better. The conversion rate can become user segmented , such as device, demographic, location, new vs. returning visitor and so on, which in turn may give the wrong impression and any changes made from that, will result in an uneven outcome — a scenario that will likely see more damage done. Hence its vital to know that any variations made will differ, as we move from one reference point to another. Conversion Rate Optimization CRO is a data-driven discipline to revamp your website and make it more appealing to your visitors. Test and analyze user behavior, understand lead generation patterns, streamline paths to conversion. Dive in, research, analyze, and apply the findings to a material effort that gets you real results. CRO provides a useful benchmark and prompts the retailers that it is helpful to measure product page views when making design improvements. Deploy testing mechanisms either in real time or after studying your audience in detail. Either way, the approach, is to proceed after scrutinizing the ecommerce market. So, pretest and then go ahead or test simultaneously to see which way the traffic is more likely to improve. Producing more revenue from the existing website traffic is the sole agenda. Every ecommerce leader deserves a clear path to drive that maximum revenue from their current marketing efforts. CRO steers you in the right lane, does the appropriate audit, plans and equips you with the tools to help you perform better.Study visitor behaviors and create a model that reflects that. A precise understanding of every minuscule facet of your websites dynamics to set a plan that will yield the highest returns. Study all the key metrics that prevent conversion and make incremental changes that help to boost the visitor to buyer ratio and in turn the sales of your company. The right strategy can give you a colossal edge in the market, which then helps you to excel.In summary, CRO is a robust framework that is based on metrics, data, and testing; designed to systematically , incrementally, and consistently improve marketing results. It’s data-driven all the time, and when done right, it always builds exponentially, generating a high ROI. An important measure of CRO is to ensure that no content is wasted and pretty much every visual holds the right amount of credibility, to tempt the visitor into spending more time. An immersive experience like that will shake the rust and put the zing back on your website. Types Micro- conversions are the one in which only a percentage of your preset goal is fulfilled. It moves the visitor nearer to target but is yet to translate into a full-fledged order. A newsletter, subscription emails, basic registrations, watched a tutorial video, followed you on social media and showing a moderate leaning towards the products offered. Maybe even willing to spend more time on the site compared to other transient visitors. Macro-conversions are the more concrete changes that will benefit you in the long run. The biggies that will check an offer and check out, instead of free roaming the site and then exiting. They might buy a product, subscribe to the services, or fill out a lead form. These are the ones you want to study, invest and grab at all costs. The way they maneuver the site may help you to penetrate the psyche of every spending consumer and then just set your website around that. Tell whatever is pivotal to your brand, this is the data that is not disposable, and regardless of how you design your site, this would surely have to be featured somewhere.
