title: 18 Common Magento Mistakes Agencies Make
text: Magento is one of the world’s most renowned shopping cart solution with an overall 26% e-commerce market monopoly. It powers more than 1,50,000 Magento stores across businesses and is a clear winner when it comes to e-commerce platforms. And countless Magento development agencies are working on the platform armed with highly proficient teams of Magento developers and Magento experts. They are adept at Magento development, designing and customization services. But all these are performed by humans. That means even if you engage Magento certified developers to do your job, there is always a chance of human errors or process mistakes. Most times these mistakes cost you severely. For example, it can compare to your buying a Formula One car with the dream of participating in the prestigious Formula One racing events. And you customize it with the cheapest of accessories available. How will that look and feel? That is how badly your simple mistakes can affect your e-commerce store and business. Let us delve into some of these common mistakes made and tips on how to improve/prevent them from happening to you or your clientele: I. Common Mistakes from the Front-End (Developers and Designers): 1. Problem: Modifying Core Magento Themes is generally not recommended by experts. Solution: Create a custom theme instead to build an appealing platform for yourself or your client. 2. Problem: Not Understanding Package/Theme Relationships Solution: Ingenious Usage of Package/Theme Relationships could help customization matching the client needs. 3. Problem: Using Wrong Starting Theme necessitates packing in a lot of unnecessary codes, slowing the developmental process Solution: Use ‘blank theme’ instead to evade unnecessary CSS styling, which in turn aids in speeding up development. 4. Problem: Not Building CSS Specific to Magento Solution: Using a demo site for viewing the source and cloning the source as HTML when building your CSS could help in refinement as per Magento attributes. II.Common Mistakes from the Back-End (Programmers and Engineers): 1. Problem: FTP Installation of Magento – This is considered one of the most common mistakes and ends up in giving you an unstable version of Magento. Solution: Instead of downloading the full version and installing via FTP, you need to use the Magento downloader option to get yourself a stable Magento platform. 2. Problem: Not Backing Up the Data – No backup on your client’s sites means your data could be lost at any time due to cyber attacks, IT infrastructure failures, accident deletions, hacking and system breach which would ruin your client’s business completely. Solution: Make backup a part of the site’s regular maintenance task so that it is never missed out. 3. Problem: Overwriting the Core Class While Extending its Functionality – most developers do the overwriting by placing the file in the same relative path on the local code pool, app/code/local/Path to core class/ (i.e., app/code/local/Mage/Checkout/Block/Onepage.php). This may cause compatibility issues and breaking up when upgrading to a new Magento version. Solution: Use class rewriting while overwriting, with the new class inheriting from the class you wish to extend and not by just copying and pasting the original code in the new class. This facilitates an easier upgrade to new versions and resolves module conflicts when third-party modules rewrite the same class. 4. Problem: Nested Collections – This will slow down the speed considerably Solution: Need to be wary of the nested collections as every collection is a query, meaning if you have a collection inside a loop, it effectively means you have a query inside that loop. 5. Problem: Not Testing a Newly Written Module with hole-punching and full page caching on. Solution: Make sure that after writing a module, it is checked with full page caching on and see if it is compatible with an FPC enabled staging environment. 6. Problem: Namespaces Used for Custom Modules Solution: If you are not careful about the namespaces used for the custom modules, they may conflict with the core Magento modules. III. Common Magento SEO Mistakes 1. Problem: Not Optimizing Title Tags – Not changing the default settings for title tags or doing it in a completely wrong way would bring your site’s ranking down on SERPs . The top blunders committed on title tags are : Not creating a relevant title tag instead of the generic ‘Home’ tag Not altering the alt title text on images and logo Not modifying the default Homepage Title ‘Magento commerce.’ Title duplication created by same titles for multiple pages Long titles omitting search keywords Solution: Open Admin Area → Go to System → Configuration → Design → HTML Head → enter an optimized, keyworded, unique themed title reflecting your business goals in the “Default Title” field. Ensure to limit the title to 60 characters and descriptions to 160 characters. For changing the alt text of the logo, Go to System → Configuration → Design → Click on ‘Header tab’ and change the logo source to your respective filename or path and change the alternate text to a keyworded relevant title. 2. Problem: Not Changing the Default Keywords – though Google Search Engine tend to ignore keyword meta tags, the phrases you create should be logical, unique and in level with your business goals. Solution: Go to System → Configuration → Design → HTML Head → Default Keywords and change the default keyword setting. You can leave the space blank instead of the default keywords, because if the space contains words not precisely reflecting your business needs, it may impact your Magento store negatively. 3. Problem: Duplication of URLs – Having redundant URLs in the webpages will affect your SEO. Solution: To avoid this, Go to System → Configuration → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization and assign ‘No’ to the field ‘Use Categories Path for Product URLs.’ 4. Problem: Canonicalization Issues – not handling canonicalization would end up being detrimental to your SEO. Solution: Go to System → Configuration → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization and set the fields ‘Canonical Link Meta Tag For Categories’ and ‘Canonical Link Meta Tag for Products’ as ‘Yes.’ 5. Problem: URL Rewrites Not Implemented – URL rewrites are search engine friendly and makes URLs easier to read. Solution: Go to Admin Panel → URL Options → Add Store Code to URLs → No and Auto-redirect to Base URL → Yes. Also, Go to System → Configuration → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization → Use web server rewrites 6. Problem: Layered Navigation – Layered navigation widget filters the products by price, category, size or color and is a very handy tool for customers. But it also creates a lot of identical content, and confused page titles, URLs and descriptions. Solution: Hire experienced Magento Developers to prevent your layered navigation pages getting indexed by Google. They will accomplish this through cookies or by sending fast Ajax Requests. 7. Problem: Not Switching on Indexation of Website when moving from developmental stage to live server results in the page losing out on searches. Solution: Admin Panel → System → Configuration → General → Design → HTML Head → Default robots ‘INDEX, FOLLOW’. This task has to be executed when you are ready to go live with your server. 8. Problem: Missing on Creating Google Sitemap – Creating and refreshing a sitemap at regular intervals is imperative to a Magento store. Solution: Go to System → Configuration → Catalog → Google Sitemap and create one for your site. You can also set up in a way that your google store automatically refreshes the sitemaps periodically. Hope this article was comprehensive enough for you to understand and fix your Magento store and get it to function seamlessly. These fixes should be part of every Magento checklist to build yourself a high-performance Magento store.

title: Google Algorithm Updates: What Changed From 2018 to 2026, and What to Do Now
headings: What is a Google algorithm update?
Core updates, spam updates and everything else
What happened to the 2018 updates this post first covered?

Is AI-generated content penalized by Google?
text: Summary Google no longer ships a single named update each year. It runs two to four broad core updates, a few spam updates, and thousands of smaller changes that are never announced. In 2026 so far, Google has confirmed two core updates (March and May), three spam updates (March, June and August) and one Discover update. If your traffic dropped, check the dates on Google’s Search Status Dashboard first. Then compare Search Console data from before and after the rollout. For most eCommerce stores, the fix is better category and product content, not a technical trick. Google states there is no special markup needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode. Introduction We first published this post in 2018, when the March and August broad core updates were moving rankings overnight. Back then, the advice was simple: there was nothing specific to fix, so make your content better and wait. That advice has aged better than most of the 2018 detail around it. What changed is everything around the core update. Google folded its helpful content system into core ranking, added new spam policies, replaced a Core Web Vital, and put AI-generated answers above the organic results. This guide is the rewrite. It covers what an algorithm update is, the updates that mattered between 2018 and 2026, how to tell whether one hit your store, and what to do about it. Every 2024 to 2026 date comes from Google’s own Search Status Dashboard, checked on 22 September 2026. Table of Contents What is a Google algorithm update? What happened to the 2018 updates this post first covered? Which updates changed search between 2019 and 2023? What changed in 2024 and 2025? Which Google updates have rolled out in 2026 so far? How do you tell if an update hit your store? What should an eCommerce store do after a core update? What can you check this week? People also ask Conclusion What is a Google algorithm update? A Google algorithm update is a change to the systems that decide which pages rank for a search. Most are small. Google makes thousands of changes a year and announces almost none of them. Core updates, spam updates and everything else The updates worth tracking fall into three groups. Broad core updates. Google calls these “significant, broad changes” to its ranking systems. They happen several times a year and take roughly one to three weeks to roll out. They do not target any site or niche. Spam updates. These improve how Google detects content that breaks its spam policies. They usually roll out in days, not weeks. System-specific updates. Older examples include the product reviews, helpful content and page experience updates. Most of these systems now run inside core ranking and no longer get their own announcements. Where Google announces them Google posts confirmed updates on the Google Search Status Dashboard , with start and end dates. If an update is not listed there, Google has not confirmed it. Industry names like “Medic” or “Fred” were given by SEO trackers, not by Google. What happened to the 2018 updates this post first covered? Google confirmed a broad core update in March 2018 and another on 1 August 2018. The August update became known in the industry as “Medic” because health and finance sites saw large swings. Google did not use that name and said the update was not aimed at any sector. Both updates were early examples of the pattern Google still follows. There was no single error to fix. Pages lost ground because other pages were judged more useful for the same queries. The quality idea behind them survived too. In 2018 SEOs talked about E-A-T (expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness) from Google’s Search Quality Rater Guidelines. In December 2022 Google added a second E for experience. E-E-A-T is not a ranking factor you can score, but it is the clearest description of what Google’s raters are asked to look for. Which updates changed search between 2019 and 2023? Five years of updates reshaped how Google reads pages and judges quality. These are the ones that still affect how an online store should be built. Update When What it changed BERT October 2019 Better understanding of the words in longer, conversational queries Product reviews updates April 2021 to November 2023 Rewarded reviews with first-hand testing and evidence over thin summaries Page experience update June to August 2021 (mobile), February 2022 (desktop) Made Core Web Vitals and HTTPS part of ranking signals Helpful content updates August 2022, December 2022, September 2023 Demoted content written mainly to rank rather than to help people E-E-A-T in rater guidelines December 2022 Added first-hand experience to how raters assess quality Dates from Google Search Central announcements and the Search Status Dashboard. The November 2023 reviews update is the last reviews update Google announced separately. Why the product reviews updates matter to stores If you sell products, the reviews updates set the bar for your comparison guides and buying advice. Google wanted evidence that the writer had used the product: measurements, photos, pros and cons, and comparisons with alternatives. Copying the manufacturer’s description stopped being enough. Why the helpful content updates matter even more The helpful content system looked at a site as a whole. A large amount of unhelpful content could pull down the pages that were good. For stores with thousands of near-identical product and tag pages, that turned thin content from a small problem into a sitewide one. What changed in 2024 and 2025? 2024 was the biggest structural change since 2018. 2025 was quieter on the ranking side and louder on the AI side. March 2024: helpful content moved into core ranking The March 2024 core update ran from 5 March to 19 April 2024, 45 days in total. It folded the helpful content system into Google’s core ranking systems, so there are no separate helpful content updates any more. Google said it expected the change, with its earlier work, to reduce low-quality, unoriginal content in results by 40%. Three new spam policies Google added three spam policies in March 2024. Scaled content abuse. Mass-producing pages mainly to rank, whether by AI, people or both. Expired domain abuse. Buying an expired domain and reusing its reputation to rank unrelated content. Site reputation abuse. Third-party content published on a trusted site with little oversight, mainly to rank. Enforcement began in May 2024. INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital In March 2024, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) replaced First Input Delay as the responsiveness metric in Core Web Vitals. INP measures how quickly a page responds to every tap and click, not just the first. Heavy themes, page builders and third-party scripts are the usual reasons stores fail it. AI Overviews and AI Mode Google launched AI Overviews in US search in May 2024 and opened AI Mode to US users in May 2025. Both write an answer at the top of the page and link to sources. They are not algorithm updates in the usual sense, but they change how many searchers reach your site at all. We cover how to adapt in eCommerce SEO in the age of AI search . 2025 core and spam updates Google confirmed three core updates in 2025: March (13 to 27 March), June (30 June to 17 July) and December (11 to 29 December). The August 2025 spam update took 26 days to finish, far longer than most spam updates. Which Google updates have rolled out in 2026 so far? Google has confirmed six ranking updates in 2026 as of 22 September. Update Started Finished Type February 2026 Discover update 5 February 26 February Discover March 2026 spam update 24 March 25 March Spam March 2026 core update 27 March 8 April Core May 2026 core update 21 May 2 June Core June 2026 spam update 24 June 26 June Spam August 2026 spam update 18 August 20 August Spam Source: Google Search Status Dashboard, checked 22 September 2026. Google adds an entry once an update starts and records the end date when rollout completes. What Google said about the 2026 core updates Google described the May 2026 core update as a regular update to better surface relevant, satisfying content from all types of sites. That is the same language it has used for years. Neither 2026 core update came with a new named system or a specific fix. New spam rules in 2026 Two policy changes matter more than the spam updates themselves. In April 2026 Google announced a spam policy against back button hijacking , where a site stops visitors from returning to the results page. Enforcement started on 15 June 2026. Google has also made clear that its spam policies cover attempts to manipulate AI Overviews and AI Mode. If your store uses exit-intent scripts or pop-ups that interfere with the browser’s back button, review them now. How do you tell if an update hit your store? Most traffic drops are not algorithm updates. Seasonality, tracking errors, a site migration or a lost backlink cause just as many. Rule those out before you rewrite anything. Line up the dates Compare the date your traffic changed with the start and end dates on the Search Status Dashboard. If the change started during a rollout, an update is a likely cause. If it started a week before, look elsewhere. Wait a week, then compare in Search Console Google recommends waiting at least one week after an update finishes before judging it. Then compare a period after the update with the same length of time before it, in the Performance report in Search Console. Which pages lost clicks. Product pages, category pages and blog posts usually move differently. Which queries lost position. Losing generic queries while keeping brand queries is a common core update pattern. How far positions fell. A move from 2 to 4 is normal movement. A move from 4 to 29 needs a real review. Whether impressions held but clicks fell. That points to AI Overviews or new SERP features, not a ranking loss. Check for a manual action Open the Manual actions report in Search Console. A manual action is a penalty applied by a person at Google, and it is listed there with the reason. Algorithmic drops are never listed. What should an eCommerce store do after a core update? Google’s own guidance for core updates is to review whether your content is helpful, reliable and made for people. For a store, that translates into a few specific jobs. Fix category pages first Category pages usually carry the most commercial traffic. Add a short, useful introduction, clear filters, and buying guidance that helps someone choose. A grid of products with no text gives Google little to rank. Replace manufacturer copy on key products If 50 other retailers use the same product description, Google has no reason to rank yours. Start with your top-selling products and write descriptions that answer the questions your customers actually ask: sizing, compatibility, what is in the box, and who the product is not for. Clean up thin and duplicate pages Tag pages, empty categories, filtered URLs and old out-of-stock products can bury your good pages. Consolidate, redirect or noindex the ones that add nothing. Our WooCommerce SEO guide walks through this for WooCommerce stores. Pass Core Web Vitals on templates, not pages Core Web Vitals are measured per page, but problems come from templates. Fix the product template and every product page improves. Check the Core Web Vitals report in Search Console, not a single lab score. Do not chase AI-specific tricks Google states there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, and no special schema or AI text files to add. Standard SEO is the requirement. If part of your catalog sits behind a login, read why gated B2B catalogs are invisible to AI search . What can you check this week? These checks take a few hours and tell you where you stand. Open the Search Status Dashboard and note any update that overlaps your traffic change. Compare 28 days before and after the latest update in Search Console, by page and by query. Check the Manual actions report so you can rule out a penalty. List your 20 highest-revenue category and product pages and check whether each has original text. Open the Core Web Vitals report and note which templates fail INP or LCP. Test your back button from Google results on mobile. It should return you to the results page every time. Search your top 10 non-brand queries and note where AI Overviews appear and which sites they cite. People also ask How often does Google update its algorithm? Constantly. Google makes thousands of changes a year. It confirms only the larger ones, usually two to four core updates and a few spam updates each year. How long does it take to recover from a core update? Google says some changes can show in a few days, but it can take several months for its systems to recognize improvements across a site. Many sites see the clearest movement during the next core update. Is AI-generated content penalized by Google? Not for being AI-generated. Google targets content made mainly to manipulate rankings, however it was produced. Mass-produced, low-value pages fall under the scaled content abuse policy. Conclusion The lesson from 2018 still holds. Core updates reward the page that best helps the searcher, and there is rarely one thing to fix. What changed is the bar. Thin category pages, copied product descriptions and slow templates now weigh on a whole site, and AI answers take clicks from pages that only restate common facts. Start with the dates, then the data, then the content. If you want a second pair of eyes on a traffic drop, talk to our team . Frequently Asked Questions What was the latest Google core update? The May 2026 core update, which ran from 21 May to 2 June 2026. The most recent confirmed update of any kind is the August 2026 spam update, from 18 to 20 August 2026. Where can I see official Google update dates? On the Google Search Status Dashboard. It lists every confirmed ranking update with start and end dates. Third-party trackers report volatility, but only the dashboard confirms an update. Did Google stop doing helpful content updates? Yes. Since the March 2024 core update, the helpful content system is part of Google’s core ranking systems, so its effects show up during core updates instead. Do I need special schema to appear in AI Overviews? No. Google states that no special schema.org markup, AI text files or new machine-readable files are needed. A page must be indexed and eligible to show a snippet. Can a core update affect only part of my store? Yes. Core updates are assessed page by page, with some site-wide signals. It is common for blog posts to drop while product pages hold, or the reverse.

title: Why AMP? Benefits, Limitations & Next Step
text: E-commerce focuses on creating an enjoyable shopping experience for customers which suits their online shopping behaviors. To ensure user delight and pleasant shopping, every online brand molds the way they market to their potential customers. Off late, the drastic change in the adoption of mobile technology has triggered the need to streamline mobile shopping experiences. Realizing the need for mobile-optimized sites, Google introduced “Accelerated Mobile Pages” (AMP) to set web pages which load faster on mobile devices. In short, AMP was initiated to assist publishers and online brands to fasten load speed and avoid waiting time. Why AMP for E-commerce? Speed is an integral part of web page designing. Slow and longer loading time may force users to leave a page. As quoted by KISSmetrics , “about 40% of people will abandon a web page that takes more than 3 seconds to load.” It is hypothesized and proved that a site which earns $100,000 per day, may cost $2.5 million lost in sales every year for a 1-second page delay. This means, 1-second delay in mobile browser load time can lower conversion rate by 3.50%, reduce page views by 9.40% and increase bounce rate by up to 8.30%. In December of 2015, Google stated that Accelerated Mobile Pages acts a catalyst for better ranking. As per Google, the AMP plugin reduce load time for about 15% to 85%, in the initial tests. Webmasters, SEO’s and marketers started to analyze how AMP affect mobile web pages and came up with several facts that states AMP has a positive impact on mobile search engine rankings. To be precise, AMP optimized sites are faster and rank better. These pages bring more conversion rates as they convert more visitors to customers. In the past one year, more than 650,000 domains became AMP enabled. At present, Google index has 150 million pages and approximately 4 million plus new pages are added to the index every week. Why so? As rightly quoted by Google, “AMP is a natural fit for e-commerce because AMP makes web pages fast, and help pages with purchase conversions.” The benefits of AMP are plenty : Reduce bounce rates resulting in an improvised user experience Improve page load speed increasing conversion rates Fasten load times attracting users to engage with your website continuously The lightning bolt tag placed next to results lead to an increase in click-through rates because users understand that they connect to faster loading speed Improvised site ranking because of faster pages (Google’s algorithm approve faster pages and that brings your site up) To be precise, through page optimization, speed and usability, AMP brings drastic changes to your e-commerce business beyond your belief. AMP allows retailers to serve the growing needs of mobile customers in a better way. What Are the Potential Limitations or Drawbacks of AMP for E-commerce? Since AMP is a newbie, there are a few limitations and drawbacks. These shortcomings can be resolved with proper planning. But, as an e-commerce store owner, it is always better to be aware of the constraints. An understanding about the below points will help you to handle the drawbacks in a better way : Limited control over the design and customization of pages Though amp-analytics can be utilized on many platforms, many more need to be developed Google Analytics recommends website owners to set up a different method for AMP measurement because Google “support for e-commerce analytics” is in the initial phase How Are Accelerated Mobile Pages Implemented in E-Commerce? AMP is essential to improve customer experience, but it is not necessary to introduce AMP on every single page. After thoroughly checking the flow of visitors, you can launch AMP at the appropriate sections. This processing is essential because the clear and easier AMP framework permits pages to function smoothly. The three major elements required for this framework are AMP HTML, AMP JS, and AMP CDN. On the contrary, AMP may limit or restrict other CSS and JavaScript, eg, no iframes. Does AMP Have Analytics? Yes! AMP has smarter analytics. To stop multiple analytics which can slow down a site, Google has introduced the method of “measure once, report to many.” The Amp-Pixel Element and The Amp-Analytics Extended Component are the two paths that enable analytics functionality with AMP for your website. What Should You Do Now? If your concerns are about the page speed and managing complex functionalities in lesser time, then AMP is essential for your store. AMP creates better opportunity to provide excellent mobile experience and in fact doubles the conversion rate. If you think moving according to the changing trends and innovations in technology is something great, then it is better to enable your store with AMP. Want To Get Started? Starting AMP is simple and more accessible because Google has come up with several resources like the AMP Project Website, Google Search Guidelines for AMP pages, AMP Webmaster Help Forum, and Google Search console to help store owners to create AMP supported pages. If you wish to be a successful store owner, it is imperative for you to have a track and understanding about the latest trends as well as the demands of the audience. This understanding is inevitable to run an online business successfully. Nowadays, the public is more inclined to use mobile pages which undoubtedly makes AMP the future of e-commerce. We, as an expert e-commerce service provider , recommends you to enable your page with AMP because in the last few decades business scenes have witnessed a breakthrough in online platforms and technological advancement has brought unimaginable changes in the field of e-commerce. Be quick to boost your marketing and sales with AMP enabled e-commerce websites!

title: WooCommerce vs. Magento: Which is the Best eCommerce Platform for You?
text: The WooCommerce vs. Magento argument has been around for a long time. They are both similar yet versatile at the same time. They are often considered similar in functional capabilities and flexibility. The fact that both of them are open-source platforms only raises confusion. This article is an overview of the similarities and differences between Woocommerce and Magneto. We discuss the key features, security, performance, pricing, user-friendliness, product management, etc. Magento is a platform customized for web development experts and massive online stores. High aspirations and robust features make Magneto reliable and suitable for high-end provisions. Whereas, Woocommerce is the powerful plugin of WordPress. This is a powerful plugin. It can convert your WordPress site into a full-fledged eCommerce store. Furthermore, you get access to many plugins. You can use them to put in place advanced eCommerce features in your WooCommerce store. You can put in place these changes while retaining the user-friendliness of WordPress. We discuss the following aspects involved in the WooCommerce vs. Magento argument. After reading the article, you can get a comprehensive picture of the two platforms. You can make a well-informed decision for your unique business and its requirements. WooCommerce vs. Magento: Overview WooCommerce vs. Magento: The Pros WooCommerce vs. Magento: The Cons WooCommerce vs. Magento: Pricing WooCommerce vs. Magento: Performance WooCommerce vs. Magento: Security WooCommerce vs. Magento: Product Management WooCommerce Vs. Magento: Overview WooCommerce, being an open-source eCommerce platform, needs to be set up with the help of a web host. WordPress is popular because it is free. It supports a countless number of products. WooCommerce also comes equipped with a robust extension system. WooCommerce supports all major third-party applications. WooCommerce can handle any WordPress themes thrown at it. Whether it is a premium, free, or third-party does not matter. What is more enticing about WooCommerce is its superior customization capability. The easy-to-use nature of its interface only adds to its advantage. Furthermore, the WooCommerce platform facilitates all major payment gateways. This makes it easy for the users to make purchases through their preferred medium. Magento is an ideal eCommerce platform for both beginners as well as enterprises. It comes in both community and premium versions. This platform has the facility to add as many products as your business requires. It also has an innate interface for admin along with advanced product design tools. Magento comes equipped with well-organized APIs. You can integrate it with any advanced third-party applications. It also has attractive theme-based systems and options and advanced security features. Magento has many rich functionalities that come out of the box. It is one of the factors that make it suitable for large companies and start-ups alike. WooCommerce Vs. Magento: The Pros WooCommerce Magento Free Store Set up:   WooCommerce is a free, open-source eCommerce platform. The store setup will be free except for the web hosting expenses. Furthermore, WooCommerce offers an extensive range of free plugins. The free plugins are not ideal once your business starts to grow. But, you still have the option to make the most out of it while you still can. WordPress Based:   The WooCommerce platform has WordPress as its base. This means that it comes equipped with the reliability of WordPress. If you have basic knowledge of WordPress, then WooCommerce should be easy for you to handle. Content-Centric:   WooCommerce WordPress-based, the best content management system in the world. Woo allows you to use advanced content marketing methods in your WooCommerce store. Modular System:   WooCommerce offers one of the best modular systems in eCommerce. It allows the admin to add any option he/she wants. It can work in sync with your favorite WordPress plugin. This means that you can install any advanced feature on your website. Unlimited Customization:   WooCommerce is open-source. You can change or customize it from head to toe. With WooCommerce, you have complete control over your eCommerce store. You can choose what to show your customers, and how to show it. You can change it until you find the optimal solution. Superior Documentation:  WooCommerce offers one of the most superior documentation capabilities in eCommerce. It covers everything, including hook, filter, API endpoint, major release, and extension. The meticulous documentation ensures that you can access all the relevant information. Catalog Management:   In a single import, Magento permits the upload of diverse product control. This saves you valuable time and effort. This is especially true for businesses with an extensive range of products. The Dynamic management specification of Magento also assists the platform. You can use it in different product categories. You can also use it on wish lists, comparisons, search results, related products, and many more. Flexible Pricing Options:   Magneto allows you to hide or adjust the product price. You can change this depending on your unique business needs and target audience. Magento cart allows different cost paradigms at one time. It enables your eCommerce website to have a superior and flexible pricing option. Product Alerts:   Magento allows sending alerts or notifications to customers. This is useful when a product is back in stock or when introducing a new product. This feature helps to plan your marketing efforts. Multi-store Enabled:   Magento supports multi-language websites with an outstanding store view. It also allows you to set up different stores for each industry or product line. This feature of Magento helps stores to meet the requirements of international customers. Custom User Interface:   Magento stores have the option of altering designs. They can also change themes based on product categories. This permits more than one ‘storefronts’ established on a single back-end system. The easy-to-use user-interface allows stores to provide a better user experience. Furthermore, it also increases conversion rates. Order Processing Integration:   The wide-range integration partnerships of Magento give a variety of order fulfillment options. They can connect to your Magento store. You can interact with the store partners. You can then update shipping methods, order status, and tracking information. This results in streamlined order processing. The Winner The pros of both WooCommerce and Magento are unique. WooCommerce has the upper hand in flexibility and ease of use. Magento is the winner as far as functionalities go. WooCommerce Vs. Magento: The Cons WooCommerce Magento May Have to Familiarize two Platforms: The users may end up having to familiarize themselves with two platforms. This includes both WooCommerce and WordPress. Expenses can add Rapidly: WooCommerce supports a lot of free themes and extensions. But, once you start using premium themes and plugins, you may end spending money. Requires Basic Development Skills: Magento needs specific development skills. Hence, it is more usable for developers than regular users. Not the Ideal for Small businesses: Although open-source, Magento may seem costly for small owners. Even if you are using a community edition, it has a high operational cost and is resource-hungry. The Winner When it comes to cons, WooCommerce does slightly better than Magento. Familiarizing oneself with WordPress is much easier than learning development. Hence, from a user perspective, WooCommerce is the winner in this round. WooCommerce vs. Magento: Pricing WooCommerce Newbies can depend on WooCommerce and can learn about it using online tutorials. WooCommerce is a completely open-source platform. You can download WooCommerce and set it up on any server as per need. But, the premium extensions are expensive and charge an annual subscription rate. Apart from this, the cost will depend on the size, scope, and complexity of your project. Magento Magento is not as easy-to-use as WooCommerce. But, if you have a decent idea about web development, Magento is the perfect platform for you. On the flip side, Magento comes with plenty of out-of-the-box capabilities. You do not need to install any external plugins and even have superior security. The Community Edition of Magento is free depending upon the hosting provider. On the contrary, the Enterprise edition is expensive and best suited for large companies. The Winner When it comes to pricing WooCommerce takes the lead again. WooCommerce has access to various free plugins. There are few integrations available for Magento. But, it does come with plenty of out-of-the-box features. WooCommerce vs. Magento: Performance WooCommerce When it comes to performance, it is hard to compare the two platforms. Both of them have areas where they shine and where they stall. The performance of WooCommerce is much better when dealing with content-rich websites. WooCommerce is your best choice to incorporate advanced content strategies like content commerce. Magento Magento is often termed as one of the most powerful eCommerce platforms, and for a good reason. Magento goes hand in hand with WooCommerce when it comes to performance. Although it can’t quite keep up with WooCommerce when it comes to content delivery, it does a decent job. Furthermore, depending on the hosting provider, you can optimize the Magento store’s performance. The Winner WooCommerce goes hand in hand with Magento when it comes to performance. Although Magento does gain the edge in pure performance. Whereas, WooCommerce is optimizable for better performance. WooCommerce vs. Magento: Security WooCommerce WooCommerce has several flexible security features. You can ensure WooCommerce security through Password Security and WordPress two-factor authentication. A better password strategy is to install WooCommerce security. Updated plugins and themes are essential to safeguard a site. An extra level of WooCommerce security is the “secure socket layer”( SSL ) certificate. SSL creates an encrypted link between the server and the user’s browser. Any expert you go to will recommend SSL for your website’s security. It is worth noting that most security features need WooCommerce plugins. They do not come equipped with them out of the box. Magento Magento offers dedicated security patches to its users. But, it is not that simple to apply unless you are familiar with web development. Magento is very advanced and reliable when it comes to security. One of the main security features of Magento is “Captcha.” It helps to cut automated attacks. Placing a captcha at the right place is essential for security. The Captcha may act as a barrier to malicious attacks. The captcha should be active on the admin and customer forms as well. The captcha should also be active on the login and forgotten password. You can also put in place for checkout as a guest, and register during checkout. The Secure Payment Bridge included in Magneto provides PCI Data Security Standard. Furthermore, the login prompts help to reduce password hacking. Another important security feature of Magento is Directory Index. It allows people to access only one folder but can’t see the files inside these folders. The Winner Magento takes this round as it already comes optimized with advanced security patches. Whereas, WooCommerce comes equipped with basic functionalities. But, you can add them by installing plugins. WooCommerce vs. Magento: Product Management WooCommerce When it comes to product management, WooCommerce has the upper hand. A long as you are familiar with WordPress, you can manage products in WooCommerce. WooCommerce offers you a practical approach to product management. This is true regardless of whether your product is digital or physical. Putting up new products is straightforward, particularly if you’re familiar with WordPress. Besides, you can expand the functionality using plugins. Magento Magento comes equipped with advanced product management features. When it comes to functionality, it is superior to WooCommerce. If you are a newbie or someone with zero experience in web development, it may not be so easy. You can have superior product management on your Magento website. But, you need to know your way around Magento or have a reliable eCommerce partner. You will have superior capabilities to most other eCommerce platforms, including WooCommerce. The Winner Product management is far easier in WooCommerce if you are familiar with WordPress. Even without WordPress familiarity, it is easy and straight-forward. This round goes to WooCommerce because of its easy management features. Conclusion Comparing WooCommerce vs. Magento is not an easy task. No single platform fits endless requirements. WooCommerce should be your choice for an easy-to-use eCommerce platform with advanced capabilities. But, if you are familiar with web development then Magento is the ideal choice for you. But, this is a broad classification of the two platforms. The actual requirements of your eCommerce website will be more complicated. For example, you may want to give personalized pricing to your customer. Some companies give personalized pricing for a group of customers. Similarly, another company may want individualized pricing for each customer. You need an expert developer like Virtina who has a demonstrated history of delivering such complicated requirements. Businesses often have unique requirements even if they specialize in the same niche. For example, consider a fashion store that sells both clothing and accessories. Such a store could benefit from cross-selling, where when a customer adds a product to cart, a small list of suggested products shows up. This list will include accessories that go well with the item in the cart. On the other hand, an online fashion store that specializes in clothing alone would better benefit from upsells rather than cross-sells. title: 7 Ways To Boost e-Commerce Sales
text: In this digital world, relatively a large number of people prefer Online Shopping and Online stores. With the rise of many online stores for same products, “sales” turn out to be a challenging task for every store owner. So what do online stores do? How do stores drive traffic and improve sales? As Rightly quoted by philosopher Sun Tzu “People should not be unfamiliar with strategy. Those who understand it will survive and those who do not will perish”. This quote is very much applicable to online sales because familiarizing strategies and implementing it, is the only way to boost online sales. So, what are the most appealing strategies for e-commerce platforms?? Let us look into the details…. As a complete eCommerce solution provider , we have tried to list 7 ways to boost your e-commerce sales. #1: Focus on a Single product Focusing on a single product helps you to give maximum attention to the growth of that particular product. When handling Single product, you will have a better understanding of that product and its pros and cons. This understanding will, in fact, help you to tackle any problem the store face, thus to resolve it at a faster pace. In precise, focusing on single product will help you to gain customers trust and loyalty easily. #2: Upselling and downselling Up-selling is one of the favorite technique used by e-commerce platforms to convince their customers to buy a product which is even more costly than the one they are planning to buy. This method encourages customers to purchase additional, better or larger products by spending some extra money. Upselling increases cart value, give rise to profit margin and also results in better customer satisfaction. To get a clear picture, Let us take KFC as an example: You are with your family, and If an individual fill up costs $5 per item, you will choose $20 family, and that is exactly what upselling is all about. On the contrary, down-selling is the best way to retain a customer who tends to leave the store before making a purchase. When applying this technique, the store owner should adjust offers suitable for buyer’s budget. This process involves offering low-budget products with same features as that of the product, the customer was planning to buy.This results in customer retention, promotion of brand loyalty and to serve clients with different budgets in a better way. #3: Advertise In e-commerce, social media plays a crucial role in promoting the products and sales. By advertising your products and stores in Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Google AdWord (PPC) campaign, etc. you can witness an increase in sales. #4: Create subscriptions Most of the e-commerce stores provide an option to make product subscriptions. This option invites more sales and attention from customers because in no time they keep getting new products of their choices or preferences. #5: Recover abandoned shoppers By recovering abandoned shopping carts, you can boost your sales. For that, you have to keep tempting them to complete the purchase by using different methods like Exit-intent popups with offers and deals, retargeting, web push notifications, follow-up emails, etc.. For many stores this has worked out well! #6: Optimize your checkout process Many times carts are abandoned because of the complexity of checkout procedures. If customers find checkout as time-consuming chances for them to leave the e-commerce shopping cart is higher.To overcome this issue, analyze the abandonment rate, and then introduce an optimized check-out process. Also, ask for information that is very vital for sales and encourage buyers to create an account, without forcing them to do so. Also, On the check out page introduce the product image because finding the picture of products bought before making the payment will help customers to confirm their purchase and avoid confusions if any. Apart from that, introducing different payment options and bringing Mobile apps also give a significant rise in sales. So if you take care of all these, you can boost your sales to a greater extent!! #7: Referral programs It is a good idea to introduce Referral programs to boost your sales because a buyer will be aware of what their peers or family is preferring. When launching a referral program with simple offers like earn 20 bucks with referring, will show how powerful word of mouth can be. Referrals help stores to be connected with new buyers and also to maintain their existing customers in a more relaxed way. When implementing these tips, you should also keep in mind that to be a successful global store you also have to act like a local because only then you will be able to attract and maintain customers from far and near. It is certain that these strategies will give a rise in your sales, but the list never ends here. There are many more things you can do to boost your e-commerce sales. However, these seven tips are the main strategies that you can apply immediately. With the right approach, these handful strategies will be enough to get an unexpected increase in your sales. title: Are You Risking Your Business with Social Media Integration?
text: Today, businesses and Websites depend on Social Media to drive massive traffic and to achieve a higher exposure in the market. It is evident that a practical and strategic social media approach is crucial for any online businesses as the power of Social Media is undeniable in today’s marketing world.Every enterprise and website use Social media platforms like Twitter, Google Plus, Tumblr, Facebook, LinkedIn, etc. to communicate and engage with their customers. For that reason, integrating social media platforms with businesses and websites is crucial in this technology-driven world. Social Media creates excellent business opportunities, but the risk is even higher.Social media for websites/ business is not merely liking, voting, sharing, etc.….it has much more to do. Isn’t it? On the process of engaging with customers and creating a brand name, what does social media do? Is Social Media always positive and beneficial for customers?? No, Not at all! The latest Facebook controversy regarding the use of information gathered from Facebook profiles by Cambridge Analytica is a warning sign for all social media users too. Have you ever thought of the security threats involved in integrating social media channels with Businesses/Websites? If not, it is high time for you as a social media user to consider the cons of the same. Let us get into it; There are many security threats a website face during social media integration. Here, We have listed, five main security threats when integrating social media platforms with businesses. 1. Human error The human errors like accidental tweets, unknown clicks, etc. are some of the unimaginable security threats to websites or companies. Many times it was reported that an unexpected click on a malicious link,a conversation with a fake social media account, or mistakenly filled spammy profile had put the reputation of the brand identity, finance, etc. on a stake. Any digital mistake that seems to be simple can result in a colossal loss hence companies have to be cautious about human error. 2. Lack of personal attention on social media If you don’t keep a track on your social media presence, then it can lead to Unimagined consequences. If you leave your online store’s account unmonitored, then the chances for an attack by a malicious virus, is doubled. Unmonitored accounts are more prone to malicious activities, and they may generate spam messages to your followers which questions your brand’s integrity and trustworthiness, social media attention is something that is must for every online store. 3. Malicious software attacks Reports from 2016 state that on an everyday basis, over 4000 malicious software attacks occurred. These attacks including virus, spyware, trojan, ransomware , etc. could harm the system entirely. These types of attacks are something every online store owner should be aware of, and they should find ways not to fall for it because the risk they can cause is unbelievable. 4. Lack of Privacy and phishing scams Social media acquire personal data of profiles and share it with different users, without the consent and knowledge of the profile owner. Apart from that, the Phishing scams in Social Media platforms trick people to provide personal information including bank details, passwords, etc.. A “phishing” e-mail is one that pretends to be from a bank or a company such as eBay or Amazon.com. The e-mail asks you to login to your account and verifies your account details, often claiming that suspicious activity has been observed on your account or that security upgrades have recently been implemented. A web link for this purpose is usually included in the e-mail. Clicking on the link takes you to a counterfeit web site that looks very similar to the legitimate one.Unsuspecting victims are tricked into thinking they are logging in to the real website. By hijacking well-known corporate brands, which individuals are inclined to trust, phishers obtain credit card numbers, account usernames, passwords and Social Insurance Numbers.This gives the fraudsters enough information to gain access to your accounts or commit other crimes using your identity. E.g., Facebook “fake friend” phishing scam. 5. Privacy settings Lack of strict privacy settings can make business websites, and personal profiles fall for hacking. E.g., Burger King, Mcdonalds, etc Without doubt we can say that social media is vital for marketing and customer engagement, but how about these risks? It is an open secret that social media use personal data of users to make their marketers job easiest. It is known that brands should educate themselves the risks of social media integration and then should take necessary steps to safeguard them from these risks. Business WebSites use many Softwares, and the vulnerabilities with each software component vary from one over the other, and these can result in many threats for enterprises! Online sites face risks ranging from proprietary exposure to lawsuit invitation. What has to be done to tackle this?.Should businesses pull away from Social Media? Never! Because Communication and regular conversations are essential to build a brand name. Risking important stakeholders interactions and the opportunity to create a market space in social media is not the solution. Every Website for business has to use social media platforms to communicate with their customers across the globe. But at the same time companies should keep all these risks in mind, and should come up with a systematic approach that can shield their brand from any troubles. Now we know the threats an enterprise can expect, so let us ponder on how to avoid these security threats that can happen during social media integration? Is it possible? Of course, it is! But how? It is simple too.Websites and businesses only have to follow certain tips to safeguard themselves from these threats. Tips to protect your firm from security threats; 1. Follow a Social media policy For every online store, social media policy which act as social media guide for employees is a must. This corporate code helps individuals to know what they can share to the world digitally. Most times, even the experienced employees may not be aware about the rules and consequences in sharing the firm’s information publically. A social media policy will help them to be aware of the risk involved in sharing sensitive information to the external world. This helps people to be cautious when they make brand related communication in the digital world and it also helps the store to be away from negative publicity . 2. Provide Social media training for Employee Training sessions on Social Media Policy have to be arranged for employees, and the company must make sure that every employee has understood the policy in a better way. Employees awareness on social media policy will save the company from financial, legal or any other sort of issues that can pop-up anytime.When you train your employees, you are in fact making them capable of taking the best decisions at the right time keeping the reputation of the company in mind. When you implement a policy and provide training, you are not chaining them; rather you are guiding them on how to utilize every single opportunity of social media, without getting into any sort of trouble. Mentoring platforms can reinforce this guidance by offering real-time advice and scenario-based learning. 3. Limit social media access for employees Restricting social media usage is beneficial in different ways. This not only save work time but also helps to prevent the spread of spyware and viruses too. Closely monitoring or restricting social media is useful in many ways including the maximum usage of employee productivity, reduce the risk of malicious software attack, safety from online theft, etc. … When considering all these factors it is advisable to limit the social media access for employees. 4. Appoint a Social Media In-charge Appointing a social media in charge is always wise when you run an online store. The social media manager will be responsible for the brand’s online image. The manager will monitor and evaluate the contents before sharing it online, maintains a positive relationship with clients, and creates social media strategies to tackle threats if any. A community manager will be well-versed with the store’s online presence and ensure social media presence is effective. 5. Invest in secure technology (Safeguard your passwords One social platform to rule them all, Scan for threats) Every online store will have multiple social media accounts and managing each account separately is not advisable because that is when they are more prone to security threats. To avoid these uninvited guests, it is always better to depend on password management tools, usage of a single platform (e.g., HootSuite ) and regular scans to find out threats which include scams, malware,brand impersonations, fraud, viruses, and any other form of cyber attack. 6. Regularly Monitor Social Media channels Chances are there that every online or offline store will fall prey to threats or security issues at least once. To resolve or avoid these issues, you must be aware of the problems that are going around, and it is not that easy. You should know what you have to look for and to identify the issues immediately; you can choose different monitoring tools like Google Alerts, Twitter Advanced Search, HootSuite, etc.. When you use these tools, from a particular dashboard, you can look into and track the troubles you face in the digital world. With the help of these tools, you can plan and execute a social media strategy immediately. 7. Carry out Social Media Audits regularly (Network privacy settings, Access, and publishing privileges, Recent security threats) Up to date Social Media Security measures are essential for every online store and for that reason it is wise to carry out regular audits on social media platforms. These reviews will help you to know that no potential security threats have occurred recently. Also, to be up to date, you should Often check the Network privacy settings, carry out regular scans to find out security threats, and also should keep a track on who all access social media platforms. Social Media is full of opportunities, and as a business, when you use all the opportunities it provides, you must also be capable to safeguard yourselves from every single threat it can create! title: What is GDPR & How Will It Affect Online Businesses
text: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the legal structure in European Union (EU) that ensure privacy and data protection of all citizens and residents within EU. This rule will be valid from May 25, 2018, and applies to all companies that acquire and use personal data for businesses. So, this is going to be a serious affair, isn’t it? Yes, in every sense. The implementation of GDPR is going to have a significant impact on Digital marketing and E-commerce , which means everyone in this technological world must have an insight on this topic. Let us take a sneak peek into the details and impact of the new regulation executed by the European Parliament regarding “protection of individuals concerning the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data.” Major GOALS of GDPR Curious to know why GDPR? This law has two primary goals; Firstly , Set up a single data protection law across European Union since EU initiates the regulation. However individual countries can include additional rules without altering or removing any part of this regulation. Secondly , GDPR intent to provide individuals, the power to use and distribute their data. With the execution of GDPR customers can enjoy personalized experiences as well as privacy too. The Basic Principles of GDPR Now let us take a quick look at the foundation or the right users can enjoy with this system; 1. Right to access: Individuals have the right to access their data from the organization that holds their personal information. If requested the data controllers should provide a copy of the data, and the individuals have all the right to know where and how their data is used and processed. 2. Right for erasure: Upon the request of individuals, the data controller should erase the personal data of individuals and should also ensure that third parties do not use their information. 3. Data portability: Individuals can avail their data in electronic format and can also transfer their data to any service provider they choose. 4. Data breach notification: If data breach like hacking, leaking or losing USB, etc. then data controllers should inform users within 72 hours. 5. Privacy by design: Privacy of Data should be ensured from the first stage itself, i.e., designing a new project or system. 6. Data protection officers: Public companies or Data procession companies should have an onsite data protection officer instead of informing local Data Protection Authorities about their activities. Legal ways of data processing under GDPR: You might be wondering how GDPR regulates data processing, right? Let us look into that. There are six legal ways of data processing; (a) Consent: the user permits to process their data for a particular purpose. (b) Contract: If data processing is necessary to inform the user to take specific steps or result. (c) Legal obligation: If the processing is required for you to abide by with the law. (d) Vital interests: If the process is essential to assist someone’s existence. (e) Public task: If the processing is critical to execute an official function or to safeguard the public interest. (f) Legitimate interests: If the processing is needed for legal interests or involvement of a third party unless there is a great reason to safeguard personal data which overrule those legitimate interests. Will User’s applaud for GDPR? A survey was carried out by Page Fair on “How users feel about providing personal data,” and the result was, 80% of users don’t like to provide data for advertising purposes 21%-32% of users expect to know the details stored about them 21%-39% of users will demand to erase the data This report states that majority of users doesn’t prefer to share their data to receive advertisements. So, with the implementation of GDPR, obtaining client consent is going to be a real challenge for users and for that reason online marketing will have to undergo a drastic change in the implementation process of GDPR. As a result, privacy led marketing will become more important. This approach focuses on collecting minimal data, being transparent with consumers, and respecting their privacy preferences. Marketers will need to prioritize trust-building strategies, ensuring that they gain explicit consent while offering value-driven, non-intrusive experiences that align with privacy regulations. The Effect of GDPR on E-Commerce Businesses E-commerce Businesses and organizations have to abide by this data protection rule. It also does not matter whether the data processing happens within or outside EU which means to carry out an activity to EU citizens and residents then the organization has to act as per the rules of GDPR. Since it is new initiative confusions and complications, will be a part of it. Every organization should appoint a data controller or a data protection officer who will look after everything related to GDPR. If a company doesn’t abide by GDPR rules then a fine up to 4% of annual global revenue or 20 million Euros, whichever is greater will be levied. To be precise, GDPR is not merely an IT issue, it is much broader than that and includes everything related to marketing and sales. Expected Impact of GDPR on B2B E-commerce Is GDPR adverse for eCommerce marketers? Why? We can’t say that GDPR is adverse, but it is a challenge for small and large digital companies. Even Facebook and Google will be affected by this law since all these organizations largely depend on user’s data for sales and marketing. When GDPR becomes effective, obtaining data is going to be risky because ; User’s declaration or permission With the implement of GDPR , every eCommerce company needs user’s declaration or permission to use their data for advertising and marketing. It is going to be a real risk for marketers as they have to obtain individual consent to use personal data of the user. 2. Marketers can no longer show retargeting ads GDPR considers cookies and IP addresses as personal data. Also, e-commerce marketers, without the permission of individuals, cannot exchange Client-IDs or profiles between two parties even if it falls under same ad network. To tackle this risk, eCommerce marketers will have to come up with very, creative and competent technical solutions to create an online space for stores and products. CONCLUSION GDPR will be mandatory within few months, and it will be better if organizations initiate few things to welcome this new set of rules to avoid legal issues. The digital marketers must raise internal awareness to ensure that the primary stakeholders and board members are aware of the new scenario. It is also better to audit and document all the data, the organization holds. The organization should review the current privacy policy and should plan for changes if required. Identifying legal basis, updating subject access procedures, investigating data breaches and tackling the same are also essential for smooth organization’s growth and marketing. GDPR seems to be very risky, but in a broader sense, it has excellent opportunities as well. Let us hope, with the implementation of GDPR; Marketers can find who their loyal customers are and build more relevant and valued relationship with them. Have questions? title: YOAST 7.0 – What You Need To Know
text: Yoast, the WordPress SEO plugin is the favorite SEO tool used by millions of website users. This plugin seems to be very attractive for Search engine optimization because of its features like user-friendliness, documentation style, and reliability. Recently, Yoast has introduced a brand new version, YOAST 7.0 with many more features and updates. Let us take a look at the features of this brand new version. A streamlined user interface The main attraction of Yoast 7.0 is a simple interface which is easy to understand and convenient to navigate. In this version, the menu has got only fewer items in it. In the search appearance, you will find titles and Metas which regulate your site’s presence in search engines. A couple of visual changes in this version are as follows: Titles and Metas appear in Search field. A United General and Homepage. XML sitemap which depends on search indexation. The toggle switch in the Advanced features tab is removed or merged. Under Search appears Breadcrumbs and RSS Feed In Tools appears ext link counter calculator. Media menu item is introduced. In “General” finds all “features” command ( General > Features). Simpler Indexing & XML sitemaps This version has got a more straightforward content indexing method. For example; Instead of XML sitemap settings page, a feature toggle is introduced with a feature tab and a question “Show X in search results?” in the search appearance. This attribute defines the function of that specific setting which seems to be more convenient and comfortable for the user. Similar changes are noticed in the follow/unfollow links too. Apart from these now, Yoast has also got an option to make author’s archive visible or hide from search results. Redirecting media and attachment URLs A new menu, “Media” is introduced in the updated version of Yoast. With this setting, the attachment URL will be redirected to the URL that has original media or image. Whenever a video or image is uploaded to WordPress, it will be automatically added to the library, and an attachment URL is created for this media item by WordPress. This feature is included in new installations by default. Deleted Features During the cleanup process, many functions, and codes were removed. Though it was a complete cleanup process, Yoast has given enough time for every integrated plugin to adapt new features and updates. Though the brand new plugin is smaller in size, the speed and performance are increased to a great extent. The features that got removed are; The function of automatically removing stop words from slug as it is noticed that this feature often creates slugs with a different meaning of what the post meant. Since canonical was introduced, clean permalinks feature is deleted because Yoast SEO adds rel = canonical everywhere which manages to figure out issues and resolve it. The replytocom variable which allows replying comments without the activation of java-script is now turned off. Nevertheless, every comment gets its link which ends up in the search engines. Hence these variables were removed by default. This brand new release of Yoast SEO 7.0 is a significant milestone in SEO optimization. It is certain that beginners and experts of SEO will love and enjoy this better, simple, easy and faster version of Yoast, alike.

title: Magento 2.0 Performance Boost Explained For Non Developers
text: Faster User Experience: Magento 2.0 offers faster page loading and browsing overall on the browsing side. Following techniques achieve this faster performance. 1. Web Page Compression Web page compression is achieved by optimizing all the components of a web page displayed on user’s browser using various compression engines on the server side. A web page is comprised of four elements: HTML code with textual content, Javascript, CSS, and images. Magento 2.0 reduces the total weight of the HTML page on the server by applying various compression engines in each of these four elements before serving the page to a client browser. The compression engines used for each of the elements HTML + Textual Content is compressed using a custom compression engine Images are compressed by PHP GD2 image compression library. CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) are compressed using Austin. jShrink is used to compress all Javascript/Jquery embedded within a web page. 2. Full Page Caching Magento 2.0 employs web page caching on the server to store frequently used items in the server memory so that the server does not have to read it from the hard drive or database for every request and thus improving the page rendering time to the browser. By default, Magento uses smart web page caching using an open source cache software, Varnish. Magento 2.0’s page caching is smart enough to separate dynamic contents (customer data, order/cart data, etc..) from static contents( images, product data, etc..) and cache only the static data but combine the dynamic and static data together in the right order and serve to the browser. For enterprise-scale Magento installation with high demand, Varnish can also be deployed on to its servers for even further scalability and performance. In Magento 2.0, Full Page caching is on for CMS (Content Management Pages), Category Pages, Product Pages and Error Message pages and same is off for Account pages (login, create an account, address book, wishlist), Cart page, Checkout page and Checkout success page. However the some of the pages in the latter category, private content, can be cached by the browser cache as explained below. 3. Browser caching Browser Caching is the method by the browser to make sure that only the absolute necessary part of the web page is retrieved from the server only when necessary, improving the subsequent page load time on the browser and reducing the load on the server. In Magento 2.0 , optimized web page components are cached by the client browser intelligently during the initial load to improve the speed in subsequent page loads. The intelligent caching works this way. Javascript and CSS are cached in the initial page load along with other static content and page begins to be displayed using these cached content. While the available content is being rendered, private/dynamic data are being fetched from the server and displayed, giving a much faster user experience. From a user experience perspective, pages begin to load immediately without staring at blank pages. Additionally, Magento 2.0 can retrieve all private data (username, items in cart ..) in one Ajax or Javascript call from the server instead of having to make the call for one piece at a time. 4. Asynchronous Operations Synchronous calls and operations make the user wait till that operation is complete. Whereas asynchronous operations allow the user to continue with other tasks on the page while a task is already running. For example, during the checkout process, a user is allowed to fill out all parts of the order checkout page while address validation is routine is called. User does not have to wait till the address verification to complete so that he/she can fill the rest of the form. Magento 2.0 has multiple built-in asynchronous operations mainly in the order page, cart page and check out page. These asynchronous operations also allows CSRs (Customer Service Reps) or administrators to do back-end operations such processing phone orders, or pick and ship orders or updating product descriptions without causing process interruptions to other parts of the eCommerce site. This feature becomes very important for enterprise-scale Magento sites with large number of SKUs or many admins/CSR processing the orders/products on the back end. By combining browser caching and web page compression techniques Magento 2.0 serves up near instant catalog browsing experience and reduced response time for order page and check out page resulting not only faster page loading time but also lowering cart abandonment rates. 5. Job Queues [Enterprise Edition Only] This is one of the features that exist in the Enterprise edition to bring additional scalability and faster responsiveness. Using a job queue server, RabbitMQ, different tasks are put in multiple queues and picked up and executed as the server becomes available. The queue workers (not humans, but the applications meant for processing the tasks in a queue) can be run from separate servers to achieve further optimization. Some of the scenarios that can benefit from Job Queue mechanism are deferred inventory level updates, asynchronous order insertion, sending emails and database indexing, Magento 2.0 is planning to introduce more tasks compatible with job queues in future releases. 6. Improvements to PHP Magento is written in open source programming language PHP. Even though Magento 2.0 can be deployed in older versions of PHP, using the latest version of PHP 7 framework gives Magento 2.0 an additional performance boost. 7. Segregated Database Masters [Enterprise Edition Only] To further isolate processes to gain additional processing speed, Magento 2.0 enterprise edition allows to divide the back end database into three databases representing three business entities: Product Data, Orders, Check out. Using this mechanism, all database operations (Select, Insert, Update, Delete) of these three business entities can be distributed across these three databases efficiently improving the processing time. Additionally, each master database can have its own slave databases to support select/read operations to realize an additional increase in speed. These mechanisms ensure that check out processes in an e-commerce store do not stall the product browsing or adding an item to the cart. Looking for Magento upgrade?
