How High-Risk Payment Processing Works for eCommerce Businesses 01 Assessment and Application The high-risk payment processing service is customized for eCommerce businesses in industries or markets defined as high-risk by financial institutions. These business ventures are considered ‘high-risk’ because they are exposed to more chargebacks and legal challenges or because of the goods and services they offer in areas such as adult content, travel agencies and affiliate services, online gambling, or luxury items. High-risk merchant accounts are, therefore, essential for eCommerce businesses, as they enable firms to work with secure and reliable payment processors despite the associated risks. High-risk payment processors are aware of these challenges and provide specific services to help businesses mitigate risks and operate smoothly. The process begins with a thorough assessment of the business applying for a high-risk merchant account. Payment processors will evaluate several factors, including the industry the business operates in, its financial history, the products or services offered, and its chargeback ratio. This assessment helps the processor determine the level of risk and the appropriate measures to manage it. 02 Underwriting and Approval Once the application is submitted, it goes through a rigorous underwriting process. This stage involves verifying the business’s financial stability, reviewing past processing history, and checking for legal or regulatory compliance issues. High-risk processors typically take longer to approve accounts due to the detailed analysis required to mitigate potential risks. 03 Customizing Terms and Conditions After approval, the payment processor will establish specific terms and conditions tailored to the business’s risk profile. This may include higher transaction fees, a requirement for a reserve account, or caps on monthly processing volumes. These measures help the processor manage the increased risk while allowing the business to accept payments. 04 Integration and Setup Once the terms are agreed upon, the company integrates the payment processing system with its eCommerce platform. High-risk payment processors typically offer robust, customizable solutions that can be tailored to a business’s specific needs, including fraud detection tools, secure payment gateways , and advanced reporting features. 05 Transaction Monitoring High-risk payment processors also always keep an eye on the transactions that take place so that they can track any fraudulent activities. Such monitoring is useful in reducing chargebacks and other costs related to high-risk businesses. The processor may also generate notifications for suspicious activities, helping the business take necessary action. 06 Reserve Account Management The processor holds back a portion of each transaction for businesses that maintain a reserve account. This reserve safeguards against potential chargebacks, refunds, or other liabilities. The terms of the reserve—whether it’s a rolling reserve, capped reserve, or upfront reserve—are determined during the underwriting process. 07 Chargeback Handling High-risk payment processors are equipped to manage higher rates of chargebacks, a common issue in high-risk industries. They often provide tools and support to help businesses dispute chargebacks effectively, reducing the financial impact on the business. 08 Ongoing Compliance and Support High-risk payment processors ensure businesses follow industry regulations and standards. They may offer ongoing support to help the business navigate regulatory changes, optimize payment processing, and address any issues. Benefits of High-Risk Payment Processing High-risk payment processing offers a range of benefits crucial for the success and sustainability of eCommerce businesses operating in high-risk industries. Let’s explore some of these key advantages: Access to Merchant Accounts High-risk payment processors specialize in helping businesses in high-risk industries secure merchant accounts, which are essential for accepting online payments. This access opens doors to a wider customer base and enables businesses to operate seamlessly in the digital marketplace. Reduced Risk of Account Termination Unlike traditional payment processors, which may abruptly terminate the accounts of high-risk merchants, specialized high-risk processors understand the nuances of these industries and implement measures to mitigate risks. This reduces the likelihood of sudden account closures, giving businesses stability and continuity. Fraud Prevention and Chargeback Management High-risk payment processors employ robust fraud prevention tools and chargeback management systems to protect businesses from fraudulent transactions and minimize chargeback disputes. This safeguards revenue and helps maintain a healthy merchant account. Customized Solutions High-risk payment processors understand that every business is unique. They offer tailored solutions that cater to different industries’ specific needs and risk profiles, ensuring optimal payment processing experiences. Global Reach Many high-risk payment processors offer multi-currency support and international payment processing capabilities, allowing businesses to expand their reach and tap into global markets. Enhanced Security High-risk payment processors prioritize security and follow industry standards such as PCI-DSS, protecting sensitive customer data. Improved Customer Experience By offering various payment options and ensuring smooth transaction processing, high-risk payment processors contribute to a positive customer experience, fostering trust and loyalty. Business Growth High-risk payment processors provide reliable payment processing, allowing businesses to focus on their core operations, expand their customer base, and grow sustainably. When operating a high-risk business, selecting the right payment processor is crucial for ensuring smooth, secure transactions and the long-term success of your eCommerce operations. Here are key factors to consider when choosing a high-risk payment processing provider: Industry Experience Choose a payment processor with substantial expertise working with firms in your sector. Providers who understand your industry’s issues and laws are better positioned to offer personalized solutions that meet your requirements. Their experience may be extremely useful in managing the complexity of high-risk transactions and maintaining compliance. Fee Structure Transparency Selecting a service with a clear cost structure is crucial, even if high-risk payment processing sometimes entails higher rates. Understand the associated expenses, including transaction fees, chargeback fees, and any additional charges for reserves or setup. A trustworthy company will clearly explain its price structure, allowing you to avoid unforeseen charges. Security Measures. Given the heightened risks, ensure the processor uses robust security measures like modern fraud detection and encryption to safeguard transactions and client information. A provider that prioritizes security will help protect your company from potential financial losses and reputational harm. Customer Support and Service. When dealing with the complexity of high-risk payment processing, you must provide responsive and skilled customer assistance. Choose a service that offers dedicated assistance, with personnel accessible to help you with any concerns or queries. Consider companies that provide 24/7 service, primarily if your company works abroad or outside regular office hours. Customizable Solutions High-risk enterprises may have special requirements that traditional payment processing systems cannot meet. Look for a service that provides customizable payment processing alternatives, such as flexible payment gateways, personalized reporting tools, and connectivity with your current systems. A supplier who can adjust to your unique needs will be better able to assist in your business’s growth. Reputation and Reviews. Assess the reputation of possible payment processors by reading reviews and testimonials from other high-risk firms. A service with a proven track record and excellent feedback from clients in related sectors will likely be more dependable and effective. Be wary of suppliers who have received multiple complaints or poor feedback since this may suggest problems with service quality or reliability. Global Reach and Multi-Currency Support If your company works or intends to develop globally, select a payment processor that supports many currencies and has a global reach. This guarantees that you may take consumer payments worldwide without causing additional problems or hefty conversion expenses. Flexibility and Growth Potential As your firm expands, your payment processing requirements may alter. Choose a company whose services are flexible and scalable. This will allow you to change terms, enter new markets, or boost transaction volume without encountering substantial restrictions. Frequently asked questions What is high-risk payment processing? High-risk payment processing is the card payment service that specialist providers offer to businesses banks see as more likely to produce chargebacks, fraud or regulatory trouble. It usually comes with higher fees, stricter underwriting and sometimes a rolling reserve. Which businesses are considered high risk? Common examples are CBD and hemp, vape, firearms and accessories, adult content, nutraceuticals, travel, subscription and trial-offer businesses, online gaming, and merchants with a high chargeback ratio or a limited processing history. Why do payment processors label a business high risk? Processors look at chargeback exposure, refund rates, how long before the customer receives the product, legal restrictions on the product, average ticket size and the merchant’s processing history. A weak score on any of these can move a business into the high-risk category. How much does high-risk payment processing cost? Expect a higher per-transaction rate than standard processing, often above 3.5 percent, plus possible setup, monthly and chargeback fees. Many providers also hold a rolling reserve, a percentage of sales kept for a set period. Compare the total cost, not only the headline rate. Can I use Stripe or PayPal for a high-risk business? Only if your products fall inside their acceptable-use rules. Both can freeze or close accounts that break those rules, even after months of normal sales. Many high-risk merchants therefore open a dedicated high-risk account and keep a backup gateway ready. How long does it take to get approved for a high-risk merchant account? Approval usually takes from a few days to a few weeks. Having your business documents, bank statements, processing history and clear refund and shipping policies ready shortens the wait. How can I reduce chargebacks and keep my account in good standing? Use a clear billing descriptor, publish plain refund and shipping policies, verify orders that look suspicious, respond to disputes quickly with evidence, and contact customers before they call their bank. Staying under your processor’s chargeback threshold matters more than any other single factor.

text: Ecommerce Warranty Services: A Comprehensive Guide for eCommerce Businesses Summary By understanding the different types of warranties and carefully selecting a WSP that aligns with your business needs, you can enhance customer satisfaction, reduce returns, and create new revenue streams. The actual buying process for online purchases differs significantly from the physical shopping process familiar to retailers for decades. Therefore, customer loyalty has changed, and different approaches have been employed. Furthermore, in traditional retail, that is, store-based retailing, returns on products are considered a negative sign of failure. In an eCommerce context, they can be repurposed as a marketing tool. Notably, returning warranties can affect consumer behavior in unprecedented ways. Understanding this dynamic means that retailers can enhance their warranty policies and overall workflow, which will, in turn, increase their average customer lifetime value. Customer satisfaction depends on finding the right product and a seamless shopping experience. This satisfaction is further amplified when products come with a reliable warranty. That’s where Warranty Service Providers (WSPs) play a crucial role by offering protection that benefits your customers and your company. So, selecting a WSP can be revolutionary, increasing customer retention, decreasing returns, and generating more revenues. But from the vast number of WSPs, how do you decide what is best for your eCommerce store? Whether you have been in the eCommerce niche for a long time or are completely new to it, this guide will provide you with all the information required to choose which WSP you should use and how to optimize the potential of warranty services. We will also discuss essential aspects such as pricing, the features offered under the plans, the flexibility to integrate it with other platforms and tools, and customer support services to help you better decide which one to choose. Knowing eCommerce Warranty Services Warranties are not mere legalities and printed words on pieces of paper, which are usually barely glanced at by customers. It is a handy fact that they are as effective as customer relationship management tools that help to build trust with clients, improve satisfaction rates, and stimulate business development. This stage of knowledge regarding different warranties is significant for eCommerce firms. It means that you can address the needs of purchasing customers and guarantee their requirements by providing the necessary warranties, thus increasing satisfaction and customer loyalty to your company. Types of Warranties While browsing various online stores, you might have encountered different warranty types, and here, we will brief you on them. Manufacturer’s Warranty A manufacturer’s warranty is a standard guarantee that accompanies most new products. It assures the buyer that the product is free from defects in materials and workmanship for a specified period. While this type of warranty offers basic protection, it often has limitations in terms of duration and coverage. Extended Warranty This warranty is called ‘enhanced’ since it covers what other manufacturer warranties cannot. It can be purchased at the time of purchasing the product or after some time and  deals with general problems. Product Protection Plans These are more comprehensive than warranties, where customers are shielded from accidental damage, voltage spikes, and even ordinary fatigue. These offer societies a full blanket and assurance to the clients who seek the most secure and highest yielding on investment. Accidental Damage Protection This type of warranty covers accidents, such as a phone being dropped, spilled, or having a cracked screen. It is one of the most sought-after insurances for electronic devices and fragile items. Theft Protection This warranty protects its owner against loss or theft of a product. It may get an agreement from your insurance provider to remunerate its worth or to replace the item. Tips for Integrating Extended Warranties Into eCommerce Business Are you geared to grow online sales and provide customers with desirable peace of mind? Let us discuss how in detail. Benefits of Warranty Services for eCommerce Businesses Warranties to your customers through a WSP are not only insurance for your clients but rather a valuable marketing tool. It’s a business decision that could help take your eCommerce business to the next level. Increased Customer Loyalty People who believe that they can return a product because it is under warranty will be more confident in your brand and, hence, frequent customers. Warranties show that you are a firm that cares for its customers and helps develop loyalty over the long run. Reduced Returns and Refunds Warranties reduce the rate of returns and refunds because consumers rarely return products under warranty to be replaced or repaired. This reduces the cost you, as a business, will incur and provides better customer service. Enhanced Brand Image Proving the warranty states that the products provided have been produced with quality workmanship and are lasting. This in turn enhances your brand image and is unique to competitors not offering similar protection to their clients. Additional Revenue Streams One of the most common WSP business models is revenue share, which gives you a percentage of sales commission on each warranty sold. These can generate an additional stream of sales for your eCommerce business, which can be highly profitable. Competitive Advantage Buying warranted products can also become a competitive advantage in the eCommerce industry. It has an added advantage over other competitors who are not undertaking similar services, thus pulling more customers and expanding market share. Data-Driven Insights WSPs might also offer useful information and statistics regarding warranty claims and customer habits. This can assist you in identifying concerns regarding product quality and making changes to improve them; it could also aid in decision-making for your business. Choosing the Right WSP Allow Customers to Compare Warranty Plans Side-by-Side Present warranty plans in a side-by-side comparison format, such as a table or slider, to make it easy for customers to weigh their options. When it comes to warranty services, it is crucial for a company to select the proper WSP that can satisfactorily fulfill the service commitments. Below are some key points that can be useful in making the right decision. Product Categories Consequently, the WSPs are different in ensuring that they address various products. When choosing such a provider, it is crucial to match the provider’s specialization with the range of products provided. For instance, select a WSP that works in the electronics sector if your organization’s sector is electronics. Target Customers Be aware of potential buyers’ age, gender, and other characteristics, as well as the stuff they like and want to have. It is important to know if they are more interested in the costs, coverage range, or other policy aspects. Choose a WSP in your targeted market segment that offers related products and services. Budget Check the price range you are comfortable paying for warranty services and compare the WSP pricing models. Remember fixed-price, commission-based, and sliding-scale expenses so that you can find a relevant service within your affordable price range. Customization Most WSPs offer adjustable warranty packages through which consumers can select the coverage and terms they prefer. If flexibility is relevant to you, make sure that you select suppliers who offer this option. Integration It is equally important that you have it integrated with your eCommerce platform so that your clients could have the best time. Choose a WSP that has a close relationship with the platforms that are commonly used, for instance Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce. Claims Process Evaluate the claims handling process offered by different WSPs. It is preferable to deal with services that offer an efficient way of processing customer claims to avoid any hindrances. Customer Support In general, buyers as well as sellers need efficient and friendly customer service. When choosing its WSP, it is recommended to choose one that provides its clients with quality customer support, that can be reached at any time of the day, and through numerous communication channels. Taking all these into consideration, one is able to make an informed decision about the best WSP to choose so as to suit the business and customers hence creating the perfect synergy for the growth of the eCommerce business. text: eCommerce Conversion Rate Optimization: A Comprehensive Guide Summary Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) is an ongoing journey that requires constant attention and adaptation. By regularly monitoring your website’s performance, testing new strategies, and staying ahead of trends, you can continuously enhance your online shop. Implementing the tips mentioned will create a more engaging and user-friendly shopping experience and significantly boost customer satisfaction. As customers find it easier and more enjoyable to navigate your site, your sales will naturally increase. Remember, the key to a successful CRO is to keep experimenting and refining your approach, ensuring your online store remains dynamic and competitive in an ever-evolving market. Imagine the thrill of seeing your online store transform into a bustling marketplace, with visitors not just browsing but also exploring, and making purchases. This is the power of eCommerce conversion Rate Optimization (CRO). It’s not just about creating an inviting and engaging virtual shop, but also about encouraging visitors to do those ‘cool things’ you want them to do, such as exploring more, clicking on items, and having a great time. CRO is the key to unlocking the full potential of your online store. Don’t be intimidated by the term ‘CRO ‘. This is not about complex strategies or overhauling your website. It’s about making small, strategic changes to understand what drives guests to delve deeper, click on something, and enjoy their experience . It’s about making the visitors’ time on the site engaging and entertaining while they shop. CRO is a simple yet powerful tool for your online store’s success. In this blog, we’ll explore tips and best practices of CRO to make your website the best place to spend time online. This will help you focus on conversion rate optimization for eCommerce business. Maximize Your Store’s Profit Potential What is eCommerce CRO? You may have heard the term eCommerce conversion rate optimization at least once. It does sound fancy, doesn’t it? Undoubtedly, it’s a fantastic way to make your online shop even more impressive! Imagine owning a toy store where you want all the best toys to be easy to find and a joy to play with. eCommerce  CRO is like redesigning your toy store, adding new signs, and creating exciting displays to see what keeps kids engaged! eCommerce  CRO involves tweaking your website to understand what entices people to explore further, click on links, and ultimately buy your products. People choose online shopping because it’s convenient, competitively priced, offers a wide range of products, and is always available. eCommerce CRO helps you discover what people love about your online store and how to improve it. And the best part? It’s not as daunting as it seems, and the impact is often immediate and significant. Now, we will break down the concepts for you. B2B eCommerce Conversion Rate This is the percentage of website visitors who complete a desired action on a B2B eCommerce  site. The desired action could be making a purchase, requesting a quote, or signing up for a wholesale account. Example: If 100 businesses visit a site and 2 make a purchase, the B2B eCommerce conversion rate is 2%. B2B Lead-to-Customer Conversion Rate This is the percentage of leads (potential customers who have expressed interest) who are converted into paying customers. Example: If a company generates 100 leads and 25 of them make a purchase, the B2B lead-to-customer conversion rate is 25%. B2C eCommerce Conversion Rate This is the same concept as the B2B eCommerce conversion rate, but it applies to B2C eCommerce  sites. Here, the desired actions might be adding items to a cart, creating an account, or completing a purchase. Example: If 1,000 consumers visit a site and 25 make a purchase, the B2C eCommerce conversion rate is 2.5%. B2C Lead-to-Customer Conversion Rate Similar to the B2B lead-to-customer conversion rate, this is the percentage of B2C leads that become paying customers. Example: If a company has 500 leads from consumers and 30 of them purchase, the B2C lead-to-customer conversion rate is 6%. Key Takeaways: What’s Happening Here? B2C Generally Outperforms B2B On average, B2C eCommerce  sites see higher conversion rates than B2B sites, both in terms of website visitors and leads. This is because B2C purchases are often more impulsive and less complex than B2B decisions. Industry Variations Conversion rates vary widely by industry. For example, the food & beverage industry sees high B2C conversions (those midnight snack cravings!), while health & beauty has a strong showing for B2B (perhaps due to bulk orders from spas or salons). Lead Conversion is Crucial The lead-to-customer conversion rate is generally higher for B2B than B2C. This highlights the importance of nurturing leads in the B2B sales process, as these leads are often more qualified and closer to making a purchase. Optimizing Conversion Rates: A Data-Driven Approach To improve conversion rates, businesses need to adopt a data-driven approach. This involves tracking key metrics, analyzing customer behavior, and conducting A/B testing to identify the most effective strategies. Capture leads through email sign-ups and retargeting campaigns. Quick Tips to Skyrocket Your eCommerce Sales eCommerce conversion rate optimization can double your sales, making your PPC expert look great with an outstanding placement on Google. Picture Perfect Product images and videos are essential. Imagine walking into a store with everything hazy and unclear—it’s off-putting, right? Online, high-resolution images and engaging videos let customers feel the product. Show different angles and interactions and zoom in on features to increase the likelihood of clicks on the ‘Add to Cart’ button. Free Shipping Frenzy Free shipping is universally enticing. It amplifies product desirability and can sway consumers to choose between your product and a competitor’s. Offer it as a limited-time promotion or for orders over a certain amount. Incorporate shipping costs into your total product price if necessary, as free shipping often outweighs direct costs in the customer’s mind. Coupon Countdown Use limited-time coupon codes to create a sense of urgency. Offer warranties, seasonal sales, and discounts for first-time customers. Advertise these codes via email, social media, or website pop-ups. The fear of missing out (FOMO) can significantly boost your sales. Price Match Magic Consumers appreciate price insularity. Monitor competitor prices and offer competitive deals. While moderation is key, cheapness isn’t always the best. Offer price matches and bundle deals to attract customers, emphasizing value beyond monetary factors, including overall customer experience. Checkout Express Lane Your checkout process should be seamless. Each click or unnecessary action risks customer abandonment. eCommerce checkout conversion rate optimization is crucial for business. Optimize and streamline the process, allowing guest checkouts and providing clear, concise information and secure payment options. Cart Saver Superpower Use abandoned cart software to send reminder emails to customers who left items in their carts. Personalize these emails with product suggestions and discounts. Sometimes, a gentle reminder can convert an almost sale into a successful transaction. You can double your sales with  conversion rate optimization ecommerce store. Chat Champ Live chat and chatbots offer instant customer service. They provide quick assistance and guide customers through their purchases. Ensure these tools enhance rather than hinder the website experience. Safety Seal of Approval Display security seals from companies like McAfee or Norton. Clearly state your privacy policies, terms, and money-back guarantees. Use a secure payment solution and ensure your website is encrypted (look for the padlock icon). Trust is crucial for converting hesitant visitors into confident buyers. Treasure Map Organize your website for easy navigation. Use clear categories, sub-categories, and filters. A prominent search bar is essential. A well-mapped site helps customers find what they want quickly, increasing purchase likelihood. Clear Checkout Signs Make your checkout process straightforward. Use plain language clear graphics, and provide crucial details like shipping costs and delivery times. Offer multiple payment options. A clear and simple process reduces cart abandonment. Cart Tracker A persistent shopping cart icon should be visible on every page, displaying the number of items. A simple click should take shoppers directly to their cart for review, encouraging impulse buys and helping customers remember their selections. Guest Pass Allow guest checkouts to reduce barriers and speed up the purchasing process. Don’t insist on email sign-ups for customers who are just browsing or making one-time purchases. Cater to everyone’s preferences to boost conversion rates. Storytelling Superstar Engage your audience with lively product descriptions that tell a story. Highlight the positive aspects and advantages of your products compared to competitors. Explain how your products solve problems or improve customers’ lives, making them more appealing. Review Roundup Customer reviews provide social proof and build trust. Encourage reviews by offering incentives and making the process simple. Display reviews prominently on product pages and use a star rating system. Positive reviews can reassure potential buyers. Button Bonanza Make CTA buttons clear, well-designed, and strategically placed. Use contrasting colors and bold text. Your CTAs should guide customers to the next action, be it purchasing, checking out, or signing up for a newsletter. Ensure they are noticeable and irresistible. Return Policy Rescue An easy return policy boosts customer confidence. Clearly describe your return policy, including time frames, postage costs, and refund periods. Offer free returns or exchanges to encourage purchases. Happy customers are likely to return for more. Mobile Makeover Ensure your site is responsive and performs well on mobile devices. Most internet traffic comes from handheld devices. Test your site on multiple devices to ensure a smooth experience, preventing frustration and abandonment. Phone a Friend Display your phone number prominently to offer reassurance and accessibility . Consider adding a click-to-call button for mobile users. This human touch enhances customer trust and satisfaction. Helpful Hero Use content marketing to provide valuable information about your products. Develop blog posts, guides, or instructional videos to educate potential customers and establish your authority in your niche. High-quality content attracts new readers, builds brand loyalty, and drives sales. Email Express Use newsletters to reach your clients directly. Collect email addresses via sign-up forms, pop-ups, or contests. Use email marketing to highlight new arrivals, offer promotions, and share valuable content. An effective email campaign can turn subscribers into loyal customers. Eye-Catching Entrance Your homepage is the first impression visitors get. Use colorful banners, clear product images, and creative headlines. Develop a straightforward and compelling value proposition. An engaging homepage prompts interest in exploring other sections of the site. Button Balance Avoid overwhelming visitors with too many CTAs. Focus on the most important actions for each page. Use whitespace to make CTAs stand out and guide users through a logical path toward purchase. You’re the One Highlight your unique selling proposition (USP). What makes your shop different? Communicate your USP throughout your website and marketing materials, letting customers know why they should choose you over competitors. Spelling Bee Proofread your website content meticulously. Use grammar checker tools for extra assurance. A polished and professional online presence reflects positively on your brand and builds customer trust. Scoreboard Check Track your conversion rate and other key metrics like average order value, cart abandonment rate, and customer lifetime value. Use analytics tools to monitor your progress and identify areas for improvement. Data-driven insights help refine your strategies. Browse Booster Target users who showed interest but didn’t purchase with browse abandonment campaigns. Send personalized emails reminding them of the items they viewed, offering discounts, or highlighting related products. This nudge can re-engage potential customers. Testing Time A/B testing is crucial for CRO. Experiment with different website elements, such as headlines, images, button colors, and layouts. Test one variable at a time to isolate its impact. Analyze results and implement the winning variations to optimize your website for conversions. Personal Shopper Leverage customer data to offer personalized shopping experiences. Provide product recommendations, customized discounts, and targeted email campaigns. Personalize by addressing customers by name and displaying recently viewed items. A personalized touch increases repeat purchases. You can get help for conversion rate optimization for eCommerce websites. Progress Power A progress bar during checkout gives customers clarity and control. It shows how many steps remain, reducing anxiety and cart abandonment, especially for complex checkouts. Filter Finder Filtering options help shoppers find products in large catalogs. Use categories, price, size, color, and other features. Ensure filters are easy to access and use. Efficient searching improves user experience and purchase probability. Unlock the Full Potential of Your Ecommerce Store

title: Accessibility
text: Virtina Accessibility Statement Updated: February 2024. General Virtina strives to ensure that its services are accessible to people with disabilities. Virtina has invested a significant amount of resources to help ensure that its website is made easier to use and more accessible for people with disabilities, with the strong belief that every person has the right to live with dignity, equality, comfort and independence. Accessibility on Virtina.com Virtina.com makes available the UserWay Website Accessibility Widget that is powered by a dedicated accessibility server. The software allows Virtina.com to improve its compliance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1). Enabling the Accessibility Menu The Virtina.com accessibility menu can be enabled either by hitting the tab key when the page first loads or by clicking the accessibility menu icon that appears on the corner of the page. After triggering the accessibility menu, please wait a moment for the accessibility menu to load in its entirety. Disclaimer Virtina continues its efforts to constantly improve the accessibility of its site and services in the belief that it is our collective moral obligation to allow seamless, accessible and unhindered use also for those of us with disabilities. For online stores, an ADA and WCAG accessibility audit is the fastest way to find and fix these barriers. In an ongoing effort to continually improve and remediate accessibility issues, we also regularly scan Virtina.com with UserWay’s <a href=”https://UserWay.org/scanner” title=”Free Website Accessibility Scanner”>Accessibility Scanner</a> to identify and fix every possible accessibility barrier on our site. Despite our efforts to make all pages and content on Virtina.com fully accessible, some content may not have yet been fully adapted to the strictest accessibility standards. This may be a result of not having found or identified the most appropriate technological solution. Here For You If you are experiencing difficulty with any content on Virtina.com or require assistance with any part of our site, please contact us during normal business hours as detailed below and we will be happy to assist. title: Brand Stories
headings: What is in it for Aspiring Entrepreneurs?
text: Virtina Brand Stories Welcome to “Brand Stories,” a special corner of our website where we share the unique tales behind different eCommerce brands. Do you always find someone else’s success story inspiring? Does it motivate you to do something great on your own? Do you feel your success story has the potential to inspire another set of fellow entrepreneurs? Then this is the perfect spot for you.“Brand Stories” is a unique corner on our website that celebrates the triumphs and journeys of our fellow eCommerce entrepreneurs so that someone new to the scene can learn from them. What is “Brand Stories?” Each of us is looking for a role model for guidance and motivation. This place provides just that. We bring you authentic and raw narratives about successful entrepreneurial journeys.Virtina would love to regale some inspiring success sagas from established and self-made eCommerce entrepreneurs nationwide. The U.S. has no dearth of diversity in ethnicity and culture. Every individual has a story of their own to tell. The entrepreneurs we feature here are from diverse backgrounds and have taken different career routes. Their road to success, innovative ideas, and struggles are different. By showcasing them to you, we aspire to inspire you to chase after your dreams and make a mark in doing what you love. What Does Being Successful Require? Persistence is the key to achieving success. Coupled with hard work and strategy, you can do wonders for your business. Having a disruptive mentality and understanding market requirements is a must. But above all, every enterprising business owner looks for mentorship and guidance. They look for someone who can steer them through their business course – someone who has already traveled the route before them. “Brand Stories” desires to be that mentor to budding entrepreneurs. What is in it for Aspiring Entrepreneurs? If you are a start-up owner or an enterprising entrepreneur looking to scale your brand, “Brand Stories” is a safe space on our website to find motivation and creative ideas to get your business on track. It is a place where you can refer to when you are plagued with business hurdles. Sometimes, ideating and kicking off an online business can feel overwhelming and cumbersome. You might have come to the brink of quitting many times. Whether writing a business plan, procuring a business loan, or creating a website, “Brand Stories” anticipates being your reference book to derive inspiration on how to build your eCommerce journey. I’m Successful in My Rights. How Can I Contribute? If you are an established entrepreneur with a successful business -small, medium, or large – we fancy hearing about how you got there. We are sure you have had your ups and downs before you got to where you are. There might be times when you even thought about giving up but did not. You might have turned around a failing business or started on an incredibly skeptical idea and swung it into a thriving business. Whatever your story, we would love to showcase your journey as an inspiration for the coming generation of eCommerce entrepreneurs who can learn from your innovative strategies and entrepreneurial setbacks. The extension seamlessly integrates with our existing system, providing advanced features and boosting conversion rates. It’s a game-changer for our business! Ruth Poulin April 2023 FAQ B2B eCommerce development: frequently asked questions What is B2B eCommerce development and why does it matter? It is the design and build of an online store made for business buyers: account-based pricing, bulk and repeat orders, quotes, approvals and integration with your ERP and other systems. It matters because B2B buyers now expect to self-serve online, and companies that let them do so lower order-handling cost and win more repeat business. What industries benefit from B2B eCommerce? Manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, industrial suppliers, building products, healthcare supply, packaging, automotive parts and food service all see strong results. Any business with repeat buyers, large catalogs or negotiated pricing is a fit. Will B2B eCommerce handle my complex business processes? Yes. We model your pricing rules, approval flows, credit terms, minimum order quantities and multi-warehouse inventory, then connect them to your ERP so the store follows your real business logic. How long does it take to build a B2B eCommerce website? A focused build on an existing platform often takes roughly 2 to 4 months. Projects with custom portals, punchout and deep ERP integration take longer. We give a firm timeline after a short discovery phase. How much does a custom B2B website cost? Cost depends on platform, catalog size, number of integrations and custom features. We scope every project individually and provide a fixed or phased estimate after the free consultation, so you know what you are paying for. Which platform is best for B2B: Magento, BigCommerce, Shopify or WooCommerce? There is no single winner. Magento suits very large catalogs and complex rules, BigCommerce balances speed and APIs, Shopify Plus is strong for managed simplicity, and WooCommerce offers flexibility and ownership at a lower cost. We compare them against your requirements before you commit. How good is WooCommerce for a B2B platform? Very good when built properly. With wholesale roles, tier pricing, quote plugins and custom portals, WooCommerce can run a full B2B operation, and it gives you full control of your data and design. What are the different methods of B2B eCommerce integration? The common approaches are direct API integration, middleware or iPaaS platforms, EDI and file-based exchange, and punchout protocols such as cXML and OCI. We choose the method that keeps your data accurate without adding fragile dependencies. How is a Punchout catalog helpful? Punchout lets a buyer open your catalog from inside their own procurement system, shop with their negotiated pricing, and send the cart back as a purchase requisition. It removes re-keying, speeds approvals and makes you easier to buy from for large accounts. How do I choose a B2B eCommerce development company? Look for proven B2B experience, integration depth, platform breadth, certifications and references. Virtina has delivered 2,500+ projects, is ISO 9001:2015 certified and works across all major platforms. How do you measure the success of a B2B eCommerce platform? Typical measures are share of orders placed online, average order value, repeat order rate, quote-to-order conversion, cost per order handled and customer self-service adoption. We set baselines at launch and report against them. Take the first step to a successful B2B ecommerce strategy Join 1500+ happy clients. The robust platform provides a variety of features, such as inventory management, marketing tools, and a flexible shopping cart system. It also has a highly customizable source code giving it extraordinary flexibility. Magento users also get a user-friendly interface and intuitive navigation. The platform also has a variety of third-party integrations and extensions. It supports multiple payment and shipping options. How good is the Magento community support for my business? Could you help us with the differences between Magento Community Edition and Magento Enterprise Edition? CE, or Magento Community Edition, and EE, or Magento Enterprise Edition, are two different versions of the Magento eCommerce platform. CE is a free and open-source platform that provides basic eCommerce functionalities. At the same time, EE is a premium version that offers more advanced features such as customer segmentation, content staging, and 24/7 support. The system enables businesses to generate accurate and personalized quotes based on customer-specific requirements, ensuring transparency and facilitating the negotiation processes. Virtina’s B2B experts create pricing engines that handle various pricing rules and calculations based on customer segments, order quantities, discounts, and contractual agreements. Customized Contract Pricing This is a crucial feature in B2B eCommerce development and allows businesses to establish special pricing agreements with specific customers. It enables enterprises to negotiate pricing terms based on customer grouping depending on factors such as order volumes, long-term contracts, loyalty, and other personalized arrangements. By implementing a robust customized contract pricing system, businesses can enhance customer relationships, incentivize long-term partnerships, and drive revenue through tailored pricing strategies. Personalized Pricing and Quoting B2B eCommerce websites need a flexible and intuitive catalog management system that enables businesses to create, update, and organize their product catalog efficiently. Tailored User Management System Implementing a comprehensive user management system that allows businesses to create and manage multiple user accounts with varying access levels, permissions, and roles is a crucial feature for B2B websites. It ensures secure and controlled access to the B2B platform and facilitates efficient collaboration between different teams and departments. Our B2B specialists develop robust user registration and authentication systems that include features like account creation, password management, and role-based access control. Shared and Multiple Shopping Carts Shared and multiple shopping carts are factors of substance in B2B eCommerce development that enable companies to collaborate and streamline the purchasing process. With shared shopping carts, various users from the same organization can add products to a single cart, facilitating teamwork and collective decision-making. Additionally, the ability to have multiple shopping carts allows users to create separate carts for different projects, departments, or purchasing scenarios, improving organization and efficiency. text: What is a Customer Data Platform – CDP? CDP or Customer Data Platform collects, organizes, and presents customer data to help you build a granular, unified, and 360-degree customer profile. CDP provides a single digital platform with multiple views that connect both structured and unstructured data in real time.  CDP creates a persistent, unified customer database, in sync with existing software and marketing solutions, which helps the organization build better customer relationships. The platform accepts, consolidates, and cleanses customer data from multiple sources. Customer Data Platform – All You Need to Know CDP helps you to extract and compile intuitive, informative, and actionable data about your buyers into a central hub for easy access and zero silos Behavioral Data Transactional Data Demographic Data Use all the above from every key touchpoint to develop a holistic 360 degree understanding of your customers. No more relying on vague and cluttered data.  Furthermore, the true omnichannel potential of CDP means you can reach out to your buyers with personalized and impactful messaging on any channel. The tool includes upgraded APIs that help sellers create custom BOPIS resources for buyers. The release has new Inventory and Pickup Methods APIs to handle inventory and pickup strategies. John Thompson eCommerce Development Company in Philadelphia – Frequently Asked Questions How do I know the best eCommerce platform for my business? Choosing the right eCommerce platform for your business is rarely an easy decision. Provided that platform selection is potentially the most important decision, it is not one you want to rush. It is best if you come up with a list of desired features you want to implement on your website, along with every aspect of the business requirement that you feel relevant for your online store. You can then choose a platform on what you need and what the platform can offer you. Can I build two separate eCommerce stores with separate domains that are manageable by a single admin? Yes, advanced eCommerce platforms like Magento come with multi-store capability. With a powerful eCommerce platform like Magento, you can seamlessly run two or more eCommerce platforms with separate domains and also easily manage them through single admin access. Virtina has experience developing multi-stores for a number of businesses and can help you create one for your business without a problem. Can you create a prototype for my website before developing it? Yes, Virtina has a fully interactive, state-of-the-art eCommerce prototyping that enables you to get an idea about how your website can look and feel even before the actual development. Virtina’s eCommerce prototyping is fully interactive, which means you can even access basic functionalities such as the main menu, inner pages, and more. Is it necessary for me to have my eCommerce store optimized regularly? Yes, timely eCommerce optimization is necessary to make sure that your eCommerce website functions in its optimal condition. Neglecting eCommerce optimization could have adverse effects on your business. If your store goes unoptimized for an extensive period, it will get slow, and the slow loading will eventually lead to cart abandonment by the customers. Therefore it is essential to have your eCommerce website optimized periodically. Is an open-source eCommerce platform better than the SaaS-based alternatives? An open-source-based eCommerce platform has many advantages. It is cheaper, more flexible, and modular. However, it is not necessarily better than the SaaS-based alternatives because that would depend on your unique requirements. If you want to be able to customize your eCommerce store heavily and change it up often, then open-source is indeed the ideal choice for you. But, if you are looking for an easy-to-set-up platform with its own hosting, then a SaaS-based one would be more suitable for you. We have a broad Range of SEO specialists who are familiar with the SEO technicalities of every single eCommerce platform. From internal linking, URL optimization, keyword research, meta tags, and sitemap changes, they can expertly assess and resolve all the flaws. We’ll help you rank higher and increase the organic traffic to your website. Can you create a custom theme for my eCommerce business? Yes. As a leading eCommerce design agency, we have extensive experience in designing custom themes for various online stores. We’ll evaluate your business needs, establish your brand identity, review your industry landscape to create a wireframe and prototype, which’ll then, once approved manifest into a fully functional theme in sync with your brand. Can you help me create a responsive eCommerce store? Yes. Virtina as a leading design company understands the importance of a responsive design in this day and age. We can either make your existing design responsive or create a responsive design from the ground up for your eCommerce store. Regardless, your visitors will receive an exemplary user experience on mobile devices. Shopify News RFID Inventory for Shopify Launched by SimplyRFID at NRF Show February 19, 2023 SimplyRFiD launched Wave RFID Inventory for Shopify. The software is said to increase revenue by 10%, providing merchants with quick and accurate inventory access. The company demoed the latest version, Wave 3.3.9, launched on January 20th at the NRF Big Show last month. SimplyRFiD’s Wave RAIN RFID system generates weekly or daily inventories within minutes with 100% accuracy as opposed to the manual barcode counts that took hours and only produced 75-85% correct data. Once merchants sync their product tables to the Wave global accurate inventory system, it assimilates the product table from Shopify in a single click. It also creates an RFID tag for each item and assigns a product name through the UPC. SimplyRFiD Wave App runs on Apple iOS 16 and newer versions, connecting the CSL CS108 S, the most potent retail RFID scanner. Littledata Platform Extends Complete Support for Shopify Checkout February 3, 2023 Littledata, an ecommerce data platform for modern DTC customers and an alpha tester for Google brands, has automated its GA4 tracking services. The company has moved its complete server-side GA4 tracking system out of beta, giving complete Shopify and Shopify Plus checkout support. Implementing this first-party tracking solution eliminates the need for manual integration, Google Tag Manager (GTM) or Universal Analytics. The feature automatically captures recurring order features like revenue, conversion, and subscriptions. It also compiles checkout steps and upsell orders after purchase, sending this information to data destinations like Google Analytics, Segment, and Facebook Ads. Brands like the skincare brand Geologie have started benefitting from the new move by saving 50 developer hours using the new product. New Integration to Streamline NFT Processes for Shopify Merchants January 21, 2023 Shopify (SHOP) has a new integration that lets users design, mint, and sell Avalanche NFTs (non-fungible tokens). This integration helps Shopify merchants streamline their NFT processes. Retailers with minimal technical knowledge and no crypto wallet can sell their NFTs using the Venly Shopify Merchant App. The new NFTs turn into products automatically and can be displayed and sold on their storefronts. Instead of an existing crypto wallet, the merchants can access a new Blockchain wallet through an email link. The new integration simplifies Avalanche NFT sales from design to distribution. Shopify merchants also gain royalties on every secondary NFT transaction made via the Venly Market. With this venture, Shopify aims to nurture the expanding Blockchain ecosystem to promote direct NFT sales, increasing Web3 participation. Shopify News RFID Inventory for Shopify Launched by SimplyRFID at NRF Show February 19, 2023 SimplyRFiD launched Wave RFID Inventory for Shopify. The software is said to increase revenue by 10%, providing merchants with quick and accurate inventory access. The company demoed the latest version, Wave 3.3.9, launched on January 20th at the NRF Big Show last month. SimplyRFiD’s Wave RAIN RFID system generates weekly or daily inventories within minutes with 100% accuracy as opposed to the manual barcode counts that took hours and only produced 75-85% correct data. Once merchants sync their product tables to the Wave global accurate inventory system, it assimilates the product table from Shopify in a single click. It also creates an RFID tag for each item and assigns a product name through the UPC. SimplyRFiD Wave App runs on Apple iOS 16 and newer versions, connecting the CSL CS108 S, the most potent retail RFID scanner. Littledata Platform Extends Complete Support for Shopify Checkout February 3, 2023 Littledata, an ecommerce data platform for modern DTC customers and an alpha tester for Google brands, has automated its GA4 tracking services. The company has moved its complete server-side GA4 tracking system out of beta, giving complete Shopify and Shopify Plus checkout support. Implementing this first-party tracking solution eliminates the need for manual integration, Google Tag Manager (GTM) or Universal Analytics. The feature automatically captures recurring order features like revenue, conversion, and subscriptions. It also compiles checkout steps and upsell orders after purchase, sending this information to data destinations like Google Analytics, Segment, and Facebook Ads. Brands like the skincare brand Geologie have started benefitting from the new move by saving 50 developer hours using the new product. New Integration to Streamline NFT Processes for Shopify Merchants January 21, 2023 Shopify (SHOP) has a new integration that lets users design, mint, and sell Avalanche NFTs (non-fungible tokens). This integration helps Shopify merchants streamline their NFT processes. Retailers with minimal technical knowledge and no crypto wallet can sell their NFTs using the Venly Shopify Merchant App. The new NFTs turn into products automatically and can be displayed and sold on their storefronts. Instead of an existing crypto wallet, the merchants can access a new Blockchain wallet through an email link. The new integration simplifies Avalanche NFT sales from design to distribution. Shopify merchants also gain royalties on every secondary NFT transaction made via the Venly Market. With this venture, Shopify aims to nurture the expanding Blockchain ecosystem to promote direct NFT sales, increasing Web3 participation. title: eCommerce QA Services
headings: Ensure a Seamless eCommerce Experience With Virtina’s QA
Why Your eCommerce Website Needs a Comprehensive QA Process
text: Virtina brings you the industry-first eCommerce focused Quality Assurance or QA process. The QA process is unlike any other testing type. Even though many methods, including user testing, functional testing, requirements testing, and so on, have similar goals as that of QA, they are simply not the same. Furthermore, Virtina’s eCommerce QA is specially designed for eCommerce websites to ensure that the test considers an eCommerce business’s capabilities and goals. It is quintessential for eCommerce websites to work seamlessly. Failing to do so could directly result in loss of sales and revenue. Ensure a Seamless eCommerce Experience With Virtina’s QA Virtina’s eCommerce focused QA is a unique quality assurance process that tests eCommerce websites to find mistakes, errors, or oversights that may have escaped your notice in the development and design phases. Virtina’s eCommerce focused QA process kicks into operation as soon as the website’s requirements are laid out and even before the development begins. The more holistic the approach to QA, the better will be the quality of the website. For ensuring a seamless eCommerce experience, Virtina considers multiple factors. Some of the significant factors considered include the audience, the type of eCommerce website, mobile testing, risk level, estimated number of users, etc. Each factor we consider before the QA process gives us valuable insight into what your eCommerce website really needs. Taking a closer look at your eCommerce store’s audience helps us narrow down the testing environment for your websites, such as the browsers and devices to conduct the test. Similarly, the process also finds out the need for mobile optimization. Our process clearly defines the assumptions and preconditions and employs real data for more accurate results. Furthermore, working with an estimated number of users gives us valuable insight into the traffic that your website can handle. Why Your eCommerce Website Needs a Comprehensive QA Process  Become a Reputable Brand The main reason behind QA or Quality Assurance is to come across as a reliable and reputable brand to your customers. No one wants to transact through an eCommerce store that offers a shady user interface and below-par functionalities that may or may not work. Virtina’s eCommerce-focused QA process addresses all the points that could sway the opinion of the customers on your eCommerce store and provides the ideal solutions to fix these issues. Avoid Dire Consequences Unlike a typical informative website, eCommerce websites transact money through it, and hence security is a prime concern here. Virtina understands the uniqueness of eCommerce websites more than anyone. Our eCommerce-focused QA process dives into the intrinsic details that include but are not limited to the website’s security. Every aspect of the eCommerce store is analyzed, and their cumulative effect is drawn to figure out the ideal solution for the issues in your eCommerce website. Deliver a Reliable eCommerce Store The reliability of an eCommerce store is determined by its customers based on several factors. An eCommerce website needs to be accessible 24/7 without any issue. Even a small glitch can cause customers to abandon the site leading to valuable loss of sales. Virtina’s eCommerce focused QA process ensures that everything in your eCommerce store from pages to backlinks is working seamlessly to provide the optimal user experience to your customers. Save Time and Money Virtina’s holistic and eCommerce focused QA approach enables you to find any form of bugs well before it can cause any damage to your eCommerce store. It is more economical to have your eCommerce store bug free before it goes public. This further ensures that none of your users face any problem on the site due to any bug. It thereby saves you any loss from users abandoning the website due to any form of glitch. Finally, our QA process ensures a smooth and friction-free shopping experience on your website. How Virtina’s eCommerce-focused QA Works? Requirement Specification Virtina follows a holistic approach to its eCommerce focused QA process, and it is one of the most effective processes in the industry. Our QA process begins by listing all the requirements of the client. The requirements are listed based on their business and their unique needs. Requirement Analysis The listing of requirements allows our expert to understand the tests that may be required on the client’s eCommerce store. Furthermore, Virtina’s eCommerce focused QA process starts from the design stage itself, working throughout the development and delivery phases, ensuring constant changes. QA Testing Phase The most significant part of any QA process is the testing phase, where multiple tests are carried out to find out where and how your eCommerce website needs to be fixed and tweaked for its optimal performance. A detailed QA report is then prepared, including the title and description of the issue found, along with the relevant links and attachments. The report will also contain details on the severity, priority, and due date to fix the issue, along with expert comments on the particular issues. Follow-up Review Once the testing phase is finished, Virtina conducts a follow-up of the QA process just to ensure that we missed nothing in the process. Retesting of Fixed Bugs The bugs found during the QA testing phase are immediately fixed and tested. The fixed bugs are subjected to retesting in this phase. Regression Testing The regression testing phase in Virtina’s QA process re-runs both functional and non-functional tests to ensure that everything is working properly. A “QA Approved” status is given to the project after this phase. Interim Testing The interim testing phase is where our experts classify the pending bugs they have unearthed from your website and prioritized in order of their severity. The report is then sent to the internal/external personnel in charge depending on the client’s wish. Smoke Testing Before the delivery of a project, smoke testing is conducted on the client’s eCommerce store to reveal simple failures that may be severe enough to affect the site from going live. Internal Project Delivery The project is now all set for delivery to the project head, who then assesses the QA process conducted on the client’s eCommerce site along with the test report. Final Project Delivery Once the project head’s final assessment is finished, the project is ready to be handed over to the client along with a copy of the QA report. title: eCommerce Prototyping
headings: Bring Your eCommerce Website Idea to Life With a Prototype
See How Virtina’s eCommerce Prototyping Can Help Your Business
Why You Need to Build an eCommerce Prototype With Virtina
Easier Error Detection and Internal Collaboration
text: When it comes to eCommerce, it is never a good idea to dive headfirst into the development, thinking you can address the issues as you go along. It is a mistake that could very well cost you valuable time and effort and, by extension, your money as well. This is where prototyping comes into the picture. A prototype can help you bring your concept to reality and ensure it captures all your requirements right from the initial stages. It is the lack of planning and involvement of the client that often leads to the high failure rate in eCommerce, which, according to Google, is a whopping 80%. Virtina’s eCommerce prototyping uses advanced tools like “Just in Mind” to give you a high fidelity interactive prototyping experience. Having such extensive and detailed prototyping allows you, the client, to be involved and be an active part of the process ensuring that the site is built exactly the way you want it. By doing so, Virtina does the impossible and turns the industry statistics of an 80% failure rate on its head. Virtina’s eCommerce prototypes are comprehensive and customer-centric prototype creations done explicitly for eCommerce. Virtina creates an adaptive prototype for your eCommerce store capable of reshaping itself based on your requirements. Virtina’s eCommerce website prototype gives you an interactive demo of your website to help you get a comprehensive picture of how your website would look like before the development phase. The prototype enables you to unearth the design and functional aspects needed for your website that you yourself were not aware of before. Bring Your eCommerce Website Idea to Life With a Prototype Typically, building a prototype could mean several things. It could be a paper sketch or an HTML based one which is clickable. But at Virtina, we employ a prototype model that lets you navigate from page to page, actively interacting with the pages and even use certain functionalities like drop-down menus. By doing so, we enable you to get a more comprehensive understanding of how the look and feel of your website will be. Prototyping can be carried out in various ways. You can create a very simple clickable prototype using a PowerPoint, PDF, even MS Word. Although these basic methods do get their job done when it comes to eCommerce prototyping, such juvenile methods are not enough. Virtina makes use of specialized prototyping tools for its eCommerce prototyping process. Virtina employs the “Just In Mind” prototyping tool for creating the eCommerce prototypes. The tool comes equipped with fully interactive prototype designs capable of supporting clickable wireframes to completely interactive advanced prototypes. The “Just In Mind” prototyping tool also offers a full range of web interactions and mobile gestures. See How Virtina’s eCommerce Prototyping Can Help Your Business Why You Need to Build an eCommerce Prototype With Virtina Provides Functionality and Interactions Unlike a static mockup and wireframes that cannot convey animations or navigate you from one page to another, the eCommerce prototypes built by Virtina are interactive to their core. The prototypes built by Virtina are purpose-built and optimized with eCommerce functionalities unique to your business and its requirements. Furthermore, you can interact freely with the prototype and even leave your comment on what you like and what you don’t. Easy and Effective Communication The eCommerce prototypes built by Virtina are interactive and equipped with functionalities that can actually work. The highly interactive nature provided by our prototypes enables you to experience first-hand how your eCommerce website may look and feel. title: eCommerce Performance Optimization
headings: Enhance Your eCommerce Store’s Performance with Virtina
Load Testing of your eCommerce Website
Why Choose Virtina for eCommerce Optimization?
Let’s Optimize the eCommerce Store Today
Don’t Let a Diminished Performance on Your Unoptimized eCommerce Store Eat Away Your Conversions
text: The high abandonment and increasing bounce rates can be attributed to the slow page loads, non-responsive, badly cached pages, weak hosting provider, and many other critical issues that increase the Time to First Byte (TTFB) and Time to Interactive (TTI). Both of these components drag and slow the performance of an eCommerce website. As such, you lose sales- which in-turn affects your revenue and profits. Enhance Your eCommerce Store’s Performance with Virtina The unlimited potential of eCommerce performance optimization ensures you derive all of the following benefits from its impactful and conversion-centric tactics. Improve Your Rankings in Search Engine Increase Retention Rate Lower Bounce Rates Increase Revenue and Profits Increase Click-Through Rates (CTR) Increase Credibility of the Brand Increase Conversion Rates Increase Customer Lifetime Value Load Testing of your eCommerce Website Virtina’s load test focuses on testing the performance of the requests to your backend. The most fundamental aspect our load testers analyze is the maximum load any URL can sustain at a given time. Our load testing protocols generate the most accurate load with real browsers. We create the most logical representation of a load on an eCommerce site. Virtina will create realistic runtime scenarios that take into account the number of users, browser types, network limitations, and schedule. Check all the parameters like the number of connections, response time, performance throughput, transaction times, and more. Standard Package Number of URL – 1 Concurrent Users – Upto 50 Number of URL – 1 Concurrent Users – 50 to 100 Number of URL – 1 Concurrent Users – 100 to 250 Custom Package Scope – Entire Website Build – Create different Buyer Journey’s Buyer Journey – Buyers arriving on a unique URL of your eCommerce site from Social Media, Home Page, Search Engine, PPC Ad, etc. Analyze – Comprehensively study each Buyer Journey Standard Package The standard package will execute severe load tests on a set number of pages for multiple users. This test will help us to determine the extent of load your eCommerce website can handle. The load testers will check for the maximum number of simultaneous users generating HTTP requests to a web server.  Furthermore, we will also check for the maximum number of simultaneous users loading a single page repeatedly in a browser. Not only that, but we’ll also test your website from multiple locations around the world. We will adjust the number of users in real-time to measure performance in fluctuating conditions. The load testers will discover how your eCommerce website responds to various loads and identify performance bottlenecks before they cause any damage to the production environment. We will extract insights about how your website scales and whether it can perform under pressure. Price The price will vary depending on the number of users being tested for every unique URL (Page). Result The eCommerce performance engineers in Virtina will submit the performance analysis of the page. We will generate a report containing the various metrics and performance outputs of the page being tested for a given number of users. Ultimately, we will create and forward a report containing the maximum user load that the URL can handle. Custom Package The Custom Package will carefully curate your eCommerce website. A holistic analysis will help our load testers to discover various buyer journeys. A buyer could land directly on a product page, get there from the home page, social media, backlink, or anywhere else. A variation in the journey could potentially see changes in performance behavior. Our experts will meticulously assess each buyer’s journey. We will test the most frequent user journeys. We will mimic the precise user journey or user scenario and create a logical flow of how users interact with your website. A load test here will simulate a user’s path before landing on a designated page. We can create performance scenarios to test for any condition you want to test. Our load testing measures seamlessly replicate intricate user journeys.  In essence, we will script various user paths and flows and test them under different load conditions to help you identify potential issues that can break your website during peak times. An eCommerce store owner knows fully that all these critical user-flows need to be working correctly under high traffic. Most SaaS providers do not offer data backup and it is limited to bulk backup intended for unprecedented disasters like a server crash. In short, there is no undo button for your business on a SaaS platform due to human error. In an eCommerce store, you are always under the threat of data corruption or loss. Any unintended changes to your original data caused by an error that occurs during writing, reading, storage, transmission, or processing can be termed as data corruption. Human errors are the most common reason for eCommerce failures, and even the most insignificant error could cause a chain reaction and bring down your store. A real-time backup means you have the ability to start afresh. Complete Control Our shadow backup gives you complete control over your eCommerce store’s data. title: Retail eCommerce
